pros: I joined the company in July 2014 as a Financial Reporting Analyst/EMEA. The leads and colleagues are very professional. I learned a lot of things from them on how to deal with foreign counterparts. Being a financial reporting analyst (integrated close) is very challenging. You have to be keen to details and creative enough to cope up with their manual FDL reduction initiatives. You are encouraged to think outside the box and suggest ways on how to improve the current processes. I enjoyed my stay in that team until the top management decided to migrate the financial reporting tasks to Citi Mumbai. We were then transferred to various departments within the company, and unfortunately I was transferred to the Fixed Asset Team. The leads at that time were rushing the lateral transfers, and we were not given enough time to carefully study our options. As a CPA, joining in the fixed assets team would intake very limited opportunities to grow.
cons: Company policy regarding the meal and transportation allowance is not properly communicated within the teams. Some teams are not strict in approving the meal receipts, so if you're unlucky enough to be under a strict supervisor, then you have no choice but to follow.

advice: No clue what to do here, this place is toxic. Try to make banks more appealing to tech workers if you don't want your tech to suck?
pros: Higher than average salary (probably because of all the cons), flexible work schedule... i honestly can not think of any other positives.
cons:
There is a one hundred step process to anything that you do. Citi is using some very current tools when it comes to automation, configuration management, software development, etc, but all the features that make these tools so great are disabled or implemented incorrectly. 

The amount of "red tape" at this place is an enormous hindrance on creativity. The simplest of things are made difficult for no reason other than to check a box that was designed by some business person that somehow obtained their CISSP.

The hypocriticalness of this is massively amusing.. you don't have administrative rights on a Citi provided laptop, but business units supporting the trading markets are allowed to run 30 year old operating systems with huge vulnerabilities.

The culture is nothing short of depressing. Some reviews on Glassdoor will suggest being remote makes for difficult collaboration, but I can assure you that you're better off being remote, as being in the office is very demotivating.

There are people in roles that they definitely shouldn't be in.. my advice to anyone looking for a career in technology is to stay away from big banks.

advice: Pay people more. No one cares about meaningless titles.
pros:
There are a lot of opportunities to move around laterally. 
Training in Buffalo is decent and the people are nice.
cons:
Senior management continues to move jobs from NYC to Buffalo to save money. This is a good thing if you live in Buffalo. This is bad if you live in NYC. 
The pay is low. Generally people don't receive raises and if they do it's usually only $300 to $700 more a year. Which is fine but starting pay is normally between 28,000 and 32,000 for entry level jobs. 
There is a running joke that anyone can be an AVP at Citi. They'll give you the title but no money. 
Managers are mixed bag. Some are really good but many are terrible. There are times where a manager will mess up and just throw one of their employees under the bus. 
Benefits are terrible. Health insurance is basically a high deductible or a high deductible. 
You never get to take all of your vacation. There is always a reason for why you can't take off.
Groups are run bare bones. Some departments have a 2 for 1 policy. Your team has to lose 2 people to hire 1 person. Which in itself is awful but then office politics come into play and your 1 might be given to someone else.

advice: Cons- It is in Tucson. Tucson lacks a diverse business community, it lacks experienced business managers at all levels and the city seems mismanaged and it struggles along. I mention this because if you are starting your career and want to network, Tucson may not be the place for it.  CITI will offer little options to network with upper to senior management. You will not find the Harvard, Wharton, Sloan or for that matter a Marshall, Anderson or Thunderbird MBA's here in Tucson. You will be able to learn the mortgage service organization but little else. So if you do choose to come here,CITI in Tucson, think of it as “punching your ticket”, learn as much as possible and bolt to a bigger city were you can prosper and apply the organizational knowledge and find mentor tutelage.BTW CITI cut the bonus structure in half. My review accounted for a bonus of 12K per year, which was my average. Going forward cut that in half.
pros: Pros- Benefits are good for Tucson. Work environment is good for Tucson. Fellow employees are great to work with, good people.
cons: Cons- this site location has limited upside mobility for employees.

summary: Ok place to start, nothing more
advice: Value your employees and don't let them know they're expendable from the get go.  Offer some incentives to reward those who are doing their best to make the company successful instead of increasing responsibilities and offering nothing in return. If a simple cost of living increase is too expensive, then shut the office down and hire contractors, because taking advantage of the people who keep the company going is the greatest disrespect of all.
pros: Generous PTO, decent benefits, good place to gain experience in the industry, ability to work from home
cons: The training is laughable at best and non existent in most cases. The Buffalo office is used for cheap labor from the local universities and nothing more. Do not accept a position here if you're looking for a long term career or have previous experience as it doesn't matter. You will not get rewarded for your hard work with practically no opportunity to move up (within your first 3 years) and no salary increases as well. Don't let the big name or the recruiter talk you into it unless you need to get your foot in the door and have no other options.

summary: Like the titanic it is taking a long time but eventually it will sink
advice: Look beyond cost savings and try growing the top line for a change.
pros: If you work in Cybersecurity then this is the place to be.
cons: Where to start. All top management worries about is the bottom line, cost cutting and squeezing you as hard as they can. Clueless as it relates to building top line growth. When asked about monetizing their IT prowess the answer is "we want to remain a bank. I wonder if the buggy whip executives said we want to remain the pre-eminent buggy whip provider. Bonuses non existent unless you work on the revenue side or are an MD. Once you get hired be happy with the salary you negotiated as that is what you will have for a LONG time. Raises are sparse and sadly pathetic- in the 1% range. They used to have a great program where you could earn a masters in IT from Stevens in Newark but cost savings made it go away. If you are contemplating joining this place, consider this -the most talented Citi people are alumni like I - the talent drain is unrelenting so you will not have anyone of any value to mentor you nor make you grow - do yourself a favor -  look elsewhere -there are better places to work than Citi.

summary: Full of learning resources and opportunities for everyone
advice: Make sure you implement equitable performance review standards for new grads and entry level jobs, it becomes less important once they get promoted to management roles since then it becomes more about 'getting things done.' New grads won't make enough of an impact on your operations for you to 'notice' who is performing better.
pros:
Citi is a great company to work for if you play your cards right, they support work-life balance and provide excellent benefits. The internal website is full of useful information about the company and other educational topics that you should take advantage of.

It's size makes it easy to get 'lost' in the shuffle, if you don't find a way to stay relevant then you will get eaten. They make sure they get their money's worth with the salaries they give their employees, even though it might look like a relaxing environment, people are always expected to deliver. Performance reviews are always thorough.
cons: Performance measurement can be subjective in relationship driven roles, a bad review from one manager early in your career can be almost impossible to recover from.

summary: Good comp, some flexibility, disorganized and convoluted processs
advice: Improve documentation requirements throughout the departments. Standardize audit processes, to make audit cycle more efficient. Focus on managing work life balance for employees. Consider evolving to fully remote environment.
pros: Competitive comp and benefits - 17 days PTO at AVP level, 22 at VP; 6 socks days, can purchase additional 5 days at salary cost. Good PPO plan, HMO isn’t great compared to other companies. 6% 401k match after one year. 12 weeks fully paid medical leave available. Lots of opportunities to move up. Well defined audit universe, and entity structures. Good training materials.
cons: Disorganized company processes, convoluted (too many procedures for simple processes), audit department lacks structure and standardization (different managers have different work product requirements), planning phase takes up the entire audit timeframe, recurring audits need to be done from scratch each time (no standard audit programs available in a library), audit tool is cumbersome. Work life balance is terrible at the VP level and above, there definitely are expectations of working 50+ hours, including AVP level at times - this can be driven by the manager which style vary widely IA group to IA group. Strict hybrid model, no fully remote roles.

advice: Citi's brand was severely damaged in the crisis, Mike Corbat seems to have the right plan and is executing. He seems to be steering the ship in the right direction but this is the Titanic, so it has and will take time. Pay the groups that matter and contribute to the bottom line, not the loudest one(s) in the room. Way to much power given to technology in allowing them to dictate critical timelines, approval processes, and business tech improvements.
pros: Great people, global organization, various avenues for career paths. I was in a great group with a terrific team and highly intelligent Global Head, this can vary from department to department and location to location from my understanding.
cons: Scaling back on benefits that matter (expensive Medical high co pays/deductibles only covers 80%), aggressive cost cutting in the businesses, hiring freezes, preach meritocracy but not fully executing, lots of chiefs make for heavy workload on the indians. Too much preference is given to the analyst program hires without an equal emphasis to define proper talented non program existing employees for career growth within.

advice: Spend more time developing your employees than your software.  Give clear guidelines for employees pursuing advancement.  And share this with supervisors so that their time and ours aren't wasted.
pros: The benefits are amazing, and if you work hard and receive favorable employee ratings, they will move heaven and earth to work with you on a work life balance.
cons: The leadership is spotty.  Unit managers have considerable autonomy over their employees and work group which has many pros and cons.  My biggest complaint was in advancement.  In 16 years, I never was clear on what goes into advancement decisions.  Honestly my direct supervisors were equally clueless.  They would mentor me and other employees for weeks on their own time only to watch as we weren't granted interviews.  It is not unusual to see a 20 year old on his or her first job obtain a supervisory position while people who had degrees and years of experience in similar roles at other companies never be considered.  And the corporate culture is obsessed with change.  If something works, it will be replaced by a new process with limited testing.

summary: Big company, work your way around
advice: Actively ask and listen to the minions doing the menial work. You’ll get further quicker.
pros:
Lots of mobility opportunities. Citi really encourages people to cross train and learn other functions as a way of dipping your toes into other waters, so to speak. Of course each department is run differently and each manager has different leadership styles, but with such a huge site and many networking opportunities, you are not doing something right if you aren’t involved in one of the many networking and social groups. This is key to moving ahead in an especially big organization.

Up to a 6% 401K company match, other healthcare discounts through Red Brick

Generally speaking and depending on your area, working remote is not a huge issue.
cons: You can become a number if you don’t speak out and drive your own path. (However, even if your manager is bad there are so many other people to speak to to get direction in your career). The healthcare options are OK. Parking is becoming increasingly a bigger issue due to town of Amherst zoning laws not permitting parking garages.

advice:
Force analysts/associates to take at least two protected week long vacations a year to avoid loosing talent to tech firms and make it a priority to have at least one day a week off without having to check emails. These policies are already in place but nobody enforces or monitors them and it is not advised by the Senior bankers to take vacation at all.  

Monitor work load better by creating staffers so that there is a proportional amount of workloads among analyst and associates.  As of now some juniors will work 90 hour weeks while others will only work 40 hours a week and nobody seems to care and that is not fair.
pros: Great experience and great training.
cons: It is hard to use Vacation days and will scorned by your VP if you take them because they feel you do not yet deserve them. Hours are tough and it is hard to have a life outside of the office but that's the nature of investment banking.  Working from home is also frowned on by the senior bankers so expect to be in the office at least 12 hours a day, 6 days a week.

advice: Please listen to your employees who are working directly with Citi customers,  cut back on conference calls, reward your employees with encouragement and positive feedback.
pros: Pretty good starting salary. Citi has a good brand name and has a great reputation for their employee training program.   Citibank has an international presence and has branches in over 120 countries so it makes it easy and interesting to work with international customers.
cons: Horrible work life balance.  Will work you into the ground between the short staffing in the branches and the "call nights" until 8pm.  After you've been worked until you're completely burnt out, they continuously change goals so it makes it impossible to get a payout.  The bank is doing very poorly in the Boston market which is why they have closed 9 branches, downsized to 1 banker per branch, and wiped out all business development officers. With absolutely no involvement in a saturated banking community such as Boston, how can one ever succeed?  It's really a shame because as a bank Citi does have a lot to offer, but the employees working in the branches are paralyzed by red tape and useless mandatory conference calls 3 times a day that do nothing but waste time when real work could be done.

advice: Better communication required at times - I think that sometimes because senior management have spent so long discussing an issue or a change in operations that they assumed all staff were aware of what was going on!!
pros:
I worked for Citi for over 13 years and although there were times where I wasn't happy with certain decisions there are areas which need improvement I do feel that Citi is a good employer.
There is a good work life balance and  I feel that there is a company wide attitude that you should only work core hours if possible!
The people are what make the company and there is a real sense of working together.
Holidays and benefits are very good.
cons:
There is a lack of any structured training. For some people pay is not in line with industry levels.
The HR department is not very good - always felt that rather than wanting to do their job they had the attitude that they were doing you a favour!!!

advice: Don't be so rude and pushy towards your employees. You say you have an open door policy when in reality when one wants to meet you, you say "I'm a big manager don't be wasting my time." You all wonder why turn around is so horrid. There you go.
pros: Offers some pretty good benefits (Medical, dental, etc) and pay I believe is fair. Has some extra groups you can get involved in. Pretty good people around you co worker wise, not manager wise. I did make a lot of friends there. Security on site, pretty relaxed dress code.
cons: Managers can be unfair and can do a lot of things against policy. Very harsh when beginning. Not the best food in cafeteria. Training will tell you one thing when it's really another. Force you to go to "town hall meetings" on your break, or you don't go at all. Horrible shifts for starters (mine was 11:30-10 my entire time) When you bring up ideas for the groups you can join, I did a red friday for military idea, it was never brought up. But when I left they basically stole my idea and went on with it.

advice: Terminate the employees who have been in the company for a longtime, and under perform.  Provide new and younger employees with higher raises and incentives so that they will not leave.
pros: Plenty of opportunities for overtime, and an on-site cafeteria. If you are patient, you can move to a different department if you do not like the one you are currently in.
cons: If you are a recent grad, beware! Citi loves two kinds of people to employ: New grads to take advantage of and underpay, and professionals who have already had years of experience under their belt and have a Master's to compensate nicely. Unfortunately, I fell into the first category. If you apply to an "Operational Analyst role," you may be thrown into a bad department, and overworked there to fix mistakes from previous employees who have long left the company. Incentives and promotions as an associate (entry level) are minimum to non-existent. The older Co-workers who have seniority in the company do minimal work, while you may be given their work if they are deemed to "not" be able to do it.

advice: Keep to appointments especially HR
pros: Medicover health insurance and Multi sports card
cons: Delay on feedback to staff

summary: This is a heaven for people who want to learn financial markets.
advice:
1) Instead of doing same old and holding the fort, get out and think differently.
2) You should also force rotate people and put them in different teams, so employees will learn how Citi as a whole works. 
3) Learn from Google/Facebook on how to treat employees by bringing better onsite amenities. Spend some money on employees instead of losing in Forex market.
4) Put technology in center piece of everything you do. 
5) Hire really smart people and not just average people whose goals are to pay mortgage and tuition for their kids.
pros:
Work/life balance
Good benefits (onsite amenities could be better)
Relatively fast moving
Diverse
Great locations/buildings (388 Greenwich in NYC looks awesome inside/out)
cons: The technology is behind. The CTO/CIO needs to embrace new technology fast. They should provide super fast development machines, access to cutting edge technology trainings and drive the business to adopt new technology. The user interface of most applications are outdated. They really need to spend money on how customers are using their applications and change the UI design of every single application.

summary: Good, stable place to work with good benefits, large company with too many chefs.
advice:
Make it easier for leaders to manage out people that are not a good fit for roles.  Once a person gets a job, they can stay there for years just by not seriously screwing up.  
Define career paths for subject matter experts and high performing individual contributors. Not all people are talented people managers or strong leaders, however can bring incredible value to the company.
pros: Diverse role and location opportunities, competitive compensation. You can be very successful if you are politically savvy and can devote time to running unofficial PR campaigns for your initiatives.
cons: A very large organization with too many decision makers.  Brilliant ideas are often dulled by incorporating too many decision makers or influencers.  Mid level managers are very competitive, and often politically motivated. People who do great work but keep their heads down are not rewarded organizationally.  The organization does not do a good job of shedding sub-par performers or people who are not a good fit for their role.

summary: Good place for BFSI Analytics professionals, Growth is team dependent
advice:
Keep eyes on mid level management. Though there has been efforts to make the culture great, some people managers and employees bend the rules based on their needs.
Other than that, Citi is a great place to work
pros:
1. Open culture
2. WFH
3. More leaves as compared to other firms, 20 public holidays+ 30 PL + Unlimited Sick leave
cons:
1. Bureaucracy- your rating is dependent on your relationship with manager and US stakeholders

In case of manual works, one has to follow US stakeholder as well as manager's instructions on unproductive works and make them happy by doing hard work

summary: Citibank Human Resources Group needs urgent reform

Again because of the hiring of friends individuals do what they want on the job while real hardworking individuals abide  by the rules..

summary: Only good for experience, nothing else

pros:

3. they doesn't care about the high turnover that is happening and would continue to hire contract basis worker to help fill in the gap.
4. top management would conduct a team analysis on the worker in the dept, but nothing would change if the top management itself is the reason for the work stress itself

summary: Great company to kickstart your career
pros: Great people, amazing opportunities, lots of training. Very diverse and inclusive.
cons: Lots of workload for a starting rank

summary: Things are good until they aren't
pros: Room for growth when it's available. Great salary when you get to underwriting (no bonuses). Great people to work with, and benefits are very good.
cons:
0 loyalty, 0 transparency, and 0 HR assistance. Citi will treat you well until they don't need you anymore, then they will be happy to lay you off or make you work an insane amount with no thank you. There is absolutely no transparency from upper levels of management. They will break endless promises and shift you as needed. 

If you run into issues with your paystub or Citi related benefits, good luck. I was still on their payroll over a month after my last day (quit voluntarily) and had to reimburse them all of the money they accidentally paid me. I couldn't even get a letter saying I didn't work there anymore so I could sign up for health insurance elsewhere. And couldn't even get someone on the phone (except for a call center in India). Would hate to think of what happens to people who REALLY need HR help. Escalated ethics concerns as well but didn't see any changes. 

Like any other corporation, Citibank is willing to screw you over if it benefits their bottom line. They are great to work with until they aren't, so tread carefully.

pros: Company culture was very good
cons: Pay was not the best

advice: Increase the annual bonus amount
pros: Good work culture and Brand to work with
cons: Nothing specific. Majorly comparable with industry standards.

pros: Pay, leaves, health benefits, work life balance
cons: Pressure will be more at times

pros: Diversity, company culture, professional atmosphere.
cons: Have found no cons to share.

pros: Pays well and provides good opportunities
cons: Lot of overtime and lot of data issues

advice:
- Invest in young talent, not only in hiring them, but giving them more say and more power.
- Making the organisation leaner would be better going forward.
pros:
- Given its size, it is great for internal mobility, especially across geographies. There are always opportunities, and there is flexibility in movement, though it may take time.
- Because of the large footprint that Citi has across the globe and across different segments of finance, there will always be ample opportunity to leverage this for the benefit of your business.
- One of the more stable banks. They may pay less, but the job is more secure, culture is not aggressive and competition is not cut-throat.
cons:
- Workforce is very top-heavy; not a lot of young talent around, though they are now trying to change it.
- Very bureaucratic; there is generally a lot of politics involved, and your work alone does not guarantee success. Also, any work takes a long time to get to completion.
- Compared to its competitors, not really at the forefront of innovation and technology.
- Compensation generally lower than competition.

advice: Pay attention to your staff that can be pushed/groomed further instead of going by the book of checking the queue of "who should be in line next". The general thinking is that ALL people need 2 years to become familiar with their 1st stage of the ops process, which pushes many people to leave, seeking validation elsewhere as they aren't considered for further grooming (even if they are better than perhaps the person in line before them) until the 2 year mark...
pros:
-great environment, people are friendly and welcoming
-operations are smooth, you will always be able to ask for guidance if unsure
-great courses offered outside of work timings that you may sign up for on your own time
-shuttle bus provided
cons:
-promotion opportunities are limited and their method of choice is rigid
-roles are specialised, so cross training is not provided often and as a result, in the long term, one's knowledge becomes limited
-little compensation for OT (requiring fulfilling a certain criteria) you're expected to "do your job" even if it is past your working hours

advice: Invest in your people and in better, more up to date technology.
pros: This was a good place to start my career.  I was able to move up several times during my tenure.  The benefits were good and the people were easy to get along with.  When the economy is doing well or the rates are low, this is a great place to work.
cons: Some in management were allowed to "run wild" as long as they produced results and if you got in their way, you were gone.  As mentioned above in the Pros as long as the economy was good or the rates were low, times were great, however once the rates go up and the housing market becomes stagnant, which it tends to do on a regular cycle about every 5-10 years, things go south fast.  There were constant layoffs and this stressed everyone out and productivity tanked.  The systems were ancient as were the processes surrounding them.  Compensation was low when promoted from within and bonuses were low or non-existent.

summary: Always there if you need to get by
advice: When you are going through a period of trying to make the department better and get things on track, communicate with the people who are actually doing the job and treat them good to keep moral up.  Sometimes lunch can go a long way.
pros: If you don't burn your bridges, you can always go back if you go through hard times.
cons: Pay is not competitve and they do not take your education and experience into considering.  Most jobs are just that "jobs" and all you need is a high school diploma.  Someone with no experience or education can come in and make the same money.  Management clearly does not know what they are doing.  Change is to be expected in any workplace but pure incompetence is a different story.  You will most likely make lateral moves in this company. Growth is not optimal.  They expect you to engage and pick up more work like train employees and take on team lead duties but they won't pay you more.

summary: Wish I could work for Citi again!
advice: A little hike on salaries or perks could get a lot more motivation from employees.
pros: Lots of autonomy given to employees who prove they are able to handle it, flexible hours, the opportunity to grow with the company and the mobility to move to any of their offices in your region, great work-life balance where you are forced to take 2 weeks off in a row to ensure that you have a good rest throughout the year and are able to come back fresh, great value for thinking outside the box and going above and beyond your assigned tasks, office culture excellent and very young - made lots of friends at Citi, game/rest room to take breaks in, access internet, play games and get a chair massage!
cons: Bonuses given are not the best but that also might be because of the recession, since I worked for a remote manager, it was sometimes difficult to get paperwork or other approvals done locally, salaries are not that great but are considered based on your tasks at work.

summary: Addicted to reorgs and no appreciation
advice: Team morale has been declining fast. There needs to be better training for managers to provide their team the right tools on how to prioritize work loads. In addition, managers definitely need training on how to appreciate their employees more. Compensation helps but there are many other ways like certificates, star awards, verbal etc.  In the long run, it only looks like they are only in it for themselves which is a shame because they don't know how to push back with their direct managers.
pros: Flexible work schedule, generous vacation, benefits & 401k.
cons: I am fine with change and keeping things fresh but this company is constantly reorganizing and as a result it really does little to improve the business & the quality of life for employees.  There have been long periods when there has been lack of leadership in some departments. Depending on your manager, there can be long hours & little appreciation. There was a time when it felt like a family, now it feels like you're just a number.

advice: Try to streamline some processes that clients are involved in.
pros:
-Citi has a lot of people who make this place special
-The large array of products and segments allow Citi to help many people inside and out with their financial needs
cons:
-There are some very manual parts of the business that could be automated
-Compliance does not usually grant any exceptions even if it means clients are caught in the middle of red tape

summary: Lots of good things to say about Citi
pros:
Many opportunities for training and development - self-paced online, webinars and in-person - plus you can learn a lot from the people around you, depending on your role and team
Also many opportunities to get involved with various employee networks and other activities, particularly if you are located on a Citi campus
Good compensation, PTO and other benefits
cons:
These aren't exactly "cons" but more so "comments": 
As with any big company, there's a lot of variability among businesses/departments and some are definitely better to work for than others
And as with any big company (and many smaller ones), it can be easy to get "lost" if you don't have good management support - again, some managers are much better than others
That said, if you are looking to work for Citi, try to get to know the hiring manager and the department as well as you can before you commit. New staff who figure they'll get a foot in the door anywhere and then make a move are likely to be disappointed or frustrated.

summary: impolite culture between teams. poor communication skills observed even among vp and svp positions.

They expect you to work extended hours

advice: Upper management is not in liason with staff to better service the customers, is like military type of management, if you don't do what they say the punish you with long calls and intimidation
pros: online banking international exposure, company's culture used to care about employees well being, good incentive plan for bankers
cons: the retail banking side of the company is briging top executives from Wachovia and they are changing the company's culture for worse, cutting benefits, micromanaging every single process in the branches, putting manager to work over 60 hrs a week taking advantage they are salary and not to pay overtime, setting up unrealistic goals and causing a lot of employees turn over. A lot of preassure to sell provide good service without giving enough tools. Upper management is not in liason with staff to better service the customers, is like military type of management, if you don't do what they say the punish you with long calls and intimidation. You get promoted based on who you know and not in what you are bringing to the table.

advice: -Bring fresh, diverse leadership in to the MD ranks. Quickly. The bad behavior and culture won’t end unless changes are made.
pros:
Exposure to people and cultures around the world
In many orgs, if you work hard, and show commitment, you can grow your responsibilities and get promoted. 
If you have a strong, supportive manager, things can be great. 
388 Greenwich building renovation, nice new facilities.
cons:
-Ego-driven, political, and very competitive. Many people think more about what a project can do for their career, rather than how it can help the company or team. 
-Teams and individuals compete against each other, rather than market competition. 
-Not enough movement or diversity in senior leadership ranks. People stay put for many years, leading to stagnation in culture and ideas. 
-Extremely limited resources and a lack of prioritization across businesses. As a result, many poor quality work products are delivered, and business goals are not achieved. 
-Many employees are overworked and stressed due to lack of resources and prioritization. 
-Corporate title structure and related power dynamics are a massive culture driver. There isn’t adequate validation of business initiatives. If an MD thought of an idea, it’s taken as gospel.

pros: Benefits, work/life balance, competitive pay and room for advancement. Great atmosphere, definitely enjoy what we do. Great place to work
cons: None to be honest. The bank treats all employees fairly and has an inclusive culture. Best in class across the board.

summary: If you are a good employee that works hard make sure to promote yourself.
advice: Citi is shaped like an upside triangle. Senior Management needs to stop taking blind unrealistic measures. Listen to the rank and file and quit depending on out side firms that pull the wool over their eyes. Citi has some really good employees with little or no hope in regards to their future and security. Citi was built by the hard work and sweat of many of the common people. The firm is still suffering from the problems of the 2008 bubble being burst. Stop hiring outsourced management firms that promise huge savings i.e., 30 million annually. Let your in house team manage to a number. That worked for many years!
pros: 5 years ago I could list many good reasons to work for Citi, can think of any at the moment. Job security and knowing if you work hard you will be taken care of is not the case any more.
cons: Citi used to be a firm where you knew your future was safe. Now if management changes in New York, all that you worked for could go down the drain. Not good when you are trying to retain talent.

summary: Great start, decent pay, no room for growth
advice: Promote individuals who show consistency and are putting in the effort to further advance their career.
pros: Citibank can be a great stepping stone. Their training program and bank platform are spectacular (albeit very slow majority of the time). The compensation for personal banker positions is one of the highest if you're coming on board from another financial institution. Great financial products and modern bank solutions for clients.
cons: I will be with the company for 4 years come this March and have submitted many job applications to help further develop my career. Majority of my applications have gone unanswered and the ones I do receive a response to say that "they have found a better qualified candidate". The positions I have applied to are nothing out of the ordinary for a personal banker to want to develop into. There just seems to be a lack of opportunity and growth potential. I've brought much business and deposits into my branch, my monthly compensation from surpassing "hurdles" will reflect that and the only reason I can imagine for not promoting me is because I'm an asset to them while holding the position I'm currently in.

advice: Find ways to cut out some of the administrative overhead. You seek to hire knowledgeable technology pros, yet when you do, you then put them in the position where those skills languish and go unused, simply because the Enterprise focus seems to be on the bureaucracy.
pros: Good work/life balance and an even better, highly flexible work schedule/alternate workplace policy. Generally speaking, as long as you deliver, you can work from home with a reasonable schedule either when needed or on a regular schedule. Your mileage may vary depending on the specific group you're in but across the TTS Technology landscape, just about everyone works remotely some portion of time.
cons: Bureaucracy, plain and simple. You will spend 80% of your work like of purely administrative tasks, responding to exception reports, doing things to stay off exception reports, etc. Then there are all the organizational "asks" - fill this out, collect metrics on this, etc. All of this is on top of the 100-200 emails per day that a typical mid-level or higher technology person gets. Forget about doing anything meaningful or value-added - this is the type of place that you just put your time in and collect a paycheck.

summary: Great experience - barring the fact that they don't recognize and promote talent as well as they should.
advice:
Recognize and promote talent and help employees develop and grow within.
Vision should permeate down the line.
pros:
Great work life balance - at least in the business units I have been exposed to.
Great to have on the resume.
Management has been striving to make changes after the financial meltdown debacle and they have been successful in implementing key regulatory and other changes,
cons:
Lack of job - skill fit. Managers does not show an active interest in developing team member's and helping them grow.
Complete lack of appreciation for a job well done.
The company expects you to utilize all your skillsets (not just what you have been hired for) and then would not appreciate or compensate for providing services and going the extra mile.
I literally have contributed to 3-4 jobs while getting paid for one. The company realized huge cost savings from the the automation and ideas I had a stake in developing but I did not get as much as a "good job".
Some managers do try and steal the credit for a job well done - when it was all your effort that led to the well done.

advice: For a change, give performing employees if nothing then atleast inflation rate raise to keep going and continue performing. Lets see how managers work with lighter bonus for a change. Afterall some of us actually spend weeknights and weekends trying to meet all the deadlines.  Reward the people who actually do the work. Also, management should be upfront about what is the teams' future (instead of bluffing or scaring employees about their jobs). If you are going downsize, then tell them or don't tell atall. The company may survive just fine in the future based on how stingy they are and taking advantage of good employees.
pros: International- so plenty of departments you could transfer in when there are openings. Things constantly change, so there are always new things to learn. Good benefits-insurance.
cons: You can go years without getting a raise. During offer call, catch line is that there is bonus potential. A year after employment, you find out you have  to get a certain rating. When you do get that, no bonus and not even a inflation rate increase. Company profits, but few employees overwork (are abused)  thinking their efforts and performance will be paid for b/c rating is so good...until you see no bonus though you met all the standards. Surely management got bonuses when company reported good earnings. But if you ask, response will be "be lucky you got a job".

advice:
Follow through with promises you make to your employees.  Employees get tired of carrots that never materialize.
Accept responsibility if you make a mistake.
pros:
-	The health benefits are actually good for the area I was in.
-	401K match to 6%
-	Work from home was available on an as needed basis
-	Most of the people were dedicated and care about their job.
-	They place a heavy emphasis on volunteering and helping other people.
-	Mandatory paid time off
-	Health rewards cards and benefits
-	Employee break room is well stocked.  I was impressed.
cons:
-	The 15% bonus “given to the highest performer” annually is subjective.  This is a real deterrent to doing high quality work.
-	A lot of the good talent has already left the company.
-	Women leaders are not empowered to make decisions.  The company talks about tolerance yet none of the women in our area, who were promoted to higher management, made the decisions.  This is very backward.
-	You’re lucky if you get more than 3% per year in pay raises.
-	Exit interviews are not given to all employees.
-	Lots of micro-managing.  Heaven forbid if you have your own mind. 
-	Little training is provided on the system.
-	Vague and often unattainable annual goals that must be completed usually before October.

summary: Much depends on where you are in this huge multinational
advice: Cross the gap between senior management and front line employees and listen. Then connect to customer needs and perceptions. There is some ivory tower thinking and inward looking at senior levels. Leadership should be talking about customers, competition, competitive advantages--not the next reorganization.
pros: Mobility between businesses. Opportunities to work and travel overseas. Rich and deep corporate history and culture. The work can be meaningful and motivating if you are responsible for a business unit. It is a company that operates on a truly grand and complex multinational scale.
cons: At the entry level Citi payroll is pretty low as a percentage of total expenses. In other words, they do not pay well compared to other institutions. There is a highly politicized corporate culture. It is this way in two senses, internal politics is more significant than other companies, the "who you know is the most valuable skill set" approach. Secondarily, the company is woke to a fault. If you do not see your role as transformative of society towards fashionable social trends as well as profit driven, keep your thoughts to yourself.

pros:
Smart co-workers
Pay is good
cons:
Zero job security

Will drop you so fast, regardless of well you perform

summary: Great place to learn, not so much to stay for a whole career
advice: Better managers are needed, ones that can lead with purpose rather than following the process "just because". For entry level jobs it's fine to do things a certain rigid way while they learn, but for ssr to sr jobs it is insulting.
pros:
Complex organization with many modern standards to learn from. Global reach, lots of professionals to work with which opens many opportunities to grow as an individual.

If you pay attention, you will learn a lot!
cons:
Does the right thing for the wrong reasons. More than once you will find that the metric is more valued than the "what", meaning as long we are on green we are fine, doesn't matter if what you have to do is completely absurd or repetitive.

Latam's IT team is going totally astray with their Agile approach, because again what matters seems to be how it looks like rather than what it is. Be careful if you wish to work here and learn "good practices" because they are totally second priority to them.

advice:
Be clear with goals, be clear on how to achieve high ratings/promotions, allow personnel to achieve those goals, and hold yourself accountable to being objective and professional.

Citi managers promote and give the best rating to their friends. Even the best managers are guilty of this.
pros: Good work/life balance, vacation time, benefits in general. Certainly could be better, but could also be a lot worse.
cons:
Do more with less. Then, do more with less. Then, do more with less. All that really happens is less gets done and less quality gets produced. The culture of Citi management is to be vague with goals and professional expectations, so that mid-year or at end of year the managers can arbitrarily decide if you did a good job or not.

I was also a manager for a short time. One of my direct reports did a phenomenal job for their level, but my manager told me that person could not get the rating I believed they deserved. Reason: their rating was too low the year before and it wouldn't look right.

advice: Start valuing your long tenured employees.   Too much lip service is paid to the worn out phrase "our people are our most valued resource" but the way they're treated says otherwise.
pros: Work from home 4 days a week, sometimes more.   Too bad it's only certain groups.   Always looking at ways to enhance processes and deploy new tech.   22 vacation days.
cons:
Unless you work for one of the businesses don't expect to receive regular bonuses and raises.   For the past few years my IRS refund, 4k or so, has exceeded my raise and bonus combined!

Lots of former coworkers lost their jobs due to cost cutting measures.   Jobs were moved to Budapest or Texas.  People were told they could move to new location at their own expense and take a nice pay cut in the process. 

Employee share of benefits cost continues to rise. 

No pension plan.  Company 401k match capped at 6% but you don't get the match until March of the following year.

summary: Great benefits, but little opportunity for women or POC in management positions
advice: Take a hard look at your diversity in the management ranks.  Don't just window dress, take hard actions to hire women and POC in the management ranks.  Look to the NFL...Rooney Rule!
pros: Great benefits, 401k, health, dental, vision etc.  Four weeks of vacation if you are an officer and comp days for any weekend work.  Really great nice people, very little cattiness or cut-throat attitude in the finance area.
cons: Very hard to move up in the ranks if you are a woman.  They have a lot of women working , there, but the management ranks have very few women.  For example, when I left, in my reporting line, there were only 3 women out of 45 persons, and the women were only in the lower ranks.  Also, they do not promote from within and allow tons of external hires for management positions.  Finance is continually being outsourced to lower cost areas so NYC jobs will be scarce in a few years.

advice: Have the DS work in a sandbox. Don't limit them, it goes against innovative thinking
pros:
Good pay
No pressure for the most time
cons:
To be a developer in Citi is not the best experience to say the least. You have the proxy of hell, you can't download anything, every software require premission from the pope. Going to be production? Good luck now you need to approve your stuff to be uploaded somewhere . For the most part developer can cope, because if you write in Java you probably have what ever you need.
 BUT if you are a data scientist and wish to have some experiments, good luck...
After 5 years there I became a pro, but for a first timer you need to change state of mind.

To bring an innovative software that requires a budget? No can do...
Even to get money for mechanical turk it was nightmare when in the end I got 150$ (yes, there is no typo) and I payed from my own credit and got the money back after almost a year.

summary: The left hand doesn't speak to right hand.
advice:
Quality over quanity please! 
Don't lose sight of the long-term for short-term sales goals.
pros: As a Financial Advisor at CPWM, you truly can help individuals achieve their financial dreams. You impact your clients lives in a big way through providing sound investment advice. Your schedule is flexible. You are the master of your domain. You have the ability to run your own practice according to how you see fit. The bank staff, your business partners serve as the primary source for new client referrals. This stream of incoming referrals is a huge advantage for a new FA to establish or grow a new book of business.
cons: Citigroup is a former Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) company- meaning the company was bailed out during the financial crisis of 2008. Therefore Citi & all of its subsidaries (particularly the investment division, CPWM) is a hollow company with aninefficient infrastructure. The intranet platforms are clunky. The business is not sreamlined & burdened with out of date technology & poor business practices. It takes way too long to do get anything done. No reliable back office support and no company morale.  Middle management is unreliable because they are spread too thin and over worked.

advice: More Director - agent communication. It seems like most issues that employees have with management is getting lost at the OM level.
pros: Extremely flexible with hours and they provide SO MUCH vacation and sick time for a position with such little experience required. The benefits are truly amazing.  There is a lot of opportunities for growth in the company, specifically the Florence KY site, but you do have to put the work in to get your name out there. Networking is probably your biggest hurdle when it comes to getting promoted- not just your performance.
cons: It's a very typical corporate structure, so there are a lot of managers and red-tape. It can be frustrating to get anything changed to make your job better. Typically, each layer of management has an open door policy, though. So if something isn't getting done that needs to be, you aren't punished for just going up to the next level to escalate the issue. You just need to use a lot of discretion when doing so.

summary: CET Pune : Great techie work but lots of politics too
advice: Keep eyes/ears open and talk to leaf nodes to understand how your management team is performing. Technical decision should better be left with techies and not MDs. Managers are super powered without check and balances, may be formalize 180/360 feedback.
pros:
Cutting edge work
Great ownership/responsibility
Some of the best minds to work with in NJ/NY
Above average salary 
Mobility options
cons:
Too much politics, sometimes higher management is confused what not-to-drive e.g. they can't drive day to day technical affairs and decisions. It better left to techies.
Politics, highly unstable management hierarchy, 
Hasty decisions specially for Pune office by people sitting in NJ e.g. creating local managers without empowering them enough to take decision.
Manager has too much power
Mobility is tough for senior people and above if you don't have the best relation with your current manager.
Salary / Bonus are not too great.
Overall if you are tough material and not bothered too much by management noise it's good place to own and execute some great projects.

advice: Get involved!
pros:
Benefits are great
Benefits start at day 1
cons: Mind numbing job.  Most management has no direction and no lead over their own staff/team.  You rarely see anyone that you directly report to.  Once you're out of training you are pretty much on your own and the only communication you receive is what you're doing wrong.  Not that that is a horrible thing, because you do need to know what you need to correct but it's just not worth the mind numbing job of sitting on a phone for over 7 hours each day talking to people that love to spit venom at you and tell you that they make more money than you do.  Older credit card customers literally HATE Citibank so you'll get used to that speech.  You'll seriously hear the hold music in your nightmares when you sleep.  Training is great but there are a lot of times that you will get misinformed about serious information.  There are also times that you'll annoy trainers by asking questions.

advice: Managers should be trained to manage people.  Stop sticking people in management roles just to check off a box, and start creating real pathways for new and different perspectives.
pros: The work can be interesting.
cons:
Terrible Management, poor leadership, favoritism, nepotism, lack of diversity. 
Citi talks a good game, but doesn't walk the walk. The culture is stiff, impersonal and cold and conniving. Teams are small, so you're always stretched so thin. They lure you in with a decent salary, but you soon realize you literally sold your entire life to them and it isn't worth it. No work life balance. It wouldn't be so bad if managers actually did a better job of managing and leading. You can provide results without antiquated fear-based managing styles, and instead inspire your team to work hard and be their best because it feels good to win. Nobody wants to work hard for bullies or managers that don't lead.
I have worked at other banks that are lightyears ahead of Citi in technology. business practices and colleague engagement. It's a shame to work in a place that claims to be so innovative and progressive, and you pull back the curtains and it's an old dinosaur in disguise. Be better, Citi.

summary: Great experience, little incentive to stay
advice: You need to start investing more in your people and be transparent with your intentions.
pros: Work is challenging and there are plenty of opportunities to grow and build experience, Especially in ICG. People are generally good to work with and the company has an excellent work-life balance.
cons:
Citi Is constantly in financial crisis, especially in operations and technology. Citi has an unfortunate culture to pay to lure good talent but once a person has joined the firm offer little to no raises or bonuses. Even with a good rating one can expect to be flat every year unless you make a big stink about it, which in that case they will offer a raise but for undisclosed amount at a undisclosed time. 

Citi is also highly political. Reviews don't really matter. Senior leadership only care about what you did for them to get a good review not the performance of the individual. 

Opportunities for advancement are political as well. Most moves will not result in better pay, promotions have been made much more rigorous but generally are bypassed by people who simple show management a competing job offer.

advice: Branch staff very rarely gets the chance to move to corporate side of business . Lots of opportunities available for senior leaders to develop their careers but not to branch staff. There should be more programs assist those would like to remain with the company and develop as a professional. Scope of career path basically Teller to  Personal Banker, to Small Business Banker to CG Relationship Manager or Assistant Branch Manager to Branch Manager, then Area Director. No clear path to other roles.
pros: Company with global brand recognition. Strict compliance requirements that enable you to know they take ethical selling very seriously. If surpass goals there is good room for commission.
cons: Customer service surveys taken very seriously. Bad surveys will affect monthly commission pay outs as well as branch quarterly. External candidates will be paid more than internal most of the time.  Entered company right out of graduating with a Bachelors degree with hopes of developing career with company. Unfortunately if corporate route is what you are seeking don't start out as a branch employee. Very rarely do branch employees transition to corporate roles or other areas outside branch.

advice: If you're going to hire employees you need to train them. If you can't train them, then you probably shouldn't be in management.
pros: The pay was substantially higher than what someone my age and education level would receive at the time.
cons: There was no training. There was no guidance. There was nothing. For the first 30 days I didn't have a desk or a computer. I came in every day and flipped around from one desk to another. Finally, when I did get a desk and computer of my own, I did not have access to anything I needed to do my job. Gaining access was a long grueling process and it always seemed like I never had enough. I would gain access to one system but then would need another to use the first system. I would be granted access to the subsequent system (so that I could use the first system) only to be told I needed additional permissions to retrieve information from another database so that I could use the second system. I spent one whole year running in circles getting nothing done or learning anything. There was zero productivity in our business unit. I am hard-pressed to even describe what my job was... I don't think I will ever know what it was I was hired to do.

pros: Challenging work, Highly technical job
cons: Bureaucratic organization, no work life balance

advice: Promotion should come internally. Aggressive people look good in the meetings but they do more harm than good for the company in the long run. Treat employees with respect.
pros: Work life balance was better than others, although my manager tried to give me hard time using it. Remote access is quite good. "Citibank" name looks good when seen from outsiders. Convenient mass transit (subways) and minutes from NYC.
cons: Managers (SVPs) are mostly clueless yet very aggressive and overly ambitious. They think of their direct reports as second class citizens. No corporation between departments. No information sharing between groups. Managers are mostly enemies each other and sometimes yell at each other in the meetings. People with louder voices and thick faces usually get promotion, so it's a war zone here. It's common practice to steal others' work and senior managers do not care as long as their people look like working hard. Everybody thinks everyone else is idiots. Very stressful work environment. Good work leads to lot more work and no vacation. While on vacation abroad, my manager kept calling me for trivial issues multiple times. If candidates seem smart and ambitious, they usually don't get hired. Managers are mostly not intelligent so some smart people do get hired but they usually leave in a year. Worst place ever to work.

advice:
Insufficiency of effective and specific training for employees to perform their daily vital tasks.
Promotion criteria are not really set up to internal stakeholders
Internal career opportunities are not properly, formally and transparently communicated to internal stakeholders. 
Reward systems are not clearly and effectively communicated to internal stakeholders.

Citi has traning organised for internal employees but they are mostly on-screen and not classroom. Management should try to come out with personal coaching programmes to grow talents or classroom training to improve effectiveness of training. 

Management should closely grow talents and reward them sufficiently to retain them. Citi is very globalized  but  it does not seem to appear that it has rigorously leveraged on its global resources to groom talents from within.
pros:
Global presence with great synergies
Brand reputation
Being a reputable technology bank
Good in innovations 
Employees engagement in place
Having belief in internal mobility 
Plenty of career opportunities worldwide
Fast-paced culture 
Remuneration set based on market standard 
Promotion of work-life balance
Having exposure to dealing with other internal stakeholders within Citi
Prompt and great customer service 
Client-focused
cons: There might be things that are very automated, hence you may not have good insights about them.

summary: Good experience but some things are very slow, too much politics and people are not always rewarded for their effort
advice: Stop playing power games, focus and getting things done, reward the people who deserve it and understand when it makes sense to take some risk.
pros: You can get some good experience working for this big, global company depending on the business/group your work with. There are some very smart people so you can learn a lot if you care. You need to be open and flexible, you can move around within the company looking for your right place to be.
cons: Too much politics, too much red tape, certain things are very, very slow. Career advancement is limited if you do not have good connections with the right people, being excellent at what you do is not enough, you have to play the politics game all the time. There is too much politics, too many managers, PMOs, management reporting, boring meetings. It all takes too much time and this time is wasted. Sometimes they play it too safe here. And still I often do not see good people being rewarded as they should.

advice:
Please take a look at the incredible employees, especially your office managers.  I am particularly
referring to those who are no longer with Citi.  I would be happy to grab a flight to New York to tell my story.  Or, at the very least, read this message. I lost my heart and my life when I left my job.
I am wearing my 25 years- of- service watch.  When I left, my supervisor whispered on my ear "Sue
us.  PLEASE sue us!'. I cannot sue you.  I loved you all so much.
pros:
Freedom to provide client service as needs arose in  difficult situations.  I was always supported on a customer level. 
Total compensation was excellent.
Exceptional financial center location and environment.
cons:
Long hours as a financial center manager.
Large disconnect between what is expected in the role of a Financial Center Manager in managing
branch staff vs. what actually takes place. 
Although always polite on the surface, there is constantly an underlying fear of making the slightest error. 
   There is no relief from the fear.  
As a manager, one can feel extremely alone.

advice: Need to bring down workforce urgently to break status qua and improve sense of responsibility amongst employees. Many consider it similar to life-time guaranteed Govt. jobs and openly speaks about it.  Reduce management level employees %.  Improve performance evaluation and compensation process to motivate every employees to perform and EARN their values in the organization. Need to take harsh decision by reviewing people's last 18-30 months deliverable and ask people who could not deliver in this period to move out (low productivity might not be individual's failure but company has no time & money to investigate and correct all areas). Getting rid of old woods and bringing new talent force is critical for company to move forward from here.
pros: Very large and complex organization with vast areas of work oppertunities; Excellent organization to learn & get hands-on experience in different areas of banking business; Open atmosphere - employees can work freely and express opinions.
cons: Too large to manage efficiently; Less than 20% of work force delivers more than 80% of  deliverable; Too big to manage quality performance management and correct normalization of compensations;  High bureaucratic process.

advice: HR really needs to look after the attrition rate, why people are leaving the their jobs and joining other banks.
pros:
1. one gets to learn new things which may help him/her in the future
2. re-location opportunities: if u want to re-locate due to some personal reasons, Citi considers that
3.Job movement (internal Transfer): after 2 years at one position u can freely move to any other (considering your eligibility).
4. Teams: we have an amazing fun loving team in Hyderabad, who loves to giggle and laugh all day which tends to minimize the day to day pressure
5. If erroneously you have made any mistake and if the bank needs to bear the charges, don't work they won't cut your pockets
cons:
1. Slow Growth: you may stuck in the same profile for min. 2 years. Don't think of promotion before that no matter how much you've done the work.
2. Timing issues: there is no work life balance. there were times that girls use to go home by 11 in the night
3. pathetic appraisals: don't think of high appraisals. you cannot expect more than 10 % even if you have 1 rating.

advice: Unify corporate culture and reduce barriers to make things happen. I understand that it is the status quo of the industry, but look at the high tech companies that foster a different environment.
pros: they pay well and depending on the region they are a very well recognized brand to add to you resume. Most people are friendly and helpful specially the middle management. The offices are really nice and the perks are decent comparable with other financial institutions. I would highly recommend this organizaton to start a career in the financial services.
cons: At higher levels of management people tend to be more selective with the people they talk to, and in most of the cases they are very hierarchical. This creates an environment where you feel that sometimes projects are not getting done because of bureaucratic issues. However, I must say that this is pretty common for larger institutions. But specially challenging for large financial institutions like Citi. Also, another downside is the fact from division to division the environment is drastically different. I don’t feel there is a unified sense of corporate culture within the organization. The result is that there are very different people across divisions with little commonalities on corporate culture level, making it challenging to deal with those people on a daily basis.

advice: Look at the bonus structure please and come up with a plan to distruibute it to lower management and ranks that get the work done.  When the big wigs get thousands of dollars of bonus and the people who work hard to earn the results get nothing, it dfoes not speak well  of the respect that senior management has for its employees and also gives the idea that cost cutting applies only to the lower ranks while it does not to the upper ranks. Please look at a plan to allocate resources to get the job done, otherwise you will have to get satisfied with satisfactory results and not excellent results. Also, trust your managers with what they do - micromanagement wastes everyones time and is often counterproductive when unwarranted.
pros: Employees have good benefits from the benefits provider
cons: Excessive work with little support - goes against work life balance, bonusses applicable only if you are in middle-senior management, poor recognition of efforts - hinders new idea generation, meagre/no pay increase despite your hard work (maybe due to the tough economic times, but these times have no effect on the salary increase of senior management), poor HR practices - little effort spent on providing timely and constructive feedback to internal hires who apply for internal job postings.

advice: Performance review process needs to be revamped so that employees are judged soley on their contribution and performance instead of being compared to others within the organization. Remove the bell curve so that employees are rated fairly as well as compensated fairly. Don't claim to be a meritocracy when you fix the performance review rating system. Remove the layers so that employees have the opportunity to get promoted instead of having employees who have been in there officer titles for serveral years without being promoted, while people coming in off the street are coming in at higher officer titles.

summary: World Leading Company, great place to work, but.....
advice: Employees are not liabilities!  We are assets, especially in a service based company like this.  If you did a true survey and asked employees how safe they feel in their position, I can say with certainty that a very large percent of employees do NOT feel safe.  I’m in a position to talk to several different employees in several different businesses and the feeling is the same across the board.  From help-desk all they way to SVPs, nobody at Citi feels safe.
pros: Good strong company, known worldwide for its leadership in the financial industry.   Great technical opportunities, as long as you are willing to work extremely hard.  Citi is on it’s way to being a global leader with all aspects of IT and I am proud to be a part of that.
cons: IF you are not working harder than everyone else, your job is in jeopardy!  Citi is always cutting costs and laying people off, while executives are getting huge bonuses and salaries!  Every single year, they are cutting benefits for the worse, to save more money.

summary: Citi is a wonderful brand that is being completely mismanaged
advice: Senior execs need to walk the talk and enforce their strategies through words AND actions.  They need to reinforce their strategies constantly or no one will take them seriously.  That's partly why they have had such a hard time recovering from the banking debacle.
pros: If you are interested in global companies, Citi is very global and there are many jobs where you will have the opportunity to interact with colleagues overseas.  And the people are by and large quite smart.
cons: Senior management (as of 2009, at any rate) were a bunch of chickens.  When there were headcount reductions, it was never the most senior executives, it was always a few levels below.  That way they didn't have to face the pain of firing someone they know, they just made their underlings do it.  And they didn't have much rhyme or reason to the cut backs.  They would also fund departments without requiring other groups to work with them. If the other groups decided not to, then the newly funded group was out in the cold - but management didn't care if their investment was wasted.  Again, they lacked the courage, foresight and vision to be forceful about driving change.  No wonder Citi is mired in craziness!

cons: As with many companies this large, you can get lost in the shuffle if you don't fight for what you've earned. advice:

pros: Great branch staff who go above and beyond to meet and exceed customer experience.
cons:
Career Opportunity: Limited ability of branch staff, area directors to aid in professional career within company. pros: Paid Holidays, great staff and coworkers, good benefits.  Competitive salary

summary: Good advancement potential, poor compensation policies
advice: Review human resources policies, offer employees more competitive health care premiums, and apply salary grades across the board so that people can actually be rewarded when they have performed well enough to be promoted.
pros: There is unlimited advancement potential in a company this large. With offices all over the world, once you have gained a little experience within the company, you can apply to transfer pretty much anywhere you might want to live. Citigroup also pays a portion of education expenses and promotes internal education courses.
cons: Compensation and benefits are low compared with smaller companies I have worked for. Human resources is very unhelpful, and promotions often come with little or no pay increase. A good portion of pay for exempt employees is variable (bonus based), so if the company has had a bad year, you may end up making less than the prior year in any given year. summary: I mean, only if you’re desperate for a job
advice: Treat everyone as equal, especially if they’re producing perfect handletime, surveys and compliance. My manager alone had her favorites and everyone else she could care less about.

cons: While working there, I was never able to have a good manager. Contacted HR, tried changing shifts, etc. If you have a good manager, the job is bearable at most. There are a couple of excellent managers who anyone could rely on. It’s just a shame you’re forced to contact someone other than your own. Constantly changing systems, so pay checks were never accurate. Worked there 2 years and received raises. Lost them when they put everyone at a solid $15 per hour. Even at $15 an hour, it was sometimes difficult to stay positive when constantly being emotionally abused by customers. I couldn’t count how many times I walked into the bathroom to someone crying. If you can handle mostly awful management and mean customers, it’s the job for you. Oh! Also, they’re super strict about stats. I know someone who was fired for their handletime when all their other stats were perfect. You learn fast if you’re not their favorite.

summary: I love being an employee, but it's a popularity contest to get promoted.
advice: Get your reps more involved with the business decisions and make the job more fun for reps! Also, make shift bids much more frequent, especially for those who are in school or have children!
pros:
Pay. 
Commission is good as long as you stay compliant. 
Direct management is very understanding of situations and issues at work.
Positive impact on the community. 
Happy attitudes throughout bank.
cons:
You have to be "loved" by upper management in order to be chosen for promotions or new advancement opportunities. 
Seen many people with high skill sets who were disregarded completely because they were not extroverted. 
High turnover rate due to rigorously strict schedule and adherence to phones. Offline is often cancelled, resulting in weeks on end of non-stop call taking. Many reps get burned out quickly.

No schedule flexibility.

cons: Inconsistencies in culture and team direction. Applications run on old servers with heavy downtime and most of the time is spent looking into these issues working with dedicated non-prod ENV support team as dev team doesn't have access to these servers. Terrible work life balance as most time is spent looking at environment issues, attending calls and finally actual development. Benefits are a lot less when compared to other companies.

Folks in Europe and Asia will have to stay up late on Saturday and early Sunday morning to support this activity and get back to work the next day. advice: Listen to staffs suggestions they are the ones performing the duties.  Provide adaquate resources such as technology, office supplies, training on new applications. Insurance benefits change every year and are getting more difficult to understand.  Starts programs but does not follow through for very long.  Upper management is constantly changing and middle management continues to increase while the working staff is being eliminated causing additional stress on the staff. pros: Flex place, flex time - I've been working remote now 2 years and management allows me to revise my work hours so I am able to get my kids to their after school activities.  Ability to advance.

summary: Low pay with no room for career growth
advice:
Hire real managers and get rid of the replacements. Real management know how to talk to and relate to people in a meaningful way. In my experience, there was none of that here.

There also needs to be a real structure to the work environment instead of just entry level and then management with barely any raises. There were only 2 raises given in the past 6 years. The culture endorses lateral movement which means there is no room for growth here.

This company does not value knowledge and is constantly letting it walk out the door and does not hire someone immediately to take their place. Instead management waits to see if the team can handle the loss. This contributes to the dump culture.

If you do not negotiate a high salary when you come in, don't expect to get much further away from that salary after years of working here. also expect to take on a couple more positions responsibilities.

cons: Management doesn't help mostly because they are over worked themselves. Low pay with no room for growth in your career. General management is disorganized and tend to dump work on you even when you have too much without any consideration.

advice: Management and Culture need an overhaul in many departments. My advice is to teach more about emotional intelligence and maturity and do not lead with fear based tactics. A full training program should be installed for complex transactional departments. Management should not pin people against each other and play favorites thinking that this will create friendly competition.  This approach only causes a selfish unproductive  mentality that only leads to more stress and anger amongst team members. Sink or swim mentality is really bad approach and will only lead to failure for all. Focus on team building and giving back to your employees as you will see that they will do even more for a kind word of encouragement which costs nothing. Give professional constructive feedback rather then biased feed back because you want the person to quit or because you do not like them when you burnt them out in the first place! At least give your employees the illusion that you care and that you actually want to encourage them to do better for the company putting your personal feelings aside. Update systems and give your employees the proper tools to succeed and do the job correctly.
