Encountered myopic managers who are highly "political" and form cliques and  are known to deprive employees in their progress towards their career ambition with lame excuses (such as inability to hire replacement or harbor personal agendas).

summary: Associate with the Corporate & Investment  Bank based primarily in New York City at 388 Greenwich
advice: More transparency to junior leaders from senior management.  Better incentivize  management in developing junior leaders.  Incorporate the principal perspective in dealing with clients.
pros: When I started in 1998 the pay was very competitive for investment banking associates.  The caliber of professionals working around you are top shelf. Substantial resources at your disposal to perform your job.  Highest caliber clients.  Truly global universal bank provides geographic flexibility.     Substantial institutional knowledge.   Outstanding training program for those joining at the entry level.  Extremely interesting work.
cons: During my tenure managers were not good at managing subordinates.  Extremely long hours.  Working as a banker with Citi as an I banker was a life style decision.  Break down of compensation causes employees to assume substantial risk for the year.  Its up or out and very competitive.  Can be a political mine field to stay at firm.

summary: A good job, but not without flaws.
advice: Visit the lower and mid level agents/managers more often, Continue to unify teams and business units rather than keeping them in competition, Streamline processes and show you want to help, rather than send piles of paperwork saying Citi wants to help.
pros: Good 401k,  Dental, and Vision plans, decent incentive structures, professional atmosphere. Volunteer work and community giving is encouraged by business. Paid volunteer day.  CEO seems intelligent and driven. Will train even with no mortgage experience. Pays well for the area. Quarterly town halls and other VOE events.
cons: Health insurance benefit is very expensive for such a high deductible. Different centers and Business units handle process differently, lack of unity and direction. Unnecessary layoff/site closings makes job difficult for those left. Very little room for advancement, unless you 'know somebody'. Not a teamwork driven atmosphere, feels more like a competition between other teams and agents. upper management very rarely visits, causing an overall feel of being disconnected. Not very innovative and very bureaucratic in helping customers.

summary: Don't work in TTS (Treasury and Trade Solutions)
advice: Pay your people more and show them that they are valued. There's a reason we have such high attrition rates!!
pros: Decent work hours, people are reasonable and the job is not as life-sucking as others in the ICG (Markets, Banking). If you are really really good, you may be able to move internationally. If you work in a good product like Trade, you will learn a lot, otherwise prepare to be bored and get treated like a second class citizen (compared to the rest of ICG).
cons: Very low pay scale compared to other ICG businesses, especially when you compare our margins to those businesses. No space for personal development...the work is very boring...almost Admin work. The tech systems are a complete mess...you will spend a lot of time fixing things rather than building new systems/innovating.

advice: None.  They say the 'C' in 'Citi" stands for change and it's never a good thing.  I have no problem with change.  I've worked there for almost 12 years but I'm waiting for Hell to open up and swallow Citi.
pros: The Benefits are great.
cons: The pay is pathetic, they don't care to keep the employees they have because they know they can find someone to warm the set and they will pay them less.  You are not encouraged to be creative and when you are you will not get any credit, it goes to your manager and your manager will not acknowledge you.  The job description changes monthly if not daily.  You will never be kept in the loop of the recent change and you will be reprimanded for not doing it correctly.  You will never be respected or thought of in any positive manor and that goes for entry level all the way up to upper management.  Be prepared to always be wrong, finger pointing occurs often.  The list of Cons can go on and on.  I would not tell my friends of job openings unless they are desperate for work.

summary: Good, if you can handle politics
advice: Walk a day in an employees shoes. Literally sit with and shadow one employee a month, their job on phones is not easy, the compliance tactics you have to comb thru make things tougher, relying on other departments to accomplish items is burdening. If you put yourself in your employees shoes and did their job for one day you would respect the heck out of them. I did it and it made me a better more understanding and more productive manager all around. You can't understand what you don't know. Especially when you should be striving to work FOR your employees and not have them working for YOU
pros: Just the pay, the people were good to each other, teams functioned well and deals got closed on time so bonus was made every month
cons: Once you take away a bonus you Take away morale, competition and drive. They ripped bonus away from hard working team players and I'm sure they are loosing a lot of top producing employees to ever bank.

advice: Senior Management: Recognize who’s producing and watch managers in their natural habitat not just when you decide to come into the branch.
pros: You learn everything that can further your career in the long run. Whether it’s problem solving, cash handling, book keeping, sales, customer service. Everything is taught to you just through interactions with clients with different walks of life. 401k available, paid time off, insurance is pricy but it’s still offered.
cons: The training process does not prepare you at all! They sit you in front of a computer for a few weeks and then you’re at the window. There’s a lot of brown nosers there as well. Try not to form too close of bonds with people or talk ill of others trust me everyone knows everyone. Management has a tendency to delegate a lot rather than be hands on and not do things by the ‘books’. Often times you’ll meet managers that don’t know how to do operations and expect you to know everything so keep that in mind.

summary: Great place to retire and chill, big No for ambitious people
advice: Kindly don't hire from IITs and spoil the professional career of these kids. You pay them a higher salary and lock them out of getting any job outside. After a couple of years they eventually become un employable because they draw a high salary but absolutely don't have any professional or analytics experience here.
pros:
8 hour work day
Good enough pay for a campus hire from IIT
Easy work with least effort ie repetitive
Enough leaves and off time for employees
cons:
Quality of work is extremely bad, you will have to do MIS 90% of the time. Quality of analytics delivery is sub par and everything still runs on Excel and SAS
You will never have to use your brains
No opportunity of travel or mobility outside AIM. Other Citi businesses don't welcome data analysts from AIM being hired in their teams.
No tech is used other than SAS and Excel
Managers are not skilled enough both in leadership and in analytics
Promotions are extremely hard to get

summary: Very sales oriented and very corporate. That said, great job for a college student
pros:
-They really worked around my hours and have some pretty excellent perks like college tuition reimbursement.
-Lots of holidays are off (with pay)
-Decent money for a pretty straightforward job
-Quarterly commission bonuses depending on sales (2010-2011, not sure now)
cons:
-Very sales oriented with monthly sales charts (checking, savings, credit cards, mortgage referrals, etc.,.) I did not expect this when I was hired. My branch was fairly slow so I wasn't too pressured, however, I heard it was much more competitive at others
-When I worked there, the products weren't very competitive with other banks, so you had to do some sweet talking
-Knowledge that you're working for a bad bank

The only kind of people who really rise up in retail banking are somewhat delusional about the goodness they're bringing to the world. These were the senior managers, and thus, the kind of insufferable people you'll have to deal with. That said, the money was good, the customers were friendly, and the job was straightforward.

advice: Give up, leave the company. You are being taken over by the feds.
pros: The best reason to work for Citigroup was the ability to to work in different locations. The company is so huge you can work pretty much in any country if you have the desire to do so. Diversity related to this is also a plus in the company. The diversity is huge in the company. The benefits were also pretty good. The 401k match is decent as long as you don't invest in Citi and their insurance costs seemed about 20% cheaper than others that are relatively the same insurance plan. I appreciated them offering a good Health Savings Account plan. Their domestic partner benefits are also very liberal.
cons: Citi is a bureaucratic nightmare. It starts with a vague set of marching orders called the shared responsibilities. The Shared Responsibilities have to be read and signed by all employees, then they are never discussed after that. The potential in the company is enormous. Instead of unlocking all the potential in the company it is squandered protecting fiefdoms and covering up mistakes. Besides all the people who have almost wrecked the whole company and banking industry creating and having risky derivatives, the company is way too risk adverse. This makes the spirit of initiative and teamwork not exist at the company.

summary: You have to have a certain mentality to thrive there.
advice: I understand that sales are important to any for-profit company, but so is being realistic.
pros: Excellent company culture.  I truely felt that managment saw me as a person and not just a minion.  They offer opportunities to those without college degrees that most other companies would not.  They give you alot more freedom to move to different departments to find what fits you best.  If you plan to be in customer service centered work for most of your life this offers you invaluable experience as well as resume material.  Rewards are given for both individual and team performances, not for being boss' favorite.
cons: To be completely honest, dealing with the customers was the worst.  People tend to be more open to being nasty when you're just a faceless voice on the other line.  It's very fast paced problem solving and can be quite mentally exhausting.  Sales were a big part of my position and certain numbers had to be met.  Often times I felt the goals we had to reach were very unreasonable.  The more the economy slowed down the more they would raise our goals.  If you don't have thick skin and your morale is easily defeated, you won't get far.

summary: Starting there, I didn't know I'd be jumping out of the frying pan, skipping the fire, and headed for the inferno.
advice: Revisit the Values, Principles, Objectives, and Elements.  Quit spending time on thinking of the new catch phrase mottos that will motivate and produce.  Reinforce the wisdom of what you already have.  Allow honesty from employees to show you some of their reality.  Finally, lessen the micro-management.  Does the amount of time spent detailing productivity ... same information in multiple ways and programs that don't "speak" to each other ... how effective are these reports?  Allow employees to focus on their jobs you hired them to do.
pros: Pay has an edge in being competitive.  Other benefits opportunities are top notch.  Promotes volunteering and community service.  On TANK bus route.  Quick access to freeway.  Plenty of fast food places nearby ... but Citi's cafeteria is THE BEST I've ever seen.
cons: Training will either make or break you. For this new department to the Kentucky facility, training was sorely inadequate and incomplete. While instructors were very nice, many were new to Teaching.  However they occasionally gave conflicting info on procedures. Middle management members made so many big process decisions that flip flopped often.  Communication and implementation was not consistent, But Was IMPROVING.  My experience there is that for a global company that's over 200 years old, I'm very disappointed in the lack of effective training and follow through from there.

pros: never join Citi bad company don't think about full time
cons: evert thing is bad here nothing is good

pros: work-life balance is good, no long hrs
cons: repetitive tasks, flat learning curves

pros: Good brand name to work

pros: Good Insurance, but that's about it
cons: Low pay, poor work culture

advice: Clean house, update your lending software to the 21st century and shut down managers who push the mortgage consultants to upload loans that are not going to be approved and closed.  Throwing wood in the works simply falsely inflates numbers and generates false expectations.  Also it gums up the works and prevents the necessary attention and time need by underwriters to work on and close real loans.
pros: Nice Bank offices, good benefits,semi flexible schedule
cons: The single most disorganized, dysfunctional, poorly managed, archaic software.  They pay no real salary yet expect to mandate that the mortgage consultant man a desk 6 hours a day waiting for a mortgage to come in.  The u/w software approves the loans based on fannie guidelines and Citi manually kicks them out in Underwriting.  The state they have lending programs that they don't have.  The upper management blatantly lie to the mortgage consultant, the bankers, and the borrowers. In 10 years in the mortgage industry Citi mortgage is the single most incomptent lender I have ever encountered.

summary: I wouldn't recommend personally - there's better out there
advice: Get rid of that Activtrak desktop tracking software. People don't like being tracked, even if it's not at an individual level. People searching reddit or stackoverflow for a solution is productive and you shouldn't classify it as unproductive. Allow fully remote after the pandemic. Cut out many recurring meetings or let people bail out once their time is finished.
pros: They were 100% remote during the pandemic. Some smart and nice people (but not all).
cons: During the pandemic they installed tracking software that tracks what you do (they said it couldn't be zoomed into a specific employee but also told us people managers not to let our teams know). They won't be fully remote after the pandemic (in fact they renovated the offices during the pandemic). Pretty boring work and people. Too many really long recurring meetings means you have to work extra hours to keep afloat. Need to be able to move outside of your country to possibly get ahead. Variable comp could be way better.

summary: Top Tier Banking business environment with talented motivated employees
advice: Not all of your clients are comfortable with the digital age.  Co. loyalty to long term employees is out the window in favor of business results.  This will have repercussion in the long run.
pros: Cutting Edge Technology, i.e. ATM, Credit Card, 24 hour Client Access by Citiphone, Paperless technology in branch environment, has embraced the digital an will lead the charge to easy access by it's clients, no matter where in the world they may be seeking access from.  This is an aggressive sales environment where top performers are recognized and rewarded.  For clients that  have business contacts, family in India, this is absolutely THE PLACE TO BANK!  This company pays attention to the social network discussions and has plans on moving up in it's JD Power rankings.
cons: The environment is evolving and this has been good for the shareholders, and not so good for some of the employee benefits, staffing levels and some of the fringes that were previously available.

advice: 1) Fix the software systems. 2) Bring back incentive pay. 3) Don't have meetings just to hear yourself talk.
pros: For a call center environment there is a little more freedom than most. Lateral moves are common. Benefits and vacation offerings are excellent. Even layoffs give you considerable post employee pay. Good food at the cafe.
cons: Manager hired from BOA several years ago to lower expenses. Therefore layoffs are constant. Those in my position and others that have managed to keep their position have had their pay go down significantly as the incentive pay was eliminated. Many positions moving to India and Philippines. This causes the moral to be very low. The software programs and systems are atrocious. Sitting and watching blow-ups, site not found or simply watching your cursor/mouse spin is a constant part of your day. Promotions are non-existent. Positions are often posted, then the position is suddenly eliminated. Like other companies you take computer ethics training, but are then verbally encouraged to take the shortest route even if the ethics are questionable.

advice: Need to come down to earth and stop the BBQs in Mexico....  Mid-Levels are the ones carrying and keeping the boat afloat.... For Mexico, the premise of "think global, act local" has to mean something... You cannot have foreigners covering clients in a country with a high nationalistic component... No business sense.... Mobility is being used to (i) get promoted and (ii) have a good time in a new country....
pros: Learning a lot because Senior Management does not lead by example and just know how to give orders
cons: Everything is politics.  Career advancement depends on who you know and how can that person vouch for you.  All the initiatives (Voice of the Employee, Voice of the Client, Multi-Perspective Feedback, KYC count) are designed to justify Senior Management in giving you (i) a poor bonus, (ii) no promotions (despite the "promote when ready" copycat from JPM), and (iii) tell you that work needs to be done....  So, if people rate management poorly on the Voice of the Employee, they are basically shooting themselves in the foot...  Survey has to be perfect....  A survey!!  Your voice!!  Otherwise, it is used as an excuse to punish the whole team....  Go figure....

summary: Good Leadership Team, Challenging environment in terms of Size of Company
advice: Continue to focus on Lean approaches. Scale at Citi brings so many challenges at the decision table that even seasoned managers are stumped. Don't lose sight of the eventual goal to keep the firm competitive, profitable and responsible , amidst a challenging regulatory environment. Just keep ploughing through. Always distinguish between - "do we own the process" OR "does the process owns us". Hopefully the former and not the latter
pros: Overall the senior leadership team cares about keeping the firm competitive and cares about the employees and their respective careers. For folks who are good with proactively reaching out and outspoken (Type A personalities) , firm is a great place to learn and expand career.
cons: Challenge is that Citi is so big that the message dilutes and changes by the time it gets down to the organization (game of telephone). Turf wars, personal egos and personal agendas always trump doing the right thing. The sheer size makes it hard for anyone to execute a strategy

summary: I worked for the Las Vegas, NV. office in their mortgage department.
advice: Be more pro-active in streamlining the processes and getting out on the floor to see what is really going on.  Be part of the solution to get the assembly line working, review the work being done and give promotions to the people who will actually do the job and help the team on the floor to do theirs.
pros: The ability to work overtime to meet quotas for bonuses.  The benefits were great, as was the opportunity to transfer to another site.
cons: Promotions were based on sucking up to your manager, not on merit.  Lots of nepotism.  Too many layers of management, where the knowledge and work ethic diminished the further down the management chain the position was.  Extremely political, which often happens in such a large environment (about 1000 employees at this site). This was the third time the company opened this site and closed it down again.  They just can't seem to get it right.

summary: constant changes in policies and procedures
advice: Treat your employees with respect, when your increasing job duties make sure you compensate your employees for the increase in job duties.
pros:
Training, great for a first job,
Just above average pay. Great connections. Sawgrass system easy to learn. Great for an complacent person that doesn't seek advancement
cons:
Management constantly changing, PTO available does not mean you should take it or it could negatively effect your scorecard and regardless of the circumstances if your not meeting metrics (even if because of death in family or Short term disability) your reprimanded for not meeting goal. Micro manage environment. C in Citi stands for change this is true and also Confusion there is no solid structure. Management does not receive the necessary training. Do not care for employees or the time they've worked for
The company to advance. Skill does not matter it's all about who you know. Job duties increase and pay remains the same
Which makes the job not worth the hassle. They say assume positive intent with customers but they don't with the employees.

advice: When I was there, it seemed a consistent management strategy was to create co-heads to avoid losing someone if they didn't get promoted; then usually they would either not get along or one would get fired.  Bizarre strategy.  Don't make people co-heads unless the job is really big enough for two.  Also, don't just follow Goldman or JP's strategies.  Come up with new business strategies on your own and get there before they do.
pros:
Huge international reach
Great for career networking
Still a great name on your resume despite being laid low in the financial crisis
On-site medical clinic (at least at 388 Greenwich)
cons:
Size/breadth can be a liability - steady drip of scandals requiring huge settlements/fines, always created some excuse why we couldn't get good bonuses even though the scandals had nothing to do with my business area
Some people pull for the team at Citi, others are only out for themselves
Politics can be tricky, you need to find multiple strong senior backers or you're at risk

advice: Develop a clear, simple, solid and unchanging mission from the top that informs culture. You think you have that with the current mission, but it's in constant conflict with other internal changing missions (changes with the wind depending on which executive in place). And it's not enforced, so what's the point! (not to mention, it's not all that clear). Change radically or die!
pros: Excellent pay as a contractor (but horrible pay as a FTE).
cons: Huge, massive company that doesn't care about its employees. If an employee has a positive experience, it's only a result of having a great manager -- but beware, reorganizations happen about every 3 months. There's a lot of cross-hiring as well as attrition, so your team could look radically different from year to year, and even month to month. There are also a lot of processes that are done "just because we've always done it this way" - so be prepared for ridiculous, anti-business wastefulness. Last but not least, nasty politics and backstabbing - and an Ethics team that is busy, but lacks fangs depending upon which executive is involved in whatever ethics violation (e.g., sexual harassment).  Lots and lots of busy work and re-dos, just so much waste.

summary: Top heavy salaries and an HR team that is oblivious to employee issues
advice: Try to promote from within the ranks instead of hiring outsiders as the bosses. This will hopefully result in the top management's approach being based on ground realities. Overhaul of support functions like the HR, Compliance and Risk teams urgently required. These teams need to be in sync with business objectives. Please encourage right sales behaviour instead of chasing impossible targets.
pros: A far better work culture than what is found at Indian banks. You can progress rapidly if you can manage your supervisors well. The bank is trying to address gender related issues in the workplace positively.
cons: Shameless self promotion is the only yardstick of success. Pay is better than Indian banks but far below other MNC's. Promotion is slow for work horses. Clear hierarchy in the ICG, GCG and O&T businesses. Few opportunities for leadership programs. Crazy cost cutting has resulted in zero perks.  HR, Compliance and Risk functions fiddle around with rules that only apply in Utopian scenarios.

summary: A great start to your financial services career
advice: You set the tone with how you act and what you say. Culture starts with you, so you being negative, pessimistic, and generally miserable while at work doesn't inspire your subordinates. It actually causes low morale and high turnover. Look in the mirror and act more professionally.
pros:

summary: Worst employer I have ever worked with ( Citi Toronot Service Centre, in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada)

 then came to the office before 9:00AM next day, but the manager just didn't care, and still kept blaming you here and there

7. too much more.....

summary: Excellent place to get you ready to work anywhere and for any company
pros:
Amazing team and management. Excellent support in all areas for a bank - if you have any personal things going on or training wise. Health insurance and pension. They rarely ask for overtime. No cameras on zoom. 
Sort of con - never worked more in my life and more in depth, but they say once you worked in Citi for 2 years, you can literally work anywhere and smash it
cons: I hear they keep pushing people to go back to the office and nobody wants it yet they have no nerve to say it. Low salary in comparisson to work and time you put in. It seems progress is only available if you switch teams. They will ask if you want to work additional hours over weekends on a Friday at closing time. Super exhausting and pointless daily calls where you have to account for uour work in front of everyone-not good for morale and own sense of wellbeing.

pros:
I was hired as a contractor then was turned into full-time after 5 months. When managers like you, they will find ways to keep you in their team.

The overall culture in the tax department is very nice. Everyone talks to you with respect. They don't make you feel excluded as a temp. Contractors and employees are all supported by the management, but contractors don't have PTO for holidays. (of course, you need to perform well to earn the support, you don't want to make many mistakes but still, want your colleagues to appreciate you)

Work/life balance is very good even in the busy season. You have a fixed sign-on and sign-off time but are still flexible if you need to go to appointments or personal matters.
cons: Career growth is not clear. There are many opportunities within the company but not within your department or group if you work in tax. You will have the opportunity for a higher-level position only when that person is leaving that position.

summary: Pays well but you’ll be working like pawn
advice: Top level management need leaders not managers.
pros: Compensation and Benefits are definitely above market. If you want more money and willing to do anything for it, then Citi is IT. Just do your tasks and money keeps coming - you’ll forget your dreams, even at some point, who you really are.
cons: You do what they tell you to do. Dealing with clients and vendors/suppliers is fine but managing BIG egos is the most challenging part. People tend to stay and grow old here so there’s so you’ll have the best cars and shoes but the roads and signs are rough and old. There are very few leaders in the upper level management - as there are managers. To give context, managers are all after work and tasks, while leaders make you grow as individual and as an employee at the same time. I think it’s safe to say the there are more people here who care more about money than they do care about people.

advice: Work to improve morale by encouraging a team enviroment. Establish a process to review promotion opportunites yearly for the top rated employees. Establish a mentoring program.
pros:
-Great benefits (4 weeks vacation, paid holidays, short term dissability paid at 100%)
-Normal work hours (typically 50 hours a week or so. Generally 8:30 to 6:00)
cons: If you are interested in a highly motivated environment this is not the place for you. There is little room for advancement once you reach the branch manager level. There is no official mentor program. The company attracts employees by saying that there are lots of opportunities due to the globality of the company. However, management will block any possibility of loosing a good employee to another business within the company. As a manger you are not given much opportunity to make decisions. Everything is very cookie cutter. It is my understanding that other areas of the business are not this way but this is what I can say about my experience at Citibank.

summary: Citigroup Fraud ok for someone just starting out in the work force.
advice: It would help if management and quality would listen to the employees' feedback on the performance because it is hard for someone that is not doing the job to successfully understand how to grade one's phone call effectively.
pros:
Citigroup is a very family oriented company, they always have some kind of family activities going on, on the campus site.  And even have a complete daycare that funcions during the day and also a summer program for the kids during the summer.  
They also offer many different work shifts if you are looking for something other than a 8-5 fulltime job.
cons: Some of the downsides where that there was not much room for growth within the fraud department.  And the daycare that they did have was only really available to people that work during the day.  Raises where almost impossible to achieve based on their rating system for the fraud department.

summary: Okay job if you can't get anything else for the moment.
advice: At lease once a year, talk to your employers and see how they are doing. don't get feedback from the mangers, talk to the employers at the lowest level and get their review of the mangers.
pros: The only reason I stayed for few months was because I needed a big company's name on my resume.
cons: I had to sit in a lab with about 40 other people. The manager never came to the lab to ask how we were doing. An another contractor (who was our team lead) only came down at lunch time or 5pm to ask us how many scripts were done. QA is about testing quality of the software, instead they only cared about how many test cases (scripts) were done in a day. The team lead never showed any respect. He used to give us work at lunch time or at 5pm and told us to complete it at the end of the day without paying for overtime. Some of us used to just leave because we never got paid for overtime. It felt like I was working in a call center in India.

advice: Create a better system - find a solution to the root of the problem so there is better work-life balance. Be more fair and compassionate towards employees.
pros:
Co-workers were mostly great - driven, helpful, cooperative. Great family environment.
Managers do not micro-manage, as long as work gets done efficiently, schedules are pretty flexible. Benefits package comparable in industry. There is definitely job autonomy. Liked that career opportunities/rewards/performance ratings and bonuses are not based on years of service but almost entirely on capability and contribution. Very Very important to retain talent!
cons: Upper management not very compassionate about family matters - reluctant to grant days off for funerals if not for immediate family (nerve of them to say grandparents/uncle is not 'close' enough). Workload is crazy half the times, and no OT pay despite frequent 2-3 hour OT days, which leads to disgruntled employees. If you consider the no. of hours worked and oppt. cost of losing time with family, the pay actually becomes quite meager.
