advice: Push to buyout or expand to get more exposure.
pros: Not only is Citigroup a common name in the world, it is also one of the largest companies out there w/ many affiliates. Citibank has great opportunites for growth and advancement.  Provides great benefits and compensation. Sky is the limit, when making money, I am always motivated to make more each month. There are extra incentives every week, that make the job exciting and compatetive with coworkers. Hours are fair and covenient for employees to have a life after work.
cons: Not enough banks yet, especially on the Western and midwest. Everyone is concentrating in finding something wrong with banks nowadays, putting Citibank in the headlines all the time. Stock market has been down the last couple of days, due to economy and loss of Wachovia buyout.

advice: Management should not survey it's employee for better ways to manage.  If your a manager / leader / officer of the company isn't that your job?  It's frustrating to know big bonuses are being paid to managers who get told how to be better.  If the idea is mine shouldn't i get a cut????
pros: Remote work is awesome for a work life balance.  I work with some very intelligent people.  Lot's of room to grow and learn existing technologies.
cons: As a software developer i want to stay away from making widgets.  I want to work on projects that are interesting, and give me a chance to build new technologies.  Citi as a company isn't focused on this.  They care about reducing cost (as they should), stockholder perception (as they should), etc. I am projecting my career goals here; however, there are limited opportunities to invent.

summary: Use CitiBank because they will use you!
advice: Nothing, I think they already know the problems but will never change the culture at Citibank (i.e. love of money) because they are a bank!
pros: Benefits. Compared to other companies in the financial sector they offer good rates for health insurance for POPs, as well as dental and especially vision.
cons: The high turnover rate at Citi Cards in particular make the workplace hard to function due to the poor knowledge of new associates. Weight is put strictly on the ability to meet goals. Most of the jobs are going to India - because it makes good business sense - so don't expect job security. Moreover, the vertical structure at the bank, where managers look-up to senior managers, is a little sickening. This type of vertical structure makes it hard to give proper applauds to employees that offer good work in other areas besides what upper-management seems is the best.

summary: Too many senior managers running the show with insufficient knowledge or ability to do so.
advice: Far too many decisions are politically driven and make no sense.  Lower level managers recognize this and are extremely frustrated at their lack of input.  Stop patronizing employees and lower level managers with VOE surveys and breakfast meetings that produce no changes.  Stop lowering the ceiling on these same employees by bringing in outsiders and recognize the people who have learned the business from the ground up and are more than ready and capable to lead.  Empower these people rather than shutting them out.
pros: Very fast paced work environment, able to learn different things, whether within one group, job posting to other groups, or involuntary reorgs.
cons: Senior mgmt decision making process very "shoot from the hip"; constantly changing priorities mainly due to indecision; extremely political environment; extremely difficult to advance with constant hiring of outsiders into senior positions.

pros: As a first year, I was lucky that one of my VPs didn't believe in unnecessary face time, and was a little more understanding of your life outside of work, as limited as it was.
cons: On the other hand, he tended to have anger bursts/explode at the tiniest sign of you questioning his authority, while one of the associates was more of a passive aggressive type who would smile and pretend everything was okay, but then talk behind your back and sabotage you. I witnessed this with one of the second year analysts who left shortly after I started. I also found that HR really only sees you as another replaceable part to be worked to death and ditched - and then they wonder how come their retention rates are so low. And once you're out, it's as if you never even worked there. After I quit, my administrative assistant failed to submit my expenses before they closed my internal employee account (and he had plenty of time to do so), so then they billed me. Regardless to say, I would never work there again in a million years.

summary: Overall, a good place to work. It's all what you make of it.
advice: Do we really need ALL those layers of management? Let's flatten out a bit ladies and gentlemen...
pros: I happen to have a set of good senior managers directly around me, so it makes things quite satisfying. I have also managed to acquire a good team under me - excellent people. The work is for the most part interesting, and the work-life balance is good. They do recognize top talent, just wish there was more of it.  There are some good people, there are some bad. Still trying to figure out who's who sometimes...
cons: Just wish we had a higher percentage of really good people...I think Citi is just too nice sometimes and really needs to clean house a bit more. Most of the groveling comes from those who should have departed long ago. Sorry if that sounds harsh, but it's the truth.

summary: Good institution with great flaws in key areas of startegy and employee retention.
advice: Senior management has to give regional management more leeway and control in determining compensation and deciding best strategy to deliver returns to shareholders. One size fits all is not the answer when it comes to positioning Citi as number one in local markets.
pros: This is a global institution which has best-in-class standards in terms of product offering and dedication to clients. Good training is offered to employees (or at least used to be offered before the expense cutting regime started). Among local banks, Citi is still revered as the best place to work due to misconception that compensaton is the highest.
cons: As a global institution, Citigroup is often tone-deaf to local needs in terms of compensation increases and benefits packages offered in order to attract the best talent. Very hierachical and full of career-bankers who believe that years worked in the institution equal talent.

summary: For the most people the "job for now"
pros:
- great people
- company does pay extra for extra hours, which sometimes doesn't happen in Poland
- it was pretty easy to get promoted fast
- considering the size of the market, after few years you can get paid really well
- because of the security of the systems, you actually work only in the office, no taking work home
cons:
- lack of reasonable internal movement opportunities (guy who knew Arabic was working with North America transactions, just because nobody cared, even though the same hub was working with Middle East too)
- the initial salary haven't changed in few years
- quite often there was a pressure of working after hours or on the weekends
- the job isn't as interesting as they are presenting it; most of the time you work in the Excel, google maps and google in general, doing job which in 15 years will be done by computers anyway

summary: Great people to work with but dated and monolithic culture
advice:
This is for Directors and above:  Take responsibility to cross aisles, rationalize responsibility and reporting structures - one manager per worker.  Use tools like LEAN for their strategic analytical insights rather than as justifications for moving forward in predetermined paths.

Also, this is the layer of management where the promotion for merit breaks down.  The conversations with first line managers are real, but after that, the promotions are highly political.
pros: The long term employees are very committed to training and mentoring newcomers, and first line management seems to be merit based and communicates expectations and corporate goals well.
cons: The management lines are so gerrymandered and execs are so loathe to take responsibility that any change or task requiring crossing basic organizational structures is Sisyphian.  The services catalogs are either non-existent or fractured, and responsibilities are being thrown at buckets that make no sense.

advice: You cannot transform the bank if you don't encourage new ideas (even sometimes radical ideas). Too many senior people who have been with the bank forever and are highly defensive to new ideas. Bank is trading well below tangible book. Need a wake up call.
pros: Joined after the crisis expecting to find a culture based on admission of past mistakes and a desire to make the bank better. There are still some very smart people there, and at least some of them do think that way. Willingness to give you responsibility and ability to get involved in very important things
cons: You can be given significant levels of responsibility and then discover you will have no budget or resources to actually deliver. Senior ranks heavily comprised on people who have never worked anywhere else, and have no idea about industry best practices. Diversity of opinion and credible challenge is not something that Citi embraces.

advice: Listen to your people, give them a chance to provide honest feedback without repercussion, they are the resources that matters.  Forced rankings, inflated VOE scores and the good ol' boy/girl network is driving away the best talent that Citi has.
pros: Still a good place to work with great benefits, vacation time and flex opportunities for your work life balance.  Senior Executive Management has made a big push to improve the employee relationships with management.
cons: The Senior Executive Leaders are engaged, supportive and working hard to improve the Citi image.  This looks and sounds great in the news and in print.  Middle management, i.e. Managing Directors, Directors and the SVP level, they only care about making their bonuses.  They will sacrifice anyone as long as they make their numbers and bonus.  When they no longer have the leverage, either your gone or they take the package and run.

summary: Do NOT join. It's all glossy from outside but dark inside
pros:
1) Infrastructure
2) Salary and Insurance
cons:
1) Upper mgmt is too arrogant 
2) Inferior people get promoted if they become "Yes Man" of boss. 
3) ISG lead thinks of himself as god of corporate and infact lacks empathy, has poor command over people mgmt and knows a dime about development and its complexities. 
4) Old female employees feel they cannot be terminated/ asked to improve, because they know female-friendly policies. I have seen people getting fired because one female employee found a male too competitive and wanted to get rid of him. 
5) The focus of the organization is on legacy tech and it too hostile. On the other hand they launch programs to encourage creativity and innovation, and employees fall flat on their faces every time because its just some employee-engagement gimmick by HR and Bosses

summary: This company is good place for retirement, but not for people who want to make some achievement.
advice: The company should provide more motivation to employees to work  hard to get work done, not reward people for "follow procedures" but never get things done.
pros: Lots of vacation time--I almost feel guilty for having some much time off.  The company is strong and stable. The company provides fitness facilities and nice cafeteria. Some people go to exercises and have a shower during lunch break. Most people go to lunch at company's cafeteria and it is easy to socialize with coworkers. The foods are good and prices are very reasonable.
cons: It is very hard to get things done. Lots of unnecessary and absurd procedures to follow. Some people only care about following company's procedures or policies and keep themselves out of trouble. It is so frustrating if you want to get something done.

summary: A very demanding place to work
advice: Take better care of the people while you still have them.
pros: It is a very progressive environment in which to work.  For a big bank there is a focus using current to advanced technology.  Policies and procedures are clearly defined in an online knowledge management system.  In the event one cannot find the answer online there are phone reps available to provide support.  Compensation is generally above the industry average.
cons: There is significant pressure to perform.  Work/life balance is difficult to achieve and not well supported by the business.  The corporation as a whole is struggling, as is the rest of the financial services industry, so there are a lot of changes that are unique to this business cycle.  There have been at least three to four rounds of lay-offs in the past 18 months with more streamlining anticipated in the future.

summary: Strong brand and credibility in marketplace
advice: More support for new FA's. Put new FA's on teams for first three years or have a more disciplined process for training.
pros: Distinguished organization with strong brand. Strong analytical support including help desks for all topics. Flexible platforms allow for customized investment strategies.  Focused on comprehensive financial planning and tools are satisfactory. Compensation package is attractive. Very entrepreneurial environment which works for more established FA's.
cons: Very big and too much information to navigate.  Too many platforms for advisors to choose from, each with a different fee schedule. Lately, issues with financial stability affects prospect perception. Employee cuts may affect customer service. Not much support for newer FA's. Throw you out there and figure it out on your own. No marketing budget so you have to spend a lot of money to make money.  A lot of focus on cold calling rather than other marketing strategies.

summary: Challenging and in need of efficiency
advice: Communicate with your team. Obviously certain team leads provide different advice and stress different important elements. Talk about the fact that management will disagree over certain practices. Stress to your team what you expect and what you believe is important. Tell your team to  pay less attention to what fellow coworkers or doing/getting away with.
pros:
The work is interesting and their is always room for improvement.
The days fly by because their is always plently of work to do.
Everyday is different, twists and subjective decisions make you stay on your toes.
cons:
There is a disconnect between management and what lower us lower level peons are doing.
The nature of the division forces 300+ people to make subjective evaluations. 
Continuity and objectives need to be unified.
Or providing continuing training while also increasing analyst freedom.

advice: The red tape. Really. 3 different systems to raise a database update, and 2 weeks to process this is simply embarrassing.
pros: Salary very high for position. Willing to try new technologies for applications. Management (at least in my experience) has been very nice and approachable. Office is in a very good location of Dublin. Also office is of very high standard.  Overtime is not a major part of their culture in my experience - apart from releases which take part on Saturdays (from home). Ability to work remotely.
cons: All the red tape. My god the issues they have for even requesting the most simple of updates (like database updates for example) even in test environments. In my experience, very little social interaction between employees. Teams can be across different continents (even 3!) which creates time zone issues and lack of clear / constant communication.

advice: While size does give economies of scale, it can also limit the ability to be nimble and adapt to the changing market place. It also can foster a culture of layers and hierarchy that stifles innovation.  While the management has done a lot to ensure that these things do not happen, it needs to be vigilant to ensure that Citi continues to have an open,  innovative, forward looking and merit based culture.
pros: Citi's Global reach and large volumes and applications pushed me to think big and think globally. It allowed gave me exposure to multiple asset classes and business lines. It gave me opportunities to visit countries like Russia, Bahrain, the UK and the US.
cons: Being a large company, they have several HR policies which are of a 'one size fits all' kind.  The green card processing policies left much to be desired and caused a lot of frustration.

summary: Citi is still a good place to work, it pays the bills when many are struggling.
advice: Listen to new ideas and continue to reduce expenses. There are idea's within the company to generate billions in revenue that are being completely ignored. I was given the opportunity to present my ideas and even though everyone agreed they were great, they have decided to postpone acting on them. In a climate like this, I think it's important to look at new revenue streams even though it does mean some small risks. The risk reward potential is huge, if we can just make even one work, this company can be great again.
pros: Flexibility and benefits. It's a large company with plenty opportunities. Good stability and very flexible with people that want to work from home.
cons: The company is not doing well financially. No raises, very tiny bonuses if anything.

advice: The most important aspect is to keep the employees happy to avoid a mass exodus when the economy actually turns around.  Most people are just waiting for the next opportunity, whether it be a better one or the same.
pros: One of the best reasons to work at Citigroup would be the amount of potential exposure you can get to all of the different aspects of banking/financial services.
cons:
Career advancement is poor - there is not much mobility.  This is definitely related to the current market conditions, although all other banks are performing at a much better rate.

This is a company where if times are good, then things are good.  If times are bad like right now, it is quite depressing.  The morale is very low as there is no incentive to do any more than your minimal requirements.

summary: Citi has to get out of it's own way
advice: Stock holders, kick out the current board, and re-tool, even dismantle this awkward and unmanageable business.
pros: Citi is a place to learn the craft of banking, within whatever profession one works in, for me, I became both an executive and a talented architect for technology while I was there. It has a smart work force, all dedicated to doing a good job. It has sufficient power in the world, so that a person can build a great external network.
cons: It suffers great paternalistic centralized control, which leads to an arrogance in which the best ideas from below, and from the regions are not given sufficient weight. This leads to frustration in the work force, poor results for the business, and great nepotism in the work place. Most folks I know at citi are simply getting a pay check, hoping things will get better.

summary: Great company if you are in the right group
advice: Mentor, coach and actually move forward.
pros: Work/Life Balance, Insurance, 401K and plenty of opportunity to try different jobs/careers if you are unsure.
cons: The company always has a flavor of the month and lacks direction.  Recently it has gotten better, but we'll see if they stick with it or not.  Many people have long tenure, which can be seen as good, but it also means that advancement sucks and everyone is resistant to change.  It seems that Citi wants to move forward, but they can't do it with the same old thinking that got us here in the first place, which is what they have.  Politics and multiple layers of management that have been in place for 15+ years and are just concerned about checking the box and will probably retire in the same position in another 15+ years.

summary: Citi, like most IBD programs, offers a great place to begin a career.
advice: Pay more attention to maintaining and promoting a sustainable franchise that is not solely focused on short term gains.
pros: Citi does very well to invest in its juniors, and there's a focus on retaining some for eventual promotion. Some other firms 100% assume that as an analyst, you're not going to stay and therefore will not invest in you as heavilty (e.g. client exposure). Most banks on the Street, Citi included, however, are supportive or their analyst recruiting after their 2-year program.
cons: Despite its excellent training for analysts, Citi has had some trouble with managing its brand, especially with how much change the organization has gone through in the past several years following the collapse. Pay traditionally has lagged behind the street, but recently there has been some effort to match the street.

advice: My direct manager is the best manager that I've ever reported to in the course of my career on Wall Street, so I am grateful.  For Senior Management, my advice would be to remember that at the end of the day, the people who work for you are your greatest resource.  Support, encouragement and humility go a long way.
pros: It has been a pleasure working at Citi.  I've worked at other large banks and found the corporate culture at Citi to be more welcoming, collaborative and supportive.  I'd definitely recommend working for this firm. Of course, variances may occur depending on which department you work for, but overall, I'm pleased.
cons: Recent reorganization and cost cutting efforts (which are experienced across the banking industry) have reduced staff and changed many functions.  Of course, only time will tell if the changes boost the bottom line.

advice: Employee morale is down consistently over the last few years because managers do not show genuine interest in viewing people as resources.
pros: Flex time and freedom to work from home. The salary is slightly ahead of the industry package and the bonus is consistently 15%. The salary package makes it very difficult to leave. The company matches up to 6% in stocks and the medical and dental coverages is up to 90%. The contractual work week is 37.5 and over the entire year, that number is fairly accurate.
cons: There are jobs posted on the company intranet for internal movement but candidates are already flagged for these positions so the jobs aren't really open. Management seems disconnected and uninterested in viewing people as resources. Training courses outside the city are frowned upon.

advice: Stop listening to the accountants.  People gain experience at the firm and as such are more valuable than anyone who just walks in the door.  To fire the person with experience to replace him with TWO that do not have experience makes no sense.  The two newbies take forever to reinvent and rediscover what the experienced man already knows.
pros: Large firm, secure and intelligent staff ready for support if needed with lots of room for improvement leading to opportunities unparalleled in a smaller better run institution.
cons: Lots of know it alls who really don't know it all.  Too much bureaucracy to be considered a dynamic institution.  They are completely under the government microscope fo compliance and as such cannot move fast even if their corporate life depended on it.  Run by accountants who do not understand the quality of investments in personnel.

pros: Citi is an amazing place., The peer group is excellent and the opportunity to learn is really great! I love working with Citi and would strongly recommend Citi for people who have big ambitious goals in their professional life. Some may consider Citi to have an aggressive culture but it works really for people who are competitive in life. Citi is a large Institution with Highly Skilled & Talented professionals , the workforce is diverse , not just limited to Gender but all walks of life, geography , skill expertise , culture & ethnicity . Teammates are supportive and the management is transparent. Communication standards are very well defined and applied; role and responsibilities very well set. The organization policies are good and offers good benefits and compensations. Overall everyone seems concerned and responsible for what he/she is doing.
cons: Nothing as such, best in everything

advice: Don't forget about your employees regardless of the size of your team.
pros:
The benefits.  They are very generous with their dental plan and fairly so with their education reimbursement.

My manager was also quite flexible with giving time off when requested.  However, she was more of the exception than the norm.

Because of the size of the company, you get to meet a lot of people and network.
cons:
It is a very large company and it is very easy to "get lost in the system".  This often means that it is possible to be passed over for promotions and advancement.

They do not hesitate to lay off their employees either.  Often employees hear through the media before they are told by their management.  Even managers who have been with the company for 20+ years are laid off without notice.  It may just be the culture.

advice: Hire managers with direct and right experience and put them in the right position.  Cut down the number of middle managers. The learning process for new managers is too long and often lead the team in a direction against business.    Above all,  they also need to be empowered and be accountable.   The lower level employees just want to get their work done rather than spending much of their time reporting to so many managers.
pros: learn a lot of banking business
cons: Managers coming in and out.  Organization structure is too complicated.   Without  proper restructuring,  the organization needs to hire more internal communicators to smooth out operations which make the organization even more complicated.   It is hard to plan for a career in an always changing environment.  No clear business goal and guidelines.    Oral promised incentives sometimes can not be delivered after reaching the target.

advice: The Voice-of-the-Employee every year shows that employees do not believe senior management will act on the results of the VOE. Citi management should ensure that significant investments are made into employee morale, culture, compensation and development. Citi has turned into too much of a revolving door for many middle level managers and non-managing middle level employees.
pros: Citi is a vast company with many diverse and different people to meet and work with while your are employed by Citi. Working for a larger company like Citi provides security during good financial times in the industry.
cons: When the financial industry starts to encounter tough times, Citi is typically the first to be impacted. Since the crisis, Citi struggled to grow revenues while trying to manage its expense base. Cost cutting and reductions-in-force are quite common during the tougher times in the industry. Citi also strategizes to be middle-of-the-road to average in terms of compensating employees.

advice: My advice to management is to spend more time understanding the job you are tasking us to do. All too often direction is changed without truly understanding what effect the change in one functional group will have on another.  I would also recommend training in change management for leaders to understand the importance of engaging employees to buy in to change when it's transformative.  This will increase productivity and moral.
pros: The ability to career path and learn many aspects of the industry. The mission and values have meaning and can benefit you if you own them.
cons: The pay structure for internal transfers is not competitive. If you are qualified for the job you should be paid accordingly.

summary: Stable employment, not the best for ambitious people
advice:
Management should focus on improving important processes and working with new technology.
Exceptional employees are not appreciated enough and instead are treated equally with people who just wait for the weekend whole week and don't develop in any way.
pros: Salary is decent. Great benefits. Good work-life balance. Friendly people. Relatively stable employment (depends on the department though). A lot of diferent opportunities. For somebody that looks for a stable employment and doesn't want demanding or stressful job, Citi would be a great company.
cons:
Citi is huge and it suffers from poor management in some areas and bureaucracy. A lot of processes that are vital for the organisation are far from being optimized. Instead they are being constantly patched by different teams and incompetent people.
Don't count on fixing your HR problem easily if it's something more than sick leave or vacation request. 
There are big discrepancies for the same salary grade in different departments.

summary: Well compensated high stress working environment.
advice: Keep up the willingness to promote the benefits and the encouraging aspects of the workplace. Focus less on sales and more on customer satisfaction. The lowered stress will prbably bring increased results
pros: The Compensation was good $11 dollars an hour to start with about 3 dollars a sale bringing it to about 17 dollars an hour. Not bad for a kid right out of high school. They were also very encouraging and supportive. The management sincerely tried to make you feel at home. After perfoming my first few months in the top 20 in the nation they offered me a promotion.. After less than 6 months of employment. Very admirable i thought
cons: It was fairly stressful. Sales were so important that it often made me feel sick if i could not meet quotas. Many people leave the sales aspect of the job to just do normal customer service because of the high pressure

summary: If you rate them negatively on a survey they will retaliate
advice: Stop running a double standard. There is a clique there in Gray,TN that sticks together and eliminates people to keep themselves in power. The obsurd "qualities" that calls are rated with is ridiculous. The unit managers act like we can solve customers problems by interrogating them over and over. The programs they have aren't life changing and don't give unemployed people jobs. Stop pretending that reps are so dumb they can't follow your guidelines. When a manager is struggling he blames it on a rep and promises if they fire them to the OM things will get better. Stop retaliating against people that give bad ratings the the company for the VOE. It is a sham anyway and yes men and women are rewarding if they rate the company high by keeping their jobs.
pros: good health insurance benefits, good parking
cons: Low pay, get beat  out of bonuses, managers throwing reps under the bus to save themselves, had a successful rating based on monthly results then at year end taken away and rerated to unsuccessful and no raise and tuition reimbursement lost.

advice: invest in human capital. hire, train, and maintain high quality 'wall street' analysts. Pay them and you will retain the talent. Please, lay off the pity candy and soda handouts, they are extremely ghetto and immature and insulting. Management handed out 'payday' candy on pay day as a thank you when a generous bonus or raise would suffice. Please don't tell me that funds are not available. Have managers actually have a case load to see how analysts feel and do their jobs. Also hire from within and based on merits or work performance and not based on who talks the most.
pros: flexibility in working arrangements, work at home schedules, excellent benefits and vacation
cons: middle management fails to recognize the utterly importance of its analysts. Analysts right now are struggling with excessive work loads and analysts who can't handle it, just walk right out. Initial training for the analysts is severely lacking.

summary: Poor Management and opportunity and outright corporate misbehavior
advice: Dump your employee review process. Forcing people into a bell curve doesn't make sense. Managers should be able to make honest reviews of their employees and not be forced into giving undeserved (or unearned) ratings. Listen to people, don't dictate. Figure out who Citigroup is and build it. Don't be everything and fail to accomplish anything.
pros: Good benefits. I hate to say it, but that's about it.
cons: Typically poor management, including severe office politics and under qualified management teams. It would be one thing if people were capable of getting better, but typically management makes the same mistakes over and over. Strategies change very often, with dictates from NY that fail to drive beneficial status, while they refuse to listen to people who know what they are talking about. Management even outright lied in a town hall saying Citigroup had "no significant part in the mortgage security crash" in 2008. Really?

advice: Consider investing more in training with hands on. Update commission structure.
pros: Decent base pay. If you get to a busy branch and figure out how to make the commission work for you, you can make commission. Great place for self learners.
cons:
It's almost impossible to make any commission for the first 6 months. They have these "flavor of the month" products regardless of client needs. We're selling HELOCs. Everyone is getting a HELOC. If they need it or not.
If you got hired because your sales experience and have no prior knowledge of financial products. You're in for a treat. You will get training. With ZERO help on the sales floor. Basically you're to learn the textbook and then just figure it out how to apply it in real life situations. It can be very tough at the beginning. Also the commission structure is made so that you don't ever make any money. You can sell a lot and barely get paid.

summary: The C definitely stands for Change!
advice: Choose strong, committed, respected, in-touch leaders and stick with them! Give them time to develop and implement a strategy, then roll it out through the entire organization with support from all levels.
pros: Citi has a strong retail brand in several major US markets and is known worldwide for its financial services. Starting salary was competitive. Very positive work/life balance given that my manager and the team I supported were hundreds of miles away and I could work remotely as desired. I was in CA, not NY where Citi is headquartered.
cons: Constant change at all levels of the organization. The company is still trying to recover from the financial crisis of 2008 and is keeping a close eye on expenses (which makes sense). Constant change means layoffs, changes in management and other concerns to keep you up at night. NY runs the show, which can make it tough for other regions to get their voices heard.

summary: Big company, too big to fail, too big to succeed - both as a company, and for the individual employees.
advice: Eliminate layers, recognize the talents of your emplyees.
pros: Citigroup is a big company, there are lots of opportunities to grow if you seek out to them. A person can meet people that he/she never thought existed or learn about things that he/she never heard of.
cons: Big company, you can easily gotten lost if you are not aggressive. Like everyone else said, you are just a number - or as they put it, a P & L. In business, it's about how much you can bring in. In back office operations and technology, it's all about how many people you "manage". Huge disparity in pay scales depending on your group - in fact, there is no "Citigroup" culture, it's all about the culture of whatever group you wound up in.

summary: If there aren't any other alternatives, at least its a job
advice: Forget about forcing services down your client's throat and concentrate on superior customer service and your NPS scores will be better.
pros: Citi has superior insurance, including dental and vision.  The facility is well kept and inexpensive daycare is available as well as a gym, post office, and medical center.  There are family movie night in the cafeteria and various weekend events throughout the year.
cons: Pay for sales and service representatives is $11.60 per hour.  The "bonus" you hear about in training is almost unattainable because of the complexity of the bonus calculation formula.  Managers want perfect customer satisfaction surveys but encourage high pressure sales techniques.  Everyday you hear about talk time, offer rates and sales results.  Don't expect any respect from your managers or the people you talk to on the phone.

summary: Always save a paper trail to cover any errors that might come your way
advice: In one year my department lost 12 employee out of 20. Open your eyes something is wrong
pros:
Is a reliable job
There is some really good coworkers
cons:
There is always someone to put the blame on. I remember my first manager used to tell me you always want to save a paper trail because when the bomb blows you don't want to be the one that is holding the burned paper bag.
The management tend to be unsupportive
Shady individuals
The volume of work is high and it is not enough pay compare to other competitors
The structure of how work is divided is not fair some individuals could get from 50 to 70 deals while other could get 15- 20 deals. 
Management allows for other departments to come down on you. Too unprofessional.

advice: Do not use contract employees for high level subject matter positions, hire internally. This way the internal employee knows what to expect without the cost of on-boarding new contract employees which may not work out which equals wasted time.
pros: Some very nice people depending on your department. I cannot stress how important it is to know how to gauge your work environment, management and peers.
cons: Extremely cut-throat, I cannot work in a place where everyone throws everyone under the bus. This is the environment or at least department I worked in, no hard feelings I wish I was told this by staffing agency. My trainer was a pirate and his boss was a perfectionist so it was a very intense dynamic. I would not recommend this to any contract employee, basically your setup from the get-go unless you come from a previous environment like that where you know to operate.

advice: Remember Non-exempt employees matter. A lot of them see all the benefits that exempt employees get and find it unfair when they are working just as hard if not more with no overtime pay. Give them more flexibility.  A lot of them who are are in non exempt roles are not newly graduates, don't get bonuses, and don't get to work from home when this is technically a fin/tech environment. Make them feel valued as well in other ways
pros: There is a start and an end. The team and people that work there are smart/fantastic/passionate. You learn a lot from each other, and the work life balance is great
cons: They do not make non-exempt employees feel valued. If you are exempt you get a lot more flexibility. Even if you get a good year review, you are not guaranteed a merit increase. Salary tends to be on the lower end.

advice: Don't lie saying it's for the good of the customer when you know it's possible to change the system. Customer focused you say but all you care about are profits. Which is understandable you're a for-profit bank.
pros: Wonderful Benefits, sub-par pay and a nice amount of time off. It can be where you move further, but there may be some issue depending on getting past the lower part of the job first. Really work hard and you might get a promotion.
cons: The call center mentality, there is a reason it has roughly a 6-month retention rate. It gets a bit difficult, there is a difference in handling customers face to face versus over the phone. Have a thick skin or don't accept the job. There is some help, but scheduling and trying to switch departments you have to quit and reapply hoping they have a different shift available to you.

jobTitle: Credit Specialist II Retail Credit Services
pros:
Paid training, and the work is very easy as long as you pay attention; it's just extremely repetitive.

They give great benefits, and almost a months worth of paid time off. You just have to be careful to not go over the "unplanned" time.

There are some good options to move up, but they are free and far between.
cons:
You won't know how to do the work being expected of you once you're done in the training. You'll be put on the floor, and told to read procedures and figure it out, but the people around you are usually willing to help out.

A lot of the problems just come down to bad communication, but management would rather keep saying it's the agents responsibility to stay up to date rather then actually talking with line level reps to make sure everyone understands, and is in a good position to succeed.

advice: Take ethics complaints more seriously and focus on doing right by people instead of strictly looking at things arbitrarily as dollars and cents. Ultimately if the right thing is done, I do believe that will pay it self back to the company ten fold in so many different ways.
pros: There are a lot of great opportunities throughout Citi considering how large it, and also in the audit department. There is space for promotion or movement in the company between departments.
cons: Because of how large the company and the audit department is, and with teams being compartmentalized, it's also a hit or miss regarding your growth opportunities depending on the team you're on. Some senior managers empower their teams, some don't, and others are outright unethical. But that's to be expected in such a large company, not everyone is going to do the right thing.

summary: GREAT COMPANY, GREAT WORK LIFE BALANCE
advice:
Ramp up digitisation efforts to mitigate strategic risks. Citi is well equipped to do so. Other banks just started earlier that's all.
A lot of processes at Citibank is not optimized and are very slow like waterfall not agile.
pros:
Great benefits, more than other banks in SG, especially the Flexible spending amount and medical insurance. 
Great work-life balance, very different from other banks too. The pace is comfortable and the people are really nice and helpful.
Great culture than other banks. (no-joke man, some dept in other banks are damn toxic but not at Citibank. OMG completely life changing.) [I could see myself here for a long time :)]
Shuttle bus service for office at changi.
cons:
Employee engagement could be better. like events and townhalls, but these are a bit minor. 
digital services are surprisingly not up to par with some banks despite being equipped to do so.

advice: Remember that the goal of transformation is to be a better bank, not to rush to the finish line.  The finish line can wait until we get it right
pros:
Lots of opportunities to be promoted 
Competitive pay
Good benefits
WFH most of the week
Great for networking 
Good opportunity to learn the nuts and bolts of what makes a bank
cons:
Citi is undergoing alot of change due to the consent order. Because of this there is ALOT of work to do and alot of hiring. The downside to this is that 
1-  projects are complex and high risk 
2- burnt out staff quitting has caused high turn over 
3- mgmt is hiring as fast as it can which has resulted in desperate unqualified hires
If you’re willing to sacrifice your time and at times sanity you might stick around long enough to be given a promotion

summary: If you are thinking of being a temporary worker, beware!
advice: The CEO gets tens of millions of dollars in bonuses, yet the company can't afford to provide benefits to employees working more than 40 hours per week?
pros: Interacted well with other analysts who started at the same time as me. Trainers were helpful during the training period.
cons:
I was among a group of anti-money laundering analysts working at Citigroup through a temp agency. We were told that the job was temp-to-permanent, and that as soon as we passed a quality check we would be hired as official Citi employees. Instead, toward the end of the assignment date, all were dismissed (and informed not by our superiors at Citi, but by temp agency employees) without warning or notice, because the positions were being eliminated. What’s worse, I checked online the following day and the temp agency has posted more identical job listings for a new group of analysts. Seems like the positions were not eliminated after all.

No vacation time, no benefits, not treated well.

summary: Just a big name to work with and tell your friend that I work for CITI
advice: Salary is an important factor  especially on a entry level employees who put in efforts to out stand,work hard and take no leave in their initial period with company. please do give some nice increment package or a nice bonus when contract is reviewed and extended or confirmed.
pros: flexible,good name in banks, work from home, training and vacation benefit
cons: Very poor salary package for beginners, hardly peanuts :(( Infact temporary staff gets 3-4 times the salary then the permanent ones. Very jealousy and unhappy with pay package as it include super and tax which leaves me with nothing. Boss appreciates ur work but no rewards, no bonus, no increment in salary packages nothing.Just very dry Feel like I earn so much but still I don't own anything .Wana go Shopping Spree for ages with a secured bank account ;)

advice:
Four years ago it was stated that regional management would go away and we would be managed by business, all that happened was an additional level of management was added so now there is both, This is par for the course on management shake ups. Due to events like this Citi is too top heavy, we need a healthy cut to the size of management.

Operations has also grown too large to be properly managed and it relies far too much on poorly conceived in house software platforms, both of these should be cut.
pros: If you are a star performer you will be noticed because there aren't that many there
cons: Overall the company lacks a clear strategy, for years it was buy everything in sight and grow that way. Now we no longer do purchase companies but due to poor integration of prior acquisitions the company does not perform as well as it should.

advice: Treat the people that provide your data with respect. Show them that the data is important and it couldn't be done without them.
pros: Health insurance used to be amazing. With the new CEO, things have gone downhill. The culture is great, if you are part of a group. There are fundraisers for the community, pot lucks, and bake sales constantly. The break rooms are full of coffee and vending machines offering anything you can imagine.
cons: They are constantly restructuring the company. They expect people to do the jobs of 3 people. Some of the higher level management is completely clueless. Others are brilliant. You have to hope that you get a good one, or your work life could be awful. There is a lot of favoritism within the company. They promote meritocracy, but employees never see it.

summary: A very 'corporate' workplace with great culture
advice: We invest so many resources to make the workplace great but it would be very beneficial to take one more step and PLAN changes out so that transitions are smooth.  So many things feel pieced together on-the-fly.
pros: We have really great people. Even though there are 1,800+ employees, most people feel like more than a number. Benefits are above average, pay is fair, time off is excellent (146+ hours paid per year), some 4-10hr schedules, lots of overtime opportunities. The list goes on and on. Best environment I've ever worked in; almost unbelieveable for a site this large.
cons: Policies and procedures change frequently and there is always conflicting information (published on intranet, passed down from supervisors, sent around in emails, hear-say on the sales floor, etc.).  The IT infrastructure is lacking: the systems feel as though they were pieced together with no sight of the "big picture."

advice: Try to make the organization a bit more unified and organic. I don't really feel like a Citi employee but rather an employee of another company that simply borrows the Citi logo.
pros:
High salaries for those entering the company from outside
Brand recognition with a large international company
Mississauga office is easily accessible and well maintained
cons:
Canada is generally ignored as far as the organization is concerned as a whole
Company is heavily segmented. You literally have no idea what's going on in the rest of the organization
Inflated job titles mislead people (everyone is either an AVP, VP or SVP)
Most of the perks/benefits that come with being a Citi employee are only useful to Americans.
CFSC does not pay bonuses... maybe somewhere between $500-$800
No clear transparent bonus compensation plan.  You get a couple hundred dollars at the end of the year but have no idea how it's tied to your performance evaluation.

advice: Job site needs a major overhaul and facilities upgrade.  A Petri dish placed in any area would probably discover numerous diseases. Chairs are stained and uncomfortable. Technology is from circa 2004. Ask management a question ; they are sure to answer with "see your team lead" which never amounts to getting an answer.  The business is too afraid of getting fined by OCC to be effective. Employees don't care about their jobs; nothing ever gets done.
pros: Great cafe with a Starbucks; great fitness center and nurse station
cons: Awful technology; poor,  inexperienced management; filthy facilities. Great job for VP level or higher; awful for everybody else. Culture is egotistical snobs that cater to rich clients and the hell with everyone else.  You can work there years and never meet the people on your team since there are no name plates or any way to identify anyone who works there.  Benefits are expensive and cover less and less.  Career opportunities are a charade, hidden in a maze of acryonims and corporate jargon meant to disguise and deceive jobs that really suck.

summary: A typical big bank in many ways
advice: We are all connected. Treat others like how you like to be treated. After 2008, no one can sit around and BS any more, so support your bottom associates or expect an early retirement.
pros: You will be working amongst awesome international retail associates and clients. They will enrich your views about the world outside of U.S . It has been a previlige to meet them.
cons: Very little support from the back office which are mostly located overseas. You will not be able to call them to get clarifications. When things become challenging, you will be left on your own to deal with angry clients who are constantly screwed over by the back office. Your sales efforts are constantly captured incorrectly which require constant follow up. Upper management sits around collects big paychecks and does not care about associates real feedback on what needs to be improved. You are pressure to meet goals that are unreal and expect to be set up to fail. They will make stuff up to throw you under the bus to save themselves from any liablities.

advice:
Recognize employees more often. 
Get managers under control with the favoritism.
Listen to what employees say and respond to them, even if you aren't going to do what they suggested.
Keep promises.
pros:
Friendly environment. 
Good Advancement, depending on your location.
Work from home.
Dental and Vision insurance are great.
cons:
Medical insurance could definitely be better.
Often release updates, policies or changes without "thinking" first and then the employees have to make up for upper managements shortcomings. 
Depending on your department, you are basically a 'hybrid' agent that is supposed to take calls for one department, let's say the commercial dept., but ends up being forced into training for another department, for example consumer, and then constantly gets calls for consumer even if you are there for OT with the commercial department.
Advancement opportunities are really all about who you know. Most of the time they know who they are hiring for it before they post it.

summary: Good opportunities depending on where you're located.
advice: More transparency.  I guess Vikram is doing what he needs to do to try to get this company back on the right track, but only his top executives know exactly what that is.  The rest of the employees are left in the dark and wondering when they're going to receive their pink slips.
pros: Given the company's size and scope of financial services offered, there are lots of opportunities to network and move around within company as your career interests change.  Compensation is on the higher side if you work in the right group (Markets and Banking).
cons:
This is more possible only if you work at headquarters in New York.  

It's a huge company with a lot of bureaucracy.  Morale has been pretty low lately given all the negative issues surrounding the company and about three rounds of layoffs since the beginning of the year.

advice:
1. Change old management philosophies. A person who was 'fired', should be able to apply in other groups. Your middle tier is worst for a large size company.
2.  Change non-performing directors. They are the worst parasites and eat all the bonus.
3. Ensure that money and bonus comes to ground level. Money and bonus are scooped on the top layer itself.
4. Have an independent team to evaluate the ratings. Biases are extremely prevalent and must be shunned in order for you to survive and grow. Else you will perish.
pros: Citi is an okay company. It does not have a 'better' in any group, but you can end up in a group 'worse'.
cons: In some groups, politics is very high and very dirty. Backbiting is a very common thing. Staying 2-3 years is okay in such a place but don't prolong it.

advice: Micromanagement needs to stop
pros:
Pay is decent
Benefits are not terrible
cons: I have worked for multiple banks and this is by far the worst one. Their equipment is 100 years old and their systems are just as bad... slow and inefficient. Employees are whipped and work for this terrible place because they don't know anything else. The company is compliance heavy to the point of obsession. This company does not trust its employees - likely because they've been sued so many times already. Do not work here unless you want to be micromanaged. Their turnover rate is so bad they actively try to prevent it by having you sign certain documents before you're hired - won't indicate what specifically, but it's bad. It's very corporate and I should have known better when I accepted this terrible offer.

advice: Streamline remote working style for employees
pros:
I joined Citi during the lockdown period in 2021. The first week few weeks were filled with warm welcomes, process trainings by in-house experts and tremendous support from all directions.

The core culture that one can observe in Citi is inclusiveness. Irrespective of my newness in the organisation, there were multiple opportunities to work on various projects, share ideas across the table and have timely interaction with the leadership team. 

Something that stands out in Citi is employee benefits  such as wellness programs, health care, leave policy, etc. Another key aspect to talk about is Diversity. Diversity is not a buzzword in Citi. It’s way of life for us in Citi! 

I am #Citiproud and I look forward to grow and learn in my journey with Citi.
cons: NA - - - Not applicable

advice: Training is vital to a new employee. Please be sure to give them the proper training and extra help needed in order to succeed in their new job. Also pay attention to individuals not performing their jobs at all.
pros: Compensation, Career Advancement.  They pay very competitively to a college graduate looking for his/her first job and there are numerous networking opportunities. Lunch & Learn seminars help individuals network with senior management. The training you receive is very helpful as well. Team oriented environment helps one to get acquainted with fellow employees as well as learn in an efficient matter. There is a lot of flexibility and many co-workers have switched industries, workgroups, or locations.
cons: Some employees are annoying. For example, they do not do any work, but just joke around the entire time.

summary: It's who you know, not what you know
advice: It's not about the platform, it's about the people. As with many other institutions, the old boys network should just be done away with. It obscures talent and, as seen in the latest financial fallout, prevents sensible risk management when the old boys are all trying to better one another, and too busy having drinks and golf together to see the impending disaster.
pros: According to ex-colleagues who had moved on to other banks, Citi Private Bank is comparatively non-political, and truly tries move forward for the business. Colleagues are pretty collegial and open, except for a few mid-level management who can be nasty, as with any workplace.
cons: Despite the usual talk about meritocracy, it really is about being at the right place at the right time for any movement, lateral or otherwise. Being someone's pet also helps.

advice:
Insure that everyone is doing his/her fair share of the work.
Pay attention to the "little" people a little more - when it comes to shelling out the money at the end of the year - don't keep it all for yourself.
pros:
Fairly reasonable work  to private life ratio.
You can work remotely at times and thus avoid always having to be in the office.
cons:
Some employees are doing most if not all of the work while others hardly doing anything at all. They are being paid to just show up thereby by placing an unfair burden on others who are forced to work that much harder and pick up more than one's fair share of the workload.
Management is distance and hardly even acknowledges you. Forget ever getting a hello or goodbye if you're not on the VP level or higher.

advice: stop changing the verbatim closing please
pros:
-if you're lucky enough to sit near a window you might get a nice view of the lake
-i honestly have not met a person there that i dislike. most are very friendly
cons:
-very stressful
-clients are extremely rude
-breaks are very short- 1/2 hour lunch gives you just enough time to grab something in the cafeteria use the restroom and get back in your seat. weekends are worse because the caf is closed. if you dont pack a lunch then you get to sprint to burgerking (the only thing close) and jam the food in your mouth on the drive back because if you're a minute late you'll hear about it
-false promises from management- told we could advance within 6 months. once the six months rolled around we were told we have to wait at least a year to advance
-you're surrounded by people but you never have time to talk to them or get to know them because you're on the phone constantly
-the pay isn't that great

summary: Profitability Must Return To Increase The Stock Price
advice: You cannot cut your way to profitability and a higher stock price. Sooner or later your business lines must make money. The technology organization is completely mismanaged and preventing true competition among the other players on the street.
pros: The new CEO Michael Corbat has the vision to return to a core set of products and services to allow the Bank to make money in the 21st century and start a growth trajectory, but it will take many, many years at the current rate.
cons: Citigroup has not yet determined fully what it wants to be when it grows up. The new economy has them reaching for profitability by cutting products, services and talent. A new strategy is required to create a balance between cost cutting and growth. Right now, the strategy is very much dependent on cost cutting.

advice: Treat people better. Use the surveys to identify areas and managers that need to be fixed.
pros: Variety of work. Company supports the community. Flexible work arrangements-easy to work at home. Lots of training.
cons: I worked there for 10 years. Very bureaucratic and difficult to get things done. Constant reorgs, layoffs, shifting priorities and difficult to get resources. It was a job but thats about all I can say. The longer I worked there, the more numb I got to it. Kind of like a lobster in a pot. The water gets warmer, but you don't realize suddenly it is boiling and you are dying. Many years with no increases. Policy is to never give more than 10% increase even when you get a promotion. Better to leave and then come back, than to take a promotion.

advice: Lighten up, stop trying to impose your made up rules on new employees. Help groom newer employees so they will be happy working for you. Be transparent. Don't get angry when asked questions about the company etc. Its not 1985 you should get with the times and learn that it doesn't work the way it did back then.
pros: Its  a respected global company. Health insurance is good, they are involved with the community.
cons: No room for growth, not every plays by the same rules, no raises, my boss told me I could not use my sick days. Citi has the option to work remote but if you get a boss like mine that only applies to employees who have been there for many many years not newer ones even tough your entire team is mostly remote 95 - 100% remote.

summary: The worst example of H1B  Culture!  Avoid if you are a non-immigrant.
advice: Hire more Americans.  The current IT staff  that exists is  80-90% H1B immigrant from 6 week technical schools in India and have no idea what they are doing.  This seems odd in a country that is less than .1% Asian immigrant.
pros: There is nothing redeemable about this company from an IT standpoint.
cons:
Everything bad about an H1B 'culture' company.

Like most H1B companies the workforce is underpaid and exploited and the managers (mostly foreign born Indians) are hostile to non-immigrants and operate as if they were running a Mumbai call center.

They will do everything to underpay, overwork, and exploit the working relationship.  When confronted they will lie and/or ignore your emails, phone calls, etc.  This would work well if you were in Mumbai or New Delhi.  However as an American Company they need to do better.

Just do yourself a favor - say no and look for work elsewhere.

advice: Review GIDA Team workloads more often, screen job candidates better.
pros: Comfortable working environment, nice, respectful culture and people. If you like to be busy every minute and don't mind the monotony of tickets after tickets, then this is a good place. Teaches how to handle conference calls, connect and juggle communication between several teams and push through with and complete urgent requests and escalations. Good for building problem solving skills and learning how to work in a team and independently handle situations on your own as well. Also teaches you to see where your team is located in an end-to-end process, and helps build competence in handling applications quickly and routinely.
cons: Very slow position to advance and workload is unbalanced between teams and individuals. High stress levels and not compensated properly for it compared to other multinationals in the area.

summary: Great pay at cost of Poor Work life balance
advice: Highly important to prioritize automation and standardization of processes as to increase efficiency of processes and help employees make the best of their time. I feel Citi has a very high attrition rate due to employee burnout and it occurs  for a reason
pros: The company compensates its employees very well. Teams are largely collaborative and there are lots of tools for self development and training. The company also offers some of the best benefits in their country. Including health insurance, affiliation to employees association, and so much more
cons: Despite their claim to care about work life balance, there are so many workstreama and forecasting exercises, and very very little time between them. This creates a huge demand on your time, which means you may end up working 12 hours a day on average during peak periods.

advice: Be smarter. Get some knowledge.
pros: Interesting job, good strong process in place. Nice people. Citi  foster a culture in which the best people want to work, where people are promoted on their merits, where we value and demand respect for others, and where opportunities to develop are widely available to all. Considerable management  Flexible Work is a business strategy that enables employees and managers to consider different ways for how, where, and when work is accomplished.Citi enhances its ability to provide employees with the highest technical and professional development training programs available. Classroom training, self-paced learning, accelerated learning paths, and multimedia delivery options are just a few of the learning channels that await anyone with the desire to learn and advance his or her career.
cons: Bureaucracy could prevail sometimes over the real thinking. Inconsistent management decisions would be implemented as the result.

summary: Not the best place to be now.
advice: Pay the managers (all levels) that have worked their way up the same as someone coming into the company as a manager
pros: Good company, easy to stay for a long time with the company, decent benefits package (at least up to this year, now it costs much more than in the past), still a good amount of time off
cons: Don't plan on getting any advancement or moving to other departments.  Also, if you do manage to work your way up the food chain, you will be paid much less than the new hire doing the same job that is alwasy asking you for help. The rules keep changing, restrictions are making the job more difficult.  Policies keep changing.  Pay is low, difficult to get a bonus, call quality scoring is a joke and almost impossible to pass.

summary: I hear that back in the 80's Citigroup was a great place to work
advice: Actually speak to the people who work in the branches - hear what their ideas are, since they are the frontline.  They are the ones who hear about the positive and negative changes directly from the customers.
pros:
As an officer, received 4wks vacation.
Was able to obtain my series 7, 63, and life and health licenses while there, and Citib payed for the classes.
cons:
The "C" in Citibank stands for change. Ask anyone who has worked at Citib and they will agree.  Just as there is an understanding of what needs to be accomplished, along comes another Sr manager trying to make his/her mark, instituting an entirely different marketing idea; and not necessarily a better one. 

I worked at Citib for 13 yrs, in numerous postitions, and it was a pressure cooker.

summary: Don't expect any promotions within the Amherst/Getzville Offile
advice: Listen to employees and provide some sort of structure.  Make management training mandatory for people in management roles because management skills are lacking withing the workforce.
pros: Great building, amenities, work-life balance (in some departments), large area for parking, great cafeteria and gym.
cons: For the finance group, everybody ultimately rolls up to senior management in New York City.  They rarely promote people in Buffalo and when they do, it is only in title and not salary in many situations.  There is no way to work on career advancement within this office other than being networked into one higher level executive.  Company has a strong NYC bias.  Management moves people around at will without posting and interviewing for jobs.  Many positions do not have formal job descriptions.

summary: great place to work, great people, but lots of systemic flaws.
advice: get into the details...yes, it´s messy and overwhelming...but it´s where the battles are fought.
pros: good values, will things to get done, great school, good intentions...this place is so big that you can bet your lastdollar, that someone, somewhere, has already done what you are trying to do.
cons: conflicting objectives sometimes, separation of authority and responsibility, broad spreading of responsibility (causes things to fall through the cracks, and the "I thought you were doing it" situation), too many objectives, inward looking, earnings and revenue driven, technologically very backward, huge inefficiencies, lots of talk and little action, undisciplined business reviews, commitments are made but not followed upon...too much employee rotation at senior mgmt level leads to short-term earnings focus and lack of good long-term business building decisions...lots of flaws...but still a great place to work...inexplicable.

summary: Very nit-picky... Management is never happy...
advice: More one on ones with your teams. Less time on the phones, stop pressuring people and stop micro managing people, and they would probably stay longer. (this place is a revolving door)
pros: Great people. The environment is laid back, mostly younger people working there. The salary isn't to bad for this area. I was making $13.75 when I left. The benefits are pretty good too, you get health, dental, vision, 401k, and much more.
cons: Your boss, will never be happy. I felt like I was walking on egg shells all the time. They listen to 8-10 of your phone calls every month. When you times that by 10 - 15 people on a team, you never get time with your boss for training, or mentoring on what you can do better.

advice: Actively pursue department transfer opportunities for good employees like me
pros: This company values its employees and does its best to make working there a pleasant experience.  All managers i was in contact with were both professional and caring.  You also have many opportunities for transfers and promotions. Great benefits and low employee costs for those benefits. Pay rates are very competitive.
cons: I worked as a customer service rep and received recognition for my ability to handle callers and solve their problems. But all phone jobs have time requirements, and i was never able to meet those time requirements.  I finally left when i was overcome by stress.  The company gave me plenty of time to improve my times but, probably due to my ADD diagnosis, i was never able to meet their requirements.

summary: Great Company to work for in the past
advice: Reminder to senior management  that when your staff is happy, your customers will be happy and if managed properly your should have double digit revenue growth.
pros:
Good salary and benefits including time off! 
Opportunity for personal growth and advancement! 
Most employees are professional, conscientious, hard working and results oriented when properly trained and coached by their  managers.
cons:
In the past the company was one of being known  for taking care of their employees and  customers all while growing their business and bottom line.

Over the past several years they changed many of their senior management team who are all trying to reinvent the wheel. Many layoffs causing remaining staff to be overworked with unrealistic goals.

The staff does not tell management their feelings  for fear of being managed out.
High staff turnover in the branches causing customer dissatisfaction.

summary: Decent environment  in the investment bank,  but a lot of dead wood
advice:
shake up the senior management in the investment bank. 
 focus less on  single year pnl  for comp.  Traders greatest specialty is tweaking their books.
 do a better job in determining what a certain seat should generate.  Too many untalented  people in seats where it is easy to do well
pros:
good benefits ( health care options, 401k  match, etc)
great global reach.  citi has a footprint in nearly every country.
 relatively stable compared to other investment banks
cons: a lot of senior management comes from the Salomon/CitiCorp  days,  and are very far behind the times.  Many wind up being simply cheerleaders or,  worse,  simply bad managers.  Unfortunately,  being on great terms with these dinosaurs is key for moving up

advice: Keep your employees and clients happy, the rest will happen.... Sure, it is indeed difficult to balance the desires of employees, customers and shareholders, but this is the key to success in the long run.
pros:
Global presence gives you global mobility opportunity, exposure and a wealth of knowledge. If you are patient, consistent and willing to pull your weight, you have a great opportunity to succeed.
Citi has many great training resources, which include online and in-class alternatives. These are frequently updated and are available to complete at your own time and pace.
You will meet and learn from a greatly diverse base of professionals that will undoubtly develop you personally and professionally.
cons: Huge companies sometimes have limitations - bureaucracy, lengthy decision making, decisions that sometimes seem unfair. Also sometimes feels as decisions are purely driven by desire to please shareholder instead of client and/or employee satisfaction.

summary: Experience in IT very good the first 10 years but over the past 5+ years, morale & environment have gone off a cliff.
pros: Opportunities to advance and learn were great.  Remote work option was encouraged from upper management on down (within IT areas not requiring a physical presence).   Benefits and time off policies are pretty standard for the industry.  Most people work well together (even across disciplines) to get the job done.
cons: Recent management changes placed focus on reigning expenses, with an increased focus on personnel (versus productivity, automation, etc.).  This has contributed to low morale within IT areas.  Company is focused on moving IT staff to lower cost locations (midwest and overseas) and/or outsourcing certain support tiers.  IT management power structure has shifted overseas.  Trust within regional teams has become a major issue between staff and IT upper management .

summary: Big Company with typical complexity, but doing good things!
advice: Remember to treat all with respect, even if they aren't at your senior level.  Keep an open mind and realize not all employees will be "stars".  Be more receptive to criticism.  Involving impacted teams in decisions/process changes will go a long way toward making positive strides.
pros: Good health benefits - Vision coverage always gets positive comments from the various optometrist I have used.
cons:
As with any big company, with whom you work will dictate your experience.  I'm blessed with a good boss, but some higher-ups are a bit more closed-off to suggestions and may not be as in-touch with lower level employees as they could be.
Always too busy to take desired training for growth.

summary: Good people to work with but poor upper management that doesn't care about employees.
advice: Try to manage your work centers across the country better. Keep certain centers you've opened specific to a job function and stop opening other centers to do the same job knowing that at some point this will cause one center to be closed and thousands of people will get let go as a result.
pros: Enjoyed the festive decorations and atmosphere for holidays and various events throughout the year. Even If you did not feel like going to work that day walking through the front door and hall can lighten and cheer up your mood which is always a good way to start your day.
cons: Too many changes made not enough focus on longevity, just looking for the quick short sighted gain at the expense of employees with little or no care from upper management.

summary: great place to work and grow
advice: parking can be better at citi, the AML department is constantly changing procedures and sometimes can be confusing and seem disorganized. My manager was amazing. I learned many valuable life and work lessons through her and can't thank her enough
pros: great place to work everyone is very helpful and proffessional and there are alot of opportunities for career growth Great management. Intelligent coworkers. Interesting Work. Allows multiple Work-from-home days per week. My schedule has always been flexible since ive been working here.
cons: parking can be better at citi, there is a high turnover of employees to toher banks for better pay. they start almost every employee as a contractor at first so when you do get hired your eligibilty to be promoted does not incoroparte the time you spent as a contractor. May be losing work from home days soon.

In all my years in banking (10+ years) Citi sets the branch level employees up to fail as no other institution I have ever known. I would not recommend this employer to anyone.

pros:
1. Good pay
2. Good enviroment
3. Okay colleagues
4. Interesting tasks
5. Presitigious brand
cons: The biggest negative was management. This inevitalby has to do with the size of the company, the lack of manpower in a lot of cases, and in lieu of manpower, investment in automation is also missing despite promises of support. advice: Care for your employees; they are your lifeblood.  Centralize the firm to get rid of the fiefdom mentality that is so prevalent.
pros: Institutional structure; generally friendly people; plenty of support if you know how to find it or can get it; room to network with others in this behemoth of a company.
cons: You're immediately thrown into the fire.  There is no process surrounding training and your supervisors are generally too busy to care about you.  It's sink or swim and sinking is generally quick to occur.  Politics is very much the game and if you don't play, leave.  Email "requests" are essentially ways for a party to delegate their assignment away.  All in all, a very stifling institution.
