summary: Citi has a good culture but be aware of layoffs
advice: Stop sending US jobs overseas.
pros: Citi has a good culture in that they care about employees. They took great care during Covid to follow the science and make decisions that kept employees safe. I was able to work from home for over a year and definitely felt that Citi cared about my well-being.
cons: I worked in IT and every year there would be big layoffs. Mostly US jobs in order to outsource to India. This caused a lot of anxiety since I never knew if I would be laid off. Also, this caused time zone issues since we could only have meetings with our Indian counterpoints in the morning. Not an efficient way to manage a project when you're so limited on collaboration time.

summary: Tough skin needed to work at Citibank
advice: The "Citi" entity is too large to manage.  Basic support such as IT is completely frustrating.
pros: The bank offers tremendous advancement potential if you are willing to move to New York.  There are also other divisions that an individual can transfer to.  The bank's brand is extremely strong.  Compensation both monetary and through other benefits is very very competitive.  this is evidenced through the longevity of many of its employees.
cons: Citibank has a reputation for being a "big business" bank and not caring to service smaller clients.  In my experience this is true.  Also, the bank is huge and support for the individual is almost non existent.  One must be completely self sufficient to survive there.  Lower level managers are not that great in my experience.

summary: Know what you are getting into before you work at Citi
advice: Get it together.  They should divide the company into small parts because it is too big to manage effectively.
pros: It was a tough time to look for an internship so I accepted the offer because it was the only one I had.  However, one benefit of working for Citi is that it is a household name and people know it.

cons: It is easy to get lost in the shuffle.  Here, the size plays to the company's detriment.    One could easily feel like a cog in the machine, dehumanizing one's belief in one's self worth.  There also isn't much corporate sense of loyalty.  This is probably pretty true of most large corporations, but consequently, it leads to less loyalty among the employees as well.

pros: Large upside potential if you are willing to put in the work. If you can contribute to the team in a unique way, you can be given the flexibility to adjust your job description and directly report to more senior people which equals more visibility and responsibility. The pay was great, too. Analysts, associates, and directors really work very well together, but this is definitely a case-specific, team dependent assessment.
cons: Great performers are rewarded with the highest bonuses, but they won't promote ahead of schedule. An astute employee knows the latter is much more rewarding because (1) your financial earnings power over the long term will be much greater and (2) titles still matter and should reflect the level of responsibility. The hours are long but you have a good amount of flexibility over your daily schedule.

summary: Great company to see many sides of the business and gain exposure
advice: Too many people leading.  More defined leadership roles vs reporting to 3 different managers.
pros: Huge company with ability to move around if live in major city.  Many different departments if looking to try different positions.  Great benefits package.  Developing relationships with other deparments will help moving up the job ladder.  Bonuses have been good the last couple years.  We will see how they are this year though as most probably will not be very good.
cons: Firm is very large.  Company has been beat up in the media.  Tough to get ideas implemented.  This company is Corporate America.  Senior Management has made bad decisions in handling assets of company and we are now in the news nearly everyday in a bad way.  Annual Salary increases have been pretty low the last couple years.

summary: Benefits are good. But you pay for it in kind. Long hours, very bureacratic.
advice: Consider Telecommuting and flex time arrangement for better work life balance which will inturn boost morale, confidence and loyalty in the company and management and help with retention.
pros: Compensation is good. Both Pay and bonuses are higher than market averages. Benefits are excellent - 3 weeks vacation to start with for non officer level exempt employes. Maternity Leave benefits are very good. 100% paid leave for 12 weeks after 1 year of service for exempt employees.
cons: Long hours. Unofficial expectation of over 9-10 hrs per day for middle office type roles. No room for work life balance. Telecommuting and flex work arrangements are not encouraged. No concessions made for Special circumstances or temporary personal life situations. Also difficult to move up unless you are 'in' with the right decision making crowd.

advice: Please provide good education on financial planning and products.
pros: I've been with Smith Barney for less than a year now as a Financial Advisor Associate, Smith Barney has a good reputation, technology, and talented employees within the wealth management industry.
cons: The firm only care about how much assets you bring in as a financial advisor. Therefore, the firm train you well on how to prospect relentlessly but you have to basically self-learn about products, how to use technology, and how to do administrative paperworks. You are really independent from day one, and it is quite overwhelming. I was so disappointed by the firm's lack of support in terms of product or financial planning education for new FAAs. You have to bring in about a million dollar a month to be a very successful FA and it is very very difficult unless you have rich family background or established book of business.

advice: At some point, you have to realize that you've cleared out your "dead wood" and that you're now managing out and/or laying off people who are talented and have a lot to offer the company. Rather than assume someone should be let go because they've been there forever, try to see if they can work with new technology or new people.
pros: Great work-life balance. Lots of career-oriented, smart people to work with. Terrific benefits package.
cons: Compensation was far below industry standards and what my peers were making. Promoted twice with any increase in salary. Career mobility options are more limited than they should be for a company of this size, due in part to frequent purges of talent and downsizing. Moving between business areas is almost impossible due to "good ol boy" mentality. Absurdly slow to embrace new technology.

summary: Great place to build a career
advice: Keeping the employees engaged can be a tough task if the work isn't there. Find tasks/opportunities to constantly push employees to the max. I've been lucky, I've had 3-4 managers over my time here and all of them have been great.
pros:
Huge company name located in Buffalo
Many different back/middle office positions here.
Pay is pretty strong for the area. Good benefits. 401k matches 6%.
Work/life balance is good
Lots of paid time off
Ability to work remotely
Co-workers are typically pretty relaxed, low pressure
Pretty good promoting within
On site fitness center
cons:
Can be a little bit boring/slow at times
Can be a little bit overwhelming/fast at times
Front office/product/sales types from NYC/London seems to look down on you. Not everyone, but some of the cranky NYC people do
After getting used to a role, the challenges become less and less
It's a very, very large global company. At times you're just another cog in the wheel.

cons: Everything else you can literally think about on a workplace aspect. Seriously. This company does not follow what it preaches. advice: Interesting your stock price and dividends have finally gone up past years, yet you chop employees who have spent decades working hard for you.  You won't keep good talent for long if you keep this up, folks like a certain amount of job security.
pros: Good health and dental benefits, generous PTO policy.  Management pretty hands off and doesn't make you work OT.  Good support for policy questions, co workers friendly and supportive for the most part.
cons: Layoffs are always in play at Citi, so go in knowing at some point your likely to be dispensed. I've seen employees with 10, 20 or more years been chopped over the past several years.  The office environment is pretty lame, but can be better depending on what manager and group you work with.  May or might not get raises every year so don't be shocked if you don't get one.

summary: A great company to complete a career
advice: The only advice that I would note would be to train the Supervisors to be able to perform the same duties as the agents so that they are able to assist more effectively when an agent has some issues with their system or policies and procdures.
pros: Citi Mortgage was a good company to work considering the employee benefits and appreciation.  If employee performance was good, the company would reward the good performance with bonuses.  An employee appreciation activity was held every 6 months. This company always kept employees up to date on training and laws that affected mortgage lending and servicing as well.
cons: The company continually experienced computer issues resulting in excessive amount of down time.  Also, some of the leadership took advantage of their positions and did not assist the employees as needed.

summary: Worked on a business analyst project for the Market Data groups here.
advice: Adjust size of teams for best operating efficiency. Bring in more multi-disciplinary elements to the personnel pools. Technology support here was good: IT was efficient and the right tools were always available for completing the job; if not, they were requisitioned easily.
pros: Smart, friendly, and well-adjusted people. People willing to help whether you're part of their team/project or not. Relatively agile for a large company, good office location and amenities.
cons: Scope of projects I was given were relatively narrow. Typical problems of working in a large organization:  Lots of hoops to jump through to get management or HR/payroll/finance approval for any changes to project parameters or to do simple things like get various approval papers signed for things such as personal trading declarations. The processes for these types of things did go pretty quickly considering the steps involved.

summary: Poor diversity and poor compensation package
advice: A company that lacks diversity will never succeed in the long run. Please hire people based on his/her merits or qualifications, and not based on gender and race.
pros:
- Incredible global presence
- Great health and insurance package, flexi credits and annual leaves are amongst the best in the industry
- Work life balance can be easily achieved, though it depends on your team
cons:
- Compensation package is the lowest within the bulge bracket banks, and in fact local banks have higher annual package after bonuses
- Minimal and pathetic bonuses
- Poor cultural diversity and you will find yourself being the only Singaporean working in the bank here in Singapore
- Higher management are all Indian nationals here, and they tend to promote and hire employees based on connections and gender
- Occasionally, they speak their own languages especially in smaller group chats/Zoom calls
- Employees who stay in the bank for many years are the ones who have been stuck in the same position/role and have nowhere to go

cons:
2022 update: Bonuses are almost non existent from AVP to VP, expect about 2-3% of base salary. SVP's are around 10-14% . It will take a long time to 'get paid' so take this into consideration when accepting a job .

Promotions above a VP are very rare and take a min of two years in a role to even be considered.

advice: Management appears unwilling or unable to have a buffer to anticipate additional workload.  There needs to be a way to have additional staff "trained up" and ready to bring on board so that there is not several months of impossible deadlines before help arrives.
pros: Great People and an enjoyable, fairly relaxed atmosphere on any given day --  (when the "cons" aren't working against you".  The work is interesting and challenging.
cons: Unpredictable workload  resulting in existing staff having to "power through" any heavy months of activity.  The idea of an 8 hour day doesn't exist the last two weeks of any month... just too much to do and not enough time to do it.  This "maximizing efficiency" approach can start to feel like your full time salaried position is a definite disadvantage, resulting in earning less and less per hour.

advice: Revise sales goals to non-unreachable levels.  Bankers have many tasks to do including processing applications with multiple regulatory requirements, servicing loan applications, due diligence, marketing, in addition to operational activities.  By creating a conflict of interest with aggressive sales goals, employees are pressured to meeting the sales goals at all costs or to do their best and be reprimanded.
pros: Overtime eligible, standard benefits, average pay for outside hires
cons:
Unfriendly culture at the retail level.  Managers show favoritism to specific employees, letting them get away with things that could be grounds for termination for others.

Nearly impossible sales goals leads to employees pursing aggressive tactics or risk being reprimanded.  Fellow employees especially bankers do not help each other out and steal clients because of the cutthroat sales goals.  

No friendly or team oriented environment, managers and co-workers treat the job as a paycheck and would not enjoy staying one minute longer then required.

advice: Need to focus on good employees and work on keeping talent in house and reward the employees rather than sponsor new bikes for others to use or some other sponsorship.

Regardless of the good job that is being done, they position is moved and the quality of service and work is quickly deteriorates but at the emd of the day it is a save since itsw cheaper wages.  You get what you pay for.

summary: Good place to start a career in banking and finance.
advice: Just do the right thing. For the longest time Citi has been a brand name that many respected and were proud of...keep it that way.
pros: Most of the managers I have met have been very approachable and more than willing to share words of wisdom. Excellent training and mentoring program. Decent opportunities for career advancement.  The work atmosphere is really nice and the company makes the effort in taking care of their employees. Compensation and benefits are on par with most other banks.
cons: As in many places there is always the usual office politics going on that can affect the way the team functions as a whole. You'll encounter a number of fellow employees who are only willing to look out for themselves and will shamelessly do whatever it takes to move up the ladder.

summary: Too many layers lead to bureaucracy. Lack of accountability. Leading to failed professional performance. Bad medical.
advice: If you need to hire people - then hire more people. People's workloads are already spread extremely thin across multiple endeavors.
pros: I work in Information Security, the leadership is excellent. They listen to their people and try their best to make everything as good as possible. This organization is filled with so many talented and bright individuals. Lots of internal opportunities.
cons: Too many layers, too much bureaucracy. Leading to failed professional performance. No budget for external training. Citi's participation in medical benefits is abysmal compared to other organizations. Compare your current organization's cost to how uch Citi is contributing towards the medical plan. If you have a family, the medical insurance will practically eat 25 to 30% of your paycheck. Yes, they give you so much vacation time - good luck in trying to spend it, the workload is insane here.

pros: They will pay you just enough to not insult you for your efforts.  They are generous with "thank yous" and other forms of non-monetary encouragement/praise.

Promotions are given purely on political grounds and being great at what you do counts for very little. They expect you to keep up with hundreds of different procedures-- and they change them daily. You don't have time to blink during your work day, and they expect you to keep up with all the changes. This place is just a freakin' joke.....Plain and simple.  Don't waste your time!

advice: Tear it apart and build it again brick by brick. The only thing keeping Citi retail banks in business is client negligence/Citi double cash card. Pour money into the online services you provide. Revamp the KYC unit so it is more comprehensive. Fix the attitude of not wanting to help anyone. Listen to employees opinions. Restore or improve the commission structure.
pros:
Management to a certain extent
Occasional events that are fun but far and few between
cons: Systems are TERRIBLE, career mobility is nonexistent unless you want to be a branch manager which is a terrible job, Citi in general has nothing to offer its clients or its employees, upper management ignores glaring problems, KYC unit cripples business, general attitude is to not help anyone whether it’s an employee or customer, new issues literally every day, pay is below average

advice: Make "The Peter Principle" required reading for all people managers. Foster greater trust and respect of your employees from your management. Curb your hubris!
pros: Competitive pay. Learning opportunities. I had a good starting salary, but few raises over the years, and no bonuses for my last 5 years (even though I was consistently rated an exemplary employee). They paid for me to get a good deal of ITIL training, and once I left Operations, I did have opportunity for growth and expansion.
cons: Politics, Lack of concern for employees. In my 11+ years of constant power-shifts and routine layoffs with Citi, I never felt secure in my job. Through many years of mergers and acquisitions, a culture of fiefdoms developed, which stifled real progress, innovation, and reasonable business management. While pinching pennies on business critical initiatives, they routinely wasted millions on the absurd pet projects of executive "leaders".

summary: Don't do it if you want to work in a stable environment. Find your opportunities elsewhere.
advice: No advice for management because the bad things are ingrained in the culture of this company and all large banks in general.
pros: Good initial pay. Diversity programs throughout the company seems very good. Cafe, gym and medical services onsite.
cons: Too much red tape on everything. Very political environment so very few people will go out of their way to help you. Some teams do not care to do the right thing, they only care about the procedures even if it is obviously wrong and can be changed with a little effort. Employees never know what is coming down the pipe until it it implemented. Employees are constantly talking about how they are always nervous about their jobs. Benefits are nowhere close to where they should be for a company this size . Employees in some areas are expected to work hours that are not human with no sort of comp time. Employees complain about little or no raises or bonuses for years except for management. Parking can be a real challenge.

advice:
Improve internal process (HR, IT), things gets done at a snail pace. 
Too much redundant work.
Reduce headcount and increase compensation, people will feel happier, valued and motivated to stay/produce more high quality work.
Exhibit a good example as a leader in what you preach in the company.
pros: Great benefits, friendly colleagues, less micromanaging and understanding manager
cons:
Career opportunity limited to within the department, very slow processes (approvals etc.)

Outsource most resources (brand it as being global), makes it difficult to get assistance.

Lots of redundant and repetitive tasks. 

Bad onboarding experience, "training" done via slides with almost zero interaction, actual work does not reflect what the materials cover.

Never a month without facing IT issues.

Very high turnover for a reason, people are easily replaced, very few people stayed for more than 2 years.

Only stay if it's for your resume or you've no other choice.

summary: Great place to work...if you know how to work it...
pros: Relatively new to banking, but have been here nearly 3 years.  Overall great experience.  If you are motivated and willing to step up, you will get noticed and rewarded.  If you're looking to fly below the radar, this probably is not the place because people form opinions rather quickly and you can get stuck.  But if you're willing to get out of your comfort zone and try new challenges, you will really stretch yourself, learn a ton, and be well compensated.
cons: Not really a negative, but Citi is so large you are responsible for your career.  You need to network and form relationships to move your career forward - no one will do it for you.

summary: A great place to work with! Everyone is represented!
advice: Review employee benefits on medical insurance plan
pros:
Citi PH is a great company. A very established brand in the Philippines. Focuses on diversity and inclusion and has made sure that this is measured by the diversed candidate slate and interviewers. The company also promotes internal mobility. This allows employees to move around, discover new roles within the organization - good way to keep the employees from leaving. 
Has a very nice office location
I would say salary is competitive especially for fresh graduates
cons:
Whilst the bank offers a highly competitive salary, and has shown that it could also adjust to the changing times where focus is on ensuring everyone is well represented, benefits should be reviewed. 
Medical insurance should be extended to parents especially if the employee is single. This would attract more people to join

summary: If your not on phones you may have a better experience
advice: Get better working computer programs so that you can meet the monthly goals and get bonus. Or lower the ridiculous high dollar amounts on the goals. Also allow for phone calls to be complete before you try to ask what went wrong on a call 2 days ago. Translation 300 calls ago.
pros: People and atmosphere was great.  Managers were very knowledgeable about the processes. Also very diverse company.
cons: Collections expectations were too high and systems were not working properly half the time to be able to take a payment much less collect. We were deducted our unplanned time for being late from lunches and breaks even one minute. On top of phones had to adjust your time card or the whole team would be dragged down with percentages. And you were discouraged from getting off the phones to use the bathroom.

advice: Promote growth and take the career aspiration of full time employees seriously. Offshoring looks cheap but in the long run the company ends up paying money for production support due to the code quality and the overal product developed. Good trchnologists won't stay long in such environment. Cut down the bureaucracy setup.
pros: Great work life balance, 401k and healthcare plans. Some good managers who are really good leaders and promote growth, but  category of leaders  is very less as compared to number of managers in Citi.
cons: Offshore and consultant centric environment, promotions and full time conversions  are based on relations, too many SVPs, VPs with no behavioral skills. Less opportunity if you are a tech savvy and a full time employee because all development and design related work is done by offshore.  Working model is not different that any overseas consulting firm with onsite-offshore setup

advice: Hire an operations manager who actually knows operations so we dont have to teach them everything from square one. And managers have to set an example not come in late and make fun of their staff. Need to hire professionals not friends.
pros: Great company goals, great products as well as incentive plan. The training is amazing with great motivating staff.
cons: I had terrible management and i saw a lot of unhappy employees and people who did a lot of unethical selling just to get points and make money. But upper management pushed for more sales so how do you make them if no client really has a need? You force them to get a credit card even though they dont need one. You open more accounts even though they dont need them. Its not ethical banking.

advice: Talent is not rewarded in this organization, favoritism is. Internal rewards initiatives should not have repeat winners for sitewide awards, senior leadership should be expected to manage staff up and cultivate talent. Lack of controls around process and procedures in many businesses in the organization. Lack of continuity in practices throughout the organization.
pros: This company provides flexibility in many ways, allows people to move to different positions and learn new things. Benefits are good. Company does giveaway contests and nomination contests. Remote or work from home positions in upper level positions and some customer service roles.
cons: Manager deliverables are unrealistic leaving no time for people management. Process knowledge does not equal leadership skills when promoting people into management positions. Internal promotions offer little to no salary increases. Reactionary vs proactive throughout departments.

advice:
Really need to unite as one bank and not just talk about it. It would be amazing if each department was reachable and would be even more amazing if employees knew what they are doing. You need to put better training systems - go back to real people training. No one is listening to brain sharks. 
Also, stop taking away "positions" - it turns in more hostile environment because then everyone becomes more overworked without any reward and their original functions become secondary.
pros: Benefits, Brand, good place to bank in, not so much to work in. If you have a good team or make a good team out of the one you have, you can have a positive workplace
cons:
Lack of life work balance, 
Do most of the work that's not part of the job description that doesn't pay.

advice: Redo the entire search system used to locate how to handle certain situations its useless unless you know the exact word for word to type in to find the information that might not even help you.
pros:
Pay was good, additional earnings if you worked 2nd shift. Commission 
Great support from everyone at the start during the training period.
cons:
The job is very stressful. You are always monitored, you are working with a system that is almost impossible to navigate. After the training period its impossible to find reliable help from others to assist you when you don't know how to do something. 
If you can deal with not being able to help most of the people you talk to while they get mad that you can't help them then this is the place for you.

summary: Unethical Hiring Practices across the company
advice:
HR department watches while senior managers run the show. Work visa abuse, race based hiring are extremely rampant,  If you are white and a recent graduate forget about applying jobs on  CITI website, they do not even care to look at your resume. If you are a friend or relative of managers you will be hired in no time. some departments are filled with Asians. 

I have personally taken this issue to US Equal employment opportunity commission. All they need is more people  to report. They can seriously investigate if there are enough complaints.
pros: Work Life balance, benefits, vacation time, flexible work hours.
cons: Rampant Nepotism while hiring, Unethical hiring practices, HR department is a total joke, recognition and promotions only to certain races, work visas for friends and relatives only.

advice: Allow more opportunities to grow with in and acknowledge great work when due. Team build more with your areas.
pros: I love Citibank and everything they have to offer. They treat their employees well with great benefits. I learned a lot in my time there and started as a teller and became a banker after 2 years (I could have moved up before that, but chose not to). Paid vacations and federal holidays, 6% 401K matching, and maternity/paternity leave. Get both monthly commission and quarterly bonus.
cons: Compensation changed yearly and sometimes quarterly, for the worse never seems like for the better. Commissions and bonuses seem harder to get as time passes. Hard to move up after Banker, not many other avenues to go because the corporate offices are hard to get into if you have little experience.

summary: Great company to work for with lots of growth opportunities!
advice: Less favoritism and more equal opportunities. I myself have not been a victim but have witnessed it with other employees numerous times.
pros:
•Many opportunities to move up within the company.
•Great management 
•Overall positive work environment
•Team environment
•Lots of time off and excellent benefits
cons:
•Can be stressful if on the phones full time, dealing with angry customers.
•Can sometimes feel like a high-school type of environment with favoritism 
•Started out at $12 an hour plus shift differential and received a raise yearly afterwards, however, when the company raised their minimum pay to $15 my pay rate was not raised to match what I should be receiving. Making the same amount as brand new employees is very discouraging after working so hard to be rewarded with raises each year.

advice: Joined as a recent college graduate in 2011 and spent ~6 years (1 as teller and 5 as banker) Don't disregard the potential of those in field they can bring a lot to the table given first  hand experience and education from marketing to operational effectiveness.
pros: Great job if you seek one to one interaction with clients and find value in providing clients with the solutions to best meet their needs. Exposure to varying communities even within your market if open to covering at other branches. Great colleagues still to this connect with. As opposed to salary benefits were great.
cons: Career progression limited to retail bank division. Had to seek external opportunities given that banking experience for 5+ and a bachelor's degree couldn't suffice for roles outside retail division. After job reviews salary increase limited to cents.

advice: The way to fight racism and sexism (real issues) is not to forcefully fill in positions with minorities/women regardless of their actual skills. Build equal chances for them in the workplace instead of simply ignoring white male candidates even if they're obviusly the best. "if you can't find a person of colour for the position i'll send you someone from India" - actual feedback given by a senior manager from India after stating that that due to the social structure in Poland a vast majority of candidates are white males .... the same manager stated during the same conversation that hiring a white male is not an option... THATS REVERSE RACISM AND SEXISM, it's strongarming the problem the other way, not fixing it.
pros: Stability is the only one i see
cons: other then stability pretty much eevrything

summary: Citi is a frustrating place to work!
advice: Citi has so much constant change that operations are faltering.  A person or team doesn't even have time to change processes or systems to meet an organization changes needs before the organization is changing again.
pros: Citi is a large company with great brand recognition.  Until the recent financial melt down, I was proud to work for Citi and having Citi on my resume was a huge bonus.
cons: Citi is so large that the left hand doesn't know what the right hand is doing.  There are a lot of good things but too many bad.  Because Citi is so big, it costs a lot of money and time to fix an issue or implement a new technology.  Citi no longer has the money and we never have the time.

advice:
Start charging non customers fees to cash citibank checks especially Delaware checks. 
Make KDS better by giving 0-8 scores value instead of making everybody starve.
pros: Okay commission if you're a great salesperson. Lots of pressure at the teller line to sell products
cons:
Key driver score is a customer satisfaction survey conducted anonymously by Gallup on behalf of citibank. It's tied directly to everybody's annual bonus from teller to region manager. On a scale of 0 to 10 if the customer rated 0-8 for the interaction it counts as ZERO. 
Everybody freakin hates it. 

Also anti money laundering is big since this is a global bank. And the tellers are required to gather clients info if they did cash transactions without a debit card. That includes phone numbers occupations plies everything on your drivers license and the blood of your firstborn son

summary: A really friendly environment to work in, but not for someone who is looking for a dynamic and fast-paced role
advice: Promote a more active and collaborative culture - people often rest too much on their laurels and there are a lot of archaic processes and roadblocks that exist in the company that hampers one's ability to make an impact.
pros: Work/life balance is amazing - hovers around 50 hour work weeks at most, and everyone is very understanding if you need time off. Really nice group of people to work with and everyone is really open to help and mentor new hires.
cons: The pace of work is slow at times, there doesn't seem to be a lot of drive to results as I've seen in other companies. A symptom of the emphasis on work/life balance is that people are not as motivated - you can see if in everything from the dress code of people wearing jeans and sneakers to the pretty low salaries they offer to new hires.

advice: A lot of problems created by outsourcing. Do not believe the banks citigold clients should be passed off to outside vendors who do not seem to care about the relationship Citi is trying to build with their customers. No sense of urgency and seems to be sense of apathy toward customer service ftom dome of these offsite vendors.
pros: Friendly atmosphere. Casual work environment. Mentor programs offered. Good employee recognition programs. Management is open to ideas to improve relationships with our bank customers and most delartments try to intetact well with each other and act as allies rather than advisaries
cons: Seems to be little promotion from within. Most moves to other departments do not involve pay increases but are lateral moves even if greater responsibilties and skills required. Salaries not in line with actual responsibiltes and work done by some departments and associates.

advice: Rebuild HR and training, go back to an employee-oriented culture.  Strong employees will know how to drive value for clients, and in turn the stock price will rise.
pros: Citi is a breathtakingly diverse company in terms of its employees, its businesses, the countries where it operates, and the kinds of products and services it offers.
cons: Citi's HR, which used to be among the strongest in the industry, has been gutted in recent years, which makes it difficult to advance or even to get information about advancement or lateral moves.  Its training has become generic, and successive waves of mergers and layoffs have diluted the culture to such an extent that morale is generally very low and few if anyone there can define what the culture is.  The shareholder-driven orientation means that employees are seen as having little value.  Working here is like walking perpetually on quicksand, as you know your job is likely to end any minute.

summary: Horrible work culture and terrible leadership above the branch level.
advice: Respect your employees and look out for them. Management above the branch level is horrible, but they all look out for each other and blame everything on individual branch production without doing anything productive themselves. Stop scheduling stupid weekly or daily calls to intimidate people and actually do some work to find solutions
pros: Branch level leadership is good in most locations and all of the personal bankers and relationship managers are great to work with
cons: Everything but the listed pros. Terrible culture, intense sales pressure, intense pressure to receive perfect customer service scores which fall disproportionately on the tellers (if a client has a bad overall impression of the company or just had a bad recent experience with the company it will be captured in the teller's customer service survey, despite the fact that they may have nothing to do with it), regional level and national management is a joke; I was dumbfounded by the intelligence level and competence of people who run such a large retail bank

summary: Mixed wet mess of hair wrapped in a broken compass
advice: Keep directors and senior management in check, many abuse their power at the sacrifice of the people under.  People at the top have good directions, but everything gets messed up at director, senior management and management level.
pros: a way station to a better company
cons:
Some at director level change their minds at a whim without considering all outcomes or long term, make short term goals to fit self serving goals, career or political.  And the senior manager above them are too high up to even see the changing wind impact.  Getting access is a still a pain, years later after senior management promised change.   One could still trying to resolve access issues years in the company.  People who frequently mess up are never punished and allow to  repeat

Not only refusing to pay overtime, HR tries to cap people's salary by maintaining employees are categorized as emergency service to get around legal loop hole.

advice: It is a great disservice to exceptional employees to be unable to reassign them within Citi when a division closes. Instead of reapplying for new jobs, internal HR should find a way to place exceptional employees in new roles.
pros: Awesome employee culture of acceptance, diversity, and autonomy. Citi is a very employee oriented company that cares about you and your family. Citi provides exceptional care in all aspects of life and wellness.
cons: Even though I received the very rare ratings of 2 and then 1 consecutively, Citi was not able to retain me when my division closed. I feel this is a great disservice to its best employees to be unable to reassign. They told me to keep reapplying for new jobs, but the local recruiters did not know how awesome I was. They lost a highly exceptional employee to red tape.

summary: Horrible! Don't work for them unless you're black!
advice: Hope you all lose your jobs greedy jerks!
pros: None! Wish I could give zero stars!
cons:
Every single paycheck of mine have been messed up and docked pay, even if you contact them to fix it they'll come up with some false reason as to why you were docked pay! All the manager cares about is if they get their bonus! Racism is not a problem there since the majority who work there are black and their pay is never messed up! So if you're black, work there because you will be treated fairly! 
I had 1 call with a cust that went bad and instead of it giving me 1 strike, they said I'm on my final warning and that was my first strike, never had any problems before that with any customers! 
Every day after that final warning I have an email of "something" else I did wrong, which is nothing, the manager would just listen to my calls only and come up with a reason my call wasn't compliant!
When you call for help or call escalations they don't even want to take the call, they're so lazy it's not even funny!

summary: Great place to work and flexible.
advice: I am sure they are doing the best they can, however, I think that leadership roles needs to filled to allow the necessary roles/duties to flow down to the employees and staff.
pros: Working with the team, my team was amazing and I managed my schedule. If I had a doctor's appointment or anything that will take up a chunk of my time during the day, I can make up for it later in the evening. My team did not allow weekend work, so it was nice to be able to work standard hours. However, when we have a project and deadlines, we did anything we could to get it out the door, including working overtime.
cons: Due to the new consent order, there were new teams formed and therefore, the teams were still figuring out their cadence, which there were lots of times spent completing your CPE's and staying up to date with any new compliance regulations and updates.

pros:
-Flexible work (very considerate of work/life balance) and a lot of vacation time.
-Good benefits and opportunities for bonus and merit increases (ranking system to determine this is a bit of a political game, but it's still good money comparatively. 
-Tech org is quite wide, allowing for horizontal and internal role changes.
-Provides a lot of resources for Job Training and self-improvement courses.
-Working for a global entity with instant brand recognition. Opportunities to take part in a lot of Citi sponsored community service and outreach programs.
cons:
-Limited travel opportunities unless you're working on the latest hot item or are Sr Management. Having a Global presence makes for very early and late meeting times to accommodate.
-Senior Management is often contradictory and constantly changing across the board. Makes strategic initiatives near impossible to fully implement as intended.
-Culture has taken a hit with the constant changes in the last 5-6 years.

summary: Good benefits, flexibility, bad hours and culture
advice: Treat people as people not assets to be used.
pros: Good benefits from day 1. Great flexibility for appointments and other things that come up. Good number of vacation and holidays (32 total per year). Right now 100% work from home.
cons: They talk about work/life balance but everyone works 50 hour weeks and the work is around the clock due to having people onshore and offshore. Salary is lower than comparable positions and the annual raise (when one is given) is lower than inflation. They claim to care about their workers but when push comes to shove productivity and money come first. We’ve been working from home for 2 years and haven’t seen a dime or piece of equipment for working from home aside from the corporate laptop. Monitor, chair, even mouse have all been paid for out of pocket.

summary: Good job to get foot in the door but suspect that you would have a better experience in another bank.
advice: Take real assessments from employees to make Citi better.  Encourage openness through action, not internal marketing.  Better management and vision
pros: Salaries and benefits are good.
cons: Feel as if this is a sinking ship.  Senior management has not provided a solid vision and inspiration for employees.  Management also seems to not have the skills to lead Citi into current times.   They are more concerned about damage control from the fiscal crisis.  The structure is unwieldy and not efficiently organized with many arms not talking to each other.  The security protocols get in the way of real work at times.  Innovation and leadership are paid lip service and subjective reports are generated to propitiate senior management but the reality is that real innovation and creative thinking are often marginalized.  There is a fear among staff and employees in providing real feedback.

summary: Management team was abivalent towards new hires and offered no guidance to ensure success
advice: Have a plan for onboarding new employee's -- listen and give creedence to outgoing employee's during the exit interview!
pros: The benefits were outstanding!  22 vacation days, and 12 "personal days" which were to be taken for any given reason...that along with 10 holidays -- astronomical!! They were very concerned with VOE, the Voice of the Employee.  This was a new concept for me as I was surrounded by the mantra "VOC" Voice of the Customer and our bottom line was obviously tied to bringing in new customers and/or clientele.  The Blue Ash facility is outstanding and a real plus to the community.  I think they'll eventually make this facility the de facto Center of Excellence; but it will take time.
cons: The management team in Long Island City was horrendous about assigning responsiblities, guiding new employee's or offering constructive feedback.  I knew that I had made a mistake after just 3 weeks of accepting a job with them.

summary: Its a good job if you are willing to start at the bottom
advice: Take into consideration your talent pool and get your HR department up to speed on how to identify qualified people for positions. Education and experience should be considered and not ignored.
pros: In my position there is potential for a lot of growth if you good at your job.
cons:
They are not immune from the politics you see in American corporate culture. Is any company really immune though? 
Base pay could be a little more competitive. I took a huge pay cut to come here just to be closer to home. you would think they would have considered my MBA to be of some merit but I feel like I started from the bottom. My base pay is the same as a kid who just graduated from high school and I have been in the work force for more than 15 years.So all in all, education and experience count for nothing.

summary: Citi is Large, your happiness will depend on which group you work in.
advice: Continue to communicate to employees where we are and how we're doing.  Leverage Citi knowledge and encourage such knowledge leveraging around the
pros: For now, we're one of the few I-banks left, and we're quite committed to surviving.  Citi is a large firm with over 350,000 employees, so your happiness will depend on which group you work in.  I work across many of the businesses in a support function and find the folks here in general to be smart and helpful.
cons: I've heard that comp is usually on the low end compared to the Street.  But there's not much Street left now, so......  Compensation will vary dramatically depending on location. New York City pays in commiseration with the cost of living.  The same position in other areas will vary.

advice: More effort needs to be done to retain junior people. If not, the analyst group will continue to be a revolving door. And once the senior employees retire, there will be no experienced bodies to fill those roles.
pros: The best thing there for me was the quality of the people around me. With that said, upper management often was disconnected.  The 401k 6% match with immediate vesting was also very good. Depending on which group you're in, work life balance can be good as well.
cons: Commercial banking is in decline with relocations and outsourcing being performed. Wages also aren't going up. Even with a promotion, you won't get paid more. This isn't a Citibank problem exclusively though, the banking industry is changing. Lots of senior people continue to work there just so that they can hold on to their pension, otherwise, they would've jumped ship already.  There is no longer a pension for junior analysts, so with no retention incentives, there is high turnover.

advice: Stand by your word that when your employees are effected by a job being discontinued, that those employees get a "first look" at job opportunities. Myself and many others have applied to get back only to either get no response or not even a interview to come back.
pros: Some of the best benefits in the area as in vacation and sick time and 401K. Really enjoyed most of the people I worked with. A great number of employees were very dedicated to the company.
cons: Below ave pay, but some benefits made up for a little. Many of the promotions were based on who you know. It appears lately that they have been getting rid of tenured people only to cut costs. Many tenured effected by outsourcing of their jobs are not being hired back for other positions like promised. Citi used to celebrate their long term employees, however now dedicated employees are treated poorly and have no sense of job security like it once was.

summary: My boss didn't know what I was employed to do
advice: Get better management? I don't have a big sample size to compare with, but even in my limited experience, I can see that things are broken
pros: Great team, if you're hired into a good team. But as the managers typically do not care, a bad team rarely gets better. I loved my team though, until things go awry at a much later stage.
cons:
My boss didn't know what I was employed to do, literally. We never communicated, and I only found out when the secretary got my role wrong and insisted that it was my boss who told her.

Hence, no point talking about appraisals..or fair compensaion...or career progression... I couldn't figure what was happening..until..the secretary incident.

And when the boss makes it an all boys club, I should have known better than to have stayed and worked my ass off.

summary: Stay Away - Tough place to survive
advice: Top treating employees like disposable garbage.  Using the bell curve system for performance reviews is an outdated joke.  No one who works in NY believes the corporate propaganda of Citi being a 'meritocracy'.  Clearly, it is not.  Loyalty and years of service mean nothing to senior management.
pros: I would not recommend this company to anyone. I've been with this company 10+ years and have seen it deteriorate to the state of chaos it is still in.  Seven years after the financial crisis the work situation for employees if VERY UNSTABLE.
cons: They will work you to death, suck the life out of you and then lay you off without a second thought as they try to move as any jobs offshore or to low cost centers.  Management is ruthless and treats employees like disposable garbage.  Benefits have been slashed over the past few years and you will pay a big junk of your own medical benefits premiums.  Bonuses are awful.  They haven't even given cost of living increases to most NY staff in YEARS.  Do yourself a huge favor and look elsewhere.

advice: The company has way too many layers of management. Try to flatten the organization in order to give people a sense of ownership.
pros:
I have been with the company for less than a year and it has been the best job that I have ever had. Competitive salary, benefits, and 22 days of regular vacation time. There are also bank holidays and 6 days of unplanned time that can be used as sick days or when you just need to take off unexpectedly. 

Many opportunities to change job roles within the organization after you have been in your current position for at least 1 year and have had good performance reviews.
cons:
Huge company and it is easy to get lost in the crowd. 

The culture of meritocracy leads people to be very competitive as you are ranked against all of your peers.

summary: Working for Citibank will give you gray hairs.
advice: Fix the comp plan NOW. If you can explain to me how it is a good idea to screw employees out of their variable compensation, I'm all ears. Otherwise, get out the checkbook and PAY ME.
pros: There used to be good reasons to work for Citibank but I honestly can't think of one right now. The benefits are good I suppose. Women are granted 100% paid 13 week maternity leave. They have come up with this new comp plan called "Citimax" which is designed to pay people less. Of course, senior management sings its praises.
cons: Micromanagement, micromanagement, micromanagement. Endless firedrills, emails, stupid and ridiculous micromanaged deliverables. It's driving me insane!!!!!! I got screwed out of five grand because management RETROACTIVELY altered the comp plan. Of course, no apologies or hardly even an acknowledgement of how wrong it was.

summary: Just show up, do your job and not have high expectations of promotions or bonuses and you will be ok
advice: To get familiar with their employees and what they are doing. To get familiar with the job and what the pros and cons are about it. This needs to be done to overcome those obstacles. Do not judge when looking in and you have never been inside. Get familiar of what is going on in the inside before making a leadership decision and know how to get to where you are going before you start delegating.
pros: you get major holidays off, recieve decent benefits, work with a diverse group of people, get 5 sick days off a year
cons: Upper Management such a Operation Managers or Directors have no idea of what to do or how to answer their employee's questions. Have no leadership abilities. Very sad situation to be in when trying to accomplish a goal that is set by them when they have no idea of what the employee's job discription is or how to do their job.

summary: Avoid this employer at all costs!
advice: I hope one of your loved ones is lucky enough to work for someone like you.
pros: There are a few good managers and jobs.  Do your homework and talk to people who work there to find one of those areas and you will be fine.  They do exist but are hard to find.
cons: There is constant re-engineering to outsource jobs. All the smart people are leaving in droves. Employees hired off the street for the same job get paid more than long time employees due to salary caps for raises and promotions once you're in.  Idiots, yes men and liars do well here.  I am grateful to have found a new job and get out of there when I did. There's a lot of favoritism and unfair treatment. This is the most dysfuctional place I've worked. It was a great place to work when I started, but not any more. It is sad to see where this company is headed. I used to love my job.

advice: Grow the company smartly during the next mortgage boom. Instead of hiring hundreds of people to lay them off in a year, build a core group of skilled works, train them, and give them a pathway for advancement.
pros: Relaxed work environment, flexible work schedule, excellent 401k match, good to excellent direct management (from an interpersonal perspective), decent work/life balance
cons: You're in the mortgage business, which isn't exactly loved by most Americans these days. Mortgage industry is in a lull and the company reflects the reality of the market. Job is on the line from a quarter to quarter basis. Don't know when it's going to be your turn to get thrown to the curb. Below average pay. Non-existent training. Unlikely to move up in the company. Bureaucratic at times and co-workers can be more interested in being catty and combative instead of getting things done.

advice: U folks Need serious help with diversity issues in the US, even though you boast the largest number of countries you operate in. Anything that does not fit your pigeon holed vision for the role is not appreciated such as vision creativity and implementation in other countries. Almost impossible to upload your vision to Senior Management. It will almost never get their attention unless you are politically connected to Corporate NY.
pros: One of the best training programs, international opportunities in a very large corporate, Have to maintain a work life balance in a claws and fang environment. Huge resources that can be tapped into and great response from fellow Citi employees, culture is appreciated amongst peers.
cons: Work life balance can be a challenge in some areas. Personal growth is too. Independent thinking not necessarily appreciated. Must be a "company " man to advance.

advice: Despite Citi's size, the fate of each employee lies in their immediate manager's hands. Following a Google-esque approach where managers and their ratings are normalized across the company could help create fairer outcomes.
pros:
Citi sees some of the largest trading volumes of the industry. As such you will get access to every product and trading instrument on the market today. It's a great place to train and learn the ropes. 

To boot, if you do well, you can stay and have a successful career across citi's global footprint, changing cities, functions and rising the Wall Street foodchain.
cons:
Trading margins are shrinking and so it's getting harder and harder to get in the door. The best way is to come straight from undergrad or masters (or quantitative PhD) programs. 

Citi is a large company and so there is a fair bit of politics.

advice: Senior management were good, however lower level supervisors need to understand how to have a fair approach when managing their team and not just favor certain staff members.
pros:
Good salary
Decent benefits 
Great location
Modern building facilities
Good trainers 
Discounted food on premises
cons: If new don't request for holidays or sicks days as you wont get them unless your friends with the management. Need to be curious about some staff members as they will stick the knife in when your back is turned and just be generally nasty for no reason. All political politics so don't expect promotion soon unless your cleaning the bosses car every weekend. Workload is very high compared to most other companies and you seem to never have enough time to complete everything so guaranteed to stay at least 1.5hrs extra a day.

advice: Create and incentivize a culture of progress, hard work and collaboration. Actions speak louder than words, emails and memos from Senior Management carry no weight without a plan for implementation.
pros:
Conveniently located for buses and trains in Dublin.
I really can't think of any others, of six years here I enjoyed my first six months and my first six months after an internal move.
cons:
Complete lack of a culture - plenty of talk but almost no action. Your employees will ultimately do what you reward them to do and there are precious little
Money - six years without a pay rise (with the exception of an internal move / promotion.
Leadership - It's just non existent. Plenty of managers, but no leaders.
Training - almost non-existent, the online training portal is a jungle. I've never been set any goals or targets as it relates to training. Any courses I've taken have been off my own back having waded through the aforementioned jungle.
There are so many talented people in the organisation who have gone stale due to a lack of direction.

advice: more 1:1 mentorship for staff, provide more instructor led training with more frequency. (Get people away from their computer so they actually pay attention and do not work through the trainings) hire some motivational speakers/life coaches to brighten up the outlook of the staff. Finally, be transparent about things.
pros: You can truly build a career at Citi. In fact, you can have a wide spread career across several different operations/functions at just one site. You can learn something new everyday even when staying in one role. Huge opportunity for building a network. If you put the time and effort in , it will pay off. I like being challenged at work, so I would certainly recommend.
cons: unfavorable work life balance for many, lots of negative attitudes. high turnover, difficult to retain SMEs at the entry and intermediate level.

advice: Compensate your employees more for the very profitable work they are doing for you.
pros: Citi prides themselves in diversity which is great. They also support the community through volunteer endeavors. They pay is a little better than average as far as Call Centers go. I worked at their call center in East Tennessee. They have consistent schedules and do not do much mandatory overtime, this resulting in good Work/home life balance. The management is decent as well, some are even great. Not all of them are great, but many are. The health Insurance is amazing!
cons: The pay even though slightly better than many of the other call centers in the area, is still fairly low. The work was not fulfilling to me, it did not make me feel like I was making a difference in the world, which is important to me.

summary: Big corporate company, its better if you enter through a training program with others to be up to speed with processes
advice: Set an example to others by respecting and being nice to all levels of people around you, don't justify unreasonable workloads, and have some values that go beyond money. It is unreasonable that finance is based on the assumption that there is infinite growth when the reality is different according to all life scientists. Perhaps a change of culture to acknowledge the need for sustainable growth or de-growth is needed in these times.
pros: Nice pay, some personal growth out of conflict with senior boss
cons: Terrible work-life balance, unreasonable expectations in terms of time investment, terrible culture that promotes people to be money driven above all and no value for people or anything else. Worked in new years last minute, even though I got a raise in my salary, I was never thanked for it and instead was told that I had to react faster to checking my blackberry on holiday.

summary: Citibank was a great place to grow and become  banking ninja! you learn how to survive in any banking situation possible
advice: replace operations system to one where less mistakes can be made.
pros:
great pay
great benefits
some people are nice
cons:
no adequate training
Never leave on time
Set ridiculous sales goals
They are obsessed with HELOC apps and don't care if they close they just want the app.  Even if you reach your sales goals but don't get two HELOC apps you get in trouble.
They are obsessed with the CITI APP and if your clients don't use it you get in trouble
Once a new month starts they totally forget about everything you did last month or even yesterday. 
Forget about your two 15 min breaks you will never get them.  And you'll be lucky if you get to take your lunch on time.

advice: I have heard that some changes have taken place since I have left the company I hope they have helped. Treat everyone the way you would want to be treated, the morale is way too low and there are many ways to improve this other than a potluck here and there.
pros: Ability to build relationships with clients. Good benefits, and time off. There are some very intelligible people here. If you can get a chance to pick their brains you will find out some very valuable information that will take you far.
cons: Micro-managing at times, lack of training, overload of work from assisting other teams due to high turnover. As well as favoritism. Due to high turnover chances for advancement became a joke. Felt trapped on my team because they knew no one else wanted to fill my slot.

advice: I would like to see the future of Citibank when all you managers retire. Keep firing people, keep training them, that's how you get yourself more work. Keep the employees on the same position, see how efficient they will be. Good luck to all your favoritism management style!
pros:
-401k match? Never saw it in my 401k before I left the company, that's why with the question mark.
-commuter benefit
-health insurance within first 30 days
-easy to move up ONLY if you know people, and people is on your side
cons:
-very very very bad management.
-you don't get reward for what you do, but get reward to be favor by your manager
-you will stay on the same position forever unless you know someone
-HR is not an individual decision making on hiring, meaning not being fair, is all about what the manager demanded of  them 
-constantly changing employees, so don't be surprise if you get fire
-reduce of staff, people work for decades there, company has no concern about how you going to survive, is your problem, not their concern

summary: HR is terrible and treats us like slaves
advice:
Do a thorough investigation of pay at all levels and compensate employees accordingly. Also, whenever the compay passes CCAR, its good that you give billions back to shareholders, but employees should also get a few thousands in cash bonus each as reward for passing CCAR.

Just treat employees like human beings. Don't give bad reviews just to keep wages low. Give honest reviews and honest feedback.
pros: Name recognition, decent respect outside of the US.
cons: Low pay. Managers have to get approval to give salary increases fro HR. HR treats us like slaves. Officially Citi is all about fair pay but in reality they love underpaying folks. Very shameful considering Citi is a signatory of UN Global Compact. Double standard! I would not be surprised if managers get compensated for keeping pay low for their workers.

summary: "Bad Salaries & No good benefits in Chile"
advice: Open your eyes, give bonuses to people, don't retain the money, use that money for retain good talents...better salaries...people are not agree with Chile Citi policies, when i came to citi i thought that a big company, an international company, gives better salaries and bonuses... very disappointed, i see smaller companies, with better benefits .
pros:
Working as a team, not competitive at least in our group.
Working from home.
cons:
Under market pay
No career grow opportunities.
No Bonuses.... train people please, not CIti Courses that have no certifications!!
Have to work hard with excess of Hours are not paid, Fridays late working with no life(almost every release).
Don't retain good talent.
Compensation is not always aligned with performance.
HR, that has to help employees, only helps their interests, horrible team.
They ask you to stay late, but when you need to leave early they dont let you.

advice: Short term thinking = long term pain. Management is too concerned with the current stock price. Decisions are made on the basis of quickest return, layoffs and cutbacks are common. No one is making plans for 3-5 years forward. This company is rotting from the inside. The processes, systems and structures will be unable to support growths once the economy rebounds.
pros: Plenty of room to grow in many directions. The size of the firm allows for many possible career paths.
cons: The culture is so thick, you need a knife to cut through it. Very difficult to get things done. Politics rule the day and everyone is only interested in covering their behind. Red tape everywhere. A normal request that used to take hours 10 years ago now takes six months to complete.

advice: Change the bonus structure to be a percent of collections not a grading scale for payouts
pros: Holiday pay, vacation pay, Site closed thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas, and partial day on New Year's Eve. Very generous with time off for active service.
cons: Was promised a $200-$300 bonus based on collections. But what I came to find out is the bonus is based on averages. So the more you collect per hour the better. But what is preventing me from a bonus is my shift that has 2 hours of low call volume. Which means lower collection rates.  And to top it off if you waive late fees you lose any bonus multiplier. Also Citi 40% of the calls consist of "I never received my statement" which means either Citi did not send them, the USPS screwed up or, the customer threw it away.

summary: Smith Barney - A great place to work.
advice: Take on less risk.
pros: Opportunities to move around within the company because it is so large.  Lots of perks from deals with all sorts of vendors.  Good software in place to get things done easily.  Flip side is sometimes overly complicated compliance procedures due to wariness from 2000-02 downturn.  Guess it wasn't enough considering what is now happening.  There are some type A jerks there but that is the case at any financial firm.  Overall it is a good experience, lots of good people there.  I think they are going to have to change their model going forward just like Merrill, Morgan and the rest because they were clearly some of the biggest losers from the recent downturn.
cons: Sometimes moves too slowly due to size.

summary: Good Place to work in terms of benefits
advice: When replacing a branch manager, other candidates should be considered for the position and not just promote someone from the same branch from another position. Replacing a branch manager by unqualified person just because that person is in that branch is not the right solution.
pros: Great benefits. The company fosters work/life balance, but............ see the comments below in the Cons* section.
cons: Manangement hires you as part-time and are able to have you as full-time but  you don't get full time benefits, and they use the employees and do not value certain work/life balance situations. Certain employees at the branches  should never be promoted to be a branch manager from a Personal banker position just because they are at the same branch. In my experience, the branch manager was not even qualified to hold such a position.

advice: To pay more attention to what staff have to say, and consider everyone when promoting. Never promote someone when the interview process hasn't been completed.
pros: It is usually a stable company, but as of late it has not been so much. So, the reasons are going away fast.  There is generally a comfortable work environment, lunch room in the building and mandatory breaks and lunches, which you do not get in a lot of companies. I would say citi is a good place to work for, but I would also look in other areas.
cons: Chances for layoff, poor potential to move up. Often poor management due to the size of the company. A lot of unhappy employees due to reasons I stated above. Salary could be better and more on par with other companies.

summary: Incompetent middle management seeking to chop the tall poppies
advice:
- Value the people you "manage" (or "fail to manage effectively"), you are irrelevant without them.

- Respect the people who can actually deliver, especially if you are not one of them.
pros:
- Locations all around the world.

- A successful transaction processing business.

- A big brand name on your CV
cons:
- Incompetent middle managers whose main responsibilities seem to be to "fabricate relevance", "only pretend to add value" and "brown-nosing".

- Dirty Politics

- Tall poppies will be chopped.

- Absolutely no respect for employees & their personal time

- Startlingly low diversity, especially at the tech & ops. division. If you aren't in the "correct" ethnic group & sub group, you don't stand a chance.

- Merit has little value, only brown-nosing to be part of the right clique can get you ahead

advice:
Less politics Citi  
Learn to treat people respectfully - people literally yelled at me through the phone  "You don't know who I am ? I am ---- I have been with Citi over 20 years".
pros: Citi is large and has robust process. You will learn everything you need to know about oiling the machine. You will get to work with interns to Managing Directors.  You will get to work globally and have lots of work and learn.
cons: The company has such a high workload per person that nice people are rude because they are crushed by the volume of work. It is very corporate still and manual. There are times you need to copy the same information up to 3 times. Because of the size approving anything takes time and many people need to be involved

pros:
the team was great, very helpful, always ready to answer any questions. Our manager was very approachable with any concern regarding performance and overall feedback; supervisor teams the same way. 
Great atmosphere, great over-time pay. 
Good advancement opportunities.
cons:
Vacations needed planned in almost a year ahead. 
Any last minute emergency was not really appreciated as the call volume would increase and team performance would drop.
Culture was very lazy, people with absolutely no life goals surround you in every department and majority of co-workers felt to me as they were scared of expressing their true opinion about certain management issues and overall new rules. 
Paid maternity leave was horrible, especially if you are already pregnant when you join (had 2 girls in my team, different stages in pregnancy and each pay was worst than the other)

summary: Good place to start your career at
advice:
- Further improvement of internal communication is required,
- Salaries should not be that far apart - only 200kms between the cities and such a huge disproportion when it comes to the pay (costs of living are not that much bigger in the capital city, you know)
pros:
1) a perfect place to start your career at, right before you graduate from a university,
2) many different roles to choose from, internal mobility is supported by the managment (at least in most cases - of course there are exceptions to that :) )
cons:
1) hard working employees with very good results usually don't get enough appreciation
2) salary is basically 40-50% percent lower than in Warsaw, which is why many people are leaving the company and relocating to Warsaw (some stay at Citi, but most of them change the empolyer as well)

summary: I would recommend Citibank as an employer.
advice: More direct communication would be helpful. Especially given the current state of the company and the economy in general.
pros: Citibank really does have a very supportive, flexible work environment. The benefits and amenities at the site are really quite nice. Childcare, gym, cafeteria, break rooms, etc all make for a pleasant work environment. The direct management is a great group of people. They will go above and beyond for their employees. The training is extensive and the direct managers will do everything in their power to get advancement opportunities for you. You don't have to work there for 10 years before moving up to another department or getting a promotion. The vacation time alone makes working there worth it. I really do enjoy working for Citi!
cons: The pay scale needs to be adjusted for people that are performing more complex jobs. Based on competitor pay I think Citi is shortchanging it's front line people.

summary: My career at Citi was frustrating.
advice: It appeared to me that senior management knows the company is out of control and only cares about hanging on and cashing in until the regulators force massive changes. My advice would be to lighten up on the employees in the meantime. Why drive everyone crazy trying to do the impossible? The end is near.
pros: As a large and global company there were endless internal options for positions. Compensation levels are competitive. The office setting was always modern, and technologically advanced.
cons: Too big to manage, very political. So large that few people feel connected to success or failure. Work/balance ratio is awful. The previous pre-Sandy Weill culture was destroyed, and the new culture rewards outside relationships over performance. Employment policies that had existed for over 15 years of my career were eliminated in days, with no grandfathering in place for previous loyalty.Older employees, at the middle management or below levels are stripped of their importance and made uncomfortable in the hope they will leave.

summary: Rewarding experience but need to be flexible to adapted to senior management turnover.
advice: Citi needs to catch its breath and change from brute force cost cutting to more strategic investments in redesigning old processes and technologies as a means to gain sustainable efficiencies.
pros: Fortune 100 company with a very large global footprint.  A great number of the best and brightest individuals. Strong and stable balance sheet.  Significant financial and human capital to invest in innovative solutions.
cons: The culture tends to be passive/defense where interaction with people is guarded so that  individuals are more concerned with their own sense of job security - don't rock the boat.   The tumultuous nature of the banking industry itself reinforces this culture. Starting with the sub-prime mortgage crisis of 2008, restructuring, outsourcing and workforce reductions are common in the big banks.   At Citigroup, senior management turnover has more frequent than other banks since the 1998 Citicorp and Travelers merger.

advice: Do a better job of managing the culture...Change it from a dog eat dog environment to one that is about a little more healthy competition and teamwork.  I guarantee you will get more results from your employees and the associate turnover won't be nearly as high.
pros: Great Experience in Finance. I learned a great deal about the industry. The company is well respected in the Finance Industry.
cons: Very aggressive Culture.  Associates and managers are rewarded only on financial results, not based on how they achieved the results.  Therefore, ethics and doing the right thing are sometimes secondary actions..along with mutual respect.  It is not a surprise that they took such a hard fall during the financial crisis.  The overall business model of the company is to provide good numbers...no matter how you obtain them.

summary: I really expected more... And once I leave... I will sleep again...
advice: Please leave bureaucracy and let the people work. The people spent the half of the day explaining processes and contingencies. PLEASE leave the old school and start giving real value to the  real spirit of the company that is the PEOPLE.
pros: Lots of training's, I really had a good team, real players. A big chance to know about many areas of work.
cons: Walls ans walls of bureaucracy. You keep making reports, UAT's and many things that only make happy somebody in other country but at the end you don't understand your contribution to the Corporation and it is nobody interested in making you know it. In almost two years HR has been a "urban legend" in our country.  Everybody feels that in the last years is has been developed a culture that the bank is waiting for you to make a mistake to get fired.

summary: A great place to grow and be proud of working for.
advice: Keep communicating with employees
pros: Excellent management that cares about doing the right thing for customers and employees.  My experience with management was positive.  I was in a position to coach and influence managers and staff and I found it to be easy in most cases because of the atmosphere that management maintained.  Associated were rewarded not only with pay but with praise and recognition.
cons: Frequent change is often difficult for employees and customers.  Understanding  that the industry has been changing and the reputation of banks in general has been poor, it is still not a great idea to make as many changes as occur at Citibank.   Employees and customers are often anxious and frustrated by the changes that seem to happen on a regular basis.

advice: Update your systems! Please for our sanity!
pros: Hourly Rate is impressive and commission is definitely tangible as well as fruitful. Training was extensive and informative, Not as sales pushy as other Big Banks. Citibank paid for Gas and Hotel because we had to go up to LA. The San Diego District has a summer BBQ cookout. As far as retail banking goes it's not a bad gig.
cons: Internet and server is dreadfully slooooow. You can have a whole conversation with a customer before a webpage can load up for you. Almost everything in the system is outdated and extensive. They take the KYC account opening process to a whole new level which you have to do manually. And so much paperwork for every customer, never ending. Bankers take the role of operations and sales in the Citibank role. Where as some other banks only have you worry about the sales side.

advice: Citi's long-term success is based on the execution & capabilities of Employees.
