Large-scale outsourcing provides a quick fix to improve profitability but, it guts the organization and it sends a negative message to staff.  Invest in people, build execution capacity, and stop thinking in the short-term.
pros: If you are looking for exposure to a Global environment, Citi has a presence in many places.  There are opportunities to work with a diverse group of people.
cons:
Citi is consistently inconsistent in how it operates.  The 'get it done' culture has resulted in a patchwork of processes, systems, etc. and it limits their ability to be truly 'Global'.
Citi has downsized & outsourced its Operations & Technology, so that the few knowledgeable, experienced people left are doing the work of many.  The lack of focus & overwork is a disincentive.

summary: Citi takes care of it's people...
advice: Stop recycling old ideas with new names and marketing. Be more willing to invest in technology, to be an industry leader the homegrown tools aren't going to cut it. Figure out a way to integrate your platforms for an Omni channel real-time experience.
pros: Great benefits, paid-time off, maternity/paternity, 401K are all above average. It is a very positive and encouraging culture, employees really work to do the right thing for the client. The employees drive the culture from the bottom up and leadership supports and encourages this. There are a lot of community involvement opportunities.
cons: It is easy to become trapped in a job you don't love because the benefits and pay are hard to beat at comparable businesses. Internal growth at some sites is limited by what businesses are handled by the site. If you are willing to relocate you open yourself up to endless opportunities.

advice: Continue to look  within your ranks to address new gaps in leadership positions. It promotes ownership. Senior technology purchasing decision makers do not listen well to their senior technology staff and have frequently increased the cost to do business by choosing a less viable solution that looked cheaper on the surface.
pros: The men and women at this company work very long hours to do a good job at what they do. They have many experienced management and technical staff to help the businesses make money as efficiently and highly performing as possible.
cons: There are so many good people working here its difficult to accomplish a single task that does not impact several other tasks and goals.  If you cannot be patient and navigate the various interests involved it can be frustrating but may not lead to promotion in any case.

advice: Reward effort with money and not empty skype messages. We don't need weekly emails about masked diversity at CITI when basic principles are dishonored everyday. Train your managers and team leaders. Introduce mentorship for entry level jobs. Do something.
pros: Work from home. Medicover. Flexible.
cons: Low starting salary. Yearly pay raise around 2-4% which is extremely disappointing. Close to zero chance of getting promoted in your own position. Non-existing reward system. Everyone I know is severely unmotivated and looking for another job as an escape. Disorganization at every level. Applications that used on daily basis are horribly optimized and often unavailable, hence the work delay. Incompetent backup system. Even if you put an actual effort in your job it doesn't matter, so eventually you will not put any effort in your job. People also leave because of the heavy workload resulting much more heavy workload because of their absence, BUT there is no hiring to replace them. Surveys are completely ignored even if they are really bad (and they are really bad). You will stuck doing the same thing for years if you don't push yourself really hard.

summary: Reviews based on other departments performance
advice: Communication is poor, and many times employees have more knowledge than management. Keep in mind you may ask 3 managers the same question and get 3 different answers. You may be better off asking the employees the questions they tend to have the most knowledge and this is learned by the employees through trial error.
pros: benefits you will need them with the amount of work related stree that you will have
cons: Sales your performance will be based on others departments performance. Closings are based on processing and underwrtiting where it has been  backed up since day one and years later nothing changed.  But performance is based on your closing numbers and pull through. These are not in your control but is part of your perfomance. If you are a top producer who works off site you will to well. But if your average prepare for many poor reviews because your numbers are compared to those who do have the same working enviroment as yourself. They do hire often because most choose to leave as soon as possible. It is tough to make good money there.

summary: challenging environment - no meriticracy - lots of empire building
advice:
first, learn bankiing - maybe take a class or some training..couldn't hurt.  
it is not a mystery why "C" is a $3 stock - you have created a bloated bureacracy that is not efficient at making money or serving customer needs - you cant "market" your way out of this situation.
pros: work life balance is respected.  diversity is the norm .... salary is competitive... telecommuting is accepted....lateral job movement is encouraged... big enough to let you move around
cons: too much turn over - older employees with high salaries are shown the door and replaced with younger cheaper resources who believe they are entitled to their position.  some of senior management coomse from non-financial background and hires more non financial managers to create a culture of ignorance about banking.  Big bureaucratic environment where no one is ever responsible or accountable for anything.... many think that is a positive!!!

advice: Stop living in fear and be bold by doing the right thing. You are trying to change the culture and values and my recommendation is to live and stand by what the change is and do not revert to old and "bad" behaviors.
pros: The company is big and does hire back ex employees. They have best practices that you learn and take with you to other companies. The people are smart and I have met a few friends that I still keep in touch with.
cons: Of the 4 managers I had in 4 years 3 of them were mediocre at best. They were more interested in their own careers than helping to develop their teams. It's a political place to work in and you gotta learn "how to kill or be killed". That was a saying that one of the MD's I supported told me. And that was exactly my experience.

summary: Benefits are good, that's about it
advice: Take a management course
pros: Getting paid sick pay that you can use virtually whenever you want and however you want, getting paid vacation from the very start, health and 401K options from the beginning is also solid.  Most part timers here worked just for the benefits alone.
cons:
Having actual knowledge and skills will not be a factor in getting higher positions, if you are not part of the favorites, you have no chance of ever moving up.

HR and Ethics will do absolutely nothing in your favor, even if you have proof, it all comes down to how much they like management.

If you're someone who keeps to themselves and has zero motivation to move up, this may be the job for you.  That isn't an insult, it's meant for those who are not going to be disappointed when they find out someone who is buddy buddy with the management gets the position and you didn't.

advice: Shake up the culture, the reason the business hates the IT is because the IT executive leadership doesn't care about anything that doesn't immediately boost their resume (head count and budget).
pros: Large stable company with hefty compensation packages.  The idea of working on very large scale systems supporting mission critical financial services can be a nice challenge.
cons: Executive team had little care of real issues and focused strictly on cost per head count regardless of any other factor.  The technical teams in Dallas and St Louis had resigned to a life of not caring anymore.  The company lacked any kind of energy, with most employees readily telling you they are there to collect a check.  We saw critical system fixes delayed 9 months because no one wanted to actually do the deployment.

advice:
Talk the talk, but walk the walk as well!
Pay more attention to people 2 levels down from you, who usually know more and would be of more value to your informed decision making than their managers who manage the "politics" around when to tell you what!

Stop making people think you are a development center and duping people to join it. Instead share the actual work you do, so that people are not blinded by the package only.
Tell them that you don't believe in work-life balance and it will make future employees chose you wisely.
pros: Package, if you want it - go for it
cons:
1. They will tell you it's a development role while interviewing, while once you are inside they will give you production support
2. They will make you work in shift, while avoiding calling it shift job
3. They call it a captive and CoE, while the senior management thinks of it as a support center
4. Main work in US, only support functions are coming to India
5. Work - Life balance - Non-Existent
6. Indian HR is under the US manager. They have no voice
7. Very confused about if they are a product organization or a service organization
8. Employee satisfaction - NIL
9. Employee support - NIL
10. Employee care - NIL

pros: The organizations is large, and allows you access to a lot of facets of banking, if you look hard enough. Benefits are pretty good, and the prestige associated with the bank garners a lot of outward respect.
cons:
Company culture is inconsistent, and largely dependent on where you are in the bank. Internal mobility within the bank from one department to another seems generally discouraged or hard to come by. 

How you are treated [by the bank] differs a lot where you are. Technology based jobs within the company see a much slower and neglected environment. Bonuses are smaller, and money is tracked more carefully (100 dollars for Microsoft Visio, not happening). As opposed to client-facing positions, where bonuses might be larger, employees get more on-site benefits (such as free food after a certain time), and money flows more freely (1k USD to ship a box -- consider it done).

summary: Worst Processes with respect to HR
advice:
* Relieving letter is nothing to do with full and final. It should be handed over on the last working day of employee. 
* Exit interview is important irrespective of you consider it or not
* Don't harrese your ex-employees in the name of full and final(60 days TAT). there is no other company other than Citi that takes so long. 
* Shake your Finance and HR department which are not closing the FnF even after 60 days. They are sleeping in the organization that "Never sleeps".
pros:
It's a good company to work with respect to -
 a) Banking domain
 b) technical exposure
 c) Good working culture
cons:
Pathetic HR, facilities and finance processes
They don't want to move even a finger. They hardly even acknowledge  your mail and timely action is a luck

advice: Don't tolerate employees who back stab others. Map out pain points and fix them, to include creating processes for smoother technology changes with more robust inter-system testing. Under-resourcing teams to show expense saves is very short term and will snowball into bigger problems. Manage change.
pros: Challenging work, great resume builder. I had an excellent manager and team. Ability to work from home when necessary. Good focus on ethics.
cons: Back stabbing and snide comments are not uncommon. Long hours--to the point that my good salary was just mediocre because I was working 70 hr work weeks. Management does not recognize the changes that really need to be made to make the business efficient and effective--off-shoring may cut expenses on paper, but the technology lags and other inefficiencies will still remain and even be exasperated. Teams were under-resourced to make the books look better (6 mo + delays, with no change to workload or team productivity expectations).

summary: Declining quality of leadership/management and excessive politics
advice: Spend some time with your direct's employees and find out what their accomplishments and issues are. Listen to it first hand. You are bleeding off your talented employees.
pros: Good online and class offerings. Big company, many opportunities. High diversity
cons: Constant layoffs, high frequency of changes, no information sharing/transparency, very long work hours with no support and/or appreciation from senior management. E.g. Took a week vacation after over 8 months and every day on my vacation i had calls and texts from my colleagues/manager. Even after being on call/responding texts back at work on my vacation, I came back to work to find out all my work were messed up. I had to catch up and fix everything on my first day back to work working till midnight. Very incompetent management and senior mangers does not care anyone below VP/SVP. Good work is not communicated to senior mangers by immediate manager. Excessive politics and self interest. Full time employees are replaced by contractors.

pros:
- HR really trying to improve employee experience. Amenities being improved, ongoing free professional development classes, revamped office space.

- Culture of keeping employees within. If we lose someone in CIB, we try to find someone within the bank that can fill the role if it makes sense, good for somebody that wants to use a role at Citi as a stepping point to get somewhere else later.

- Balance sheet allows greater flexibility in winning deals
cons:
- Pays on the lower end of street, though not far from average / median

- Promote-when-ready also means you may not get promoted. Also takes an extra year to make VP versus other banks

- Poor IT systems. Spend a lot of time filling out compliance forms and dealing with IT issues from time to time

- Not willing to take too much risk on balance sheet

summary: A great firm to learn the business, but the culture needs work
advice: Focus on building a strong and happy culture.
pros: There are opportunities galore for learning and growth, but you must find the right people to sponsor that growth.  Overall, I had a great experience working there, but ultimately my career reached a plateau.
cons: If you are not from an ivy league school, your upward momentum will be stunted.  The firm is so large and highly bureaucratic, so its often difficult to get things done in a reasonable amount of time.  The culture has a mix of highly volatile people with some really great people, upper management consists of many former Lehman guys mixed with people from other firms and, as a result, there's a lot of fiefdoms and the culture has suffered as a result.

advice: Put more effort to segmentalise departments properly so that everyone is accountable. Citibank is not ready for digitalisation until a proper clean up of its processes is done.
pros:
- Used to have good commission
- Good stepping stone to banking industry
cons:
- Bankers are at the bottom of food chain. Backend departments will ask you to liase with customers as long as it is customer servicing issues. Little help will be given by most of them as they do not face clients directly.
- Alot of manual processes which are unnecessary.
- Citibank used to be considered as an 'Atas' bank many years ago due to its branding and good customer service. Nowadays, the bank is not doing a very good job in its customer service area (you can take a look at the different comments in its facebook page). Hotline can never be reach easily and bankers end up handling unnecessary complaints which they still have to route to relevant departments in charge, leading to longer turn around time to resolve disputes.

summary: Good place to start and get XP, but don't want to stay too long
advice: Take a bit of time to understand your employees and then you will know how to motivate them. Take less time on politics and spend it on actually getting work done.
pros: Citi has a great company culture, and a good work life balance.  They salary is quite good for Hungarian average, but if you are into money more then the above, you can find better.
cons: They want to believe that they are Tech company as well but they are mostly mediocre.  Management choices are entirely only for themselves not the company. Even at a low level the management is too much into politics. As an International company they want to muscle American ideals into the local employees instead of taking a bit of time to understand them and then know how to motivate them.

advice: Provide more training and coaching, and don't leave your branch managers on their own to sink or swim.
pros: Competitive pay and benefits. Generous vacation time of 4 weeks.
cons:
Terrible internal systems, company is stuck in the 80's, not allowing to help customers and have to jump through hoops to accomplish the simplest task. Unethical sales practices are visible everywhere, even though company claims to frown upon it, they structure compensation to push bankers and managers in the unethical direction, which is unacceptable. 
Company is solely number focused and do not care how you obtain them, raising the bar every year, and asking you to beat last years figures, by any means possible. Training is absolutely horrible, unorganized and completely useless. Even if you are an experienced manager, you are on your own figuring out the systems, policies etc.

advice: Revoke the no family rule. Many who got their foot in the door because they had friends or family working there are the hardest workers the company had. Knowing someone doesn't mean that you were favored or given opportunities that others weren't. In most cases, you had to prove yourself even more so that it did not reflect poorly on the person that got you the opportunity to work there.
pros: Great company to work for. Co Workers were great and very welcoming. Learned a lot working for Citi. Loved working here
cons: Came up with a no family policy and since my mother and sister worked there I was terminated because of this new rule. Many got grandfathered in but I was not able to because I was not working there long enough.

summary: CTI was a great place to work
advice: Consider the long term affects of what you're doing now, saving a dollar today should not be the bottom line.
pros: Flexible work hours.  Before the meltdown, ability to transfer between workgroups to cross-train. Most of the people I work with are great, knowledgeable and willing to share their knowledge and help each other out.  My workgroup did not cut the training budget as most others did.
cons: Morale is very low right now due to layoffs 2-3 weeks ago.  Sr. Mgmt believes 50+ hours every week is acceptable.  Due to regulatory requirements separation of duty has put every workgroup in a silo causing 1) no to very little cross training, 2) decreasing the ability to get things done in a reasonable amount of time.

pros: Great sales experience, good benefits, set schedule, good amount of time off, decent pay for a beginner in sales field.
cons: High stress atmosphere. Many people that work here have mental health breakdowns. Many of the clients are from the New York City metro area and they extremely demanding, they will scream at you, swear at you, threaten you and hang up on you several times on a daily basis. You will have to follow many metrics, most of which work against each other to bring down your sales bonuses. (I.E. They have this thing called offer rate. You have to offer sales on every call or it counts against you, while at the same time you have handle time which has to be short or it counts against you. Obviously these two things are designed to work against each other. It's a balancing act. Also many of the jobs are outsourced, as are the resources.

advice: Stability is needed.  Bring in a CEO who will stick around and make a difference.  Show some loyalty to the people who built this company!
pros: When I joined the company it was a great place to work.  We were growing and there was a lot of opportunity to advance.  We had good leadership and a good business plan that was understood at every level of the firm.  Pay was above average and co-workers were great.
cons: Everything changed during and after the mortgage crisis.  Many people were laid off and we had a revolving door of leadership and ever- changing strategies.  Company is now getting smaller, closing branches and focusing only on the affluent and lay offs are a regular occurrence.  I didn't want to wait around for it to be my turn!

advice: Hire more people to allow the team to work efficiently and have the time to work on process improvements, reporting, fix current issues
pros: Great pay, I am technically an hourly employee with a base salary and I can earn time and a half for overtime. Last year that afforded me an extra 10,000. Some jobs are very flexible with ability to work from home
cons: Team size is not as large as it should be. My current job needs about 3 more people to operate efficiently. Annual raises are distributed evenly across the floor regardless of job difficulty (this could be a good thing if you are on the “easy” teams). My opinion is that I am currently on a bad team, other teams are great working environments. My previous roles I was very satisfied with. Some employees are just there for the paycheck, not all motivated individuals

summary: Pay not competitive but environment is nice
advice: Incentive sharing!
pros:
Not as stressful as people perceived.
Working hours are highly dependent on your role. 
Mobility is really good, especially for those who wants global transition.
cons:
Pay is not the same to JP Morgan or many other banks. 
Sometime it feels like your future/pay/raise/job is dependent on how the senior view the business that year. 
When time is good, they cut cost less, and time is bad, they REALLY cut cost. 
Don't expect ridiculous bonus either.
Certain function you will see kids fresh out of college with 2 years of experience getting automatic promotion to Vice President. and at others function you see people with 7 years of work experience, from great colleges, work on much serious role, only then promote to VP. It's a big big organization, these things happen really often

advice: Take care of the ones that are always on time, make their goals, and loyal to the company and stop filling your pockets from the sweat of the little people
pros: I would like to say that there are good times working for this company! But I can’t! You’ll walk in healthy and walk back out sick.... Citibank is nothing but a sham, a shinny star looking good from the outside but darkness on the inside... I’ve made one or two good friends at the company, but that’s about it
cons: I would never encourage anyone to work for Citigroup unless you want to stay in the same position..... the management is nasty and all about themselves, it doesn’t matter how good you are they always reward the ones like, plus! If you work at a bank where there is a Spanish manager! He or she would always hire Spanish speaking people and speak they language around you even though they know it’s against company policy to do so

summary: Former Sales Assistant in PWM Division
advice: The management seems to be supportive but what I would suggest is for someone to push for a more efficient compliance process!
pros: Prestigious name brand and great learning experience.  Vikram Pandit seems to be working hard to turn the company around and if you can survive the cut off, it's a great place to learn about the markets.  The atmosphere in the Private Wealth Management division was not too cutthroat and as with most places, there are sociable people as well as the few bad apples.
cons: The culture has an "every man for himself (or every woman for herself)" mentality so if you want a collaborative atmosphere, this isn't the place to be.  As with all banks right now, they are in an unstable state so that's also something to keep in mind.

summary: If given an opportuntity to work at Citi again I would be more than happy to do so.
advice: Keep staff up to day with current events. Motivate them, appreciate them, respect them, reward them and allow them to be able to approach you to discuss any matter they may have. Happy staff ensures productivity & complete satisfaction
pros: Throughout the years I worked with an amazing group of people. Acquired knowledge and understanding of the commodities clearing process.  It was a daily challenge to learn new processes which were also beneficial in my day to day job functions.
cons: In extreme cases of data processing and heavy trading it could have been long days ensuring the job gets done. However there were always unexpected and unpredicted issues which caused management to seek resolutions to avoid next day problems.

summary: If you have habit of praising your senior management you can easily join this company and get promotion every 1.5 years
advice: Don’t do fake promises to employees. Try to retain your old staff.
pros: Salary, Different work groups, Extra curricular activities, cabs
cons: Biased Senior management, Only people with habit of praising senior management can get early promotions, management will judge your performance only on the basis of bias essentially, if you are not favourite to them, they will praise you on your face but ultimately spoil your ratings at the end of the year. Almost every senior manager has 2 faces. Managers also interfare in your personal life. No carry forward & encashment of leaves. Long working hours and no OT. Also, too much competition under senior management that if you will apply for IJP, they will not allow you to move from the organisation. No HR is active to help you out.

advice: Learn how to value your employees, especially the hard working ones that are hard to come by.
pros: Cannot think of a single one.
cons: Literally the most stingiest company I have ever had the displeasure of working for. Billion dollar company yet the low ball you in salary (they pay more than $10k less of competitors), cut overtime when pipelines are out of control just so upper management can show their managers how much they saved per quarter doing this, they don't give two craps about their borrowers and they make up absolutely ridiculous and petty guidelines in order to screw you out of a quarter bonus. Currently trying to get the hell out of here. 90% of the dept either got laid off or quit. Oh and after all these ppl quit-Citi had the audacity to go back and ask the ppl they laid off to come back. Who does that? They have posters all over the building that say "Citi, Power of One". Yeah right. Freaking JOKE.

advice:
Manage the office politics and vet folks before promoting to mid-level or managerial roles. Will be nice to have qualified next in line candidates participate in EQ and Management training before being promoted. 

Invest in remote work to expand/retain top level performers
pros:
1. Plethora of opportunities (put in the work and be rewarded especially if manager relationship is great!)
2. Continuous learning and development opportunities 
3. 1.5 to 5 percent yearly salary raises
4. Diverse to some extent 
5. Competitive benefits
cons:
1. Work life balance especially with a demanding manager
2. Some mid-level managers not qualified for their role
3. Lack of communication from mid-level to bottom
4. Pay rate below the average salary
5. Relies heavily on offshore and that can at times impede work quality or output 
6. Limitation in career advancement if not in the right group

summary: Citi - Potential for greatness, but paralyzed like a wooly mammoth stuck in a tar pit
advice: Invest more money in technology and downsize the armies of support staff. Ensure that technology staff supporting english speaking employees can actually speak english.
pros:
I believe that someday Citi will become an efficient and streamlined corporation. When this happens, Citi will truly be a benchmark company to work for. 

Citi has a footprint in every market and every product. 

As Citi restructures, there will be much opportunity to make an impact in the future of the company.
cons:
Citi is a tangled beaurocratic and technological mess. This has created a culture where employees are conditioned for process failure, inefficiency and just general complacency.

Brain Drain - many of the bank's talent has either left the firm or is making every effort to leave. 

Future compensation structure is a mystery.

summary: Overall this is a great company to work for and if given the chance I would go back
advice: Work with the actual people that will be using a tool to see if it makes sense. More open communication with the parties that decisions will be affecting.
pros:
Large corporation with a small company feel. Since the company has different divisions and they allow then to run pretty autonomous.
Great benefits package. Their benefits package is all inclusive that you do not see anymore. They have the regular stuff along with dissability, 401k with matching along with supplemental retirement. 
Willing to look at different options and ways of doing things
Employee and community concious, they provide avenues for you to support local causes with their sponsorship. Donations taken out pre-tax and company matching.
cons:
Large Corporation so they can move slow on changing to new technologies.
Decisions can be handed down without looking at the impact on actual production at a lower level.

summary: Multinational, professional, formal environment with strict procedures and lots of systems.
advice: You lose people, because your employee retention is not efficient. Your people realise that they need to leave and spend some years elsewhere and come back in order to achieve better compensation package.
pros:
- possibility for advancement
- professional growth is encouraged and supported
- clear responsibilities
- multinational, inclusive and diverse culture
- can use foreign languages in everyday work
- brand image
- not a t-shirt & sneakers environment, everyone is dressed nicely, except for Fridays
cons:
- fast-paced
- overtime is not paid
- to get a salary raise is difficult
- difficult to get in
- everything is standardized, no room for ad-hoc solutions
- there is a system for everything, you use 20+ systems (from visitor cards and login id, through travel & expense and invoices to meetingroom booking and client databases etc)

summary: Citigroup - too big but also a place of opportunity
advice: Eliminate the culture of "decks".   Incredible waste of resources and peoples time.   Stop hiring so many consultants.  Instead, hire competent people who know how to do their jobs.
pros: A large place with many different things to do, for those interested.  It's what you make of it.  There is no shortage of opportunities, but you need to be on the lookout for them -  take the initiative, talk to people and proactively seek new positions.
cons: Can be very bureaucratic.   Layers upon layers of people in some cases.   It often seems there are many people whose sole job is tracking abnd reporting on the few who actually do anything.   Very over-staffed, and managers defending their turf.

summary: Times have changed a lot since starting with this company. May be good again one day but for now- too much uncertainty.
advice: Better communication with middle management always seemed to be an issue.
pros: The best reasons to work for citigroup are the training, which is extensive and the employee benefits.  Until the last few years, company growth and new job potential was a big factor for liking the company.  The one good thing hat has come about recently is that it appears that we are finally starting to see some light at the end of the tunnel and the company may be stabalizing
cons: Downsides are the uncertainty and the cutting back everywhere within the company. WHen I first started there was flexiblity in terms of employee bonus and recruiting. That is no longer an option for either.   Watching the company stock fall to the sub $1 range

advice: This is a fools errand since no one listens.  Practice what you preach, stop the forced ranking of employees which prevent teamwork.  Your culture of the week has failed on every level.  In a mere 10 years that I was there , the retail bank went through at least 7 presidents.  How can you have a stable, sustainable culture when you have a revolving door.  Also please not that the $5 door stock is really fooling no one.
pros: There is not really many pros given the dismal last 5 years. Once a respected juggernaut now a beaten and bitter shell of its former self.
cons: Citi has spent the last 5 years reducing its staff count from 375,000 to 250,000 employees.  The culture, never a Citi strong point, is a constant slash and burn.  The bank has moved all of their back office operations out of New York and ensure all the highly competent and highly paid employees were laid off in the process.

summary: mixed bag because of crappy mid-level managers
advice: please look closely at why so many awesome resources are leaving in the Cyber Security space.. got to the root cause
pros: you get to work with some very smart folks in the cyber security space (infra pentesting, redteaming, cloud, devsecops, application pentesting etc.) One gets to be part of an awesome global firm with a great brand recognition as well work with cutting edge technology
cons: mid level management sucks.. they have been entrenched for ever and do a crappy job. new CISO and his team are awesome but they do not really know what is happening 2 -3 levels below them. several awesome resources left in the last 2 years because of crappy mid-level management ( MD, Director level and SVP level) and not because of better pay etc..

summary: Full of Bull, and absolutely no equal to Merrill Lynch.
advice: Remove the head of the snake, hire a company oriented leader that is capable of looking past his own financial wealth, for the greater good of his employees and the organization.  Establish a meritocracy where Desk Head is unable to hire incompetent industry friends, and make hires to establish loyalty to the dictator.
pros: I was able to keep my lights on and feed my family with the help of some savings.  The office is located at the Galleria in Houston, so when you have had enough for the day, you can walk the mall.
cons: Desk head is interested in limiting traders term, and collecting trade ideas from his traders to put in his own book.  Absolute dictatorship, where the leader works towards a goal of destroying individual confidence and self worth, creating an environment where the trader loses confidence in their abilities, resulting in fear of losing money. Pure definition of individual greed limiting collective goal of making money.  Environment is shaped by the leader to keep himself at the top.

pros: Paid holiday, sick leave, 2 weeks mandatory paid vacation. Great training and lots of potential if the branch to grow your client base if it sits in a good location. Great hours.
cons: A lot of responsibilities around the branch and some times its hard to focus on sales. Scorecard and bonus is heavily based on random customer survey. The metric of the survey should be adjusted since the 'passing score' is hard to reach. Survey is rated all or nothing. If customer rates you an 8/10, you pretty much screwed. Your ranking is judged by the score of the whole branch. So even if you did great and your coworker got a bad score, it hurts your branch and thus get part of your bonus taken away (up to 10% of your already heavily taxed bonus).

advice: Management seems to be secretive. I would recommend being more transparent and direct with employees. Be more proactive about coaching employees on their career.
pros: I believe that Citi is inclusive and diverse and more companies should strive to be the same way. There is also opportunity for growth with the company.
cons: Unfortunately, the systems essential to perform work are antiquated and not easy to use, for employees or customers. Almost DAILY, I deal with customers asking for help navigating the website to find simple tasks, like making a payment. This has been an ongoing issue for the entire (4) years of my employment with the company with the same response from management that “updates are coming”. Also, many process are tedious and left to interpretation by the individual agent, leading to confusion among staff and customers.

advice: stop treating your sales guys as dogs
pros: not that I can think of....except bad memories
cons:
I worked as a Universal Banker:-
1. Retail - back then, we were made to stand all day at corporates and malls, begging for people to buy a credit card or loan, like in Ghaffar Market in Karol Bagh
they want 2 files everyday, and they will put you in PIP if you dont meet target for 3 months.
it was an embarrasing job for me.
2. Suvidha (Noida) - I ran away from retail thinking corporate sales might help, it turned out even worse, i was assigned entire delhi as area, which I had to manage from Noida
i used to run like mad dog entire day. the HR people distribute your number to employees and you get calls 24 hours 7 days a week

WORST POINT - you are supposed to come back to Gurgaon / Noida office in the evening even if you are in Rohini - reason - you can not carry client files at home.

It is highly irritating

advice:
Management should treat people equally no matter of nationality. I think that recruitment process should be more transparent and should included HR as well not just TL and Managers.
 In my opinion the promotions depends of 70% nationality, 20% of connections and 10% of how hard you work. People do not cooperate and do not work as a team, they are concentrated on the titles mostly.
There is lack of equal rights and respect to each other and someone needs to take care of it.
People without potential and ambitious are promoted.
pros: Salary is quite good, positive benefits.People friendly and positive but naturally it all depends on what team you end up. Have eyes wide open and don't let anyone to disrespect you.
cons: There are some good projects which you might complete with success but it all depends where and with who you work with.

advice: Get out of the 70's and 80's.... up and coming talent is not going to be comfortable with closed door policies and stepping on eggshells.  We need to be well informed, well insrtucted and need management to be well versed.  We need people leaders not just smarts....
pros: Working in Tech Finance, they are really big on work-life balance.  It is flexible and you do learn a lot.
cons: Management is condecending and they are not as sharp as you expect upper management to be.  You expect a lot of communication and mentoring from a company of this size but there is NONE.  A lot of politics involved in this organization and you can tell that at Citi a lot of the things that happen are based on favoritsm and who knows who.

summary: Great company to work for just watch which department you go into
advice: Need to ensure that people you are putting into management positions (VP), have people skills and have previously managed people.
pros: Great opportunities, fast pace and company stability.
cons: Depending on which department you are working for it can be a dream job or an absolute nightmare!  If you are not part of the "in crowd" you will be stone walled, ostracized, and down right abused!  I've never worked for a department within a huge organization like Citigroup where people do not take accountability, back stab, and throw people under the bus as the norm.   People seem to be able to talk to you any way they want and you just have to take it.  Abuse is what I would call this particular department within the Citigroup organization.

advice: Town Halls are good forums for Sr. Management to get in front of the Citi employees and allow them to hear company news firsthand.
pros: I had a great opportunity to work with really smart people and make an impact in a rapidly changing business environment while at Citi CIB.  Employees are given a lot of responsibility very quickly and recognized for their hard work and dedication.  Management was responsive to the team's needs and always collaborated to work through problems or to reallocate work when people were overwhelmed with client needs.
cons: The company is so large; there were many redundant initiatives going on and the company made organizational changes made too frequently; just as people would get used to new management or a name change or a group re-org, another came our way.

advice: Keep your best people they make it run.  Hold people accountable for mistakes and then you won't have to layoff the good ones.
pros: Benefits, pay,  time off.
cons: Citi is far behind both large and small lenders.  Their technology is the worst among the major banks.  Mortgage department on a whole different page than the rest of the organization.  Inconsistent management allows employees at one location to not be held accountable while others were held accountable at another site.  No job security even for top performers.  Layoff decisions appeared to be made for legal standards versus keeping the best employees.  Many employees that stay are on written warnings while those let go are strong performers.  Upper management does not seek feedback from employees.

summary: A nice place to work, but compensation is stingy
pros: Flexible Work Schedules.  Very supportive and understanding local management.  Opportunity to work from home (with demonstrated experience/proficiency) a day or two a week, or during bad weather when roads are dangerous. Great benefits, comparative to other companies I've worked for in the past.
cons: Compensation is below average. Annual raises, if any, are around 2-3%. Employer requires 40 hours minimum of training each year; even if not job relevant (this may be a local expectation).  Job-relevant training can be very limited, and is often "learn it as you do it".  Constantly going through cycles of downsizing and/or hiring freezes.  Constantly restructuring the HR tree.  Great opportunity for a first promotion; however difficult to be promoted into a first-tier management position; and even more difficult to be promoted into higher management positions:  think "glass ceiling".

advice: Upper management needs serious branch training so they can see what the employees go through on a daily basis. Maybe they will realize what short staff really means and how it impacts the branches. Stop the pressure and make working at a bank fun again.
pros: Compensation plan is great. Have to grind to make your numbers but worth it at the end of the month. Meet amazing people at your level (branch level)
cons: Pressure pressure pressure. At first it was fun making numbers and being competitive at your own pace. Then it just got extreme. Upper management needs serious branch trainings so they can see what we go through on a daily basis. The company started closing branches cutting hours and expect customer service to be excellent yet inconvenient hours. Pb salary is low but compensation helps just pressure is crazy. Promotions are who you know

advice: Please work with your seniors to express the importance of "trickling down" through wages and bonuses (as applicable) the benefits of the increase in the stock price and also in the future the likely reduced corporate tax rate.
pros: A much improved and strong emphasis on work/life balance.  A solid company with a strong customer focus.  Also supports training both in hard and soft skills, anti money laundering, Oracle Financials training, Excel and PPT skills training.  Soft skills included diversity training, communication skills, and much more.  Compensation is reasonable, and my separation package was quite generous to compensate me for my 30+ years of service.
cons: An atmosphere of empowerment is needed by management, but as it is a financial institution I can understand that some critical decisions need to be made by those that are "in the know".

pros: Salary is a little better but that is it.
cons:
1. They are running a sweatshop at their Mississauga office.

2. It has a very bad crowd. People, they talk all the time, they don't even care that they are disturbing other people. 

3.  You don't have a preassigned desk, you have to find an empty desk. You also have to clear your desk after work.

4. Every desk has a VDI and you are supposed to connect to your remote machine with the help of VDI. Everything is very slow, and the machine hangs all the time. Even you cannot connect your headphones to the VDIs.

5. A lot of people do support work and get over 300 emails every day (not exaggerating), bad place to learn anything technical, just remember it is a bank. 

6.  You are expected to work over 10 hours every day.

7. They don't have coffee machines, unlike most companies. 

8. Dirty restrooms,  you will feel as if you are in a public restroom.

summary: lack of corp wide UNITY. The focus should be many, many groups, but only ONE COMPANY.
advice:
cut in half upper managment.  

focus --> everyone works for the same company.  

Hire American.
pros: looks good on your resume.
cons:
lack of corp wide unity.   All the purchased companies that make up this giant,  will not work as one.... 
there are parts of company directly competing with other parts of the same company... or taking food from 1 hand and putting in other hand...the net results is minus zero, if you consider both groups, man hours spent.
many seniors thinking they that are above the law, for short term gains, but should think for longer term. off shoring may help bottom line for next several quarters, but will hurt 3 to 7,  years out.  It takes 2 or 3 Indans to replace 1 American

summary: Had High Hopes, Shattered by Citi Management
advice: Global Markets shoud sack all IT directors and managers in Columbus and start over with a completely new slate.  They are not willing to change in order to pull Citi back up.
pros: I was asked to return to a company Citi recently acquired in 2007.  With that, I believed that the job that I was doing was going to help our clients and our staff be successful.  Instead the dysfunctional organization continued to spend money on bad decisions and upper management was not held accountable.  I delivered my work on-time, bridged fractured client relationships and began making end-roads to baselining our staff with Citi's delivery model.  Suddenly, I was caught in the middle of the 50,000 person layoff and yet am the only senior project manager who was relieved of their duties.
cons: Day-to-day, staff are not sure what changes are going to happen.  The management staff in Columbus don't talk with clients, their own staff which leads to no one really knowing where the intiatives are going.

summary: Escalated concerns of customers is being handled by one person in the Manila site; Information systems too complicated
advice: Management of Citibank BPO Philippines(outsourced by Australia) should assign more workforce (experienced employees) to be delegated more tasks to resolve customer escalated concerns of Citibank's Australia's bank customers--not only assigned to one officer (who cannot be contacted but through email-not to mention the long response time). If this is implemented, the campaign for lowering the site's average handling time would be facilitated
pros: The Information technology being used are up to date; Salary is fair and reasonable for employees with experience
cons: Information System Software are not user-friendly--too complicated; Escalated concerns are being handled by one person (female) in the Manila Site (in other places officers cannot be contacted also) and cannot be contacted by anyone for follow-ups--main reason why Australian Customers who have escalated concerns are not happy with Citibank Australia Customer service

summary: DOD Travel Card - For a company that has been established for 200 years - what a joke!
advice: I started working here before the DOD contract started, and I can honestly say it was the worst place I have ever worked. Managers have little education in the field, or in managing people. My advice is for the site director to seriously evaluate the managers and question how they are treating the associates. I believe that just about all of the management team needs to either be replaced or be given management training and product training.
pros: Select member of management attempts to keep employees motivated.
cons: There are hardly any polices/procedures that are enforced regularly. If a manager wants something they get it, but if you are not on the senior leadership team you are treated unfairly. Managers seem to have no education or background in managing people. Reviews/evaluations are given out by opinion, policies in the company-wide handbook are not enforced and employees are told to ignore them. Associates and Project Managers have more experience in this field then the managers.

advice: You won't know you've cut too many heads until it's too late... Productivity, morale, reputation, etc slowly sink and take a long time to regain. Take a look at Citi when it was run by John Reed and then compare to now... before, it was a career; now, it's a machine.
pros: It's easy to move within Citi, they have a good internal job website.  As individuals, there are a number of good / nice people there.
cons: Headcount cuts EVERY QUARTER for the last 3 years. Workload is increased, headcount shrinks. Senior Mgt has no knowledge of or interest in its employees. Work/life balance is non-existent. Take a look outside of any NYC Citigroup building Monday thru Friday from 7pm onward... there's a constant stream of food deliveries all night long. Go see, this is verifiable. There's also a constant stream of black cars all night.

advice: Learn to be compassionate concerning contractors-they may not be employees.  That's mainly because you don't give them a chance after 3-months-- you're ready to get rid of them no matter how hard they worked and contributed to the success of Citi.
pros:
You may learn a few things what I learned there is to work hand in hand with younger employees learned how to manage my time, learned about project management on my own.
Learned to get key players fellow workers in order to learn and do my job.


Good work/life balance.
cons:
Training is just enough to get you to do your work.  Micro managed all the time.  Company culture treats contractors a dime a dozen.  I didn't feel welcomed working there and left me high and dry.  Also, management is not clear. They rarely speak to you face to face and would rather have some other employee speak to you on their behalf.

Terrible experience.  If you have other options pursue them .  Think twice about citit especially if you're a contractor.

advice: Pay your employees better!
pros: Best reasons include: much learning is done on the job. A person will grow with much Business corporate experience, senior management is generally available to provide advice and nuture growth. There is a good dept culture within teams. Peers work hard to help one another in order to get the job done. Management takes into consideration family & outside responsibilities and community involvement is welcomed.
cons: Downsides included limited room for growth currently. Many layoffs and low pay compared to other financial industries. Employee turn over would minimize if salaries were at least within the range of other industries. Currently 401k matching is down, tuition reimbursement is down & salary increase are very low. Citi is losing many good people - while upper management continues to get larger salary increases.

summary: Decent pay, but company overall cuts corners
advice: Spend the profits you have to hire quality team members, and pony up for better technology. If you want to be a "world class" company you have to spend world class dollars.
pros: Pay is good, benefits are decent and bonus structure is fair. You can work in your position forever unless they have lay offs which usually only happens in the back office. Most of the employees I know have been there forever.
cons: The company cuts corners and does not spend to advance technology. The systems are horrible and everything is outsourced, so communication between different departments is horrible. This leads to poor customer service. They are slow to hire new employees when needed, so the work load is huge on the existing employees and the customers receive poor/slow service.

summary: Citibank is a great place to work, if you are one of the top performers.
advice: Make it easier for talented people to transition to other job functions -> make it easier to make a lateral transfer to another job function.
pros:
Performance based promotion criteria.
High flyers get rewarded.
Not stingy with recognizing when work is well done.
Great training and a lot of personal development opportunities.
cons:
Since is multinational, poor performance in other countries can affect the increases/bonuses that you get, even if your country's performance is better than the rest.
You sometimes have to know the right people to get things done.
There is a tendency for one to get pigeonholed as an operations person, or marketing person, making it harder for people to transition to different job functions.

advice: See above.
pros:
Good starting salary (few raises after, though)
Opportunity to travel
Great co-workers
Loyal workers
Great reward program (for employees/customers) in Thankyou points
cons:
Too much middle-management that creates unnecessary work so they can justify their jobs. 
Too much middle/upper management that is clueless as to the reality of their retail branch system- doesn't ask for input from those on the front lines
A lot of "feedback" surveys that are a waste of time. Again, people job-justifying, but not caring about what they're told.
Very goal/money driven, to the point where employees do things that may be unethical in order to meet goals. (usually given the behind-the-scenes nod of approval by whomever they report to...until caught)

Quietly slinking out of Philadelphia market due to horrible locations, and no support system for the market by way of advertising etc. Disgraceful.

summary: Good company but it seems that at the end of day, you're just another number.
advice: Please train your managers in customer service.  They should act like they care about their tellers.  They are the face of the bank who do most of the work.
pros: Citi provides you with great benefits as well as wonderful co-workers to help you in need.
cons:
Tellers do most of the work and are paid the least.  You're expected to answer the phone even if you have a line of customers.

Management expects you to walk in the first day and know everything and when you ask a question, you get looked at like you're incompetent.  That's where good co-workers come in.  Managers don't want to bother babying you.

They care more about KDS than anything else.

summary: The last company I would recommend working for.
advice: Replace current management. Revise all current processes. Improve compensation.
pros: Good soup in the cafeteria.
cons: Highest turnover of any company I have ever worked for. No employee moral. Work is thrown on you in abundance and expected to be completed in very narrow deadlines. Client interface is very chaotic. Minimal training provided. Only one or two people out of a whole team, including team leads, are the least bit knowledgable and worth going to for questions. Otherwise, its practically a guessing game. Pay is also very low compared to other banks. Management is very impersonal. Waited a full 3 full months to even speak with my manager for the first time and even then they still appeared miserable on a daily basis. In addition, after leaving the company, they continued to pay me by mistake and I have to repay the gross amount back, not the net which I received. I recommend to avoid this company at all costs.

summary: CITI never sleep and never let its emloyee to :)
advice:
Learn something from Service based industries or else you will loose your resources as usual.
Try to manage your HR teach then that they are HR not the boss.
pros:
- No Swipe in & out 
- Good Pay during Joining
cons:
- Pathetic Work Culture
- Promise lot of thing during joining but will give only baba ji ka thullu.
- No time tracking because u always have to complete 12 hr as lot of garbage is der to clean
- Job Mismatch
- No Car parking they are reserved for higher people only
- Worst transport facility
- No bonus, only promised during joining
- Interview are really  easy to crack so you will smart enough which type of team member you will have.
- Pathetic hike as compared to other IB

summary: Great company if you are in the right team
advice:
- At least at the regional level, look to promote a consistent culture
- Invest more on nurturing talent; give people reason to remain loyal
pros:
-  Global reach - opportunity to work with diverse teams and clients
-  Great people and talent if you are in the right team
-  Good entry level programs with decent mobility options
cons:
- Tends to be highly bureaucratic - decision making could be slow
- High turnover with lack of consistent leadership;  like most financial services, can fall into the trap of  being very short term focused
- While the large size and global reach create opportunities, the company starts lacking consistent culture
-  The company could better manage talent by promoting an apprenticeship culture and give more opportunities for developing skills

advice: Find another bank that will treat you better.
pros: Pay is higher than most banks. Consumer products are competitive.
cons: Absolutely no regard for the employee. Area Directors are over leveraged and will inendate employees with never ending online training, they read from scripts on weekly calls repeating "key phrases" and tell you to "help" the client by selling to them over the phone. The computer systems are the worst of all. There are too many platforms bankers need to use for just one client, these platforms are WIDLEY outdated and run off of Windows 7, which is no longer supported by Microsoft. When you clock in, expect these programs not to work correctly. You will simply be told to exit and try again, or move to another computer. Zero one on one meetings with management.

summary: Working for Citi is as good as you can stand it.
advice: Pay yourselves less.
pros: The benefits package has been very very good throughout the years, although it has also gotten more and more expensive.  It pays well but expects 150% for that payment.  Do not start there thinking it will be a breeze, it is not.  No one has been treated well, and they are all more than willing to share the misery.  But like I said it pays better than most places in this town.
cons: Long hours, expectations from management that are unclear, senior management seems unclear on anything.  Rewards are few, and are given to the people who promote themselves the most, or the people whos management takes the time to recognize them.

summary: Too big, lousy career advancement, great opportunity to progress if you are an excellent networker
advice: Try to make it 'One Citi' and dismantle silos.
pros:
- If you network all the time and are excellent at making contacts, you can build a great network and can easily move between jobs
- Despite recent economic downturn, Citi is still respected and everyone knows the name
- opportunity to work abroad in all sorts of locations
cons:
- difficult to navigate, silos, lack of understanding of business lines other than your own
- plenty of employees who are not bright nor professional
- hard to come by the truly great managers, other managers have really only got to their current position because of their tenure / have been with the bank since 1975.
- outsourcing of functions means job security is always a question

summary: Citi is a company full of bureaucracy, inefficiencies and top-heavy with incompentant, overpaid management.
advice: Get rid of the entire level of section managers.  They do nothing except waste company resources.  Pay the employees that you know are good at what they do what they deserve so 10% of your office doesn't quit in a three month period.
pros: Citi has a great work/ life balance with a flexible work schedule.  There is a young and fun corporate culture.
cons: Compensation is very poor.  Promotions are given without salary increases.  Decisions made are from so many levels above that they don't make practical sense when applied.  The company is full of overpaid managers that do very little to contribute to the bottom line while the first three levels of positions are considered expendable.

summary: People usually do their time and get out!
advice: Praise and compliments do not pay the bills. If someone is consistently out performing others, compensate them appropriately or those 'award winners' will inevitably leave the company. Do not promote solely based upon seniority.
pros: Great to have on a resume because Citigroup has a respectable reputation among the banking industry. Able to get promoted if you have specific banking experience, but little to no education.
cons: Continuing education is not valued. Promotions are rarely given on merit and / or production. The size of Citigroup makes it difficult to be recognized. You may get a pat on the back for a job well done, but do not expect monetary compensation. There are far too many 'channels' to go through to get anything of importance accomplished.

advice: All management should be required to have at least a bachlors degree.
pros: Good Benefits. They offer multiple schedules. Not a bad choice but not something you'd want to stay at for as long as I did, hind site 20/20 I wish I would have went back to school and learned something more valuable, they make it so easy to stay on the hampster wheel with all the vacation they offer and you do have job security or at least I did.
cons: Pay to retain employess is horrible to say the least and Management is some what to be desired. If your just looking for a "job" this might work for you. Its one of those kinda jobs where you need to drink lots of koolaid, you are the hampster on the wheel.

summary: Good Exposure in a very diverse organization
advice: Its better to promote internally rather than recruiting people from outside. The management should try to retain top performers!
pros: As Citi is a Global organization there is lot of exposure. You get to interact with lot of people at various levels in the organization. After 1 year, you can move to a different position internally. My immediate managers were pretty nice, learned a lot from them.
cons: As Citi's Consumer Banking is not growing in US, career growth in Consumer Banking is limited. The culture is less analytical as compared to its peers. Also, there are lot of inefficiencies, you do the same work again and again. Lot of Bureaucracy and Hierarchy is there, its tough to get approval of strategies from the management. Also, Promotions are very tough

summary: Anti Money Laundering (AML) -  HIGH turnover, HORRIBLE culture
advice: Care about your employees - respect employees at all times, verbally and non-verbally. You have / had some wonderful, intelligent, professional employees that you are losing faster than you can replace them due to the negative culture, low pay, hours that are required, threats from Team Lead's and not being honest with employees from the start of hiring to day-to-day operations.
pros: Work from home two days per week (used to be three, see below); some wonderful, intelligent and helpful coworkers; branded / known company name on your resume; at times, interesting work that you can see the implications of.
cons:
Please, do yourself a favor and read the reviews for the city / position of interest that you are considering; additionally, pay attention to the posting date and similar, highly positive reviews that should be read with caution (HR has been trying to change external opinions to try to recruit more people, as they can't keep up with the high turnover rate - hence, the use of so many recruiting / contract companies). 

Hiring Process: As many others have stated, get EVERYTHING in writing that you are told; ask deeper questions regarding the "bonus" / "merit pay increase" / benefits, etc...They are not as advertised by the internal recruiters. You WILL be working more than 40 hours per week, EVERY week, contrary to the "...on rare occasions you may have to work a couple of extra hours" that is told during the hiring process (as you will find out at the beginning of training when you start hearing and seeing the real hours).

Culture and General Work: Very negative, depressing culture, from the top-down. I am a person who can find a positive in any situation, as are many great coworkers at CitiGroup, but after working 12-16 hour days and weekends (no overtime pay), and still being told by management that we aren't doing enough and need to work harder / faster, positives are hard to find; constant verbal threats about job security / performance plans, etc...without support or how they are going to fix the unreal work imbalance across the floor. After 1.5 years of working non-stop (including holidays from home), I had had enough and voluntarily resigned; I was the 29th person to do so in only 2 months! The Team Lead's will tell you how great you are doing on your cases and QA scores, etc...and then later that same day, tell you how you need to be doing more cases, although they know that you are putting in all of the extra hours and doing great work (?? - confusing, makes you feel defeated and frustrated? Yes!). 

Benefits / Pay: 20% below industry average pay and subpar benefits. Citi is an international, huge company, yet I the benefits were the worst that I had ever had working in various industries for 15+ years. Aside from the low pay, excessive hours and negative culture, plan for $82 - $98 to come out of your paycheck (for an individual) and still have to pay high deductibles / copays, for a healthy person.

summary: Good company, but doesn't pay well
advice: To attract top talent, Citi should change its HR and recruiting practices.  Currently, it is impossible to get a raise when moving internally unless the new role comes with a promotion.  It is much easier to look for career opportunities outside.  At the same time, it is extremely difficult to find good external talent because the internal recruiters do not partner with the best agencies and because the pay that we can offer for our titles is below market rates.
pros: The good thing about Citi is that it's not Goldman, i.e., it is possible to have a life outside work
cons: Citi pays billion-dollar fines, but cannot afford to compensate good talent.  Current cost-cutting strategy is nothing but a race to the bottom.

summary: People always get work done but run into down-turns on re-organization of the company
advice: None for now
pros:
The team you work with is excellent and people really work as a team. There are very senior team members at Citigroup that are helpful and provide good mentoring of junior team members whenever required. Management also came up with a plan to talk to individual employees as part of their 'lunch meetings' which was a great idea to talk directly to management. 

Overall, a great place to start your career but make sure if this is your first job, you at least look around to understand the importance of the people you work with and respect the company. I was happy at Citigroup from work/life balance, but pay scale was below average.
cons: Current market turn-around and lot of re-orgs.

pros: There are a lot of training opportunities
cons:
Citi says it supports a work-life balance and lets employees work remotely.  Then it uses the fact that work can be done successfully while remote to justify moving the job to cheaper locations.
The matrix relationships between managers is crazy -- its pretty hard to figure out who works for who & what the real priorities are when you report to three different people at a time.
It's just too big -- it shouldn't be as hard as it is to get things done, but the organization is so complex that even the little things take forever to accomplish.
Its still very much an old boys network and doesn't take the time to really groom managers.  Some of the behaviors they reward are really beyond belief.

advice: Recognize and reward valuable employees.  Make sure senior managment understands the business and has the experience necessary to run the company.
pros: Management does a good job of communicating with employees and asking for feedback.  Opportunities for advancement were clearly communicated and fostered.  Annual reviews were completed on-time and the overall atmosphere was positive.  Emphasis was placed on customer service and many initiatives were designed to improve client retention.  Many formal internal training programs were available for employees.
cons: Salary is not up to industry standards.  Top management was not well qualified and industry savvy.  So much emphasis was put on shareholder value and quarterly earnings reports that the long-term vision was ignored.  Not enough was invested in the future since the future was the next quarterly report.

advice: Screen applicants better. Make sure they don't just want a job (or a transfer to New York). Consider moving downtown.
pros: Brand recognition. Since the building is relatively new, it has many amenities, such as a large cafeteria and a gym. Good place to start if you are a college grad.
cons: Lots of people came here because either they had no choice, or want a transfer to New York. People tend to leave after only a few years, which causes significant knowledge loss (not to mention that procedures are rarely written down). This and combined with low pay, contribute to the negative vibe you will may feel. Also, due to the site reaching capacity, parking can be terrible if you come in late, or need to run an errand during the day.

summary: Not the greatest place but also not the worst
advice: There's so much advice but does it really matter? The company asked for advice from employees but did nothing with it. It's such a large company they're more worried about profit than employees.
pros: Great benefits. Flexible work time due to open minded management. Most people were great but it is a very strange gossipy environment.
cons: Very tedious work with constant arguments between sales and underwriting. No matter how well you tried to organize your work it was out of your hands because your work depended on too many other people doing their work also. Upper management had no idea what was going on at the ground level and kept making changes. The company overstaffed without thinking of future and then fired people. It was a horrible cycle.

advice: Do not excessively shed headcount in profitable businesses / sector coverage teams in smaller regions/locations, simply on the basis of offshore / head office driven directives.  Teams then need to be rebuilt, often at far greater expense, in order to maintain market share.  Simply ridiculous.
pros:
Global bulge bracket IB
Good to get experience at a junior level
Global network able to be leveraged on both a regional and a local basis
cons:
Negativity sentiment towards the brand as a result of GFC
Poor management performance at all levels
Overly rigid process of reporting through NYC - lack of regional autonomy
Promotions based on ability to "brown-nose" rather than any inherent capabilities - in fact often it was the reverse
Lots ot pitching, not enough live deals
Excessive in-fighting when it came to revenue allocation as it drove end of year comp reviews

summary: Citigroup & Wall Street - Is it all the same?
advice: Hire strong leadership at the middle levels, there is little talent their and all are focused on self preservation and large bonus checks, not about building strong teams and growing employees.  Lower level managers are completely unempowered to grow and incentivize their people.
pros: Flex hours, work from home when needed.
cons: Benefits get worse every year, it's a race to zero.  No growth, no bonus regardless of performance.  Bell curve evaluation process, somebody must get a poor review even if everyone performs well.  New hires are over compensated with lofty titles and bonus guarantees, while existing loyal performers get no growth and no bonus.  Toxic work environment, when the going gets rough, the fingers start pointing.  Lot's of in-fighting and empire building.

summary: AML is a tough place to make it.
advice: QA reports tell all, not just the bottom line numbers.  And if the expectations were at a certain level for caseloads, those should have been stated upfront instead of getting a surprise later on.
pros:
- Interesting groups of people
- Trainers are nice
- Potential for growth
cons:
- Was brought in as temp so no benefits
- If falling behind in casework, no additional training just let go
- Quantity is valued over quality.  If someone is faster but has a lower accuracy rate, they're still on as opposed to someone with a higher accuracy rating but few cases done.  It's a case by case basis so it's not a real fair standard.

summary: Tough environment, but the challenge made me a better employee!
advice: Senior management needs to become more involved and proactive in mentoring and coaching their female employee population at all levels.   While generally yearly employee reviews are based on employee production, there are times when manager's personality dislikes taint the reviews - this needs to stop.
pros: Benefits package comprehensive and pricing to employee(s) fair.  Proactive with FMLA and disability issues.  Working environment well spaced, well lit, and generally quiet for this type of business.  Centrally located in the DFW metroplex, outstanding cafeteria, clean breakrooms, close to external food services.  Generally speaking, treatment of employees was fair and very respectful.
cons: Long hours at month-end, month-end close.  Long hours at mid-month.  Occasionally these long hours interefered with attending college courses at night.

advice: take the issue of money of the table, by compensating enough. then give your employees autonomy, mastery, and purpose. they will outperform and produce amazing stuff!
pros: Work life balance is equalized. The vacation and holiday benefits are on the higher end in relation to other companies in the area.  Low stress job, with a steady amount of work.
cons: No clear career path for a web designer.  All web designers these days are developers.  Yet, we are treated like salespeople.  Projects involving the non web designers never start with web designers involved, we are constantly asked last minute to perform miracles.  There is no one in our company hierarchy that can be viewed as a mentor, or someone to help you improve your skills.

summary: Large company that puts profits over people. Company culture that DOES NOT promote empowerment.
advice: Focus more on employee engagement and recognition.  Follow up on ethics complaints from employees.  Create a better work/ life balance especially for employees in the branches.   Create a fair succession plan to allow employees an opportunity for advancement.  (Currently a plan is in place, however it only for a few managers)
pros: Good benefits, salary was above average
cons: Worked in the HR department - there was poor communication and the directors were not current on state employment law which lead to poor decisions.  Managers/Directors had favorites, if they didn't like you then you never received recognition or special projects.  Favorites were always kept during layoffs even when they performed poorly.  Favorites were also promoted over other qualified candidates

summary: Good Experience but Left A Lot To Be Desired
advice: Cut the fat and streamline operations.  Improve sentiment across the employee population.  Let quality of work not quality of relationships, drive promotions.
pros:
Friendly colleagues - collegial and collaborative culture; there is a discernible Citi community where people come together across common goals and values.  
Flexible work arrangements i.e., work from home possibility, etc. 
Good communication from senior mgmt
cons:
Compensation is static.  Raises were hard to come by even for top performers.  Bonuses were up and down.
Morale was low due to comp issue.
Technology is a bit outdated as is the case at other firms.  A bit of a disconnect between Tech / IT and the business.
Organization is just too massive which makes it difficult to wade through the many layers to get things done.

summary: Not for College Graduates; Extremely high turnover
advice: There needs to be a restructuring of management principles. There's very few advantages to working your hardest each day because the minimal incentive checks at the end of the month don't make up for the money collected. Politics ran the place and if you happen to make a manager mad during a point in the year, you'll have a bad name for the rest of the year. Please look at replacing people that leave because there simply isn't enough people to handle the expectations each day, especially on weekends.
pros:
Work-Life balance
Training
Friendly People
No at-home work
Part time employment
cons:
Politically based.
Hard work is looked over.
Part Time employees are better off as the incentive check will equal what a full time employee does.
High Turnover with no replacements.
New hires are stuck with weekend work with no adjustments.

advice: GIve employees a chance to do performance reviews on their managers - the 360 degree review should apply at all levels.  The current culture of management infallibility while lower employees are criticised for operating without clear instructions is very demoralizing.
pros: CItigroup does offer a fair work/life balance - with management approval employees can generally work one a week from home, I never have a problem taking off a little early when there is an event at my child's school, etc.   Benefits and vacation time are better than many other companies.
cons: Communication from management is poor to dishonest, employees get better scoop from the WSJ.  Tenured employees are paid less than new hires at the same level.  Corporate culture is very harsh, political, and siloed

advice: Managers need more training. They need to be held accountable for their teams and the work that they produce. There are too many band-aids on some processess that really need to be evaluated and improved, which can in turn improve output from employees. In addition, employee recognition is important, and favortism is just not fair and it occurs frequently.
pros: Citi offers a competitive salaries, great work/life balance (with the opportunity to work remotely), employee discounts to museums, shows and other great places, a comprehensive health benefit plan and most importantly, tuition reimbursement.
cons: Unfortunately management does not provide appropriate feedback, the end-of-year rating system is not structured, career development is difficult and there is not enough emphasis on working to elimate redundant practices.

summary: Great opportunities, but beware the good ol' boys
