advice: Pay attention to morale. The culture changed quite a bit in the aftermath of the financial crisis. Retaining talent will requiring additional investment in time and training to make people feel valued at the company.
pros:
* Fun culture where people form good relationships both at and beyond the workplace
* Lots of resources, including gym, cafeteria, decent benefits
* Large company offers opportunities to move around, but there is at times very little interaction between divisions
cons:
* Can some times be a good ol' boys environment. Networks are incredibly important for promotions and opportunities.
* Work life balance really depends on your division and your group. Large variation in hours. Some 9-5 while other work until midnight every night.

advice: Make sure you have enough staff members to get the job done.  If one of the shifts works overtime, make them find a different place to sit so that the next shift can sit at their regular work stations.
pros: The pay was good and they had company parties and events that I was invited to participate in even though I was a contractor
cons: There weren't enough employees to do the job that I was assigned to do, so the other mailroom clerks and I often "scrambled" to get the work done in a timely manner.  Also, if the day shift staff wanted to work overtime, they would sit at their work stations, and the 2nd shift staff (of which I was one) had to find places to sit which wasn't easy.

summary: Strong people, but can be so much more
advice: If it changes every week or month, it's not a strategy - it's a tactic. Management needs a well articulated strategy, a roadmap to implementing the strategy, and a commitment to the strategy and the roadmap.
pros:
People: The people I worked with were great - looking back I ended up missing the people far more than I expected. Bright, competent, helpful.

Variety: As a large banking institution, there is vast opportunity for exposure to many products, services, and business units.
cons:
Bureaucracy: Hard to get things done. The institution is simply incapable of nimbleness.

Resource allocation: There is a strong disconnect between Senior Management and rank/file employees. Hence, rank/file do not feel engaged, and Senior Management does not understand the challenges/barriers rank/file face.

advice: Management training and development should include employee engagement, as well as the value in encouraging employees to take on greater roles and responsibility. Losing employees to better positions and having to go back to interviewing is a scary prospect, but holding people back from their potential is even scarier!
pros: There was a lot of autonomy in this role, the company provided some benefits, and I got to know my clients well because we had a small branch.
cons:
The managers were lacking in training, did not encourage growth and development throughout the branch, and had obvious favorites. The pay did not justify putting up with this aspect of the job.

The trickle-down of the area director's decisions didn't always translate for our small branch, so some of the goals ended up being unrealistic.

advice: Take care of the workers .
pros: Horrible there are no pros . By far the worst job .
cons: Horrible hours for part -time employees high hourly pay rate but if you don't have any hours you make the same salary as a minimum wage employee no offense .They don't care about employees and will drop you at the drop of a dime . Stay away from this company. I worked at this company for a year and half the worst they accidently over paid me and made me pay them back which wasn't my fault. The managers don't follow policy and if they give you permission to do something and it goes bad you will take the fall . Co-workers gossip about one another all day . management treats you like a slave .

summary: Relaxed environment where you can achieve as much or as little as you'd like
pros: Great Benefits - 401k does a 6% match which from what I've seen is unheard of for this type of large non-tech company. Use an online 401k calculator and you'll see it basically guarantees you're a multi millionaire by retirement if you start straight out of college
cons: Depends on what you want our of your career. If you want to dedicate your life to your job and potentially come out with many millions of dollars, then this is probably not the right place to do that. BUT, if you would like to live a well balanced life and guarantee a strong financial future then this is definitely the perfect company for that.

summary: My Time as a Mutual Fund Analyst
advice: There is nothing more that I can say, than to have a management is that much more consistent, and the same rules should apply to everyone.
pros: I was in several different departments in regards to Mutual Funds, and overall upper management was very good, the pay was excellent and I worked well with everyone and made quite a few friends along the way. The hours were great and the work was challenging,which I really liked.
cons: In my final mutual fund department, it didn't start out that way but lower management was not so, consistent. They were all hired as a group from another company and we were doing the work of forty or more people as a much smaller group. It became much harder and even more unpleasant.

advice: Upper management makes massive bonuses,  take care of the people who are actually making Citi great.    Hire within.
pros: benefits were decent, but our costs went up.
cons: bonuses cut, this was at least 2/3 of my salary.  Jobs cut and assets sent to outsourcers to manage, depart closed down for the most part.    Difficult manager, merit increases were nonexistent due to being in the higher salary range, although those salaries were never published, so its just their word, very demanding workload due to high volume of employees having left.  over 10 years working there and seen several employees with over 25 years let go.   I worked hard to save Citi money,  just one week I saved them over 50,000 in HOA fees, no good job or thank you, no bonus, no merit increase.   After 10 years,  I was making less and working harder than when I started,

advice: They need to pay attention to the voices of the "little" people.
pros: Because they are very flexible with your schedule, if you need time off ((in our department, because this is very dependent on who your manager is), I have never seen it not granted.
cons: Its...."who you know"....when it comes to promotions, senior management does not really qualify in our department to be "Senior Management".  Persons are always on the defensive because upper management does not communicate with the employees and everyone is afraid that their job is going to be outsourced...there have been a few titles already outsourced, but management waits until the last minute to tell the employees that it will affect, and will not tell the truth to the other departments.

advice: Continue the focus on bringing together various parts of the org towards One Citi! Increase the internal  communication.
pros: One of the biggest and prestigious global firm. Great internal mobility (both global and countrywide) to advance your career and opportunity to try out different areas/groups without having to switch firms. Relatively a much better work life balance compared to other financial firms. Good people, encouragement to volunteer, diversity etc. Benefits especially healthcare may not be as good as the jersey pharma firms but they are comparable to financial firms in the NY metro area.
cons: Due to the diversified portfolio of business you don't get the upside in a bull market as you would working for a pure IB. At the same time it is better to be diversified in the current environment.

advice: Can someone really take a close eye at the branch managers?
pros: The branch employees really tried to give their best. There was absolutely nothing good about working for this branch in Rego Park.
cons: If a manage states in what they call a “hurtle” that “you can flip burgers at McDonald’s” just to coerce his/her authority. What else can it be expected of the overall work environment? Managers would do the impossible to please customers who are racists, just for the sick of a key driving scores which affects the managers’ bonus. This may be perceived as a private wrong as one might say well, it might had happened in one occasion. However, in this particular branch,  it happened all the time, and the managers pretended like nothing was happening, or corrected the employee. Managers should be there to increase potential and not just to fire people because they can. The branches main focus is customer retention and not employee growth or motivation.

summary: You will be challenged, and hopefully rewarded.
advice: Act on the voice of the employee feedback provided by the entire employee population; reward outstanding workers, else risk losing them.
pros: You will be challenged and given opportunities to show your leadership. Professional advancement opportunities are available, but you have to seek them. If you're lucky enough to have a seasoned manager, he/she will show guide you through the Citigroup jungle, and help empower your career. Flexible work-life balance, if you schedule and communicate well with your management is possible.
cons: Excessive regulatory and audit scrutiny drain resources from more productive projects. You have to take charge of your schedule early on, else you will be a blackberry (aka crackberry) slave. Some evidence of old school, micromanagers still exist, although senior management is working hard to change that culture.

advice: Take care of yourselves. Be impartial. Make sure your words match your actions.
pros:
There is a lot of opportunity for growth. 
At the start of the year you will receive atleast 96 hours of vacation time, 48 hours of sick time and 32 hours of flexible holiday time. There are 3 healthcare options to choose from. Shift differentials are possible ( you receive an extra 20 percent if you work on a weekend day and an extra 10 percent if you work an evening shift). Employee support is phenomenal. In Jacksonville there is a fitness center on site with personal trainers. 401k matching is an option.
cons: The managers at Citi seem to be overwhelmed. It is a rare occurrence to run across a manager who is not burnt out.

advice: Please advise managers to really understand their subordinates. If employee made a report on certain seniors, please take action on it.
pros:
1) Higher salary for fresh graduate

2) Near to LRT

3) Nice office

4) Training is provided, hence, good for career growth
cons:
1) Some managers are not really aware of mental health of their subordinates

2) Some seniors are such a bully. It depends on which team are you in. Some other seniors are really nice

3) Really steep learning curve, heavy workloads, they expect you to know everything in short time

4) Sometimes, you have to stay back. Don't expect 9-6 office hours. No work-life balance

5) Bonus is not attractive. If you are looking for lucrative bonus, this is not the place

6) If you have mental illness, expect to relapse

pros:
- Great benefits (above average in SG). 
- Pay was market rate and was decent. 
- The hiring process was fairly straightforward. 
- Nice office building.
cons:
- Massive attrition prior to my joining and there was no replacement. As a new hire, I experienced an immense amount of workload not to mention the very steep learning curve. 
- Worked overtime almost everyday and sometimes even on Sundays. When I raised this topic to senior management, they mentioned that they could not be bothered if I had to work 24/7 as it just meant that I was incapable. 
- There was once I took time off to go for my staycation and received a scolding from senior management on the subsequent workday for not attending a meeting while I was on leave (my team mate who was at work did not attend the meeting as well) 
- I was blamed for anything that went wrong, even if they are not under my purview and expertise.

summary: Lots of opportunity but easy to get complacent
advice: People seem to fail up - be ruthless and cut the poor performers irrespective of relationships.
pros: You can be given opportunities quickly if you're in the right place at the right time, and if your reputation is strong.  Great ability to move around across the organization once you prove yourself.  Great thing is that although roles are very narrow you do have the change to try new things and move around over time.  However, be careful of getting stuck - people need to know who you are, and relationships (like everywhere) are critical. People ,ake up their mind quickly about you, and word travels fast.
cons: Absolutely need a champion - if you or your group get caught up in the politics you're toast.

summary: Enter with caution and low expectations
advice: get it together, leadership needs to come from the top down
pros: hone your customer service skills, learn what you don't want in your next job.  The work life balance is pretty good with this company.  It is a great job for university students but there is a quick burnout factor for those employees looking to make this a career.
cons: lack of support, countiuous layoffs, shut downs every few years, low pay, poor management, disgruntled employees, lack of consistency, low employee morale.  All of the good managers seem to move on faily quickly and the ones that you would like to see move on seem to stay around forever.  They do not seem to have much of a development plan in place for growing their mangers skills.

summary: They could have been a contender...
advice: The old ways did not work.  Build an infrastructure that is consistent at least within a business within Citi, if not across all of Citi.  This is a huge investment, but one that should have been done 10 years ago with a much cheaper price tag.
pros:
There was a good work/life balance in the division I was in.  Not all areas of Citigroup have this balance, although they do try to accomodate people where they can.

Working at Citigroup teaches you to deal with bureaucracy and find your way through a maze of disconnected information to get an answer.  While this is also a downside of Citi, it can help turn a negative (bureacracy) into a positive.
cons: Bureaucracy.  Lack of consistent, knowledgeable leadership.  Very political.

summary: Pros & Cons, but needs some help
advice: They need to try new things. Be cutting edge.  Try a new management model.  But don't change it for the sake of changing it.  Core was dissolved, but nothing worked until ALM was formed (a reincarnation of Core).  Then ALM was broken up for about a year & has recently been regrouped.  SBU silos don't work.
pros: They offer great benefits and time off.  Five to six weeks for most everyone was great!
cons: Well, you must be a favorite to get promoted.  And these days you seem to need to be the right color to be a favorite.  Not to say other weren't promoted, but most of the folks who move up after I left were all part of the same group.

advice: Find better ways to recognize top achievers.
pros: There is an excellent opportunity for advancement. Their training is very thorough, although some people tend to get left behind. In my opinion, most of those who do get left behind were not good fits for the job in the first place. Those that do make it through training, and the first 90 days of employment tend to be very successful. If you can tough it out in an entry level position you can work your way through the ranks.
cons: As stated previously it can be a grind to get a chance at promotion. But like most jobs that's just the way it goes. Senior management makes attempts to give employee recognition, but a lot of the time it as seen as cheesy.

summary: Used to be good, now its a dump...
advice: Keep doing a great job of making your pockets fatter atthe expense of all of the hard working employees
pros: Citi offers good benefits and if you are a new hire you will get paid much more than an existing employee
cons: You will need your benefits to handle all of the stress that comes along with the job. They expect you to be at work at 8Am and stay 3 hours after your workday is done (8pm) in order to make phone calls. New management does not care or value their employees. Loyal employees that understand the business and culture of the bank are paid way less than the new hires whom you are then asked to train. Turnover is excessive, in the past year 70 percent of the staff at my branch has either resigned or tranferred elsewhere only to deal with the same issues. In all honesty Citibank has turned into a big dump..... Retail without folding clothes

summary: Very disappointed, that after years of dedicated service I was cast aside for a few dollars in savings.
advice: Upper Management should treat it's employees like human beings and not cattle. You lose a lot of credibility when you thank long time employees for their hard work and dedication one week, and the next that their job is being moved offshore to save money. It really shows that dedication only flows in one direction at Citi.
pros: Good Pay, Excellent benefits, Many hard working dedicated employees.
cons: Very Long hours put in will go unappreciated. Upper management will give you lip service, but as I found out, it really means nothing. They Claim to care about their employees, especially long term ones, but at the end of the day all they really care about is the bottom line.

advice: Stop changing processes just for the sake of change.  Make the changes meaningful and progressive, not take away from our ability to provide our best customer service.  Busy work does no one any good.
pros: Pros are the benefits such as being able to wear jeans to work, their contribution to dependent care expenses/day care, contributions to health savings plan account, and matching 401k up to 6%.
cons: My job responsibilities have been constantly changing on a weekly basis regarding what is required of me.  They keep giving us more busy work to do that doesn't have any point (repetitive tasks) and tie it to our quarterly compensation.  They've made it harder and harder to bonus out with unrealistic expectations.  It's a moving target that has become a major source of dissatisfaction.

advice: If you want to be someone in the local Retail Business, need to invest strongly in people, technology and marketing.
pros:
Compensation is superior to the market average (related to the amount of work done)
In retail banking no one gets killed if you dont reach the business goals, so less stressful than other banks i have worked for
If you complain about a superior to HHRR, you will always be right
It is possible to have a life in this company
You may complain to HHHR if you dont like your goals.
cons:
In Peru,the retail business has not been doing good for years which has resulted in the cutting off of relevant managers and left the business to unexperienced executives. 
Long time citibankers cannot accept comparing themselves to local competition. Lots of arrogance gives awful results.

advice: To retain talent, you have to be able to pay, you let too much talent walk out the door because you want to keep board members happy by paying talent bottom dollar, outsourcing doesn't work
pros: Great Global Brand, you interact with a lot of different people and the company definitely has the resources to compensate you and accommodate you.
cons: My time at Citibank was a roller coaster of a ride, I work for a lot different parts of the business Customer Service (call center), CitiPrivate bank, traveled nationwide as a quality analyst and capped it off by working for a branch support department. All in all a lot of hard work that didn't ever payoff,  its all about politics, who you know, not what you know or do.

advice: Although accountability is a term used often by management, all too often the managers of success stories are more than happy to take credit; meanwhile, when something does not go as planned, the Teflon managers are all too quick to unload oneness to the project.  Management also needs to be more transparent, particularly with the various divestitures ongoing globally, the impacted businesses are the last ones to find out the fate of the employees doing the work.

pros: Great benefits, awesome culture for a bank and supportive management. Ethical sales is taught everyday and management will not pressure staff to sell just to meet goals. The entire organization, worldwide, is on headed in the same direction and executives have been very clear and communicative about their plans for the future.
cons: Citi is moving away from mass market banking and developing a niche as the world's affluent bank. That brings a lot of pains and changes that are difficult but everyone stays positive. Some of the people in the retail banking, particularly one's who've been at Citi for 10+ years, are happy with their positions and just want to keep doing what they're doing. Then there's some who just won't work for what they want. Weird, but upper management is supportive.

advice: Start to promote from within!
pros: Citibank was a relatively low stress work environment. After coming from Wells Fargo which was a truly horrific experience, Citibank offered less stress, higher base salary , better hours, and much more control over how much commission is earned. The commission structure has changed for the worse since I started, but still features monthly commission instead of that quarterly crap.
cons: There are many things going on at the upper management level that cause concern and unrest. I was laid off as a result. As far as working for citi, the biggest flaw Is that there is little room for growth within the branch. The company prefers to hire externally when positions arise. This caused many branch members to become complacent and unmotivated.

advice: Value your employees. Value your employees. Value your employees.
pros: Citigroup has a number of businesses.  You don't have to leave the company to diversify your career. Citigroup has a number of businesses.  You don't have to leave the company to diversify your career. Citigroup has a number of businesses.  You don't have to leave the company to diversify your career.

summary: Citi still has to improve on motivating its employees
advice: Be more personal
pros: Job security and large company benefits.  They have 401k, dental, medical, and vision benefits.  I'm not complaining about my salary either, considering the amount of effort and time i'm putting in my position.  I haven't been laid off yet, which is a plus to being in back office.
cons: Poor leadership, communication, and career advancement.  There's this wall that exists between me and my manager, and I absolutely hate it.  He's not personal at all, and I wish he could be more supportive and caring towards me.  I feel like another ant in this huge company, and sometimes I wish it can be a little smaller with all the benefits still there.

advice:
To work through their reorg and communicate with their employees. 
 Upper management shouldn't have taken bonus when a majority of workers got very small bonuses or not all.  To recognize and try to keep talent that adds value to their business.
pros: Citi has good health care and many choices of coverage.  Work/Life balance is fair because it affords you the time to attend to family needs when necessary.
cons: The lack of communication.  Citi lacks defined career paths and opportunities to expand a person's career.  For example, if you have a speciality and a unique skill set your opportunities are limited. In addition, obtaining information on how your new job titled (during the recent reorg) was determined and what KSA are required for that position.

summary: Citi is a company for now, not forever
advice: To allow employees that excel to succeed
pros: Mangement is compotent in my department, and allow you to take time off usually when you want, as long as your back up is not off.  Vacation time is pretty good and you can earn an extra few days for giving to charity
cons: No advancement, no raises, no bonuses.. health care plan was just modifed and costs increased so it was like receiving a pay cut... Bonuses are non-existent.. upper management does not allow numbers to be released, so they tell you that you are doing a good job and are ahead of last year, but you never know by how much... advancement is tough, and raises are not there

summary: Lack of leadership and interest in creating a unified culture that motivates the workers.
advice: Retire and let better blood take the wheel before the company goes down like the Titanic
pros: I can say with openness that the only good thing about Citi or Citigroup right now would be the fact that you get a pay check, as small as it is; oh yea insurance.  Other then that you will have a J-O-B with minimal pay
cons:
The board of directors have lost vision and direction, and are unwilling to make the "real" decision required to "right the ship".  The executive group "click" are not truly interested in fixing any of the real issues, instead they are only interested in ensuring they get their bonus, which they have NOT earned.

If I were in charge I would remove the cancer from the executive team, clear the deck all the CxO's at corporate and sector levels as well as their 1st, 2nd and 3rd Lieutenants.

advice: Break the Company up as soon as possible.  Wait.  Too late.
pros: Prestigious large money center bank.  Opportunities for exposure to other areas not available in smaller institutions.
cons: Dysfunctional management with minimal insight into actual banking operations.  The institution was literally too large due to ill throughout and/or mistimed acquisitions.  As a result, Numerous systems existed that did not "talk" one another.  Moreover, there was minimal inter-departmental cooperation.  This often led to mid-level management being unable to deliver acceptable level of customer support.  Compounding this issue was that certain areas were ofter moved from the Consumer Bank to the Investment Bank with little thought to the actual impact on the business unit itself and ultimately its clients.

summary: Not the best place for junior people interested in wealth management.
advice: More meaningful feedback would have been better.
pros: Citigroup has a large network and there are many opportunities for advancemenet across divisions within the company.
cons: LOTS of bureaucracy. Also, the feedback wasn't always great. People who weren't doing so well were never told explicitly. More transparency would have helped. I feel like many times my boss gave me things to do soley for the purposes of keeping me busy. Many of the projects had little to no added value. Furthermore, as a junior person within the company I was asked to do some extremely tedious, non-business related tasks. One time a more senior employee gave me a bunch of receipts for his personal expenses and asked me to create a spreadsheet.

advice: Office politics have are taken to an extreme at Citi.  In an organization so large, groups are constantly fighting over resources and hording information.  There is no sense of teamwork among the groups.  With moral sinking based on the massive layoffs the protectionism is only getting worse.
pros: Citigroup hires really bright people with big ideas and drive.  The compensation package is excellent.
cons: There is no work life balance at Citi.  My colleague had to cancel a trip to Italy for a project and he had already paid for the tickets.  The other issue at Citi is politics.  Turf wars are  common practice and institutional knowledge is something that is guarded and shared only when absolutely necessary.

summary: The steping stone in a banking career.
advice: Try to understand the community in which you are operating, the situation of your customers can be different in every area.  So, it would be favorable to adjust and offer the appropriate products that most fulfills the needs or interests of your comunity.
pros: The best of working for Citibank, is the experience one can gain from such an aggresive sales environment.  If banking and sales is something you want to do as a career, then working as a senior teller can give you both the choice between going into operations management or move on as a personal banker.
cons: If you are someone that has a hard time adjusting to change, then the current changes going on Citibank might stress you out a bit.

summary: Talk about meritocracy is just talk
advice: Invest in the existing staff. Much effort and money is spent surveying the staff, writing plans to address survey results, and then recruiting new staff because foundational concerns like compensation and quality of benefits are not addressed. Instead, focus on compensating and retaining quality staff.
pros: Flexible Work benefits, generous time off package, company daycare, global mobility options, and plenty of work from home positions in IT.
cons: 2011 will be the third year without significant raises or bonuses, even for high performing VPs. If you do decide to work for Citi you will hear a lot of talk about meritocracy, unfortunately it is just talk. Merit increases will not be given in 2011 once again, regardless of performance rating.

advice: Cut the number of people on top and give us back people at the branch level. The level of understaffing puts so much strain on the manager that he/she cannot actually do their own work. FIX RAINBOW. It doesn't work at all. ECRM is a joke and the book of business doesn't work either.
pros: Worldwide locations, you can move up a bit and then go to another bank. They also have the google wallet and new ATMs and  they are in 7-11
cons:
The systems don't talk to each other in the retail bank
They will tell you that you can grow in the company, but then employ people from outside of the bank
When you get promoted, they only bump your salary max 5% and then bring people in that make way more than you do.
They say that they care about service, but they fired all of the service officers and cut the number of tellers at every branch.

advice: you are building a house with a foundation of sand as long as you refuse to treat your core work force with respect and consideration.
pros: Great benefits, some real talent in middle management.
cons: uppper management completely misses the concept of noblesse oblige, and since they seem to think of themselves as nobility, this is a problem. They make arbitrary changes mid stream, leak the info to every company under the sun, but fail to inform their employees what is going on. Employees are shuffled around into positions they never applied for and would never have accepted if given any input into their own lives. Upper management feels that the people who do the bulk ofhte in the trenches work areirrelevant,  expendable, and replaceable in that order.

advice: This is to any call banking call center. I believe it is better to focus on quality of calls rather than quantity of them. I would rather have someone have less calls per day and more time on the phone. These people are talking to Customers & doing their jobs. When they are forced to make more calls, they are so worried about that #, quality of time & quality becomes second to that. I have seen people push for the "phone time & call minimum", they are focused on calling no answers and leaving messages in order to accomplish that.
pros: I loved everyone that worked there. My Managers, Co-Workers, etc., & eventually work at home.
cons: The Company left Phoenix & I was unable to relocate.

summary: Nice Company to work with on an overall basis.
advice: please look into the reasons for transfer request than sticking to your rigid policies...for the better growth of employees and maintaing your goodwill....bec if end is not well..it leaves a sour taste
pros:
Citi is internationaly recognised comapny with Nice culture, work life balance, good training for employees and also provides a good background to work with experienced and talented people. They also offer good pay pakage depending upon the profile and candidates cirriculam vita.

It provides you a great exposure and ability to find your inner talent during the work process.
cons: If you are less than a year then possibilty for  a transfer to other team or dept. is null....which leaves you in a mess....by spoiling your career graph.

summary: See your physician before accepting the job
advice: Be more transparent. Learn what your agents actual  responsibilities are. Stop permitting abusive tactics by agents that are detrimental to your goal.
pros: They give you a little money, health, dental, and vision benefits.
cons: Toxic environment caused by lack of accountability from  management and senior  management. Employees are rewarded for avoiding doing their actual jobs, due to the political environment. Opportunities for advancement are constantly thwarted, and external talent will always be recognized before internal. Managers and especially operations managers do not ensure equal treatment of employees or take concerns seriously. No real focus on quality of service or training. Changes to products and service are not based on client or employee experience or feedback. Many agents have to take antianxiety or antidepressant medication to function in their roles day to day. Bed bugs are a constant threat and the bathrooms are never clean. Pay is not at all competitive.

advice: Take a look at the goals you are pushing out to your sellers.   In order to meet the goals there could be a chance that someone to could act unethically.  Not the culture you teach at all.  But desperation will cause folks to do things they are not wanting too.
pros: Great staff and customers were top tier and amazing to work with.   Very family sensitive and benefits are available the first day of hire.
cons: Sales goals were not in tune with local economy.  They reduced the sales force when I was let go and the one person left is still struggling with goals.   It was not due to lack of drive or effort.

advice: Keep moving in the direction you are going.  Be fair when it comes to resource allocation.
pros: The leadership of the organization in which I belong are visionary.  They want to move the organization in a positive direction.  Working remotely if your organization permits it,  but you must be accountable for your actions and time.  If abused it will be taken away.  Great benefits, health, 401K, and time off!
cons: As with any large company it can be a machine from time to time.  Coming from smaller companies it took time for me to adjust to large corporate timeframes.  Since team is geographically dispersed it would be good to have face to faces on some occasions with other team members

pros: The only good thing about working at Citibank is that other companies look at your resume in a positive way for having worked there.
cons: Micromanagement in the retail environment. Conference calls ever 2 hours in Washington DC market.  Ridiculous sales goals and service expectations with horrible metrics.  They measure the surveys with answers 1-10, where anything below 9 is automatically a 0.  If you get a low score, they embarrass you in front of all the staff.  Also, staffing issues. AKA, they don't care if you are understaffed, they still expect you to perform at a high level.  When people call out, they don't give support in the branches.  When someone quits, they don't act quickly to get someone else.

advice: I would stress to upper management to look deeper in the branches and call centers to under stand what the works are really needing. I know that upper management has the best intentions to make the bank money but there is a right way and a wrong way.
pros: I love the idea to make a global name that is recognized across the world and to make sure the service one receives in one place is the same as is in other please.
cons: Citibank is very fast to cut peoples' jobs with out any word.  They are mostly about their money and status no matter what will do what ever it takes to maintain the a global image.

summary: I enjoy my co-workers and my boss. Feel like I am a member of the team. Benefits are great.
advice: Trust your employees to do the right thing and you will get better loyalty.
pros: Great benefits, chance to move up.  Management wants employees to do better.  Upper management can be approached as long as all are on the same page. Dress code is fair and reasonable. Vacation and unplanned time are good.
cons: One, the salary is low for what they ask.  You are micromanaged to the max. High turnover due to demands of call times and being customer service. They get on you about using unplanned time. Reviewing of calls does not take place in a timely manner nor do reviews. No merit raises but once a year.

summary: Good people, hard work and no work/life balance
advice: Management should start to value their employees by giving them comp days or salary revues.  They are going to burn out at the rate that they are working.  Eventually something will give and either it will be quality of the work or employees leaving the firm.
pros: Because of the size of the firm, there is always room for advancement and growth.  There are a lot of very sharp people and almost all of your peers and teammates are pulling together for a common goal.
cons: They pay you as little as they can get away with.  Work/life balance is non existent.  Be prepared to work long days, frequently into the night and on weekends with no additional comp.

advice:
Good place to work overall.  Id work there again.

Comment on VOE:  Great that you do them, they are a real plus.  Note that if an area has a low VOE score, there is a solid reason why and you need to replace the person getting the score.  It takes several years to "escape" from a bad manager/senior manager and as people leave, the scores may look like they are improving temporarily.

 If very senior managers aren't actively doing their own exit interviews (at least a phone call), they don't really know what's going on.
pros: Good people.  Good work.  Good company.
cons: Middle management may have poor leadership skills.  Despite "Voice of the Employee" attempt to get upper management feedback on their middle managers.

summary: irritations of a teller at citibank
advice: the whole system is a mess. banking products are overrated. stop with the detailed surveys. invest in faster hardware for efficient service.
pros: pay is good-$15 with no banking experience. hours.
cons: too much emphasis on the customer surveys. rude clients are called up by survey company and if youre in the red management will observe you daily and will critique every little thing. i used to enjoy going to work but now its just one big anxiety attack. at the end of the day I'm not going to connect with every client. some people are just plain cynics. also unrealistic sales goals even for my slow branch. and the the stupid vcic check imaging machine is a mess. let back office do all of that. :/

advice: Practice good ethics in dealings with liens and employees.
pros: Hard to get fired and you don't have to produce.
cons: Unethical practices perpetrated against the client and employee, even if a borrower can bring their account current within the month citi's management requires you to place them on a deferment so they can get the $1000.00 from the tax payers, the Irving Texas location had 250 work outs in January 2013 which netted them $250,000.00 for the month , just from federal handouts, and their stated goal is to double that amount over the next two months.  I came to this department promised many thing and out and out lied to. I just purchased a home a few months ago, I got my loan from Wells Fargo.

advice: Do what you say and say what you mean!  AND mean something - stand for something.  Strive for consistency.  Employees in non-revenue generated businesses shouldn't be penalized when it comes to increases.  Remeber morale is important to success for ALL OF US, including the stockholder.
pros: Company offers good benefits to employees, has a flexible work program, and employee networks. Globality offers much opportunity for motivated employees.
cons: Because the company is so large, it's hard to get some things done - cohesiveness isn't as strong as it should be.  Company morale is slipping to an all time because the focus is on the stock prices and not raises.  Expense management is the focus, but money continually is wasted on needless process and superferlous processes.

summary: Great place to work, but depends on the project
advice:
E-mail oriented development is not a good design process for software.
We had a horrible manager in my last months at the company who badmouthed who was not around. It was sickening and mass complaining to the HR did not seem to have any effect. The team's mood was horrible and people were lacking motivation because of that. It was a bad move to not act on this in a timely manner.
pros: I work in IT where almost everyone was friendly and brilliant. Many interesting projects and advanced technologies is use, and lots to learn. Great work life balance.
cons:
Internal processes are inefficient. Even a 4 year old PC upgrade required months of waiting.
Thousands of e-mails exchanged every day, it was overwhelmingly bad.

summary: Division or people you work with defining your experience at Citi
advice: Training and work-life balance
pros:
Citi has a global presence and may be able to provide better global transfer opportunities and experiences.
Depending on whom you work with, right experiences may be obtainable.  Work-life balance may be possible for certain divisions only when working with right people/management who care.
cons: For certain divisions, work-life balance is hard to come by; there are almost non-existing bonuses for AVP and positions below; and it is hard to get time off especially when working for more than one manager. Promotion is not based on performance evaluation alone.  It is only possible if there is an opening for the next-level up and candidates have to be aware of the opening and apply online in time, etc.

advice: Choose better people to promote. Don't use experience as the main factor, use talent.
pros: Citi has good benefits and competitive salaries. I did not think that the work was that demanding or challenging, which may be a pro or con, depending on what you are looking for. There is definitely room for career growth and plenty of opportunities globally.
cons: Citi's management is mostly incompetent. They make poor decisions and fail to listen to their employees. Also there were a lot of lay offs/restructurings while I was there. Mostly people in NY were being laid off and jobs were moving to low cost areas. Training/onboarding new employees was another weakness of Citi's. Also the bureaucracy inhibits efficient work from being accomplished and prevents innovative changes from being implemented.

summary: Currently working as a Corporate Service Manager with CITIBANK NA, GURGAON possesses 6.5 years rich experience
advice: Management should consider the existing employee knowledge of understanding the processes and should revise the salary as given to the new freshers to whom the employee mentor. Also, the freshers hired are offered best packages as compared to the ones who are maintaining the stability with the company.
pros: An innovative and unique thinker which help to the best of my ability for maintaining effective customer service for all internal and external customers by utilizing excellent, in-depth knowledge of company processes and programs
cons: As compared to the market and other new joiners at work, it feels extremely demotivating comparing the annual package after providing the loyalty of approx. 7 yrs to the organization.

advice: 1. Bring in a Six Sigma team!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! For the love of all that is holy!  2. Give EVERYONE a chance at moving up who wishes to work hard and wants to move up.  3.  Bring back working from home.  This is the modern era.  Please get with it!
pros: Lots of job opportunities for which  to submit resumes, within company.  NOTE: I cannot appropriately and accurate rate Senior Management as I have not personally met any of them.
cons: It's rare you will get anything other than a lateral move or downgrade.  Out of 300 submissions for jobs, I had (wait for it) THREE interviews, and only one was with this particular site.  Others were for other company sites.

advice: Adopt the peer review system where the performance of employees can be more transparent and give more frequent promotion opportunities based on the performances. Also, avoid giving too much power to the HRs who are trying to hire the employees for cheap; rather, give more power to the employees and managers who can chase after the best employees and give what they deserve
pros: Excellent 401K plan (6% match), good medical and life plans, very flexible schedule (WFH), supportive management teams, tons of training and volunteer opportunities
cons: Lack of a bonus since the economic downturn in 2009 crash, somewhat inefficient promotion opportunities, bad team culture due to hiring many under-qualified contractors and employees than the best talented employees, only partially competitive pay salary

advice: In terms of communication The company has been with all employees transparent and efficient. Different newsletters, emails, collaborative site. Management are taking all necessary actions to put the firm up and creating an environment of great place to work. No advice at this point.
pros: Great company, always with employee engagement and great environment, big organization to do career development across multiple functions and areas, diversity is amazing, people with different backgrounds make the company rich in knowledge
cons: In my 6 years with the company so far haven't find much cons, maybe parking space, since there are 2 campus in different areas, one of the campus has small cafeteria but the building is temporarily and they are extending the land so in the future shouldn't be a problem

summary: Showcase yourself and you will get opportunities.
pros:
1. Several lines of business which gives opportunities to work in technologies of choice through internal mobility
2. Flexible timings.
3. work from home facility.
4. Yearly Bonas
5. Public holidays (More that what you got in school :-))
cons:
1. Politics in all aspects, only completing your work is not the case, you have to handle and convince all the related teams about what you are doing as everybody gives their own opinion and you have to make sure that you get the credit otherwise chances are your lead or other related team will take away the credit for your work.
2. Formal dress code
3. No insurance coverage for family
4. Repetitive work if you are on the same team.
5. Too much vendor intervention and at times you may feel like vendors overpower you.

advice: Slow down. Get you know your staff stop playing favoritism. Men are not superior.
pros:
Love this company when I started wotking for them. They then merged our dept with another one whose staff was loding their jobs. The agreement was they had a contract to complete the work until a set date then they'd get laid off. 
 The managers agenda was to have his team learn my teams jobs them lay us off. Their team was rifed from posting into other posoptions in the co. When my staff attempted to post they never got the job so we asked was was going on were they rifed?  Lies. So I left and attempted to come back have proper notice. I believe I'm blacklisted.
cons: Some managemt they don't understand managing.

advice: Keep up the good work.
pros: We have good benefits, 401K Match, and good training within to take advantage while in company.  Flexible work arrangements and good old fashioned managers.
cons: Sometimes too big of a corporation to get procedures changed but can suggest changes anytime.

summary: Great company benefits but nothing to crow about.
advice: Value your longstanding employees, make efforts to retain them, and listen to employee feedback--especially those who know how processes run and possess the technical know-how.
pros: Citi is a very fast-paced, energetic place to work in. People take pride in what they do. Internal movement is encouraged in order to help employees find a job that best fits their strengths. Annual leave is generous at well over twenty (20) days. Additional benefits include a system for claims for various categories such as eyewear, sporting equipment, as well as other medical claims.
cons: The yearly bonus is less than a month for most employees. Oftentimes, movement between roles is based on how popular/visible you make yourself as well as how good an impression you make on management.

summary: Lack of a consistent growth strategy frustrates employees.
advice: Decide whether this company wants to be a major player in retail banking in the US, then develop a concise strategy and stick with it.  Does Citi want to be a national bank or a mega player in two or three markets?  The lives of thousands of employees are impacted every day by the lack of vision and strategy, and phenomenal talent is leaving the bank either by choice or through job discontinuance actions.
pros: Combined compensation and benefits packages are very good.  Excellent 401K benefits package and tools to learn to manage the account are very good.
cons: No job security.  Inflexible approach to banking.  No clear vision for the future.  Focus is on cutting people and expense, not growing the business.

summary: good for short term and commission and bad for long term career development
advice: Provide more career development opportunity for personal banker
pros: it's pay better than other competitior (banks) in the same position as personal banker.  such as bank of america, wahington mutual, wells fargo bank.  The base salary is almost the same, starting out 40k dollars. but then the commission is monthly.  which give an opportunity for personal banker to get pay every month.
cons: The managers and co-workers at some location are very up-tight, not very helpful for new employees.  The training provide by the company isn't that great, but able to survivie.  On the job support from management is ZERO.  The managers will yell at you if you make a mistake, don't let you go to lunch, break.

summary: Try it - it has its good points.
advice: I think that all levels of management could focus more on connecting to their employees, beyond the core networks of folks that have worked together forever.  Reach out to other staff - there are lots of great people here.
pros: There seems to be some places in company that still have a good working environment but these are now rare.  The pressure that has hit the banking industry will probably make this even less of an occurance.  I worked at the Weehawken location my first year and totally loved it.  I think that they will be a good company again but it will be a tough couple of years.
cons: Sometimes the pressure to work "extra hours"  got a little out of hand.

summary: Lack of integration makes Citi a difficult place to find success.
advice: Citi needs to do a better job of integrating the various business segments.  There is a tremendous amount of talent not being utilized to its full capacity which is preventing the organization from performing as a global leader.
pros: As a large organization with a tremendous amount of locations and resources, opportunities to work in other states in various departments are available.  The organization also values work/life balance and encourages time off along with providing flexible working conditions.
cons: Due to frequent restructuring at the senior management level, the strategy is continuously changing.  Coupled with the various silos created from all the M&A, the lack of cross-communication can make it extremely difficult to share best practices and network with internal talent.

summary: A challenging work environment in which personal loyalties are often rewarded over job performance.
advice: The VOE is not a safe tool for employees to express their true feelings without fear of reprisal, and effective change will never come as a result of it.
pros: Opportunities to learn and work with some talented individuals. When times were good, pay raises and bonuses were awarded annually.  A decent 401k plan.
cons: Department managers did not always reward performance.  There was no such thing as a "safe" environment to express your disagreements or concerns with their management style or any issues you had with how the department was run.  Managers used company layoffs as a means of weeding out anyone who didn't share their views.

advice: make up your mind, show that you value your employees, and do no block your hard working reps from getting a promotion because you can not retain your employees.
pros: flex time (when you can get it approved...) benefits, paid time off, coworkers. they are always hiring.
cons: DO NOT TAKE A SALES POSITION! management changes their mind every other day on what they want you to do, things that you sell mysteriously just disappears and good luck on trying to get your commission. once they have made enough people mad and they quit your locked into your position for over a year why they rebuild the department back (out of a class of 25, 2 will last (i am one of the 2) for a couple years).

summary: The culture has changed for the worst
advice: If you're trying to be more customer-centric then take care of your own!!! Find better ways of motivating your employees to excel in customer service instead of striping them from their hard earned salary through punishment.
pros: -Great team (may vary), Vacation, Benefits
cons:
Where do I begin?
-Unrealistic goals trickling down from upper management to branch staff
-Compensation is a joke in relation to the stresses that tellers deal with
-"Quarterly bonuses" (if you're lucky to get them) 
-Rewarding Employees with ThankYou Points (Don't think that I can pay bills with Thankyou points)
-Customer satisfaction scores tying in with branches' overall compensation (anything less than an 80% avg is considered even if cust. wrote down that the service was extraordinary)
-Low Morale 
-Absolutely no overtime!!!
-Major disconnect with upper management

summary: Citi is very silo'd.  If you work in one part of the bank, it is difficult to change to another part of the bank.
pros: Excellent benefits; ability to transfer to different parts of the world; from a policy perspective they encourage mobility
cons: Management is Silo'd and people are very territorial.  They want to keep talent for themselves.  It is less stressful to leave the company and comeback to another part of the company than to try and move internally.  Ironically, philosophically the organization encourages mobility.  The culture is very darwinistic.  You will grow fast if you amaze the right people but you can also be stuck with some one who doesn't want you to grow because they need your talent where you are.

summary: Great place for recent college graduates to get feet wet but vicious corporate culture....
advice: Hire more people, standardize your processes and mature the organization.
pros: Able to work from home; salary is decent for Tampa; great title and company for your initial resume start.
cons: People are overworked regularly due to lack of capacity planning; co-workers gossip non-stop about trivial things and are all on edge due to the aforementioned; technology is old and disorganized; and professional decorum and civility are at an all time low with regular emotional break downs at meetings and cursing. AML also does not have a standard business process so the quality of your work varies with whose eyes its before and how your manager is feeling.

summary: Good place to work for those who thrive in an ever changing environment
advice: Be more decisive; even in the dynamic industry you are in.  Perhaps under Jane's leadership this will happen.  Would save a fortune in throw-away work.
pros: There are some wonderful, dedicated people at Citi to work with. If you appreciate working in an environment where there is a LOT of change, this could be the place for you.  There isn't time for complacency, which I found highly appealing. This also gives you an opportunity for a great deal of learning.
cons: Sometimes you feel as though you are spinning your wheels due to the constant change.  Some folks are not cut out to work in this environment; if not...this isn't the place for you.

summary: If you can make it here, you probably can make it anywhere.
advice: Improve the culture more. Compensate the good soldiers better.
pros: Global footprint is its unique differentiator. No other bank has its reach-- from people to products to platforms. Very fast-paced and bottomline-driven. Very unique to feel the world at your literal fingertips.
cons: The bank caters to the triple A -- the large multinational, the large government client, the high net worth individual. If the client isn't in this category, the client isn't valued. So big and complicated, it is prone to many broken pieces that need constant fixing. In many cases, the pressure to deliver on revenues is so high, products are not built properly. Hence, the amount of re-work, fire-fighting and managing client escalations is very high.

summary: Lot of work pressure, unreasonable deadlines, No work life balance
advice:
Start thinking about employees. 
Keep realistic goals.
Be civilized
pros:
You get to see every sort of technology.
You work with lot of smart, energetic, dedicated but aggressive people
Work from home option only for certain teams. 
Good vacation package, good benefits.
cons:
You should spend lots of overtime at work. Management would not help in any way. Work is expected to be done all by yourself as an individual. No team work. Management is involved(sort of directly provokes) directly in conflicts within colleagues. 
Lots and lots of politics. You cannot survive with out developing very thick skin to tolerate. 
No salary raises. If there are, they are very low compared to the long hours you spend. 
Very bad work culture.

pros: Working in a great group with exposure to diverse projects and senior management.  Get good support from my senior leadership team.  They are great role models.
cons: Have been told I am doing the work of the next level (i.e. Director) for over a year although I have been top rated for the last 3 years, they won't promote me because there are no Director requisitions open in our area.   In general, it looks like I may need to leave my department or the company if I want to move ahead.  The irony is that there are many Directors that have no staff(I have 7 directs) and much less responsibilities yet they appear to grandfathered in.

summary: Very bad culture. No work ethics. No professionalism. No work life balance.
advice: get your management in place. try to retain people. give them on the job training. Do an introspection why people do not stay beyond the initial 5 months in Citi. There are no leaders to look upto. Money cant buy everything.
pros: Decent brand. In order to attract talent, they pay well but no hikes and bonus after that.
cons: Extremely high attrition. Not a good organization. No work life balance. No professionalism. No hikes and bonus. Hire and Fire policy. No work ethics. Extremely high politics. People even go for paycuts after citi, it is that bad. Experienced people with 10+ yrs of work experience too leave within a year. In first 5 months with citi, i was the oldest member of my team. Freshers, please do not start your career with Citi. You will never get the confidence in your career and they will ruin it.

summary: Focus on rebuilding a global financial services company
advice: Improve Business Intelligence; Engage Employees across the organization; Focus on the Customer; Delegate Authority to people closest to the customer; Eject Politicians and Build the Global franchise
pros: Global footprint, many people with a global mindset, respected by customers (more so in the emerging markets), broad spectrum of products and customer capabilities.
cons: Senior Management is unable to engage with the many dedicated and talented people. 'Who' you know seems to matter more than 'what' you know. Poor information systems leaves the management floundering in the dark. Opinions matter more than facts - politics and tribalism more important than abilities. Not customer centric at the global level, so the franchise is being neglected in preference for financial engineering.

summary: Great people, but disorganized, and lousy compensation/recognition
advice: Need to align the business and technology better. O&T make up about 1/2 the company, yet they are not treated with much respect. There is also way to much swirl at every level. Reorgs should be infrequent, as opposed to the norm. A firm strategy needs to be set and adhered to.
pros: Most of the people I work with are smart, selfless, and not political. There are opportunities to take on new roles, even in other departments. Management seems to be supportive of this.
cons: It is a very disorganized place which is constantly changing. Executive love PowerPoint, and it makes it difficult to get real work done. Compensation and recognition are not very good.

summary: Very good if you're lucky to have a supportive boss
advice: Listen to your staff and do your best to address their concerns. Be open to their ideas and fulfill promises. No empty promises, be honest.
pros: Benefits are good. They take care of people they like but you have to make sure your higher ups know just how good you are. Opportunities, financial and otherwise, were much better prior to the financial crisis.
cons: Teams are very lean which means sometimes it's hard to take time off (no back up). The organization structure, which is global, sometimes makes it very bureaucratic in decision-making or instigating change. Similarly, sometimes regional or global initiatives are forced into local business even if they don't have a culture fit.

advice: I think that they should listen to their employees on operations, because they are the ones actually working with the customers, and they should intervene when there are conflicts that need to be adressed the first time.
pros: Very flexible with schedules, great benefits, and pie job.  I enjoyed that I could go to school and work full-time, which is a luxury now.
cons: Management issues, no opportunity for growth, and you can easily get burned out.  The job was stressful because of your peers, not because of the actual job.  When the economy tanked, so did morale and management understanding that in our department, which was a LOSS department, collecting money was going to be harder than normal.

summary: It's tough being an analyst, but Citi was good for me
advice: +Should break up corporate and investment bank - currently together.  Most IBD analysts do not want to be working on corporate banking pitches - nor is it helpful for interviewing for PE, HF, Corp Dev or other traditional IBD exit opportunities
pros:
+ Global firm
+ Exposure to all financial instruments
+ Ability to move to different offices - both domestically and also internationally
+ Not as focused on which school you attended as other investment banks
cons:
+ Lost a lot of senior managers during the downturn as their equity became worthless
+ M&A often run by M&A team only with coverage providing support
+ Lacks prestiege of Goldman, Morgan - impairs exit opportunities
+ Long hours

summary: Hope to get a good manager
advice: Learn how to show respect, consideration and listen to your team.  Promote them, show gratitude.  When you see a manager who is incapable of managing a team; REMOVE THE MANAGER!!!!!
pros: Great Work/Life balance; great benefits and the fact it's a global company gives you opportunity to work in many areas and possibly relocate (depending your level of management)
cons: This company needs to make sure that a people manager at a minimum has PEOPLE skills.  Too many managers roaming this company that are clueless on how to manage people.  This can stunt your grown with this company because if your manager doesn't know how to voice how much you do...well you are pretty much screwed.

advice:
> Relook at your resource planning and structure. Stop ad-hoc hiring of people.
> Streamline your processes in your global operations. It is very messy and the obsolete and fragmented software only makes it worse. 
> Invest (even if it means biting the budget bullet) in an integrated software that combines all platform
> Have a proper project management team that actually plans in details before roll out and monitor the timeline during roll out
pros: Not a single that actually matters
cons:
> Good messaging from the top that does not translate to day-to-day actions
> Lack of funding for operations which are running on obsolete software and equipment
> Multiple dis-jointed software which are not fully integrated
> Poor project roll out management
> Very top heavy structure

advice: I don't expect upper management to ever change it's ways, this is banking after all.
pros: Fairly independent work environment, get your portion done each day and no one will bother you really. Pay is decent, nothing special unless you come in with above average work experience.
cons: Growing/moving pains as Citi pulls many roles out of NYC and moves to Buffalo. From what I've heard, they figured out they can pay someone to do the same job in Buffalo much less than someone in NYC. Rare to get a quality manager, most are overworked and extremely on edge/irritated. Advice: ask meaningful questions during interview to learn about your manager to see if you'd fit under their team.

summary: You learn a lot about office politics and the importance of brown nosing.
advice: Learn how to be proactive instead of reactive. Actually teach your employees how to do what's expected of them BEFORE penalizing them. Take some classes on ethics and business management in an effort to properly motivate your team without using scare tactics. Stick to your word and stop thinking people don't talk about the lies and false promises you spread.
pros: Great benefits and great pay.
cons: You can not trust HR to resolve issues, the management style is based on fear, intimidation, and condescension. Senior management is very fickle and have no idea how to develop, train talent, or retain talent. There is no work/life balance, and your personal business affairs will suffer.

summary: Citi is OK but struggling to find itself. Upper management changes too often and totally changes corporate direction.
advice: Find a corporate direction and stick to it.  Stop hiring Mid to upper level managers on 2-3 year contracts. Stop relaunching programs that failed in prior administrations.
pros: It's a well known firm with multiple positions and opportunities. It provides good benefits and competitive salaries. If they ever figure out what they want to be "when they grow up"poor  they might regain the respect of their employees.
cons: Poor management skills from middle management on up. Sales programs are instituted and closed before they realistically can be evaluated. Too much time is spent on counting widgets instead of developing relationships with clients. Very poor morale among employees.

summary: Citi India - Great Place to Work
advice: Keep up the HR policies, need to make the diversity program more broad based rather than just focusing on women employees as it is important to give equal opportunity and also to educate male employees on why some of the initiatives are important for them as well (esp. managers)
pros: Organization values talent, provides opportunity to grow, employee friendly, provides great options for mobility across business and geographically. Overall a great place to work
cons: It is no longer the top paymaster it used to be. Specifically due to India being one of the frontier markets, often Indian employees do not want to take on overseas role for lateral movements but only for larger roles leading to stagnation at top.

advice: More opportunities for personal growth in part-time positions is absolutely necessary. As a collector that routinely does full DCF analysis and values companies at school, I'd really appreciate the opportunity to offer more value to the company.
pros: I work part time, 20 hours a week, really relaxed environment, management will bend over backwards to accommodate my school schedule. They have been fantastic to me over the years, excellent benefits through Manulife, unbeatable for part-time work and flexibility.
cons: Monotonous job, negatively toned conversations with clients, its like you start on the wrong foot with every conversation, takes a lot of patience and the ability to be able to handle these clients and turn them into a positive conversation and relationship.

advice: Senior Mgmt should look to formulate policies to retain high performing employees, give them opportunities to relocate and grow within their global team, and not put hiring freeze in locations like U.K. & U.S., they should also provide salary increments every year otherwise there is no motivation
pros: Senior Management claims they need veterans-employees to stay back long term, good career opportunities are given to most people, transparency exist to greater degree, best inclusive work culture & work ethics
cons: No Salary increments for 3+ yrs, cost cutting on performance bonus, travels, relocation policy, sometimes managers & HR not focusing on employees with good performance ratings (especially within O&T) to provide them necessary growth could lead such employees exploring elsewhere and leaving the firm

advice: Recognize and reward your quality people.
pros: A lot depends upon your manager.  Assuming one has a good manager, one can almost define his/her role by taking on as much responsibility as possible.  If one has the aptitude and drive getting exposure to technology, quants, analytics, trading desks, etc. are all within reach.  Internal mobility is supported and encouraged.
cons:
Because this is a very large organization, there is a need to cooperate with many peripheral groups and coordinate schedules and project plans.  There are formal meetings and processes to accomplish this, but it also helps to have a good network of friends when you need favors.

Even top performers are seeing compensation compression in these difficult economic times.

summary: Good company, tough times for a big bank
advice: the bank is not doing anything to make employees feel confident that the bank will defend them if the regulators pursue legal action against them.
pros: Lots of bright people and a good culture of mentorship, lots of resources and established knowledge base/businesses, big client base, good work/life balance
cons: It's easy to get swallowed up in such a large company, lots of systems (technology support groups) are slow, out of date, ineffective, and Byzantine.  Harder to get promoted in the current environment.  Regulation has made a lot of seemingly innocuous activity potentially a violation, and you could be on your own to make legal arrangements if the regulators come after you or the firm

summary: Like very high stress, backstabbing, and low pay?
advice: they won't listen so why bother
pros:
they have really good medical benefits, fmla, short term disability, vision, and dental, 401k matching
worked with some great people
cons:
office politics
high turnover
very stressful environment
employees doing the right thing are treated shabbily even though co policy is "do the right thing"
work environment is very structured
expect to get backstabbed by management
watch out if you make a higher wage than entry level –they’ll find any excuse to get rid of you to save a buck (bonuses are hard to come by even if you qualify)
they promote advancement opportunities - but not many see any
wage is not median w/the rest of the USA or even locally

summary: ok for the start of your career
advice: Put more effort in training people. Since there is a high level of specialisation of the work, maybe consider introducing job swaps once in a while.
pros: You can really grow within the company if you are motivated enough to stay for a few years. Young and dynamic people, great contact with direct management. Relatively good pay.
cons: Not a very challenging job. I did not feel like learning a lot, work was very repetitive and boring.  I did not feel there was enough training provided and at times I felt that people did not really know what they were doing and why. Long working hours - it was never possible to predict what time would we finish the work.

advice: Back office in a bank draws a group of people who are really ambitious and want to move up.  Empowering these people to advance with new projects would be a big productivity booster.
pros: The company pays well, and management at my facility was good at enabling employees.  Overall, I thought my position was a good starting posting.  I left, but my friends who stayed moved up so getting stuck doesn't seem to be a problem if you are ambitious.
cons: Training wasn't what it could have been so being consistently curious is necessary.  Sometimes people in the upper levels would take things out on the back office, but there were no obvious issues there.

advice: Make sure if a person wants to stay WAH that they know they can instead of leaving it up in the air especially if it is working out.  Also maybe alternate days when employees have to be on the phone & working Queue apps. More Schedule options to where like day options where they could work through the week and alternate a day no the weekend every other just more options would be great....
pros:
Good start out pay 
Great to be able to WAH
cons:
Being stuck in front of computer for 10hrs with fear of getting in trouble or being made to go to office if you are NOT tied to the phone for those whole 10hrs.
Requirement of working the day after Thanksgiving, & always required to work at 1 day each weekend no matter what.
Having to wait so many years to have a shift changed which is hard on family time.

advice: Your staff is very knowledgable and has great ideas. Just because they aren't an officer of the bank doesn't mean they don't know their stuff. They are the ones whoses voices need to be heard in times of change.
pros: Benefits, especially vacation time, are good. Matching program is decent. Training program is good. Most staff members truly care about what they do.
cons: Longer your are there, the worse the pay. 10 years, 2 pay freezes, no bonuses, and 2-3% increases (if you are lucky) doesn't help pay the bills. They are quick to hire from the outside then to promote within in some areas and sometimes, that person is paid a lot more than the current, company savvy person they overlooked.

advice: Thank you! Great job!
pros: I've recently started at Citi and I feel right at home. Its great to be a part of such a massive, multicultural company. My immediate team is very friendly and supportive. They go out of their way to sort things out for me. I am allowed to work from home if I feel like it. The office building  is incredible, huge and uplifting. Even the security people in the lobby are lovely. Tonight for example on the way out they told me to be careful because it's very windy. Simple things but they do make you feel happier at work.
cons: I can't see any. I'll wait for a couple of years :-)

advice: Give regular constructive feedback throughout the year.  Stop treating your employees like children - this whole VOE thing really has gotten out of hand.  We spend more time trying to make people feel good than getting things done.  I'm an adult.  I don't need cakes and prizes, etc.  I need trust and guidance.
pros: The vacation allowance is unmatched.
cons: Politics, lack of ownership, inefficient use of time and resources, not smart when it comes to knowing who the customer is, mass marketing, no challenge, you are just a big cog in a big wheel.  Can't accomplish anything because of the multiple levels you have to go through and the lack of capable technology.

summary: Nice place to start a career but not to have a long-term career!
advice: Get rid of the antiquated force-ranked evaluation process. So demoralizing to the ranks. Take care of long-term employees who helped build the company.
pros: Work-life balance was available if you asked. Plenty of opportunities within organization for career and advancement.
cons:
Management turnover - too many high level managers leaving or taking new roles. It's like being on a boat without a rudder - trying to all paddle as hard as you can, but unable to get anywhere because you can't maintain a true direction!

Really screwed long-term employees by heavily touting stock ownership, forcing stock as part of bonus and then turning around and dilute shares by 90% with reverse split!

advice: Stop treating employees like robots/children.
pros: Pro:   Good benefits for this area.
cons: Phony employee recognition programs, feel good, touchy feely programs that become so rampant they don't mean anything. System is rigged so that the front line employee is always wrong, no matter how unrealistic management goals are.  Management pushes Great Customer Service, yet employee not given the time to GIVE good Customer Service. The VOE program (Voice of the Employee) has a lot of time spent on it, yet I did not feel that management really listened, just paid lip service. Also, the Morality of Citi being able to borrow from the Fed (even before its bailout) at low interest rates 2% or lower, and then turn around and lend that out at 28-30%  IS the definition of usury from the Bible, at least to me. I am glad to be gone from them.

pros: In the more than five, less than ten years I worked there my compensation more than doubled. Company kept us throughout the recession. Was eventually laid off with the rest of the staff, but received months of notice and a lot of support through the process. Contacts at this company actually helped me get my next job. Lots of opportunities to move around and advance, very supportive culture.
cons: Nothing really jumps to mind. Life after Citi makes it apparent how good you had it, because no job will ever do more to take care of you than they will. Note, I was a very low ranked employee. When the people on the bottom can say that, you're doing something right.

advice: Try to look at peoples work ethics, qualities and desires. Not just who they are or how they interview.
pros: Benefits and job security are good. Tuition assistance, and time off make working here a little more acceptable. Possibility to grow with the company if you know the right people.
cons: Working in a call center makes for long days that are always the same. Customer are rude because they don't have to look you in the face. If you are ok working with ungrateful customers regardless of the situation this is the job for you. Schedules usually are not great and it is a lot like being somewhere between a high school and a grade school. Job is easy and repetitive.

summary: Large Corp.  (Only worked for 4 months now)
advice: Focus on development of people in addition to recruitment.  Retention is also important. Or just compensate more.
pros:
Easy to go with the flow and keep on getting pushed up without actually contributing or adding much value (as is the case in most large corp)
