Good development for new analysts in programs, though HR sucks and you really have to ask for it.  Good job to start career.
cons:
The pros can also be seen as cons depending on what you're looking for. It isn't very challenging here. Sr. mgmt only care about their own metrics

I hear compensation sucks and am not expecting any large bonuses. I also hear climbing the ladder can also be tough after the analyst program / for non-program hires

summary: Can be frusturating place to work
advice: IT seems like the sweaky wheel gets the greese so promote based on merit
pros: Broad range of jobs if you want to explore opportunities,   Diverse employee population lends itself to working across many ethnic background and geographic areas.  The Global footprint allows for travel and opportunity as well and exposure to working with different regions.  Work can be what you make out of it.
cons: Silos exist and diversity in thinking can be a challenge as well as a benefit.  People do not seem to get rewarded for what they do but for what they say they do.  So a very pretentious incompetent individual could rise the ranks faster than a quieter more deadicated worker.

advice: Listen to your employees more to further your stated goal of attracting talented millennials.  We do not want to come into the office everyday to stay on the phone with people hundreds / thousands of miles away.  The water cooler is dead in this century.
pros: Benefits package is certainly appealing.  401(k) match at 6% plus 2% flat contribution annually.  Medical / dental have broad coverage, and vacation time is generous (6 weeks including holiday time).
cons: Management in private label credit card division is against remote work and more strict than corporate policy on number of remote days allowed before requiring executive VP approval.  In addition, high priority / high risk projects are often understaffed requiring clean-up weeks or months later.

summary: Works on perception employee should be careful about that in GDM Blr
advice: Please do not depend on perception. Please don't think bad performer is always bad and vice versa. People can improve, and improve to a great extent that is beyond your imagination.
pros:
Work culture is good
Pay and benefits are good and they pay well above Market level
Work is good and best thing is they encourage innovation
cons: Main problem: You should be cautious to save your reputation once you loose it you will be ignored, so will be your growth. Some ppl involve in bad politics for the same.  I mean a 3 can become 1 performance wise but perception wise he will be 3 because of his reputation.

summary: Good place if you are in the business side and not a support function.
advice: The size of the place makes it a problem for the individual contribution to make a significant impact on the larger scale. The recent problems in the market also make things a bit difficult.
pros: This is a very diverse bank which can provide great opportunities to in the area of choice. The UK staff are very professional and quite open. Especially if the individual is in the banking side rather than the support functions, it is very good.
cons: The size of the place makes it a problem for the individual contribution to make a significant impact on the larger scale. The recent problems in the market also make things a bit difficult.

advice: Know how the lowest ranking employee is doing his/her job. Watch them but do not criticise. If upper management would learn from how the lowest ranking employee is doing his/her job they would know what sort of procedures to put in place.
pros: Citi is obviously a massive organization. I felt fully supported and felt that I had access to multiple avenues where I could grow professionally.
cons: To be honest I have nothing to compare it to so I cannot say for sure that something is negative but I did feel at my time there that the openness between middle management and upper management was not as much as it should have been. There was quite of operational quirks that middle management knew that upper management had no clue about.

pros: Citi provided me with many opportunities for professional growth.  If you are a leader, they will give you new tasks or special projects.  The job was challenging and exciting, and Citi rewards good performance.  I was appreciated for the value that I brought to the company.
cons: Citi can have a very structured and hierarchical reporting/working structure even thought they have been working for years in breaking down barriers and silos.  New York staff tends to be competiive and individually focused. However, I do understand that in NYC operations, the stress may be greater.  Colleagues outside of New York are much more focused on teamwork, supporting each other and working together.

advice: Reduce the time spent with team meetings, hudles, leadership QA sessions. Implement better systems.
pros: If you work hard , if you are willing to work overhours  you can get promoted. I got to know helpful, talented people in the team and I met there my best teamleader. Required support from the management and training is provided to fulfill the daily tasks. Trainings are well-organized. Relative high salaries. Huge variety of social events.
cons: There are loads of social events, meetings, team huddles. Of course these can be pros as well but sometimes it is really frustrating that you don't know when to complete your daily tasks because of your tight meeting schedule. Poor, steril, 10 years old style work environment. Constantly changing team structure, processes and systems.

summary: Either you like it or you don't.
advice: Be honest, do what you say you'll do, and lose the favoritism for job advancement.
pros:
A.) Awesome benefits, hard to come by a company that provides benefits from day one. 
B.) Several site clubs to promote inclusiveness. 
C.) Gym on site for low price.
D.) Lots of good people to work with.
cons:
A.) Room for advancement isn't great, unless you have yourself in the right pockets. 
B.) There is a lot of office politics, to the point where some of the rules are nonsensical. 
C.) Sometimes you're forced to help other departments without any say in the matter, which can affect whether or not you work on holidays. 
D.) Unforgiving sick time policies. 
E.) Management, more so upper management, can be quite dishonest.

advice: Stop allowing employees to coast for years on end, update employee reviews to a modern system that’s about them and not company goals, offer real prescription drug coverage instead of prescription insurance through CVS Caremark which forces employees onto generic drugs delivered through the mail with no customer service help. Invest in US workers instead of hiring foreign nationals. US workers are the minority in my location.
pros: Salary, remote work, central office location
cons: Expensive healthcare  premiums with little coverage, coworkers who survive by doing the minimal amount of work, open office system that’s noisy and impersonal, too many H1B workers, over 75% of programmers and testers are off shore. So cheap. They cutoff the hot water in the restrooms at my location to save money.

advice: When I was there, you lost a quarter of your analysts and about half of your associates. Focus more on developing skills, providing access to necessary resources, and treating your associates as though they are work keeping. I loved the responsibilities of the job, but I got sick of being cussed out, talked down to, and abused by my analyst. Given that so many of my colleagues left despite a decent paycheck, I don't think my interpretation of the situation is unique.
pros:
Scope of work 
Dynamic responsibilities 
Access to doctors and researchers 
Ability to attend conferences
Many great people therer
cons:
Lack of resources (e.g. no access to medical articles and limited access to financial data)
Unclear expectations from mid-level bosses
Analysts treat associates like garbage
Relatively low salary for job

advice: Work on automating processes and updating technology. Revisit the remote work policies. Yes, there are benefits to some teams to working in office, however asking others to drive in rush hour traffic multiple times per week just to wander around the “over subscribed work environment” looking for an open desk and log on to zoom calls  is arbitrary and contrary to your work-life balance message.
pros: Forward-thinking corporate culture, diversity and inclusion, frequent promotion and development opportunities, good benefits, respectful workplace
cons: dated technology significantly impacts productivity, no openness to remote work even for those whose teams are not in the same office, wages and raises are not in line with inflation, HR processes are extremely backlogged and slow, very heavy and strict on compliance

advice: Although I don't agree with the way the company is run, I don't have any advice per se.
pros: There is excellent in-house training resources...as long as one takes the initiative to look for them.  Management pays more than lip service to the option of telecommuting and flexible work options, which is nice.
cons:
Let's be honest, it's a little embarrassing to have to admit that I work at this train wreck of a company!  In addition, the company is such a behemoth, that everything is so stratified and separated, which makes for an abundance of red tape.  There is a lengthy conference call for even the most innocuous of matters.  
The benefits and pay scales are paltry in comparison to similar financial services firms.

summary: Good for IT people who don't enjoy working close to technology.
advice: Pay more attention to the people who are in the trenches and a bit less to these who justify their existence by number of conference calls invitations sent or documents generated.
pros: With a bit of luck you can participate in large-scale IT projects. Working with globally distributed teams can be satisfying. The carrier path can be good if you are interested in management.
cons: A lot of bureaucracy and red tape. People are too often treated as resources. The management elitysm can also sometimes get irritating. There is definitely not enough communication between teams - people tend to hide behind processes and often focus on finding an excuse not to get involved with given initiative.

pros: There are some good people who work at Citi and if you are in the right location, you can have a plethora of job opportunities and experience (New York and Florida are ideal).  Good benefits.
cons: Very little diversity among company seniors and execs, many of whom have been around for 20+ years, can be very brash with "subordinates" and carry large egos.  If you are not in a particular demographic, you may not have much possibility for advancement.  Lots of ethical issues yet in response to the guilty pleas and fines, there are no leaders exiting.  Leaders often commit to deadlines sans input from team and end up requiring folks to work 12 - 14 hour days.

advice: Replace the MD by someone more sophisticated and that has a better understanding of emerging strategic risks.
pros: Lots of opportunities to learn, very large financial institutional with tons of opportunities for promotion and development, good pay & benefits. Good and motivated team members from diversified backgrounds.
cons: Citi is due to its size a slow moving cruise ship, and therefore strategic management vision is needed. Unfortunately, the senior executive manager in charge  (RZ = MD of Banking Book Portfolio Management) is not very sophisticated, and has no real understanding of current issues affecting the banking book. He still uses old school risk management techniquesrelying solely on limits and diversification; no proactive management with a lack of focus on impact liquidity shortage on banking book, extreme emerging risks, systemic default chains, credit transfer pricing, etc. The MD maintains an ivory tower mentality with no real reach-out to the business partners and other stakeholders.

pros: Professional environment, ACTUAL care and concern for the clients and customers, Fantastic benefits, amazing ways to give back to the community, no DRAMA (finally a job without one!) , teamwork and helping one another here is definitely a big thing, we look out for each other! Every day is a good learning experience, there is no blatant backbiting or tearing each other apart.
cons: Work/Life Balance is very off, all of my life is pretty much devoted to this job...I'd love it if I could get more time to spend with my friends and family and time to get things done (However, Citi does its best to provide that if they can, and they usually can most of the time).

summary: Credit Judge for No Preset Spending Limit cards
advice: Keep up the good work.  You made it a satisfying place to work.  It was great to have the support system and the excellent training program.  It was fun!
pros: Friendly, great training program, good benefits, good people to work for and with.  Good supervisors, good feedback on work.  Always someone willing to help if you have questions.
cons: Schedules were not the greatest but they weren't the worst either.  Working 4 10 hour days was hard at first but once I got used to it it was great because I was commuting 40 miles one way to work so it was less for gas usage.

advice: The program is large and very impersonal and interns don't really want to work at the Bank everyone just wants offers to shop around.  The program needs to be more supportive at the overall level and not completely dependent on desk you are assigned to and very inexperienced human resources group.
pros: Many different sales and trading areas to choose from and large presence in most markets
cons: Not a very collegiate environment for interns relative to other big banks, starts with human resources being very impersonal and experience is very dependent on what rotations you end up with, which you have very little control over.  Although they ask what rotations you are interested in, they don't assign you to them.

summary: Excellent financial service firm to work for
pros:
- Good pay
- Work/life balance
- Free transport facility to anywhere in Pune (although it's a pain for few remote or far-away areas)
- You'll get to dive in some of the latest technologies (for most departments) and the learnings will be fantastic
- You get to drive the vendor to deliver tasks and projects
- Work with fellow employees, who also have been through very rigorous recruitment processes
- A great brand for other investment banks (I could get in to other captives very easily given my experience at Citi)
cons:
- Very hierarchical organization, you need to get approvals for petty tasks
- Not very dynamic, employee mobility may be limited
- Graduate Trainees will be honored more than the other employees

pros: Great benefits, perks, and environment.
cons: Yearly raises don't exist so you better get every penny you can going in! Lots of obstacles and catch 22's when trying to move up from within. They have programs, and things set up to appear helpful for growth, but they are for saving face, and should be taken at face value kind of like a fully stocked grocery store in North Korea. As an example I went for a promotion in a different department; they told me I needed a cert to move to that department, I asked if I could get tuition reimbursement or help obtaining that cert. They replied they could only reimburse the cert if I was in that department.

advice: Try to get teams involved in the analyst program who will use the analyst as much as possible, some teams trundle analysts to the side which cause them to have poor experiences.
pros: The Technology Analyst program at Citi allows recent grads to have a decent variety of experiences within Citi in software. Citi has nice culture, people are generally very agreeable. If you get placed on the right team, you can get great experience.
cons: There are also a decent amount of teams that are not great to be placed on, it is difficult to control how this happens, so experiences can be hit or miss. (I personally know some who would not give the Technology Analyst Program at Citi this rating)

advice: Make it easier to move around in this company.  It is very difficult to figure out what the next logical step up should be and in addition, advancement seems to be based less on what you know than who you know.
pros: Large company means better chances at being able to advance career without having to switch companies.
cons:
Working for a large bank means you're viewed as more of a cog in the machine, rather than an individual worker.  Common practice here is to hire a large quantity of employees to tackle high volume but then once the volume diminishes, conduct layoffs in response.  
Working mortgage means job stability is often dependent on how the overall market rates are doing.

summary: Asset Servicing (Corporate actions) Germanics and Iberia
advice: Personalised training plans on demand, more direct communication with the employees, more feedback.
pros: Good location, Enthusiastic colleagues, gain experience in basic activities in Corporate actions on an entry level after graduation.
cons:
No training provided at all: I had no experience in the finance sector, so it was hard for me to pick up all the knowledge on the go while being under constant pressure. It was a struggle as the management did not provide any support at all.
The policy by Citi is to hire young enthusiastic people and spoil them all instead offering some improvement. Does not make any sense to me!
Hugh fluctuation due to such issues in the Germanic corporate action bay.
Be aware, management is dangerous!

advice: Senior managers need to balance the need to have process with lightening the burden that it creates for the employees.
pros: If you like fast paced work, this is the place to be.  The *vastness* of the network (infrastructure) allows you to experience things that you will not  experience elsewhere.  Also, the work life balance is EXCELLENT.
cons: The sheer amount of emails you get everyday can, and is, very daunting.  You really have to be disciplined to stay on top of it.  Also, sometimes, people use the "process" to slow down projects.  As they say:  "You can't fire someone for following the process"  But it can be tough to get initiatives through.

advice: Fix the products and services they are crappy. The customers hate it. The employees hate it. It's outdated, it doesn't compete, and it needs to be revamped.
pros: The pay was great and the people there were great overall. Opportunity to move up if you are liked and if you are not liked then you are talked about in "secrecy." However, like any job if you come in and work hard and leave then your day isn't so bad.
cons: The products are somewhat crappy so be prepared for a lot of customer complaints. The websites barely work and the employees' systems often crash. There is always sometimes of gimmick or catch with the credit cards and it upsets the customers off. Be prepared for an ear full everyday.

advice: Treat your employees like people and maybe they would be productive. It's something that's been known to work.
pros: Good incentives (quarterly bonus and sometimes a gift card), most of my co-workers were very nice
cons: Was treated very badly by my supervisor for no reason other than she was a miserable person, which ultimately led to me resigning. Health insurance is awful for anyone with a medical condition who goes to the doctor regularly; I ended up with a bill that took me over 6 years to pay off. Constant pressure on the tellers to make sales referrals, in person and on the phone. If we didn't meet our goals, we were lambasted for it, many times in front of our co-workers.  WE ARE TELLERS, NOT SALESPEOPLE.

advice: If you want people to work well for your clients, then be available when they have concerns and questions. You need more trainers handy for OJT questions and  have training systems work the same as real world systems..
pros: Benefits if you stay long enough, upward mobility in a year, bonuses on sales
cons: I had serious ethics concerns so I left. They tell you a 6 month learning curve to do your job perfectly but put you on the phone working with client accounts in a matter of a few weeks , telling you you are doing great while you are managing them incorrectly. The training computers do not work the same way as the real world computers so "training" is often times wasted time and ineffective.

advice: I really have something to say, but what management? The management has left and managing other firms now.
pros: Its a brand name, which means you can leverage it for finding another employer like GS, JP; however, this is less likely now given the internal degradation.
cons:
1. VERY VERY LONG hours: Citi never sleeps is the company motto and how  we lived in research. There was no weekend, no time for family  (mine forgot that i exist)
,  and the worst, YOUR WILL NOT GET time to study for CFA or other professional designation. 

2. My boss changed 3 times. Something is going wrong upstairs, but the people at upstairs talking of company loyalty while leaving the company. 

3. Salary growth is really really low. 

4. Don't get sick! 

5. Management Associate program is THE MAIN pipeline to boardroom, so you are not part of this program but equally or more qualified you still would be past for promotion.

summary: Slowly becoming more progressive, but the culture is still rigid
advice:
The big bank needs to work faster, be more flexible, and improve focus on clients and employees
The culture is not changing fast enough; it's a tough environment for collaborators and innovators
Focus on short-term profit eclipses concern for employees and customers; this needs to come into balance
pros:
Real glimmers of hope on pay equity, equal representation
Generally strong ethics
Smart and committed people trying to do their best for clients and each other
Good, strong messages about culture and values
Good career mobility
cons:
Still a fundamentally hierarchical organization
Territorial executives building empires within the empire
Despite the FinTech threats, still conservative and slow in technology innovation
Terrible meeting and email cultures
The culture & values promoted by execs & HR don't feel entirely authentic and don't quite trickle down

advice: Even though attrition rate is very low in Citi, at times it is very difficult to offer young folks the technical exposure they need.  Some thought needs to be put into retaining younger talent.
pros:
Been an employee for more than 4 years.
Employee friendly place to work.
Managers and technical folks are very friendly.
Very relaxed environment to work in general.
Very supportive on the the work from home part.
cons:
Some teams/onsite folks can make work a bit hectic. 
A lot of code base is very old, so once you have learned most functionality nothing to improve upon.
No pressure from the management to migrate to a newer/better tech stack.
As all products are in house products no real customer feedback.
Most of the releases happen during weekends.

advice: I would not know where to start.
pros: -decent salary, good location and facilities, good on cv.
cons: shocking culture, under appreciated invisible. Management is rude, they don't communicate and if you ask them for anything its like asking them to do you a favor because you should know despite the fact they give you no training. as a man I never thought I would say this, but there is a massive imbalance between the amount of male to female managers. I really dislike the culture, and I can't even imagine what it would be like to be a female working in CITI. Also you will be shamed into doing overtime, or should i say volunteer work, because you don't get paid for overtime after a certain level.

summary: Not a bad place to work if you are in the right area.
advice: Focus on the important things and stop wasting time on non core business nonsense.
pros:
Lots of room for advancement as they change the chairs around every couple years to keep it interesting for Senior Management.  Interesting ideas do get listened to but you have to deal with dinos and idiots getting in the way of progress.
Good vacation after 5 yrs/VP and they are doing a decent job promoting life-work balance -- though of course it saves us money to have folks working from home.
cons: Have seen large projects disappear into thin air without recognition of why they were a waste of time to begin with. Different business lines definitely still have issues working together.

advice: I would advice management to concentrate the efforts towards aquiring quality rather than quantity of accounts.  Compensate employees for all products sold and met goals.
pros: Higher salaries compared to other banks.  But this seems to be true during 2007-2008.  But starting in the latter part of 2009, the commissions have disappeared and bonuses have decreased by half.  This is a direct result of increased goals.
cons: After the mid 2009, Citibank began focusing  on quantity rather than quality.  Today, every PB is required to open 40-50 accounts per month.  This is very frustrating when you're an honest individual who tries to do the best for clients and find yourself without any available time.  No payouts for any loan products.

summary: Good opportunity for growth but pockets of legacy behaviors which is detrimental for company
advice: Get senior leaders to care about their people. All c16 and above should be primarily compensated via stock so they are largely vested in company performance. Employee development is a joke in most (not all) areas.
pros: Opportunity to advance, pay decent, ceo and few other senior leaders committed to doing the right thing and has bought into vision.
cons: Some senior managers are still operating under old mentality and manages their org in a silo to rest of company. Compared to other big banks I would say Citi senior managers don't care about their employees and only seek to get the most out of them instead of a two way relationship.

summary: Offers a good learning experience and work life balance
advice: Probably the HR should explain the pay package and should not mislead the candidates about it. Lateral appointments should be done in more transparent manner about the promotion's as well.
pros: Learning has be given utmost importance by my manager. The quality of work has been as per expectation of my profile. The package is decent enough. The work life balance is good and the company offers flexibility for working.
cons: The compensation package is decent but not as per it's competitors. No parity is maintained and a lot of times very average candidates are given much more than knowledgeable and more experienced existing employees. Travel opportunities are limited and going up the ladder is not smooth.

summary: Not a bad place to work for
advice: Work on diverse ways to share information like frequent townhalls, blogs, standardized links and standardized searches across all collaboration sites. 360 reviews, the most useful tool for an employee, should be pushed top-down to become part of the culture.
pros: So many areas to work in to find what you like as you build your career. Decent chances of getting a good work-life balance. 401(K) matching. Pretty decent health plan. Vast library of online training available for employees, including Udemy.
cons: Information is not easy to come by though attempts are being made to make information searchable. 360 degree review is still not implemented completely or soaked in the culture enough to make it useful across the org structure.

advice: Put your self in your employees shoes!!!! Senior Management I would ask you when was the last time did you run a branch? Switch job for a week and see how much we go through.... It's much easier to be setting in a office somewhere uninterrupted typing tons of emails & setting up conference calls!!!!
pros: Great Benefits and offers a variety of products!
cons: Short staffed and spread very thin.  Some  branches are closed on Saturdays so if you happen  to be working in a branch that is open on Saturday, you're expected to work 6 days a week.  No work/ life balance.  You become burnt out especially when you are putting in 8-10 hrs. Weekdays!

summary: Good foot in the door, corporate culture outdated
advice: Allow your employees to govern themselves more often. Stop trying to remodel the office to “boost employee morale”- buy better coffee and give better bonuses. It’ll do the same thing.
pros: Team members are very knowledgeable. Pay is reasonable but can stagnate. Training and growth is encouraged with numerous opportunities for internal networking and jobs. Management does listen to concerns and often tries to actually do something about it.
cons: Though there is a push for innovation, it isn’t often adopted. Very silo-ed work environment, despite efforts not to be. Like most corporations, sometimes it ends up being “it’s who you know, not what you know.” Budgets come from the highest level-some departments get much more than others.

advice:
It's easier said than done, but more attention should be put on ensuring appropriate coverage & staffing matches expected capacity. It's the financial world, and I get that layoffs will always be a part of it. But I've seen the cyclical trend time & time again: budget cuts come in, eliminate positions...too many positions, work piles up, remaining workers become miserable, hire new people that you have to pay to train, workload drops, budget cuts come in, rinse & repeat. 

With all the efforts to increase employees' mental health (upgraded facilities, ping pong & foosball tables, etc), it would go a long way towards actually improving that by using some of those funds to staff appropriately and provide necessary headcounts so employees don't get burnt out.
pros:
Vacation time & PTO, good health/dental/vision benefits, decent internal perks like gift cards for completing health challenges. One of the biggest benefits is a flexible/remote schedule that allows a lot of opportunities to work from home. 

Overall there's a lot of great people here & most of them will go out of their way to help you if you're looking to learn & not just being lazy. It's a great place to learn, expand your network (if you're willing to put in the time) and gather experience.
cons:
The proverbial red tape is endless. With a company this size it stands to reason, but it can be EXTREMELY difficult to make progress, conclude decisions or get agreements. Teams can be somewhat fragmented, in that team building events may be plentiful for one group & non-existent for another, even if they're in the same reporting hierarchy. 

Some reviews rave about the work/life balance here, but that varies heavily by what team you're on. Anything AML is out of control, especially in North America driving projects. It's not atypical to be expected to drive projects like a PM while getting paid like a junior analyst.

It's exciiting to work for a firm whose goal is to lead the industry through one of the most signifcant macro-economic events in history.  The firm's world headquarters are located in the same city that I live in and that makes the commute fairly tolerable.
cons: The industry is exeperiencing unpredencted change at the moment.  It's difficult  to work for a firm whose goal is to lead the industry through one of the most signifcant macro-economic events in history.  The firm's world headquarters are located in the same city that I live and that means that I have to drive to work.

advice: Even in hard times it is important to nurture talent and provide opportunities for advancement.
pros: Citigroup  has decent benefits, generous time off policies with 25 days off a year. The work atmosphere is still fairly relaxed even with the current atmosphere. If you are in the financial services industry, Citigroup is a fair bet at this time. Citi is too big to fail and if you are not part of the layoffs your employment is safe.
cons: The current financial crisis limits your options and and bonuses and merit increases. Also the Citi brand has been seriously tarnished by the financial crisis. The Citi brand as one of the most admired and trusted brands globally has been seriously damaged.

advice: be more positive. if i ever got feedback from a manager with something positive and not negative, i would be shocked. they always have to find something to bring you down, something we could have said or done differently in our calls. even though we did really good. one question i hate during one on ones when listening to calls....so "what could you have said differently or done" are you kidding me???? no matter what we say you will always find something wrong!
pros: alot of paid time off, enjoy working with peers. good hours!!
cons: not very positive enviroment, no one knows whats going on, ever!!! you try your hardest but its never good enough for them. you fail your calls for the dumbest reasons!!!!!! no incentives ever, they make it to where you can never get incentives. you get to the point with this job, you want to give up.

summary: Exactly what you would expect from a big bank
advice: You need to do a better job in safeguarding your employees.  There needs to be a sense of caring and security for their employees that needs to be even more prevalent in times of hardship.
pros: As a multi-national firm, Citi offers a wealth of opportunities to work in many different locations or interest areas.  You will find talented people throughout the company and there is a well-defined track into upper management.
cons: As in any large organization, Citi is not free of its bureaucracy.  Especially during the financial crisis, the bonuses were cut, changes weren't widely accepted, and the general culture was surrounded by fear of layoffs.

summary: Depends on what supervisor you get
pros:
Insurance benefits. 
The schedule could be a pro if you can get one you want.
cons:
Managers. Your experience at Citi will depend on your manager when you get hired in or if you can get switched teams in a hurry if you get a bad one! I had a bad one which only had new hires on her team because as soon as they can they get away from her. 
Also getting time off approved is difficult. My mom was having health problems and had to have several procedures and I requested off atleast 5-7 days before and they refused to give me time off even talking to my supervisor didn't help. So I had to use my time instead of pto.

advice: Keep doing like this. The only thing that I didn't like is that among managers and supervisors you can hardly find foreigners.
pros: More or less flexible schedule. Managers are great. Atmosphere is really friendly. At some positions you have a lot of opportunities for overtimes. The possibility to grow and to learn. A lot of trainings.
cons: I cann't find any serious really. Sometimes work environment is really intense and you feel that you should be paid more than you really get, but in the end of the day that is not the main factor. Also there are a lot of people just pushing buttons and don't understanding the sense of the process, but I feel at every company the situation is more or less the same.

advice: Breakdown bureaucracy and focus on making employees happier - much cynicism seems to have developed among many regarding the future outlook of the firm.
pros: Great resume item no matter your role, access to much information internally and a great learning experience for a young employee. For the most part, good people and the middle/upper ranks and filled with many career veterans that have spent most of their time at the firm.
cons: Bureaucracy can feel insurmountable at times, and it takes a lot of politicking to be appropriately noticed. There was a time when exceptional performance seemed like it would outweigh this type of nonsense but now that flat is the new up it's difficult to see it in that same light.

advice: Career development should be more intensive. Review of a employee and compensation should be based on achievement and value addition to the firm, rather than a formula. Senior management in IT is struck 20 years back, they have no clue on how to hire top talent atleast in C13 an C12 levels. The base levels IT employees to made more accountable by challenges. The attitude is like once you get job in CITI one is set life, 95% of the employees fly under the radar.
pros: Good Benefits, Stability and Flexibity of locations
cons: Slow pace and limited career advancement. Pay hike is based on a formula, which leaves little incentive for employees to step up, this is in IT

advice: Focus on reducing turnover and keeping talent.
pros:
+ Provided me an opportunity to work and learn right out of college
+ Made a lot of good contacts with former employees
+ Helped get me started utilizing advanced levels of Excel VBA
cons:
- Work environment wasn't as professional as I would have liked
- Fairly high volume of turnover left a top heavy management structure because employees were being replaced. 
Personal Example: 1-manager, 1-supervisor, 1-analyst (this was changing since I've left)
- I had 13 different people I reported to in 4 years; equals 1 (supervisor, manager or AVP) approximately every 112 days.  I believe this left me without any promotions or significant raises because I had to prove myself (not a problem initially) to what seemed like a never ending cycle of management.

summary: Good career progression but old fashioned
advice: Be transparent with salaries and titles within the organisation, it leads to dissatisfaction amongst staff members and you lose good people.
pros: Good people, strong work ethic within teams, management are approachable, good benefits (heath etc). The people really make Dublin Citi site a pleasure to work in.
cons: Large salary discrepancies between colleagues doing the same job, with the same title and same experience, performance (15k+ differences in my experience). Citi don't care about this even when they tried to remedy  the situation and admitting it was a problem it was never transparent exercise and people know the person sitting next to them is still on % higher.

advice: Get with the times. People who are able to work from home on occasion are more motivated and get more work done.
pros:
Lots of diversity programs
HR programs/resources were good
People I worked with were talented and knowledgeable
cons:
Work was boring and repetitive, very little opportunity to learn
Middle management was a PITA about work/life. Nitpicked over people leaving early, time off requests. Although we have the capability to work from home, some managers are old school and frown upon it, which is not family friendly. This is part of the reason there is high turnover. However, they come and go as they please and work from home when they want to. Also, there is little to no loyalty; people backstab to try to get ahead (which doesn't work in this environment).

advice: Your employees have families and lives. Playing with their jobs really is not cool. Stop telling everyone "we know nothing", when you do. So we can look for another job if need be and not wait for YOU to decide to change our lives. We are not idiots so stop treating us that way.
pros: Well known company, great pay, benefits, bonus program, hours, able to work from home when needed. Enjoy working with some talented people.
cons: Employees are treated like a number, lie directly to their employees, change benefits in the employee handbook 2 weeks before we are told Citi is selling mortgage servicing, if offered job with new company and don't accept then no severance pay, I could go on and on.

advice: Promote people based on their skills and knowledge instead of them just being your buddy.
pros: Reputable name that brings in prospective clients. Open architecture to be able to offer clients a broad range of different investment products many other bank programs do not offer.
cons:
Everybody is overwhelmed with KYC work and their technology is extremely primitive. Advisors have to waste their time with nonsense administrative work that they don’t have time to build a business. Takes days or sometimes even weeks to accomplish tasks that should be able to be completed in minutes.  

Company hires incompetent workers because they don’t want to pay what competent workers would want to be paid.  Baffles my mind how such a large institution is run so inefficiently. I worked for multiple banks, and Citi is by FAR the worst one. It didn’t used to be so bad they say before, but it sure is going downhill now!

advice: I wish they were more supportive in the process of client base development.
pros: My coworkers are very helpful, kind, intelligent, and competent.  The training program is quite thorough.  The work is rigorous and challenging but fair.   A variety of resources are provided.  The work environment is comfortable, flexible, and versatile.
cons: The pay is low, low, low.  It really could be a tad higher for the type of work we are asked to do.  The yearly work schedule is a bit up in the air.  Nothing is stated in stone, so balancing one's work and personal life is difficult. The branch is small.  Team-work is not promoted at this branch.  Autonomy is thought of as a very, very important quality.

summary: Citigroup has gone from bad to worse.
advice: Hire more people. It is not healthy to have employees work  nearly 70hrs a week.
pros: Decent salary as fair market pay goes.
cons: No fairness for time off for extra hours worked. No quality time for family life. They made billions in profits in 2010, but instead of giving a bonus or raise, they tried to have a company mandatory forum to ask people how they felt.  During the meeting when an employee tried to voice that concern, they tried to twist the words that the company had awards to recognized individuals and gave compensation. We NEVER heard of such programs. Maybe they do exist at the executive level? I guess that would make sense.

advice:
There are so many little things you could do to make your employees more productive and able to get something done but no one will champion that idea.  
Stop letting everyone escalate minor issues to upper management.  Trust that the managers who work for you have a good reason for their decision.
pros:
Benefits are very good
Easy and normal to work remote
Facilities are modern and clean
Chance to learn the latest technologies
cons: Because its a bank, security and auditing are more important than making sure we can backup/restore the computer systems.  This is evident in the amount of paperwork needed to get anything done.  Often given projects to deliver that are late before the paperwork was started which means everything gets escalated.

summary: Huge company with endless job opportunities.
advice: take the mystery out of bonusing by teaching everything there is to know in training. many people rely on the extra income because they are not getting paid enough to begin with.

cons: collectors do not make a lot of money, but there is bonus potential. the problem is that you don't learn everything there is to know about what you have to do to bonus. there are particular things you have to do to get credit, which is not taught in the classroom.

pros: Its a great experience to be working with such experienced professionals in a fast paced environment. Work life balance is actually great, and while you have to give and take a bit over public holidays if you're covering markets across different parts of the world, you have a lot of freedom to choose your holidays. Hours are also not bad, given its markets - start early and finish early. Office culture is relatively casual, but very friendly and open.
cons: The training and guidance is fantastic at the very junior level, and there are always people to guide you if you reach out. The downside to this is that these sorts of opportunities are quite condensed at the very start of your career.

summary: Great place to work, but you've got to be aware of the Changing Culture.
advice: In the works of one of the former CEOs,  Citi appears to be loosing ground but putting Stock Holders before Customers and Employees; forgetting that happier employes => better customer service => satisfied Stock Holders.
pros: Citi has a global presence and so, potential opportunities in many places around the world - if you are looking to start over or launching your career  in a new setting.  The technology side is quite tight, little or no wriggle room, and the green grass appears to be turning brown. Greater potential lies on the business/retail side.
cons: One of the greatest asset working here was the Work Life balance. That is quickly varnishing.

summary: A mixed bag, depends on what you're looking for.
advice: Messaging is very off key, it's hard to believe in the integrity of your employer's word when the CEO issues a statement about our strong earnings one day, and then later that day has managment say "no raises again this year".  Value accuracy over conformity.
pros: In my small area, I have a great deal of autonomy, I enjoy the people I work with and the environment, as well as the work.
cons: Most of the company does not have this, corporate nonsense is rampant, things are constantly changing (not for the better), and doing things a certain way is valued more than doing them correctly.  Company claims to be a meritocracy but then doesn't give raises.

summary: Great for people that love people
advice: Listen a little bit more and all managers should have the same rules/ practices,  stop doing this completely different on your team then setting your employee up for failure when they go to a manager that’s not as “laid back” As you were!
pros: Benefits are fantastic , they are true to their motto of wanting and celebrating diversity, family oriented environment, hard workers are noticed and given recognition.
cons: Just like any other corporate position, you gotta kiss butt before you can “kick” it- so for the introverted and prideful person, in regards to career advancement opportunities, might not be the best place for you. Lots of micromanaging- depending on your manager.

advice: The SMT is far removed from the realities of some of the functions and constantly making decisions by the seat of their pants, keeping only the cost;
pros: It is a great place to work with so many opportunities - even with all the orderliness and automation, there is still a lot of work to be done
cons: It is hard to motivate consultants - especially offshore - since many of them under Fixed Pricing contract - they really don't care. They do their shift and they take 3 breaks and are constantly away - Many teams throw the fire and walk away, not adhering to the policy and procedures and wait till the last minute; making some teams bend over backwards to accommodate the requirements.

advice: While Management is transparent and forthcoming with their future strategy and direction that the Bank is headed in, it would be beneficial for direct management to be more involved with assisting employees if and when current jobs / positions are in jeopardy.
pros: Great company to work for with management, and a tone at the top who care for the employees and make every effort to reward those trying to add share holder value and protect the interests of their consumers.
cons: As with every bank comes uncertainty and challenges that employers must work through.  Currently, the subsidiary that I work for within Citi recently announced that it will wind down operations and close the Bank.

pros: Citi cares about their employees.  They give you time to volunteer for charities during your busy week.  There are Diversity Networks that you are encouraged to join to learn about others around us.  There are multiple days throughout the year that Citi gives back to their employees with "Fall Festivals" or give a-ways.  They work hard to have a good morale throughout the building.
cons: There has been some restructuring in the past year and many people have been laid off.  This is not good for morale at all.  I feel like Citi prepared these people pretty well for what was coming their way, but it is still not easy.

advice: Cut the retail call center workers some slack especially escalated supervisors, the job is already stressful enough
pros: Citi is a great company to work for with a lot of opportunity for growth, the benefits are really great and you get a lot of paid time off including 48 hous of sick paid time off. They were extremely flexible with time off for school, I earned my bachelors degree while working there
cons: Working in retail customer service over the phone, just like anywhere else really sucks. Management set unrealistic goals and constantly changed things which made the job even more annoying. It's the call center life though you can't expect much

summary: Rewarding work, not so great culture
advice: Don’t just look good, do good
pros: Opportunity to work directly with some of the largest companies In the world and help them with their treasury needs. Citi is such a large organization that one will not find it difficult to find a role that suits their current needs. I love the work
cons: Culture is very political and hierarchy. Forget about being able to contribute to shaping the priories of your organization. Need to suck up to the big guys for years to do that. Culture is a bit toxic, management gets aggressive and rude when things don’t go well regardless of the reason why. Culture is about looking good to clients and others not necessarily doing good.

advice: Management should do what they say like offering shift bids and training in different departments.  Try walking the floor to see who is really working and who isn't.
pros: fair pay, great benefits and cafeteria
cons:
Loud and cramped call center, no personal space. Very immature workers especially the trainers.  "unit managers" don't even leave their desks, they just do the numbers.
Angry customers because their technology is so bad people can't even log in or register their cards online.   CSR's are not trained for all the stuff you have to know.   They outsource a lot of the departments overseas and there's a high turn over.  Stressful job that is not worth losing your health over.

summary: Worked for almost 3  Years in Citi SG
advice: See the cons stated.
pros:
- Location is convenient. It is just opposite downtown mrt station.
- Yearly pay increment of 2% - better than nothing.
- Internal mobility after 2 years in the current role. I did not manage to transfer before I left.
cons:
- Too many layers of hierarchy.
- Progression is too slow - unless you "know the right people".
- Too many people of the same nationality of the same ethnicity. This creates a culture of favoritism & biasness of their "own people".
- Not a pay master. Bonus is consistently bad - less than 1 week for me (and my team members). However, I'm in operations, so I am not sure about the other depts.

summary: Good place to work if you can hold on to the job in this economy
advice: Instead of merging and trying to get bigger under a big "Umbrella", they should focus more on having smaller departments with proper oversight. Just because the back office is cheaper to run does not mean that they are not important enough for the company's to be competitive.
pros: A lot of flexibility on the technology side. As long as the problems were solved very little or no red tape to go through. The managers were not very pesky.
cons: Getting things cross teams is a nightmare. The back office is probably one of the reason they were unable to compete with other IBs even during the boom time.

summary: Stay for the pay until you can find a place where you don't feel like pucking every morning before going to work.
advice: Get managers that understand technology and are not pure accountatnts trying to make their numbers shine.
pros: The pay is OK. The offices in Frankfurt are very well located close to the Opera house. If you want to move to London, it's a good platform, also for pepople who love finance....
cons:
Bad management. Bad work conditions (lack of space), very little attention was given that we barely had enough elbow space to work and the noise levels in the office was always very high. 
Management does not understand technical issues. 
The heavy use of outsourcing to India is an another problem. 
The outsourcer's personnel is changing all the time, they get treated like rubbish buy their own management and the results are bad quality, lack of motivation and never ending levels of miscommunication.

summary: It is a job with a well known company during an economic decline.
advice: Restructure the comp plan so the employees have the opportunity to match what is being expected, as of now, there is no chance to meet expectations based on the current layout.
pros: Well known company worldwide with excellent benefits.
cons: The opportunity to advance or make anything above and outside of your base salary is almost non existent even though it is a requirement by management to bonus, no one is bonusing. The fact is, banking is the plague, and the requirements to keep your job are not feasible. it may not be fair to completely blame JUST Citibank for this, as I think it is industry wide.

summary: Citi's management team lacks vision and understanding of customer's need.
advice:
First, it is important to enable innovative individuals to have a voice.  An innovative employee who works for a non visionary manager is bound to fail.  Have your managers learn skills to tap into people's talent.  


Please LISTEN to the consumer RESEARCH and don't be afraid to make the changes.  It is best to lead the change than to have the government dictate what the bank needs to do.
pros: The employees at Citi are intelligent and hard working.
cons: Managers at Citi are unable to think outside the box and take risks to propel the organization to be a leader in the consumer financial services space.

advice: people are great - if you work here, you can work anywhere - however, retention sucks and they are going to experience a brain drain b/c top performers keep leaving - we get messages about consistently posting profits for 7 quarters but then see our colleagues laid off and told bonuses and raises are going to be terrible.  talk about messaging.
pros:
fantastic people (mostly)
global - opportunities to work abroad
fast, paced dynamic environment
infrastructure, tech, and support are light years beyond competitors
cons:
stock price hasn't moved
fair degree of nepotism and bureaucratic behavior
mgmt afraid to think outside the box
ridiculous guidelines (timeframes, etc) on promotions - not enough value placed on performance and reach of individual

summary: The working conditions just getting worse and worse
advice: Put on a good pair of glasses, know your staffs and stuffs. Rome isn't built in a day, there isn't quick solution to your revenue, needless to mention ur crappy reputation.
pros:
At least you get paid monthly, and it is (or was) a respectable big multinational banking group.
They used to offer new recruits enough training and couching about products and services they offered.
cons: Lots of office politics, promotions are based on skill level of been a boss pleaser or simply a bottom kisser. And the worst part of it is that they don't care about clients, they are selling products that maybe not suitable to clients, but failed to mention about risk involved.

jobTitle: Vice President Global Mobile Internet Marketing
advice: Start acting like a younger more entrepreneurial company because AMEX, Captial One, PNC are eating your lunch.
pros: Benefits, Flexible work schedule, Vacation time
cons:
Old School, overly rigid, 200 year old company and it acts like it.
Focus is on Credit Cards and profit. 
Power Structure - you are allowed to talk laterally w/those in your employment grade but you cannot approach management 1 - 2 levels up w/ideas; everything must be filtered by your immediate manager whether they are on your side or not.
Very much an 'insider' company w/waiting for people to leave before you can move up the chain.
MANY people work 6 or more years in a position before being promoted and often promotion does NOT include a raise in salary.

summary: Working for Citibank has been a Learning Experience
pros: Because of the size of the company there are tons of opportunities to grow, not necessarily in your same department, but definitely outside it. Benefits are ok and salaries are ok as well. Diversity is at the core of Citibank, I had never worked for a company more diverse than Citi.
cons: Here is hard to compare apples with apples when it comes to job openings. You could have two accountants, same title and same responsibilities same location, but because they work in different departments within Citi, the pay difference could be unbelievable. Make sure to get into the right department. Benefits are good but expensive ($300-$400 bi-weekly for health insurance in Florida is expensive).

summary: Good exposure to a lot of departments/functions within the business, decent pay.
pros: Career advancement is possible however it is up to you, you obviously have to prove yourself...AND have a supportive manager.  Granted there are a lot of great managers however there are some that do not belong.  Your experience here will look great on a resume if you don't look to stay long term.
cons: Career growth is limited within Operations (one can only go so far) so look around within the business after putting in your time...pay is "decent" however one will only receive a significant raise if they are well liked/needed and threaten to leave OR if one leaves altogether for over a year and then returns.

advice:
Treat your employees with dignity and respect always.
Don't use and abuse your top people and tear them down
Give balanced feedback.   Acknowledge the positive improvements and implementations that have been put into place.
pros:
Amazing benefits
Great vacation allotment
Hours
Exposure to different areas of the business 
Being a business owner from A to Z
Ability to create own processes and have them approved by risk, compliance and legal. 
Ability to work with all levels of management across the business and learn from them.
cons:
Communication from the top down needs to be clearer and more consistent 
Ability to break down silos has to be easier
Right size staffing
Goals need to make sense
Upper management needs to be more open to suggestions and to try new things

advice: Listen to your employees and be open.  Transparency is the basis of Risk Control.
pros: Great Facilities Infrastructure - In general good global tools and processes - Interesting Global Strategies and Vision - Good pay if you negotiate upfront and can sell yourself - Global company - Work from home benefit
cons:
Don't expect salary fairness, same people with same responsibilities within same groups with very distant salaries and no strategy to level
Huge gap between senior management and middle management philosophies.  I felt mediocre people were protected, they just get moved around.
Citi never sleeps - definitely applies to the lower level employees - you need to devote your life to Citi
Everything is about the bottom line, no matter the cost

advice:
Cross Train team on calls, email corresp, projects, back office, and various queues then rotate groups so that all dept members can move up/out to other departments.

Simplify banking product fees so that customers know what they are getting and CLEARLY communicate to branch staff and customers. Clearly communicate funds availability and reduce time that funds are held. 
Go back to voluntary shifts for holidays so that most employees have the chance to have them off.
pros:
Good Bene's 
co-workers were fun to be around
Good place to get your feet wet in the industry.
cons:
Management keeps increasing standards and requirements without due consideration of time on calls. 
Management team was quite cliquish and had their favorites for projects

advice: Try to do more to retain talented people who have been in the bank for years. I know the sector is under lots of pressure, but compensation and a career plan is very very important.
pros: Great place to work if you want to learn fast and face challenges. Company puts a lot of emphasis on diversity. Internal mobility also a great thing, even moving to different countries or functions.
cons: difficult to say, depends on the division you are in, i always had the luck to find good and respectable people and work with them for years, maybe everyone is like that at Citi.

advice: No one, they believe that they are gods. So I don't waste my time on it.
pros: Great Name on your Resume. Global Bank, good online banking. Variety of financial products for your clients. You can serve domestic and international clients as well.
cons: Early 90's technology, Micromanagement does not let you produce. Citi does not care about their employees life, they just care about numbers and Senior Management. Does not have a clear direction of where they go. Managers have favoritism. Citi's procedures are similar to small and cheap Credit Unions. Citi systems work against the employee always. They made a morning meeting where they says the same thing all days, if you made good sales or receive a good survey you're Awesome if not you're a piece of... You know. Considering that Citi is US third biggest bank don't expect that your professional experience will be at state of the art level.

pros: Benefits start day 1. Gym on location. Good pay with incentive structure. Full cafeteria on location with many different choices. Fun atmosphere with co-workers and my managers were cool. There were more positives than negatives here for me.
cons: The C in Citi really stands for change as something is always changing. This actually is also a good thing as it keeps the company abreast with the industry, however from an employee standpoint it always felt that as soon as we got one thing going well, they would change the process. Also I worked for Citi auto and Citi mortgage, both jobs ended after 3 years. There was a package paid but I'm not unemployed again.

advice:
- Mean what you say
- Focus more on just the numbers
- Value employees
- Expand your notion of client
- Continue on making the investments in people and technology
- Develop your selves
- Improve your ability to function within/as a team
pros:
- Work time and location flexibility
- Generally collegial atmosphere
- Working with smart and dedicated colleagues
- Diverse set of opportunities given the scale of the organization
- Starting to make better and more investments in people and infrastructure
cons:
- Pay under market
- Much bureaucracy
- Lack of vision
- Poor mobility processes across organizational and geographic boundaries
- Leaders more often act with time poor/crisis mode mentality (even when not warranted or helpful)
- Volume of work (e.g. promotion of the idea of "double hatting")

summary: It's a huge company, experiences vary greatly.  Mostly dependent on 1 and 2 level managers for analyst positions.
pros:
Huge company.
Can work many locations and remotely.
If working on international can potentially travel internationally.
Internal jobs database that is searchable and can apply for all kinds of jobs.
Great place for any point in career.  Many people start and return later.  Enough opportunity to be a lifer but will typically have to move between businesses for significant promotions/raises.
cons:
Pretty stable overall but subject to market swings.
Work/Life balance can be real hit/miss to both extremes.  Some teams 40 hr week, others 60 hr week.  At least it is not a consistent culture of no work/life balance like other places.
Few good employees and mostly only terrible resumes coming across.

advice: Don't hire a manager because they have been there for 25 years as an employee.  Use some common sense and pick people that are actually qualified for the job.  There is a reason you have went from 3 buildings to 2 buildings....it all comes down to management.
pros: Some decent people to work with.  Depends on your supervisor you can have great motivation or it can be a nightmare and just a reason for some benefits or a pay check.
cons: The structure changes regularly. There is usually poor leadership among the chain of command which affects anyone below them.  By poor leadership I mean there is usually clichés, and if your not in it, well then you will get a rude awakening.  And while most of us don't always agree with our manager at some point, managers have to be able to listen....which I've never seen in any of my surrounding areas.

pros: You can gain insights into why capital adequacy, large exposures and liquidity are crucial and learn about the Basel 3 framework which governs the way these reports must be finalised.  A lot of knowledgeable people surrounded me who always lent me a hand when I needed help.
cons: Tight deadlines to get reports done, a technical hitch in another system can hold you up for hours as you can't access information you need. Reporting systems are sometimes exremely difficult to handle. As you download information from a reporting system, you have to process by performing many, repetitive actions in Excel. The formatted report must be uploaded in another reporting system. You can lose a few hours if you have not formatted the report carefully.

advice: my last manager was great, I wish the previous manager in the dallas market were like her. Too bad Citibank no longer has a presence in Texas.
pros: Fast-paced environment, flexible schedule for students, excellent pay with bonuses added, people were great to work with, has great customer loyalty, teller system NBS was easy to use
cons: Some managers were micromanaging, one of which found out that many people don't like like that when she resigned after less than a year managing a retail location. Very into saying a welcome and goodbye script to customer, you weren't allowed to put your personal spin on it, you had to say what Citi wanted verbatim. Everyone sounded like a robot, BUT other than that, fun place to work.

summary: Great company to work for with room for advancement
advice: Continue to give open honest feedback with the intention to grow employees and enhance their talents
pros: There are many pros to working for Citi. They care about their employees and customers. The vacation time offered, benefits from day 1, maternity and paternity leave policy. The benefits are great! You have a chance for advancement as long as you are open to feedback and find a mentor. This has been the key for me last 17 years. Depending on your location, you also get to work from home. Great company, hands down!
cons: If you work in a large call center as an hourly employee, if there are open desks the option for work from home is non existent.

summary: Great Managers Make ALL the Difference
pros: Very good managers at my office in San Francisco, has a "tech" kind of feel when it comes to colleague activities, get togethers, always have good boost in morale.   Not just the traditional boring quiet banks where managers hang over your head like a slave driver.  Coworkers are great as well, very supportive, age ranged varied  which is a good mix.  Ppl know their "stuff" for the most part and is supportive when it came to learning new things, taking on new tasks. I'm very fortunate to have worked here at this office.
cons: Very tough to  promoted unless someone gets laid off or quit,  introducing new tech  is slower than a turtle

advice: Stock is looking good, thats been the focus, so you are doing well.
pros: Time off is excellent. Benefits are good.  Paid time off for new mothers AND fathers is excellent.
cons: Lots of offshoring going on all around the business. If it can be moved to Manila or Mexico City or India it will be. This is not new, been with Citi 19 years and its been happening the whole time but now its really fast tracked. That and the hiring of contractors vs. Full time, benefit eligible employees has picked up BIG TIME. Used to be out of the 6500ish folks at this site, 6400 were FTEs. Now more than half are contract workers.

summary: wealth management  at Citi does not bode well for internal transfers.
advice: n/a
pros: Although the reputation is awful, and it is very beauracratic, there is some great human capital at the firm.  You will have access to innovative products and extensive research, both funamental and technical.
cons: seemingly impossible for most people to advance to "front office" roles.  specifically in Smith Barney, most financial advisors do not add value for their clients.  in a tough market environment, this has become very evident.  management and advisors focus solely on sales, and not enough on knowledge and market savvy.  to call many of them "used car salesman" would be a fair assesment.  also will not pay for graduate level education or certifications like the CFA.

summary: Business Banker at Citibank is a dead end job with no room for advancement.
advice: Listen to the people who work for you, and understand that they are the ones pounding the pavement to make sure you don't lose your comfortable corner office. Don't abandon ship when the going gets tough, and don't forget who got you that promotion.
pros: The job is better than most sales jobs. Or it used to be when Citibank was able to walk proudly down the street with its chest open, bragging about its ability to be a global brand. Now it's nothing more than a 4 dollar stock.
cons: Like any sales job you have some of the most unprofessional managers who seem to have got to their position through sheer luck or seniority.

summary: Underpaid, Few chances to move within the organization
advice: If you want to attract and retain top talent, you need to pay for it! Don't look to save money by cutting out coffee and water coolers, it only makes it less desirable to work there!
pros: They were great with Work-Life balance, and they were very flexible with all employees. Working from home was frequently an option if you had a conflict or bad weather, and work hours were very reasonable 95% of the time.
cons: Their pay is more than a 10% cut from the market rate, and raises have been less than cost of living over past 4 years.  They don't make it easy to move internally, and their hiring process leaves much to be desired.

jobTitle: Senior KDB Developer, Assistant Vice President
summary: Good Growth, Friendly People, Not great pay rise
advice: Make sure long term employees grow monetarily also when they get promoted.
pros: Citi is overall a good place to work. Good work if you prove your potential. Lots of leaves. Friendly peers and superiors. Sometimes, you get to do boring work but that's part of the job.
cons: Yearly hikes are not great in tech roles 10% pet year if you are good. Bonus is ok compared to other Banks, But When you compare other hedge funds and prop trading firms, bonus is very poor. But I think that's how Banks and other fintech firms compare. If you stay long and perform well, you will grow on the leadership ladder but not monetarily.

summary: Total of 7 years of service (in and out over the years). The worst work environment.
advice:
Address all the factors listed in my CONS session.
Create a culture that nurtures good values and is based on facts and real actions, not feelings and empty/uninformed opinions.
pros:
Benefits and salary at market.
Ability to work remote some days of the week depending on your job.
cons:
Worst work environment I found in my career (over 30 years).
Internal culture is trying too hard to adapt to younger generation mentality in the most unproductive ways.
Lots of focus on "How do you feel" and little on "What are the facts". 
Lack of consistency and coherence from upper management.
Lots of managers came from technical positions and have no ability to manage people effectively.

advice: Improve the program and hire better HR personnel
pros: It's great if you honestly don't know what you want to do, but if you have a strong inkling for what you want to do...pursue an opportunity that's more focused. Ex: You're very interested in marketing, go to a marketing specific role because here you'll only spend 8 months in the role and then go to retail banking or risk/controls so you won't get to fully develop the marketing skills. The program is honestly for you to get a small taste of what it's like. Depending on who you are and where you're trying to go this could be very good or very bad.
cons: HR, they don't know anything and barely communicate with you. It's sad.

advice: Create more humanizing environment, we are all just trying our best and getting yelled at all day is not an easy job.
pros: Lots of promotion opportunities. Ability to work from home. Good but not great health benefits. Fair attempt at work life balance. Overall not bad at all.
cons: Very basic training, sink or swim technique. Dehumanizing every second accounted for micromanaging similar to Amazon.  Too much multitasking. Almost no HR Dept. No one seems to know anything. Programs and systems buggy and fail often. So much duplication of worthless tasks such as taking five minutes to notate why you had to be off phones for two minutes. Clientele are majority older entitled folks who are ill tempered and abuse representatives.

summary: A bank that has stayed in the 90s
advice: Hire new people, with a fresh vision and wanting to do things differently.  By just doing the same  things as in the past decades will not allow you to compete. Also, innovation should be part of your strategy as a company but not only when it comes to technology.
pros: Bonuses, not much more. I will not recommend anyone working there.
cons: The only way to move forward is just by staying shut and continue repeating the same things as on the past 20 years and smile to the bosses. Old fashion management that sometimes do not know what they are doing. It is like working in an organization in the 90s, very behind in technology and creativity.

advice: it's getting hard to breathe under the workload.
pros: Benefits. The company has great benefits. from amazing health insurance, to a great amount of pto the benefits are by far the best thing about the company
cons: The management styles vary widly and everything is contantly changing. one month your bosses boss os insisting everyone be micro-managed, the next you'll be getting more responsibility and no pay increase. in my collections department, they have quadrupled our workload by stacking more and more partner portfolios on our heads, and keeping us understaffed. They plan to continue adding responsibility and work to our department but insist we do not need a pay raise because we are not taking escalation calls. it's bananas.

summary: Good place to gain valuable industry experience with nice people.
advice: Keep going forward with the changes in a more accountable corporate culture.
pros: The people there are nice and willing to help most of the time. There are a lot of resources for career advancement assuming the individual is a self starter. Managers are good at going over goals and making sure employees know where they stand. The health and retirement benefits are very good. There is plenty of interesting and challenging work.
cons: There too many separations of the businesses so there are some issues navigating the corporation. There is a lot of bureaucracy to work around. There is no set training (at least in the position I was brought into) for new employees.

advice:
- Raise the standards
- Don't let mediocre performers get away with it
- Don't waste money letting people travel for no reason
- Don't make people sit on conference calls at night for months on end when a trip to the US could get these things sorted in one go
pros:
- Personal banking benefits
- Global opportunities
- Pretty good pay for the technology sector overall
- Almost impossible to get fired
cons:
- Senior management all too happy to accept mediocre performance
- Very hard to get things done
- Working in technology is completely thankless
- For all the talk of a meritocracy, getting on and getting paid more is very tough
- Truthfulness gets you into trouble

advice: Don't take negative reports and performance at the words of supervisors. Understand your employee's yourself. Learn to very by understanding much of the employee's work and procedures. Interview the employee directly one on one and give them the opportunity to provide you with both positive and negative work. Then you can judge if their is more positive than negative yourself.
pros: Great salary for the position and area. Better benefits than most companies. Constant reports of what's going on and the status of the company.
cons: Management isn't very good and often hard working individuals are overlooked and not recognized. Your not allowed to promote your own wares like girl scout cookies, yet you are "strongly" encouraged to engage in their charities.

summary: Generally a great place to work, but there are some cons...
advice: Reduce the number and frequency of meetings so that some actual work can get done!   It often felt like there was more talking and writing about what needed to happen rather than actually doing it. This is likely a problem inherent in most large corporations.
pros:
Multitude of opportunities available
creativity is encouraged
good benefits
cons: Size of the company (i.e bureaucracy), frequent management changes, and outdated technology prohibit CitiMortgage from becoming best in class.  Numerous acquisitions over the past decade contributed to tremendous growth and some economies of scale, but integration activities of these acquisitions dominated the workload,  rather than improvements in processes, technology, and true innovation..

summary: There are a lot of smart people at Citi, but it a fundamentally beuracratic and disfunctional company
advice: Executive managers - continue to keep most of the booty for yourself and we'll see what happens when the market returns and people can find another job
pros: Generally good people.  Comprehensive benefits
cons: Compensation heavily skewed toward senior management.  Pay freezes for the last 5 years are not uncommon.  Generally new hire salaries are significantly more than what an existing employee gets, because they pay what they have to what the job commands on the open market.  Company has excellent benefits, but is intensely stingy, no parties, no cups in the break rooms, no knick knacks, birthday recognition - nothing.

advice: Give your employees a place where they can be heard. The PVST is a joke, people can only produce what they have been given. The results/error reports are often skewed to favor or disfavor people. The feelings of powerlessness is prevalent with the system you have in place.
pros: I got the needed job title to be able to move into a much better position in a different company.
cons: People are treated like any other piece of office equipment. The only way to get advancement was to be liked by managers. Skills were not valued. I watched people who could do a terrific job get pushed aside because a lead did not want the competition. They had the ear of the manager and were able to say what they wanted, without regard to the truth. This really surprised me, I thought a place like Citi would have better HR/management safeguards in place.
