advice: Keep it up, just maybe explain changes a little better instead of relying solely on alerts. Overall, I would still highly recommend Citi as a wonderful place to work in East Tennessee.
pros: They have competitive pay, a fantastic benefits package that starts on day one, and an open and accepting workplace. The facilities are nice and clean, and everyone I worked with in upper level management was friendly and professional.
cons: Things change constantly, and sometimes it can be a challenge just to keep up. The company relies heavily on "alerts" that come through your PC to update you on changes, but if the call volume is heavy, you sometimes don't have time to look through the articles.

advice: Maintain the focus on your clients and stakeholders, but do not forget about your employees. They are the ones that make your company great and appealing to others. Don't treat them as numbers, you're loosing talent.
pros: I had a great learning experience, good work environment and excellent coworkers. Had the opportunity to escalate my way to the highest position available in my area within 3 years. The benefits were great: 401K, time-off, tuition reimbursement, just to name a few.
cons: Healthcare and compensation is somewhat on the low scale. Tasks get repetitive quickly and for someone looking for challenges, it gets boring. Specialized units and bureaucracy makes the operation look clumsy. They are always behind on the latest technology industry standards.

advice: Nobody is irreplaceable. Please do not tolerate bullying and shirking by so-called 'star' colleagues just because they happen to have good skills in a certain area. Plenty of others out there who can do the same job, perhaps even better, minus the nasty, cocky attitude.
pros: Reasonable working hours during non-peak reporting periods, boss was kind and understanding.  Working hours varied by department, my department was a regular 9 am - 6/7 pm, which I liked.
cons: Difficult for newcomers to fit in, especially young ones. Some colleagues were dead wood, unfair distribution of workload among the team, but boss turned a blind eye. Lack of proper handover of tasks and support to newcomers. Loyalty was seldom rewarded. Compensation nothing remarkable.

summary: Great Developmental Opportunties, Lack of Upward Mobility
advice: Best tip for management is be able to identify and retain high talent within the organization.
pros:
There are many pros of working at Citi including:
-Opportunity to work with a great group of colleagues
-Work was challenging and rewarding at the same time
-A lot of opportunities to "own" your work
-Great work life balance
-Great benefits (healthcare, 401K match, etc.)
cons: While there are many opportunties to develop your  skill set for the next role, finding the next role is often difficult and requires dedicated time to find those roles by  yourself.

advice: Do not hire people that have no related experience in management and consulting positions. get rid of consultants and pay your analysts better salaries to avoid turnover !
pros: Management is very knowledgable and well trained! Work policies are much better than competitor banks e.g work remotely, lenient with days off, some depts flexible with work schedule as long as full 40 hours worked each week. PTO begins immediately upon hire and company treats employees very well!
cons: Salary is not as high as competing banks offer, causing many talented employees to leave for more $$ elsewhere. Too many entry level workers do bare minimum, causing more intelligent employees to want to leave to be surrounded by likeminded individuals.

advice: More training to new hires.
pros: The work itself is very high level and mentally stimulating, you will never be board. There will always be projects pilling up on your desk. People there are busy, but willing to help if you pull their ear - very diverse culture.
cons: Citi's management gives little to no direction to their employees, since they are overworked themselves. The working environment is the not good, most employees work in a cubical on a floor with 200 + employees. There were lines for the bathroom. Expect to work 10+ hours a day and to figure the company out on your own. It is very important to network and have your "go to people" to get things from.

advice:
You've been moving your IT division from NY/NJ to TX for at least 7 yrs now and everyone in NY/NJ are stressed and just waiting for their separation pay .. I lost years of my life stressing these changes.. JUST DO IT ALREADY! It's a very non-productive, unhealthy, no opportunity situation on for Cit IT folks outside Irving TX. 

And if you're considering joining Citi in TX, don't! Citi doesn't pay well compared to the other companies there .. Citi is a decent first job in TX if you're in the IT field but you should have other options no problem if you continue to interview.
pros: Flexible work, wide selection of projects
cons: Moving all IT from NY/NJ to TX

advice:
there a no team nights out, at times there's a group of colleagues that organises something but nothing special really.
Too stressful and some colleagues have collapsed in the office due to stress. If we had all the necessary tools and automation it wouldn't be so stressful
Not a place I would recommend at all even if the salary is good
Automate things, find ways to help us in our daily job I'm sure you have the money
All corporations should learn that employees are an asset and they should be valued and taken care of more not considered just a number.
Dull place, everyone on their PC. Haven't seen anyone doing special projects
There's seriously a lot to change in there
pros:
colleagues
salary
location
some internal events
gym on site
cons: management, too stressful, hard to progress, dull (not a lively place), training given, high turnover and some more, food is always the same and expensive

pros: I am pursuing my Computer Science major and had a chance to become intern at Citi for 7 months. This is very great opportunity for me to start as a Software Developer in Banking environments. Got to understand and learn a lot what they do and what they requires from one IT engineer.
cons: In my opinion, my department is a bit un-friendly overall. As a freshie, I tried my best to make friend and talked to them for many reasons. But at the end, I could only talk with my manager (one of my best friend in office) and another colleague (he's also new Full-Time at a company). Others seem to don't care what people around doing, just finish their jobs and go home...

summary: Depending on the Department and Boss
advice: Encourage your employees, especially Entry Level, to keep studying and utilize the tuition reimbursement.
pros: Like all jobs, it all depends on the Department and the boss. If you have a good one there is possibility to work from home. Some call centers have their agents work from home too. Because it is an international company there is definitely a lot of options to move to. Tuition reimbursement offering is a definite plus. Not many utilizes this and they should.
cons: If you work in a Call Center, depending on your boss, you may be micromanaged which is typical at a Call Center. But if you do your work and do your time you can move up relatively quick if you keep looking.

advice: Keep aware of the workloads of your teams. Don't hire people who are unqualified as they just bog down the rest of the team. Sometimes you have to let someone useless go, even if they're nice and not directly affecting your work and day. But they are negatively affecting your team members' work and days.
pros: Can work from home, dress very casual, no micromanagement.
cons: Little growth opportunity and managers detached from their teams day to day. People hired because a friend of a friend even if grossly unqualified, creating more work for current team mates to pick up the slack. Farthest from a meritocracy I've come across, unfortunately. At Citi, its pick the best friend for the job, not best person for the job.

advice: Please make sure the ones responsible for counting the incentives makes no mistake. I had a terrible experience one time with a miscalculation that that person made, and I was investigated as if I INTENTIONALLY wanted to get the money.  I hope this observation goes to the site director, not only to the hr dept. They have to know what happened to us. This affected so many people.
pros: Training, scope of the job, team leader and teammates are wonderful. You learn a lot and get paid well. And, it's dayshift. You get a lot of support from supervisors.
cons: I just wish they were a bit closer. I live in Bacoor, and they are now in Taguig.  they used to be in Makati.

summary: Best Employer and Amazing Leadership team
pros:
Amazing Leadership team - I am very impressed by the quality of leaders across the board in Citi. 

Employee Care - An employee's health and safety is always the priority for Leadership team and I have experienced this through the Pandemic. Senior Management ensures maximum flexibility is given to the employees to have an amazing work - Life balance.

Amazing Career opportunities within Citi globally for people to learn and develop their skills. Feels exciting to return to work everyday, As they say " There is never a dull moment as Citi"

Tenure - I have observed employees with a longer tenure of association with Citi, which strengthens my belief of career progression with this great organization.
cons: Never experienced anything negative so far.

summary: Hit or miss with operations management but sketchy HR
advice: Empower decision-making at the C15 and below level. Even first-level MDs don't make decisions which is apparent in how long it takes to get anything done. We get that your asinine bonus is based on those decisions but it fosters terrible leadership and lag times. No wonder Citi is stuck in the past and not actually making progress to imrpove.
pros: Mentoring, collaboration, teamwork. Easy to move around and across teams with personal support along the way from C-14+ personnel.
cons:
Poor leadership / decision making - who makes an actual decision around here?
HR is a mess which can result in bait and switch jobs after signing on and don't even get me started on their onboarded.... or honestly lack there of.

summary: Citigroup: An organization in transition handling it well.
advice: Continously communicate the vision of the organization and put more emphasis on engaging employees at work.
pros: The size of the organization offers wide opportunities, so if you could potentially spend an entire career with this company in many different functional roles. The benefits are best in the industry. Communication from senior leadership about important issues is always made available to employees via the company website. There are many learning and professional development courses available to employees.
cons: The culture is not always a meritocracy and can be highly political. Senior management does communicate but it is not always timely. Workloads can be high due to restructuring in the last couple years. Compensation for certain positions isn't the highest in the industry.

summary: Remember to recognize existing employees and promote from within.
advice: Take the longer view; remember it's easier and more profitable to sustain and grow existing customers than to acquire new ones.  Same goes for nurturing and developing current employees.
pros: There are many talented people there, and lots of opportunities to do some interesting work.
cons: Unfortunately, the work is hampered by lots of bureaucracy. Often times, corporate politics, rather than results, determine who gets ahead. The infrastructure is antiquated.  Too little attention is paid to strenthening the long term health of the company.  Every project is reviewed for quick pay back without thought to investing in long term growth.  Recent layoffs contributed to severe morale issues; just waiting for the other shoe to drop in 2009.

advice: Please compensate your employees based on their merit not based on how long they have been with the company. That's why you can't keep a talent!
pros: Large company. Many opportunities to move around. Flexible work schedule- could be bad for you depends.. see cons below. A well known brand- good to have on your resume.
cons: Currently not in a good place financially, so this will reflect on your pay, bonuses, and overall job satisfaction. hardly any work and life balance, esp. if you are in IT area. Flexible work schedule also means that you are expected to work from home if you can't get things done in the 9-10 hrs you spent in the office. Forget about asking for more resources in this economy.

summary: "Good learning opportunities, very consontrated on client service reviews".
advice:
Mgmt should focus on employee strengths and not just on numbers.
The most important asset in any business should be "their employees".
Unfortunately, the pressures from making goals, and making your numbers to keep your job has superseded that vision and is increasingly becoming obsolete.
pros:
The incentives as far as 401k match is the highlight. 
Otherwise, medical insurance is expensive.
Vacation is usually 2 weeks to start.
cons:
Basically, the name of the game is customer service and anonymous client reviews".
Anonymous ratings on your performance can literally damage your career.
These "anonymous client rveviews" or "KDS" are incorporated in your compensation.
Goals need to be met and exceeded, KDS has to be great or else your lifespan in this company 
will be very short lived.

advice: You can only do so much in non-monetary compensation to retain talent. With high inflation and increasing living expenses in Singapore, sooner than later, money talks and talent walks.
pros: Dynamic work environment. You will be acknowledged if you are dedicated and invest your time to achieve performance. The management is open minded and willing to listen to your ideas. Good track record will open doors internally - career mobility. Good flexi benefits. Good reputable name and experience in the industry.
cons: Long working hours if you want to be somebody (no work-life balance, stiff competition). Pay in operations is not competitive for those who stayed with the company more than 2 years. Poor bonus.

summary: Plenty of opportunities to add value for ambitious individuals, but bureaucracy is frustrating
advice: Senior management should embrace technology or at least come to terms that they do not understand technology and should defer to more junior people who do.
pros: If you have an understanding of front office, finance, and technical skills (savvy Excel user and VBA) you can change processes / add value / undertake projects with significant exposure to senior management.
cons: Many employees including managers have a very poor understanding of technology, which creates opportunity but also frustration as managerial support is hard to rally.  The bureaucracy at such a large firm is expected, but I am still shocked by how long simple changes take to execute.

advice: Keep it up! Citi is such a great place to be part of especially if one likes the extra challenge. Working at Citi is not for you if you are looking for an 8 to 5 job.
pros: There is a good focus on performance, talent development, employee satisfaction. Pay is heavily based on meritocracy, but is somewhat at par with its competitors in the country.
cons: Due to budget cuts and hiring freezes the past 6-7 years, employees have to put in a lot of extra hours to get things done, and so work life balance suffers a lot. But somehow the culture / environment does something about it thru reengineering or process improvements.

advice: True global offering for all clients, Pay internals, more visibility from Corbat - how about ongoing company calls to stress strategy and initiatives?, fire bottom 2-3% per year - too many underperforming long term employees working here making good money.
pros: Mobility, career growth, nice people, diverse client base, solid training.
cons: Constant change in strategy over the years, lack of integration & innovation, HR strategy failing - will pay new hires salaries 20-30% above existing long term high performing employees who haven't had raises in 5 years. Huge attrition in 2015 including HR staff. Pay high performing long team internals first! Businesses running around with their own strategies which are constantly changing.

pros:
-depending on which line of business you are in, where I worked, the work-life balance is perfect. 
-i had quite close-knit relationships with the team and other teams.
cons:
-being in mass-market/priority banking/private clients, sometimes the revenue pressure put on its sales staff brings about certain detrimental behaviour to its customers.

-in the line of business i was in, most of the management is promoted from within. While that is good as it retains the culture of that business, it is also good to bring in talent from outside, as it prevents "group-think" and allows a refreshing way of approaching the business.

-we become too "pigeon-holed" to move into other roles, despite the claim that mobility is relatively easy.

advice: If you take care of your employees,  they well  take care of the customers.  Money is important, but you can't put a price on life.
pros: A steppingstone a big recognized name to put on your resume.
cons: Citibank doesn't care for its employees, alot has changed since I first started working there.  Very long days with no work/life balance.  If you don't have a life outside of work this is the job for you.  Poor pay especially if you are an internal promotion.  Which should be the opposite.  The amount of stress, pressure, and work load isn't worth the pay.  I wouldn't recommend working at Citi to my enemies.

advice: Stop trying to make your numbers look good at the end of the year and giving the CEO huge bonuses and start focusing on those people who are doing to nitty gritty work to keep the company moving forward. Give them more incentive to work by keeping them employeed and providing bonuses (not just monetary but morale boosting too).
pros: Management was actively trying to improve the culture and it was working.
cons: There were way too many layoffs each year. I know some are expected, but every year in 4th quarter they had them and told those being let go the week before Thanksgiving.

summary: Okay - if you're fine with being a robot
advice: Treat employees like people. Make time for them. Listen to them. Don't dictate.
pros: Great incentives, benefits, and 16 weeks of maternity leave. I'll give them that
cons: The way Citi molds its people managers isn't right. All the true people managers leave because of how they see the company really squeezing the life out of employees. You have to realize you may develop anxiety from working at a Citi call center. The managers become dictators and the only way to advance is really to develop relationships with your managers (be extremely likeable) and to really do more than you are paid for. Favoritism is strong at Citi. -former supervisor

advice: Employees should have the salaries raised to match the competitors, more people should be designated to shifts so that the overhours level would decrease. Experianced employees should be not invloved in BAU process at all, but often they are.
pros: Working in multilingual environment with well educated people, paid overhours and benefits like Multisport and bonus paid holidays. Working in english, joining the international calls.
cons: lot of overhours, monotonous but often stresfull job in TC dept, no remote working, bad work conditions, non exceptional salary, no business trips, no place for car parking. Career path only for 2-3 years, after second promotion one has to be very strong skilled, or spend his/hers life at work to get next promotions.

advice: Please increase our base pay. Working here is stressful, job duties can be tedious, and a higher pay would give us more incentive to stay.
pros: A good place to start your career and to develop skills necessary to succeed in a finance roll. No micro management. The career is what you make it. There are opportunities to work in different areas of the company to figure out the career that’s best for you. High job turn over allows opportunities to advance fast.
cons: Low salaries, long work hours, outdated systems causing a lot of manual work/issued. More work Politics as you move up the corporate chain. High job turnover allows opportunities to advance fast however your salary stays low.

summary: badly organized group of talented people
advice: be managers and less selfish on average
pros: large company with lots of possibilities and career mobility within, many different structured programs, extensive training programs for new hires, and lots of diversity. also possibilities to transfer to different geographies. a big company that won't lose it's ground or coverage even when the overall economy is unhealthy
cons: too large, really incompetent managers who are too focused on themselves to focus on the entire team at end and utilizing people to their advantages, lots of politics, not a meritocracy at all. i think it very mediocre with about 30-40% of people, and they stay around for political reasons. the smart people are mismanaged and never reach their potentials.

advice: Start caring for the customers and understanding the frustration that result from lack of proper information.
pros: The health benefits are pretty good. Which is good, because you are going to need it from the extreme stress of working under pressure.
cons: Lunch times and schedules are shortened often, at will by management. Too much inconsistency in how information is given to customers. Not much support from management if you need assistance. Too much mandatory overtime required. Many customers are very frustrated with lack of real help when they need it and they hate us for it. And as a customer  service agent, you are the first to hear the customers anger and frustrations. And they are plentiful.

advice:
Monitor work from home policies. It is highly misused by staff and mgmt alike.
Encourage feedback from direct clients and customers to judge year end performance review, as a means to promoting deserving employees
Hard work is downplayed very often due to favoritism.
pros:
Great environment
Flexible working hours.
Potential for professional growth(if you have a nice boss) - copied from a previous post but couldnt have sd it better
Good vacation time.
cons:
Too many processes delays projects. 
Promotions and raises to favorites
Huge salary discrepancies even at same level of experience and no measures to correct it.
No thought has been applied to the latest Outsourcing strategies, very soon temps with little or no experience will be our bosses
Lack of planning (in my team atleast)

advice: Focus more on employee development/culture
pros: Provides great flexibilty with working from home options and good vacation/benefits provided.  It truly assists to be more balanced with your personal/home life with work.  One big plus to work here especially if you are starting a family.
cons:
Slow progression in upward mobility
Salary is not competitive to market value
Minimal training or employee education encouragement until late this year
Favoritism
Minimal attention from senior management
Employee survey  - minimal participation for improvements
Set deadlines all the time without understanding the change that it will bring and how it can be delivered without breaking what is already working properly.  Lessons learned from past need to be applied to all processes.

summary: nice but not for the long run
advice:
Treat current employees better and offer competitive packages. 
Reduce the red tape associated with getting access, requesting a change etc. Most developers spend more time on submitting VC, VSR, RFC, VT, VR for someone's approval than on actual development tasks.
pros: Citigroup is excellent place for a software developer to start and get hands on experience in the financial world. You can get exposed to a number of business areas and a wider set of technologies.
cons: The Compensation is not competitive compared to other investment banks. Citigroup seems to place little value on existing employees and, instead of promoting current employees, it believes in hiring from outside. This contributes to poor morale and high employee turnover.

advice: Reward the employees that are delivering, not the employees that have mastered the politcs of pretending to add value, which is common skill at the Bank.
pros: Global Bank with colleagues that will give you access to friends and colleagues from around the world.  Talented professionals that you will be able to learn and benefit from.  A true multi-national firm in every sense. Competitive pay, industry leader, and strong market share in financial industry
cons: Very political organization that changes quickly.  Unstable risk, need to keep a close pulse to incoming changes, or you can suddenly find yourself in a worst place. Unfortunately, it's not always about what you know, or what you deliver.

advice: Treat your employees with a little more respect, we aren't children. Find a way to move things along so we don't move at the "speed of Citi"
pros: Nice people, decent benefits. In my line of work with the company, schedules can be a little flexible.
cons:
The reality is, it's a huge company and things take forever to move anywhere. We have projects we proposed last year that only just got the budget approved. Don't expect a raise, because "HR can't do anything right now". But the management continues to give themselves new titles.

Also you will be working for a soul crushing financial firm which ruined many Americans lives in the housing crisis and the recession that followed.

summary: Great benefits, but minimum chance of internal promotion
advice: Dedication to personal growth of employees and internal advancements, notifying employees of metric/rule changes immediately instead of last minute.
pros: Great benefits, part time schedules, large call center, generous PTO bank and sick time, tuition reimbursement, philanthropy and charity efforts to benefit the community.
cons: Difficult to advance internally, especially if you work on 'the floor' in customer service/sales or collections. Many who obtain a degree and want to advance typically have to leave the company and reapply after 6-12 months and then are hired back on at the promoted rank. Metrics are very unattainable and often reset without notice in collections, which I felt were to keep from paying out collector bonuses when earned.

advice: Look at the senior management to remove dead weight.  Multiple levels of re-engineering are not considering to full scope of the positions which are being reduced or eliminated.  The balance sheet line moving should also be considered.  I have seem management move from one region into another and increasing the base and benefits paid out without the merit.  simply moving from north America's internal budget and moving to LATAM, is not saving the company money.
pros: The banking title for positions sounds great during the interviewing process.
cons: The company is still downsizing and offshoring most of the work.  Continuing to drive a lean working environment, which is forcing turnover and position hoping within the company.

summary: high stress and push for questionable sales
advice: stop with the conflicting messages. Management talks about ethics yet gives and pushes for  unachievable goals. Micromanaging and daily production tracking to the point of causing stress and anxiety.
pros: Benefits are pretty good in comparison to competitors. Also Banking products are great and client centered.
cons: Strong focus around production to the point where ethics are questioned. Push for clients depositing and/or moving existing funds into checking accounts, so retail branches can meet their  goals. High push for sales, to the point where clients leave feeling as they were sold products they didn't know about or agree to. Conflicting messages from management. Company is strictly product pushing and only cares about the bottom line

summary: Beware of yearly layoffs...it will happen to you
advice: Google the WARN notice. It's a mandatory notification for mass layoffs
pros: Great resume builder/entry level job for recent college graduates. The Citigroup name will look good in future interviews. The company provides extensive training before you start. Overall the direct managers are knowledgeable and willing to help. The work itself can be very interesting. The pay is ok.
cons: Every year Citigroup will accumulate a back-log of cases, hire an abundance of temporary employees (while converting a few 'temps' to permanent status to give an appearance of legitimacy)...... the remaining analyst will work around the clock off striving to become an exempt employee, and when the case backlog is finished upper management will proceed to layoff everybody and the kitchen sink. The work is stressful and you always get the impression that you can be fired at any given moment.

advice: Be  a little employee centric . Learn from Standard chartered which is customer and employee centric as it truly lives on it motto here for good .
pros: Some company truly lives on the values . Citi never sleep and truly it wont let you sleep . Initally I was enhusiastic but slowly I got to know how this company work , long working hours , no holidays they make you stretch I have seen employees stretching for more than 11 hours everyday .... customer centric company with little or no care to employee .They hire you with attractive pay and make you work like donkey .
cons: Stay away from this company if you seek your well being.

advice: Get another Sr Ops Mngr that understands the environment... Soon.
pros: No parking fees in Ft Mill.  Pretty good benefits.  Lots of PTO (if you can get ahead enough to take it).
cons: Not the place to be if you want to come to work and be able to use the tools provided to accomplish the job.  Not enough people locally that can help with the constant changes in policy and procedure.  Tech issues prevent work from being completed.  Hard to to tell if upper management gets it because they don't ask the right questions.  Upper management has been blended in from an hourly rate / micro managed collections center environment to an exempt environment.

jobTitle: Assistant Vice President - Senior Analyst (Project Manager)
summary: Great company culture, but poor salary and some bad managers
advice: Some managers on VP, SVP, D, MD levels totally forget that half of their main duties (besides strategy) is leading people and they totally ruin colleagues working in their line. This should be stopped and those autocratic leaders who do not respect people, and only consider them as objects should be replaced.
pros: Great multicultural environment, friendly colleagues, global projects, network groups
cons: Poor salary. Sites are getting closed due to cost saving and forcing people to leave or join teams they never wanted to. Some managers are over-stretching their directs, some so autocratic that they fire the servant leaders creating a culture of fear

advice: Have a more precise workforce allocation method when cutting heads. Some teams are left overloaded vs others are oversubscribed.
pros:
Learn to work with large teams within a high matrixed environment. 
A global experience. 
Ethical culture of compliance.
cons:
Change is slow. The constant environment is always restructuring. Many multi million projects never get finished due to this consequence. 
Must put in the years to move ahead in the firm, specific to the back office for this job market, Its better to jump around and get better pay as long as you are comfortable with change, it’s a good year when you get no bonus and a little above inflation raise.

advice: Stop running the bank like it is a regional start-up. Thousands lost their jobs due to where they worked vs how skilled they were (most of these were work from home agents, so this had nothing to do with sites closing). Pay your people.
pros: Was able to work from home for most of my 10 years. Thanks to the never-ending layoffs, was able to attain a large number of different skills.
cons: Constant down-sizing and re-organization. Outdated systems. Management merry-go-round where those who have no clue about their team's work are tasked to lead. Pay raises are slim, if any at all (I had 4 out of 5 years where the yearly increase was 0 or less than 1%).

advice: Pay more attention to what is happening in your teams than the politics of the company.
pros: Encouraged to learn new things. You have unlimited access to all Udemy courses so you can learn pretty much whatever you want in your spare time.
cons: The communication at the company is terrible. Offshore contractors barely communicate and cause a significant number of issues. Management don't seem to have time to reply to simple emails. A lot of kids right out of coding bootcamps are being hired with absolutely no experience or knowledge in their area of supposed expertise. they are also being paid significantly more than employees who have been with the company for years and are in the same position.

advice: Spend more time listening to the voice of the employees and implement immediately resolution’s to the pain points that employees are faced with daily. Increase broadband and faster processing speeds so that the everyday branch employee can work efficiently rather than spend wasteful time on phone with tech support.
pros: Great work life balance. Improving wealth management resources.
cons: Understaffed. Systems constantly crash or run extremely slow. Too many systems which are poorly integrated. ZERO back office support around fraud, KYC, client servicing, and outsourcing of service for the Citigold segment which advertises 24/7 US client support. False. Mid-line managers awful and give zero support when needed unless the issue directly impacts their wallets.

summary: Great platform to start as Returning Woman
pros: I returned to work after a gap of 3 years when I joined Citi exactly a year ago. I was skeptical about the return and unsure if I would be able to "handle" the corporate journey. Today, when I look back, it was the amazing team that I was fortunate to be part of and the support of my manager that helped me reach where I am today and experience confidence and success. Also, a wonderful organization to be part of that offers work flexibility, a free hand for trail and error on other things that makes me (and many more like me ) want to give our best.
cons: Nothing that I think off

advice: Make crisper organizational decisions quickly. Just like capital markets hate uncertainty so do Citi employees.
pros:
- Global reach. Citi's size creates specializaed functions that enables you to develope skills that are critical to the function. 
- Advancement potential. Most positions are what you make of them. Should you choose to excel and go after projects/improvements you can have an impact and advance yourself.
- Some very smart people. Most divisions have a great culture.
cons:
- Always in the regulator's scope and the public eye.
- In recent years, a very fluid organization.
- Specilized functions. If you or your funciton is moved out, no longer needed or otherwise superflous you will be at risk unless you diversify your skillset.

summary: Just a place to work for right now
advice: Get your stuff together. Offer schedules like Friday Saturday off, Weekends to Tenure Agents, or Sunday Mondays off. Your literally giving your employees nothing to look forward to accept getting the hell out of there.
pros: Steady Hours Full-time, benefits are good as well
cons: They offer bonus but don't plan on getting it your better off thinking you will never get a bonus so when you get a bonus it feels good, because when you think you might bonus they might fail you on a call.  Also they could careless about tenure employees, they would give the good shifts to the new employees first rather then the old employees. Split days off so forget about it if you have a family.  Only work for Citi if you can start as a Supervisor or Trainer not worth the stress as a regular agent.

advice: It is important to value your employees and provide them with the necessary conditions to collaborate, an overly crowded open space is not favorable for collaboration and concentration.
pros: We had Steve Gates as head of North America Design and it was a great time at Citi for designers. I had the pleasure to work and collaborate with a phenomenal team composed of copywriters, information architects,  art directors, and producers.
cons: The building does not have an area set up for designers to work or feel like a valuable asset for the company. It's too crowded and I hear that the current team conditions have not improved but rather worsen.

summary: Overall a very progressive firm in which to forge a career
pros: Ample opportunity to develop skill-set. There is a position and capacity to progress regardless of your background, strengths and weaknesses. Management structure is inclusive and transparent without endless layers of reporting lines unlike other large institutions. Internal mobility, including location migration is supported here.
cons: Work-Life balance remains a challenge depending on the line of business you work in. Precedence is of course reflected in theory (at HR level) but very much depends on line of business and managements interpretation. Like all global organizations, certain migration of processes and functions to lower cost locations means you will likely experience one or more redundancy scenario's per 7-10 year time frame.

summary: Going through a transition period job security is questionable.
advice: You get what you pay for.  If you want the best and the brightest your going to have to pay them for their talent.
pros: Great place to work, lots of opportunities to move up if you want to.
cons: Based on bonus eligible departments.   For those interested in moving up you will take a pay cut to move into a manager or team lead position.  Because no one wants to take a pay cut it greatly reduces the amount of qualified knowledgeable people who apply for these positions.  The managers you work with aren't always the most knowledgeable and this can create frustration on both sides.

summary: Citigroup: Nice place, if you can keep your job.
advice: Stop buying subprime mortgages!
pros: Good brand name for someone looking to build a resume. The program is similar to others at other large investment banks. Training was very good and amid the most comprehensive on the street. I like the people I work with but that's one very small sample of the company.
cons: LARGE, downsizing is ongoing so morale is not great. I am not really affected by the "largeness" since I am pretty much lowest on the totem pole and don't have to make requests to higher management, etc. but I can see my superiors are frustrated. It sometimes takes a long time for things to get done.

summary: Perhaps they don't understand the meaning of the word "benefits"
advice: Why change now? It's worked for 200 years.
pros:
* If you're looking for a career move in a direction you've never travelled before, it's totally do-able. Just suck at your existing job. Rather than pay to get rid of you, they'll move you into an unrelated role. What? You mean people actually train for accountancy roles!
* If you're looking for a promotion, it's also quite easy to achieve. Just talk a lot about how awesome you are and what a great job you're doing. Actual doing any work is overrated.
cons: The “special” pricing laid out in the extended benefits plans were carefully negotiated to display maximum disdain for Citi employees.

advice: Be more transparent about what's going on with the initiatives and more clear on the role and responsibilites.
pros: Citigroup offers good compensation compared to my previous job and exposure to a different prespective in a much bigger company.  The current management team currently is very understanding of the needs to address personal issues without having to worry about missing meeting / unable to meet deadlines.
cons: The Politics at Citigroup is very difficult to deal with on a day to day basis. Everyone has an opinion on how to do something and very vocal about their thoughts but at some points it becomes counter productive.  This took a long time to sync in for many people.

advice: Get rid of silos and redesign  annual performance review process. Unify firm values - can name three siloes with different sets of values in the same firm (but that's behaviour is an effect of increasing siloization)
pros: Career development oportunnities both in terms of moving to diffrent function/business lines and across geographies.
cons:
Two fundamental flaws in Citi: Increasing siloization - lots of units serving supposedly the same purpose but often with opposite objectives which  produces lots of activities with zero value either for shareholders or customers , disgrutling annual assesment of employees performance based on bell-curve distribution. 
It kills teamwork, demotivate staff and inhibits the firm to reach its maximum potential.

summary: A company needs to be half in size and double in profit.
advice: Please think do you really need that many losers in your firm! Please try to retain talents by - pay per performance, trainings, and keeping healthy environment to let have leadership. Good people are not going to be there if they don't see growth in career.
pros: Nikko Citigroup has a vast and strong client base in Japan. It is a large organization and leads in many deals every year. This could be a place to get some hands on experience on some complex and messy financial systems.
cons: Management is not efficient and competent. More people than required. Need to be trimmed in size and be efficient in operations.

advice: Take a good look at your senior team members. Some of them are not qualified to lead. They are good at making a speech and playing politics. Some of them are seriously senile. They frustrate the good employees into leaving so you end up with the trash!
pros: Intellectually stimulating environment. Good exposure because of global footprint. Some really hardworking and smart colleagues.
cons: Since 2008, the firm seems to be on a downward slide. Pay is not competitive. Hours are long because of cost cutting i.e staff strength is significantly reduced.  Firm is beset with politics therefore not focusing on doing the right things. The management that shouts the loudest wins. Too big to fail, dead man walking.

summary: Citi Cards needs to be shaken up
advice: Invest in customer research, improve technology. We have some great people saddled with not so great goals and a subpar organizational structure. Keep it simple and give people an incentive to collaborate for the greater good of the company.
pros: Even with the recent downturn and layoffs there are some very strong people at Citi Cards. There is a great knowledge base to tap into across the company.
cons: Too heavily matrixed, too siloed. Not nearly enough focus on customer needs and insights to shape business strategy. Very redundant, overlapped organizational structure. Need to make it easier to facilitate knowledge sharing. So much organizational upheaval that it's hard to get momentum going on major initiatives.

summary: Stressful place in constant transition with frequent management changes in technology
advice: Citi has to be broken back to its original component parts. This company can never operate as one. 15 years after mergers it still operates as different companies as there are no real synergies between them.
pros: It's a big place with good opportunities. Originally a very good company but not after the mergers
cons:
Opportunities exist only if you have come as a part of team with your boss from another company in the capital markets technology. Or if you are in UK where all the management is moving to.
Old citi bankers have no value - the culture is to push out all the experienced people.
Too much bureaucracy.

summary: A few things about the job
advice: Leverage the company's breadth and depth of products to be able to weather this economic crisis. Strong leadership and vision are required of anyone claiming to be at the helm and driving real change.
pros: The best reason for working at Citigroup Global Markets is the feedback you get from management. I was working in a small department where my manager was able to provide feedback catered to the project I was involved in.
cons: The difference in cultures between my department and other areas of Citigroup is striking. In my department everyone is dealing with things in a calm and calculated manner. Other areas are less peaceful and are a lot harder to adjust to.

advice: My advice would be to keep working to keep the values and culture of the company strong.
pros: Citi is a great place to work for several reasons, but the one that stood out to me the most was their concern for their employees' continued learning and growth.  The firm offers a wide variety of training across a number of topics, and the medium by which they're offered varies as well. Secondly, it's a global company which provides employees to work with others based abroad, as well as actually re-locate and work in a different country.  Lastly, the firm offers a comprehensive benefits package.
cons: The technology provided to employees could use an upgrade.

summary: Moved around a lot last year. Many managers.
advice: Keep giving people less money every year and all the best people will leave. I will only put up with it for this year.
pros: I spent pretty much an entire year doing nothing. I moved from group to group until finally I was in a position that only had around 5 hours a week of real work. I had an awesome summer where I was off pretty much the entire time. However I eventually had to give it up or risk a go nowhere career.
cons: There are still a lot of projects being canned and people getting laid off. Change is constant and drastic, never stopping.

advice: Great Management in certain branches, Area Director is awesome.
pros: Great company to work for, stress free In certain branches. The pay could be a little better, but all of management is awesome. Some branches even offer a Monday through Friday schedule (8:30-4:30)
cons: Sales Goals can be a little over bored, and if you don't make your goals you start off with verbal warnings. (Usually goals are always met). They never promote within, I have been with the company 6 YEARS and I have been declined when I notified higher management that I wanted to move up with the company, the only reason I am still employed with citi is because I love the team/co-workers I work with.

summary: Changed products mean more abusive sales practices.
advice: Decide on a market sector that you would like to serve. If it is the high net worth individuals, then don't expect them to want to be treated like a super market customer. If it is mid-level clients, then stop charging them fees that will drive them away. They don't seem to care about the underbanked (a growth market) so advice there.
pros: Good benefits package. People at the retail level who are well meaning and desire to do what it takes to keep the company alive.
cons: Upper management are disconnected with the future of banking resulting in middle managers who have very little idea what they are realistically  asking employees to do.

advice:
HR involvement with employees is zero
Employee technical growth path and learning has to be improved further
Stop focusing only on one person who is good at net-working. Also concentrate on others who can do better if an oppurtnity is provided 
Don't assume networking is everything it is only a part, networking without performance is useless
pros:
Good work life balance
My Manager was excellent and so co-operative
Takes care of employee health, life-style and trainings
Flexible work hours
cons:
Performance is not considered while Ratings
Mobility is not very functional and will not respond in spite of continuous follow up
Too many mangers has created confusion and does not know whom should be approached for promotions, hikes, concerns, opportunities and feedbacks

advice: The data driven approach to automation sounds effective but I serious doubts to the accuracy of the data being collected due to a complete and utter lack of training in how that should be gathered. I can't begin to understand why a training course on the specifics of gathering this data wasn't created and utilized.
pros: Citi provides good pay and benefits. Additionally there seems to a commitment to providing a good physical working environment that favors and promotes teamwork.
cons: There is a lack of structured investment in entry level employees while there are many trainings available, a vast majority of employees are unaware that they exist and aren't encouraged to utilize them by management.

advice:
Revisit how diversity is being looked at and mananged in all facets.  There's talk about the commitment to diversity, but nothing done to retain, commitment to promotion and formal dialogue and plan with leadership to address.

Accountability follow-up model to verify saves and solutions provide value and completed.
pros: Great co-workers, benefits and pay.
cons:
Diversity is talked about, but never looked at in promoting to leadership roles. In addition, diversity is never discussed when it comes to workforce, talent designations or reductions.

Lack of accountability for people making commitments on expense reductions with solutions that never come to fruition.  Expenses to third party vendors for solutions that add no value and could be developed in house for 1/4 cost.

summary: Not too bad to learn some good stuff and gain experience but if you stay too long you will lose your market value
pros: Good salary and benefits, good career opportunities due to large size of operations, well recognized brand. Nice office on Marynarska (although very bad location!)
cons: Crazy structure not rasy to navigate and understand, decision making authority on ver high level for everything (usually NYC) which leads to huge bureaucracy and lack of ability to make sound decision in the right time. Employees not empowered. Long working hours. You can be a very moderate employee and survive for years as lack of clear objectives and KPIs make it difficult to evaluate your input. Lack objectivity and trasparency in bonus process

advice: Do less micromanaging and worry more about the happiness of your employees. Happy employees who feel appreciated and treated fairly will stick around and will try their best.
pros: Decent benefits, excellent way of rewarding employees regularly with quarterly events.
cons: They will hire too many people only to lay them all off and this is done often with this company, they are worried solely on monitoring your amount of work done each day but less worried on why their "standards" are not accurate. Employees aren't appropriately judged, reports are skewed, working conditions not favorable, dirty environment, force you to perform special duties not related to the job you were hired to do (like spending months moving shelves around).

summary: Good for freshers, excellent for mediocre people, but can be frustrating for highly ambitious and intelligent people
advice: Please stop focus on VOE (voice of employees) surveys- it really adds no value at all
pros: Good initial pay, decent annual increment, work very easy on scale of difficulty, chilled out work environment, good employee related initiatives from HR like Zumba Kick Boxing Club Mahindra membership Home Drop facility
cons: Beurocracy, lack of strong and inspiring leadership, extremely poor work life balance, career oriented people work like slaves, number of extra hours considered as hard work (which can be inefficiency in many cases), too many people managers who are unfit to deliver functionally, too many non value add activities and initiatives, favouritism

summary: A good bank, some areas for improvement
advice: Equity Trading in Institutional Equities' could improve its senior and middle management. Compared to other parts of Citi, equity trading leadership is uninspired, unimpressive, behind the curve on industry trends and unable to generate a coherent vision for the business, much less prioritize and communicate priorities internally in an effective manner.
pros: Corbat and top brass have a good grasp on corporate responsibility, goals, vision and communication. Some areas like retail banking and private banking have tremendous upside and are on the right track.
cons: Building internal relationships and managing up are essential to succeed at Citi in Equities Trading. Knowledge, business acumen, hard work and planning are not highly valued in that particular area.

summary: Can do better-people don’t only work for money
advice:
Promote your employees who are deserving
Employee engagement
Value your people
pros:
Citi credit card and savings/debit acct for free-no annual charges
Meal and transpo allowance for OT and night shift
Good salary if moving from another company
Good salary start for fresh grads
cons:
Depending on department employee engagement and activities are overlooked at
Hiring incompetent managers from other companies
Hiring experienced employees from other companies but are not really good enough than those on lower level
Location-North and East bus have very indefinite times. Sometimes takes more than 30mins to arrive.
Increase every year is performance based and is very little! The longer one stays the more one realizes the increase since beginning has not been beneficial

summary: Find a god father to grow your career
advice: some old employee in organization don't give their 100% percent as they have become too complacent, they are still there just to get fixed salary every month.  Do something about such low performing employees as they are spoiling the culture and motivating others to do same.
pros: global mobility, big brand, decent salary, some people are very good(not all), if you are good and are in right project with right manager, you can be rewarded well.
cons: Need to have a god father to grow in career.  lot of bureaucracy- very difficult to get any thing done.  inefficient engineering process, most of the projects are just run the bank kind(no new work)

advice: Build up a proper strategy that will allow Citi to navigate its competitors and tge Fintech disruption. Design banking products that actually benefit your customers. Eyeing marginal profits first means that not a single product is competitive, and it’s no wonder Citi struggles even when against similar sized competitors.
pros: Not much to say really.
cons:
In the long term, management has no idea how to lead the company in an age where traditional Financial Institutions are under competition from nimble Fintech competitors.

In the mid term, management flip flops between their strategy, wasting time and resources reversing the work of predecessors. This includes not investing in technology and softwares, trying to hire for cheap - you get monkeys.

In the short term, middle management is staffed by Management Associates who have no ground experience. They imagine theoretical outcomes and expect unrealistic results, that is a) not sustainable; b) demoralises staff.

summary: Great benefits and competitive pay, but limited growth opportunity, no trust, and challenging environment
advice: Security and bureaucracy are implemented in a way the stifles technologists, preventing them contributing beyond already established processes. Trust, access, and scope of authority are so limited, that technologists must use internally-developed interfaces which are extremely limited and prevent technologists from full performance of their jobs. Because employees must use internally-developed interfaces instead of actual industry standard software, they cannot maintain their skills or be competitive outside of Citi. This combined with extremely limited growth potential mean there is no incentive to remain.
pros: Great benefits, competitive pay, professional environment
cons: limited growth opportunity, challenging bureaucratic processes, limited trust and empowerment, less commitment to work/life balance

advice: Try a few skip-level meetings to get a real feel for your management staff.
pros: I worked with a great team, a great lead, and a great 1st line asst. Manager. Until they decided on a restructure.
cons: There are a few bad apples that truly seem to enjoy pulling the wings of flies if they could. If she's you're manager keep your head down loooow. She's just mean and she wasn't my lead so I just observed her actually make an employee cry. At one point they transferred our asst manager's and then his manager and his VP and her SVP all left to go to another bank and left us with no leaders.

summary: Extensive Controls, Poor HR, Outdated Tech, Inefficient Vendors/Stakeholders
advice: To stop having SVPs/C-12 and above leaders buffering the ugly side of work. If its bad, your turnover rate tells.
pros: Flexi Claim and no more.
cons: HR will not put in any effort to help with negotiation of remuneration. Onboarding guides and documents have broken/expired links. Extensive controls and processes, plus risk assessments every quarter. Every campaign requires every stakeholders input, not everyone is in sync. Irresponsible and clueless stakeholders. In local banks, dedicated developers turnaround time as quick as 30mins (outsourced developers in Citi takes up to 3 days, excluding need to rectify their work). While other banks adopted swift campaign execution process(via platforms), Citi rely heavily on Campaign Request Form (in excel sheet with multiple tabs). Make product managers really wonder if its cheaper to hire outsourced developers than to build a campaign execution platform managed internally by DSM (branding marketing) team.

advice: Learn and do your jobs
pros: Paid Time off,  Paid Time off
cons: This particular line of business doesn't not reflect the Citi that everyone speaks highly of.    In the Lockbox environment the only thing you have is your Paid time off.   Satisfying the client is all that matters.  PLEASE STAY AWAY from lockbox.  All the management should be fired for all the unethical things that occur at this location (6801 Colwell, Irving, TX.).   30 min lunches, you basically have to plead for a day off.  Your hard work will not be recognize, only the boot lickers are recognized.

advice: Listen and track HR issues. People being fired to cover other people. The proof is in the pudding. THERE IS NO ADVOCATE FOR THE LAY PEOPLE!!!
pros: Benefits = Insurance/Flex account, 401K plus match, adequate vacation banks
cons: Upper Management DOES NOT follow what they preach! Power of One felt promising but is a joke and no one follows! There is no Work/Life balance, just work. Even if your titled as a people manager, expected to be an IT Tech just about! Overworked!!! No support or advocates to those who aren't part of the 'good ole fellas' club. If you are not at the top of the food chain, YOU WILL BE EATEN!!

summary: Traditional company trying to be like the startups/innovative company
advice:
They got to be truthful to what the say. 
Global mobility is no longer a selling point and they should stop mentioning that.
Senior management in NY should stop travelling and save the budget for the hardworking employees.
Should let local office has their say and let them have their own priorities.
Restructuring of organisation chart is brutal - they fire individual with less than 24 hours notice.
pros: Work-life balance, relatively high base pay compared to other local bank, many things to learn (everyday is different)
cons:
-Low bonus
-Typical American company  (Global Office (American), Regional Office (Indian), Local Office (Local/Filipinos))
- Workload can be very overwhelming with almost no off-peak period.

summary: Citigroup-not the best and not the worst
advice: Treat employees as an asset and not as an expense
pros:
It is a large company and not going out of business any time soon.
Company has many programs.

Company is large enough for relocation and job mobility.
The company offers different flexible spending options like parking, health care, and transit.
cons:
-lots of silos
-groups do not talk to each other and lots of finger pointing
-high cost for medical (2009- $82 per paycheck)
-a tendency to lay off employees and bring in foreign consultants to work slightly cheaper
-employees never meet with HR, even during benefits season.  Employees tend to get an email with updates.  There is no avenue to discuss issues related to Human Resources.

advice: Start telling the truth
pros: Im not sure what the best reason to work for citi is.  It used to be a respected name in banking but that  is not the case anymore.  I would stay away for now and hope they can dig out of the hole they are in.
cons: It used to be a good name but current market conditions have changed.  I originally felt that there was plenty of room for advancement but they seem to hire senior management from outside and are very reluctant to promote from within.Senior management has been telling us we were well capitalized for over a year however we continue to need bailout money.

summary: Is Citi changing for the good?
advice: Trim the layers of "management", trim the "fat" (and there are a lot of people who don't seem to be doing much, while others on the same floor are inundated with process/work), invest in new technologies, be nimble and quick to make decisions, communicate effectively to lower levels.
pros: Since this is a large corporation, there are plenty of opportunities for movement. As far as technology, some organizations use the latest cutting edge stuff, others seem to be stuck in legacy/old technologies. The key is being in the right team.
cons: Since this is a very large company, things don't change quickly. Due to layers of management, communication gets lost between layers and laterally.

summary: Good company to learn knowledge about one role
advice: May need to take some time to listen to the employee. Also need to give more flexibility to middle managers.
pros: A lot of resources and a lot of aspects about the mortgage industry. And you will see a lot of great, smart people around you. Teammates are great and competitive.
cons: Management doesn't communicate enough with employees. Too many restrictions on small issues. As such a big company, site managers and middle managers doesn't really have a lot of power. Some small technical issues has to go through the center of the company, which is not on the same site. Of course, that is typical in big Bureaus or government.

summary: Challenging with lots of projects and changes in systems
advice: Senior mgt could create a committee to gather feedback from team heads on the workload of employee to address issues and gain anonymous feedback for things that they would like to see being improved.
pros: A great learning environment. People tend to be very professional and are accountable to each other. Inculcate a meritocratic environment. Most of the Citibank folks here are extremely hardworking, committed and very professional.
cons: With numerous changes, employee tend to be bogged down with one project after another. Can be subjected with long working hours. This can drive potential staff to competitors who pay at a more competitive rate and have better working hours/flexible options.

summary: Hell-hole, poor leadership, and questionable decision making.
advice: The best advice to senior mangement would be to listen to the employees.  The mere fact that the firm experienced a mass exodus of Financial Advisors in 2008-2009-2010, and the threat of even more defections with the new poorly designed investment platform, should be evidence enough thaty senior management need to pay attention to what the employees are really thinking.
pros: The 'supposed' prestige...and that's it.  The firm does have a long storied history, but those days are long behind it.
cons: The new investment platform that CPWM adopted from Pershing earlier this in Feb 2011 has been a resounding disaster.  This is a company that waited until the last minute to choose a new vendor for it's investment platform, and upon finally choosing Pershing, rushed the poorly designed system to the field.  The rest is a historical embarassment.

summary: Was a good place to work but everyday it is getting worse
advice: changes within the company should not only be beneficial to the company but also to the customers and employees
pros: You have a chance to move up if you work hard or if you know someone, the environment in the branch  could be good depending on the managers, the company is well known and has a good name internationally
cons: The compensation plan for sales is not great unless you are in a branch with affluent clients , the benefits for employees have gotten worse over the years, workload has increased but the pay has not, upper management expectations are unrealistic and micromanagement can de unmotivating and frustrating

advice: Advise your kids not to work here.
pros: Hours and compensation are OK. Benefits slightly below OK. If you are a 9-to-5er, then this is for you.
cons: Too much internal politics. Too much bureaucracy. Review process is highly subjective, behind closed-doors, and not transparent at all. While compensation is OK but incentive is absolutely NOT OK. Plus it is a very mature industry facing tremendous headwinds right now, so it's not that exciting to be there, unless you think credit card or consumer lending is your calling, which is not the case for me. Oh and did I mention the many rounds of lay-offs they have in the past few years?

advice: Understand that people are the most important part of your business. They come before clients and shareholders. Without good people there is no good business. Do not say you care about your employees, show it. Your own employees do not trust you at all right now. Earn their trust by showing you care about them.
pros: I had many good reasons 10 years ago...
cons:
Complete disregard for employees.
Deep employee distrust in upper management - the main reason the company is not likely to recover any time soon.
Upper management extremely out of touch with the rest of company
Human resources function like company's law firm
Citi has instilled a corporate culture where mediocrity and futility are empowered at expense of talent and new ideas.
The company has gotten too big to be managed effectively. There was a feeling that senior management had no idea my unit existed.

summary: Citi hates nearly all of its employees.
advice: Sell or spinoff every business unit of the company. Disolve the corporation entirely in the manner it stands today.  There are no econimies of scale to be had, the amount of waste due to mismanagement is absolutely staggering. Want to cut employees? Eliminate 50 - 75% of the staff from the level of director up.
pros: You can occasionaly find a pocket of good employees to work with it can be tolerable for awhile but will ultimately be short lived.
cons: There is no shortage of department managers that are willing to grandstand, and cut the throats of their employees in an attempt to make themselves look better.  Layoff's are constant and will remain so.  Citi is to big to FAIL, to big to mabage, to big to think, to big to care for any shareholder, customer or employee.

advice: Hold managers accountable. If a manager is acting unethically that manager should be punished.
pros: Steady company. Credit Risk, Yield Book, Investment Research and Finance are decent groups to join. The management teams there are strong and the managers act in a professional manner.
cons:
Financial Planning & Analysis has extremely unprofessional management. The department manager is highly unethical. Avoid this group. 
The business model is to work people are hard as you can and get as much of out them for as little as you can. This may not sound bad but you have people working 60 hours a week for 35k a year. Burn out is extremely high.
The Buffalo site is a "Center of Excellence." The other COEs at Citi are located in 2nd and 3rd world countries dubbed low cost centers. Buffalo is the US version of these other COEs. Upward movement is limited.

advice: Don't tell your staff as long as they are doing a good job, they are safe and that they have nothing to worry about because they are meeting their goals, second highest producer in section and received excellent customer service feedback from customers.
pros: I have a job for two years and during the first nine months we received a monthly bonus.  After that, they were cut out.
cons: Loved what I did and meet goals.  Number two producer in section, but when they needed to downsize, other team members under to meet goals, or come to work remained on the team and I was let go.

advice: I know we want employees to think and act like owners but most don't. Should give mid to lower level employees stock purchase plan like other companies so employees will feel more like owners and probably care more. Cap one and chase offers stock purchase plans at discount to encourage stock ownership for all employees not just senior execs.
pros: Good company if you want to rebuild things. So many broken issues and process still today. Salary good, senior mgmt has a vision just not executing at well as it should be.
cons: Still operates in silos. No coordination and working together between groups. Still has legacy culture where things are "always done this way" in certain areas.

summary: Good for short term, but don't get stuck!
advice: Let people use the restroom, look at the big picture, give employees more input, don't be so cheap with system design and development.
pros: Decent pay, good benefits and paid time off, nice annual appreciation day  fitness center and showers, safe campus, cool co-workers, good 401k.
cons: Extreme micro-management, unrealistic goals, little power to help customers, system upgrades usually make things worse, CEO makes over 17 million , but you're in trouble if you use bathroom during shift, idiotic customers who can't read or understand basic math, never ending shifts that make 8 hours seem like 3 days.  A job that is mentally and emotionally damaging and requires constant sitting.

advice: Keep doing you! You guys were all amazing and helped me make this the best first internship anyone can ever have!
pros: I have no complains about any of my experience there. Manager was always helpful, let me decide on what project I wanted to work on, floor mates helped me if I was ever stuck or asked them from a problem, and the list goes on.
cons: I don't think I have any cons but if I was to mention one it would be the time taken the first two weeks to set everything up. This length could have been shorter, but rest of the internship made up for the lost two weeks!

advice: Stop changing everything all the time! Maybe you should also start offering part time positions.
pros: Citi gives the reps that wish to move up a chance to do so. You can almost always move to other departments as well. You will also work with a wide range of people. I didn't mind leaving Citi as much as I did the people i worked with.
cons: The C in Citi stands for change. Depending on the department that you work for, most policies and procedures will change. Make sure that you pay attention to your emails and if your boss and CA are on top of their game they should let you know most of the updates.

summary: no opportunities for growth if you start out in the call center
advice: How about listening to all your employees instead of surveying a few. Create reasonable expectations for collections and stop forcing people to beg or force people to give money when they are about to lose their house or just gone through job loss. Very heartless and employees get in trouble when they do not force clients to give money.
pros: Co-Workers in the same position were amazing. This is one of those positions where you hate the job but love your co-workers.
cons: Stressful, unreasonable expectations, showed the company had no heart, and company wanted you to do their dirty work. Pay was horrible but the benefits were great.

summary: Monkey Work in a big bank
advice: Invest in management of people instead of using them to force more work from employees. There is also little appetite for being upfront with employees so a lot of employees feel lied to in regards to what they will be told at intervview stage.
pros: Mobility. Central location. There is good networking events held which offer the ability to move internally instead of moving outside the company.
cons: Excessive overtime expected. Weak management. I would say you should identify if a role is 'processing based' ind if so recognize that you will be used to work and have to fight for renumeration.

advice: be aware that the data quality controls team has so much potential but the leader kills innovation and lies about accomplishments for her job security.
pros: Great benefits, good pay, onsite gym and cafeteria. Decent work life balance.
cons: In the Chief Data Office there are many incompetent managers. The data Quality Controls lead is so afraid of the need Chief Data officer finding out how little value she adds that she will kill process improvements or process overhauls so that they don't find out what a disconnected and inefficient process she has set up.  The morale is terrible and you only advance if you are a favorite and not based on actual skills / accomplishments.

advice: Promote a more collaborative working environment with other colleagues/stakeholders/department rather than a rivalry and bureaucratic environment. But again bureaucracy is every where so not quite sure if this can be resolved. Also, encourage employee to voice out their opinion
pros: The benefits and well fares are one of the top few, as one can expect from foreign banks. Also, there are a lot of firm wide initiatives on diversity and inclusion, which could be beneficial to all employees.
cons: Depending on which department you are in, the bureaucracy may or may not affect you. In addition, the management could be authoritarian towards the employee, which could intimidate ground level employee to voice out their opinion.

advice:
-Training Program for New Hires. 
Training Program for New Managers. They should be able to provide feedback, hold employees accountable
- You don't need more recruiters, you need more coordinators and training for HRSS team's. They are the ones who will support recruiters but without proper trainings recruiters are doing double work
pros:
-Job Flexibility
-There is an opportunity for Career Growth. Never been at the firm that promotes internal mobility as much as Citi.
cons:
-Lack of Training for new on boarders. Citi has really high turnover which makes it difficult to have experienced folks in your role to be able to train or provide guidance.
- Too much work makes it hard to find work/life balance

summary: Good Deal Flow, Average Pay for the Industry, Some Great People but Overall Toxic Culture
advice: Trim the bureaucracy, simplify the business lines, set a clear strategy, fire the jerks, and pay good people to retain them.
pros:
Some great people 
Good brand on resume
Good deal flow given large balance sheet
Potential internal mobility to other groups
cons: Certain managing directors in Capital Markets division extremely toxic (ruining entire group morale). Poor behavior tolerated by senior management who look the other way. Exodus of talent to boutiques and other institutions that are better run. At the 20K foot level, no clear vision of what Citi wants to be when it wants to grow up. Mediocre at everything with some bright spots.

summary: Look elsewhere for a satisfying postion.
advice: Learn to EMBRACE change. Take a chance and HAVE A BACKBONE!!!
pros: The benefits and flex time -- the management for the most part cares about the people, however, the communication throughout Citi is very archaic.
cons: Very little chance of advancement and we are not seeing much of Pandit throughout all this turmoil.  Where is the leadership? I believe that there are those that want to see the company survive and it will, but a lot of us feel there is a lack of true leadership in this company.  We need someone strong. Vikram is not the man, or to date has not shown this to be.

summary: Citigroup - Once a great company, today in shambles
advice: Sr. management drove this company to ground. Leadership need to change and bankers need to be put in charge of the organization. The culture brought in by Sandy Vile need to be cleansed. Need to go back and become the innovator the company once was...
pros: A truly global corporation and you will probably work with some of the best people in the industry. Used to be an innovator in the industry, though that is no longer the case.
cons: Limited career advancement potential, lot of bureaucracy and internal politics. It operates as a conglomorate of companies instead of a single corporation ofcussed on a common set of goals and objectives.

summary: Work for citi if only temporary and for the money
advice: Fire your co workers and have them do the same favor for you. the worst thing for a company is not bad economy its bad management and your company is horribly run.
pros: It's largely recognized as one of the biggest worst performing banks. it is international and has a global reach. its a good place for mediocre people who like getting comfortable with there job.
cons: CIti is the worst bank of the top 5 big banks by market value. it is managed terribly and management in the branch level is mostly not well trained. too much need and push to extreme goals of selling bad products.

summary: Glass ceiling if you stay in one position without applying for another within 2 years
advice: Take a look inside the company to search for talent not being put to use. Growth opportunities are what should be extended. Listen to your employees when they bring something to your attention in regard to job satisfaction/placement instead of bullet point suggestions easily attained for YOUR resume. Think long term for those who have been there and paid their dues. The ROI will be fantastic and you will spend less trying to recruit. WOO WOW WIN me over... sound familiar?
pros: Citi medical/vacation benefits, 401(k) match @ 6%
cons: Flexible schedule going away, systems nightmare, departmental communication, salary, bonus requirements, paperwork impact time period

summary: A good place to gain experience and learn how to manage at high level
advice: To appreciate valuable staff who are asset to the company with recognition & increament must be fair. For the past 5 years, increaments are merely averaged at 5% or less. Promotion increaments are not differentiated, in most cases are below 10%. Market benchmark is much higher even compared to CP index is lower. Sadly, a lot of talented staff will leave after less than 5 years because cannot cope with the low increament & recognition.
pros: Good working environment and best place to network with successful people
cons: Too much work, a lot of multitasking,  long hours, too many red tapes.

summary: Not a great company for technology - (Software Development)
