advice:
Treat technology with respect. Treat US citizens with respect.
Create an environment where
pros: Good benefits, competitive salary, room for growth. I worked for a smaller company that Citi bought. We had some great teams, great people to work with. Reasonably flexible work hours.
cons:
Over time, Citi pretty much destroyed the company that they had bought. The teams were broken up according to business needs. There would no longer be common architecture among businesses. Most new and challenging development is being outsourced to India. Most new hires were either Indian or Chinese. Citi took US bailout money and then gave most new technology jobs to non-citizens.
No job security. Poor bonuses.

summary: Global Bank - Citi is global banking standard.
advice: Give and develop more benefit for your staff. Also develop program to encourage and support personal development.
pros: Great Team culture and respect peers. Salary is reasonable but do not expect the best in the market. if you really want to learn banking especially corporate banking then Citi will bring you  up to the next level.
cons:
Sometimes illogical and inefficient decision making structure. Do not expect the best in market salary they only give you far below what you have in mind. 
Need to prepare your self to contribute some of your private time for traveling. The major APAC region centre is in Singapore. Man! you will need to travel really often.

summary: *NOT WORTH* You will make a lot of money, for a short time, BUT you will want to eat a bullet before the end.
pros: Only one Pro. You make a lot of money. The next best benefit is being able to put Citi on your resume when you leave.
cons: Everything else. Soul grinding, heavy rules & regulations. Absolutely everything is numbers driven, no consideration is given for personal behavior. How's his numbers? Bad=Fired, Good=Keep. From the moment you walk in the door, they are trying their best to get you fired (more money and job security for them). To survive here, for even a short amount of time, you have no choice but to become a specialist in all the CYA internal rules, regulations & procedures. Even if you spend your entire day trying to CYA they will eventually find some obscure rule to force you out.

summary: great benefits with a leading global financial service
advice: I don't think I'm qualified or have credential to offer such advice. However, I think Citi has more means and resources to better service the needs and wants of the customers. Equally, Citigroup is a great company with lots benefits to work for.
pros: I was very fortunate to have worked for Citi. For almost 8 years, I had learned and grown my career and improved financial service skills, and mortgage servicing experience.
cons: In a big company, all training modules are web-based and are quite overwhelming. Such training formats are challenges and you don't have a luxury of classroom settings where you can interact and ask questions with trainers.

summary: Good company to work for, heading down the right path
pros:
I've been with Citi for 8 years coming in at their high and experiencing the crash in 2008. The constants during that time have been:

- Great benefits
- Many opportunities for advancement
- Retain and compensate top talent
- Focus on innovation and becoming the leading digital bank
cons:
- The swirl of senior management (CEO on down) over the last decade has led to several different visions that never had the opportunity to come to fruition. Corbat seems to have the correct vision and has aligned senior management to execute in unison. 

- A lot of red tape which is to be expected in a company of this size.

summary: Citi private equity services is the worst place I've ever worked!!!  Avoid this place at all costs
advice: Quit and pray one of your former employees doesn't find you alone in the street.  Find a job that doesn't require being anywhere near people.
pros: Pretty much none. If you like seeing good people treated like dirt for terrible pay, working on holidays, sexual harassment...work here.  Bonus?  Only if you do "favors".
cons: Al blanco who is the COO is one of the worst people.  Abusing his employees and harassing them is a daily Occurance.   Good luck if you're a woman here.  40% of the staff has left in one year alone.  Have kids?   Say goodbye to them.   Management are either sociopaths or weaklings.

advice: Keep involved with the critical issues and do not worry about the day-to-day issues. Keep staff well -trained as technoology is changing quickly and new issues are always emerging and staff can fall behind if they are focused on just the immediate task at hand.
pros: Lots of different activies and responsibiities. Sometimes corporate mandates were really unnecessary for our local area but they did not take too much time. Great place to learn new skills with a good training program.
cons: Too many reports and too many corporate meetings. They got in the way of doing real work. Mgmt tried to help and keep these to a minimum so overall it was not too bad.

advice: They need to develop more the Senior employees, so they can contribute to teach their teams and have the opportunity to grow in their roles. Be more open to let people make their own decisions will be really helpful too, equal trust.
pros: The benefits they have are really good, as a former employee the compensation plan was really good. For the time I worked there I had a great work environment and the opportunities to succeed where really good.
cons: They need to work a little bit more about people behavior and how to deal with some troubles between coworkers. Communication is not always effective and can develop a huge wall between some important relations.

advice: Organize yourselves to show effective leadership in order to better develop your team.
pros: Internationally recognized financial organization with an array of products and services.
cons: Training experience is sub par. The time spent in a branch isn't beneficial, so for those who wish to truly develop or enhance their banking career should avoid this organization by all costs. The internal shenanigans that occurs are not worthy of your precious time or effort. The organization provides high quality services to the clients but are extremely limited when it comes to developing their employees. The disparity of banking knowledge and professionalism is obvious upon the first day of working alongside "seasoned" Citi employees. I worked at a several different locations and interacted with employees nationwide; so on a national scale the quality of the team that I encountered was saddening. Do yourself a favor, work somewhere else.

advice: Cultivate high performing teams - measure and reward.
pros: Great opportunities for early and mid-career, proven performers who seek them.  A great global culture.  Great people.  Never a need to suffer from boredom!  Great focus on hiring and growing talent (in the past couple of years).  Good corporate focus on women and developing their talent as executives.
cons: Can be very political.  Meritocracy gets watered down due to bell-curve ratings within individual groups and functions.  The rating/ranking system doesn't encourage or reward high-performing teams.  Holding the "corporate line" is rewarded more than hard results sometimes.

advice: Get your act together.  I had 15yrs mortgage experience working, at times, for individuals who barely knew the difference between a mortgage, TIL or GFE.  Our customers definately .referred to these at times.  Hire mortgage professionals for this position and pay them well.  Listen to their ideas... they know what they are talking about
pros: Good and clean work environment
cons: Expectations for talk time were unattainable with all the verifying and updating required on each call.  Then there were constant changes that were not always relayed or relayed effectively causing reps to fail calls.  The work load was too high for the pay. Then they take away one of our main tools for making bonus by giving it to Customer Service as well and then start laying us off. Terrible planning.

advice: Where do I begin? Stop threatening, lying to, and bullying your employees. Also, stop trying to turn them against each other in order to feel like you're in control.
pros: The benefits are good, great relationships with some customers, office is clean and spacious.
cons:
This place is a joke. They overwork, underpay employees. Managers are uneducated for the most part, and are only promoted based on their numbers. The problem with that is that now you have managers (who make around $70-80k) stealing loans from their employees (who make $30,000) and bullying them into staying quiet, probably because they're used to selling and selling by all means necessary. There's no work-life balance to speak of (it's just work) and good luck getting promoted regardless of how well you do. My personal advice is you're better off somewhere else. 

Another "con" would be interest rates and insurance. You're definitely a predatory lender when you lend someone $7,500 and expect them to pay you back $22,500 over 5 years.

summary: Great company with good benefits, beware layoffs and new departments.
advice: Be aware of where you have moved too, whether between departments or states. Practices and philosophies that may have worked elsewhere should be placed aside, as a new environment brings new challenges and people to you, old methods may not be effective.
pros: Great benefits and an HR department that looks out for the employee. You'll never feel more secure knowing that you will be taken care of by HR. Great people work here, leading to a fairly relaxed atmosphere.
cons: Unfortunately layoffs come around every so often, be prepared. New departments that come in lack direction and struggle to find pacing and footing. Although these are expected challenges, it sets a bad precedent from the start in a new department.

advice:
Create a human work environment, happy employees make productive employees. Make good employees feel valued. Focus more on talent development, encourage people to have time in their roles for training & ensure that managers don't reduce training so they can squeeze extra hours out of staff. 
I was offered double my salary when I said I would leave... this was insulting, they had not offered me a raise in years. Pay people what they are worth & ensure no huge salary discrepancies where the 'old guard' are paid exorbitant salaries.
pros: Generous pension, free health & doctor on site, gym, good canteen food, intelligent global team, flexible work hours, good view.
cons: Long hours, USA focus, worked on a global team & there was not always consideration that I wasn't in New York, grey cubicles are so 1990's.

summary: surprised we are still in business
advice: be honest with your employees. Not just your tenured agents, but all of them. Don't pacify them with answers you think they want to hear. They are CITI. They are the frontline for this company and deserve to know where they stand when it comes to their jobs. This last minute announcements of job discontinuance or merging to other divisions is ridiculous. You have lost and will continue to lose many great agents as a result of this.
pros: Benefit time is amazing! I get tons of time off each year due to my tenure
cons: Unrealistic sales goals, quick to take earned commission if you are .001% shy of meeting a goal, off shore agents monitor our calls and interpret things differently therefore causing us to get hit on call monitoring which results in negative scorecards and potential commission impact.  No growth potential at Hagerstown location. Continuously closing depts and transferring to other locations. Closing buildings and minimizing the work area.

advice: Just don't work in this bank. The bank management needs to fully be changed.
pros: Very few pros. The only thing I can say it is good to have it in your CV to get a better job.
cons:
The bank is for people who wants to be a slave to his manager. Never question anything. Never raise their opinion. The bank has no REAL diversity at all. It is more as Group 1 are against Group 2 which Group 3 is helping Group 1. I don't advice anyone to work in this unethical Bank. 

The bank claims they have a great ethical standard but the truth they don't. If you raise an ethical issue against anyone as soon as the other person has stronger connection you will not be able to do anything about it. If you raise an ethical issue it just gets forwarded to HR or they call it ER and they support the managers to frame it in a way that you are not correct.

advice: Stop regionalizing everything and stop cost cutting. Maybe I'm incapable of visualizing this but, how are you going to digitally integrate, operationalize and manage everything centrally when your country teams supporting this slow, digital transition are only operating at 1/3 the original headcount and continually seeing attrition? A huge chunk of your most talented staff have left for greener pastures, please reconsider your direction.
pros: Good early exposure to rich data warehouse, some genuine efforts to move away from traditional, non-digital workflows. Willingness to invest in digital infrastructure.
cons:
Bogged down by unrealistic, unfounded KPI targets. 
Poor talent recognition (20 dollar vouchers for executing difficult, cross-business 20% projects), poor bonuses & increments even for achieving top regional performance KPIs.
Political work environment, bureaucratic and passive aggressive work dynamics make it difficult to coordinate solutions across multiple teams.

summary: A great company that lost its way, and trying desperately to find its roots.
advice: The conservative path is usually the right path.  Do the right thing, and the rest will take care of itself.
pros: In this market climate, size matters.  It is as difficult a market climate as I have seen in 18 years of doing this.  Citi has screwed up so much in the past 8 years, it should get better from here, right?  Past management blew it, current management is trying hard to put us back together again.
cons: Always in the news and usually with negative headlines.  My clients realize that it is a huge company with a big footprint, and with a shoe size that big, the company is bound to step in it from time to time.

summary: HR department is one big dominatrix warehouse.
advice:
> Simplify the variable compensation plan.
> Don't be insecure regarding your subordinates looking smarter than you.
pros: Large company with many different types of positions. Depending on your job, it’s relatively easy to transfer to other cities and maintain salary/employer history.
cons:
> The HR department is run by women who have made it their mission to keep men out of management positions. 
> Too many businesses trying to distribute their services/products through the financial centers. 
> Very complicated variable compensation plans, that change yearly.
> Sales goals are NOT sustainable year over year. A great year must be followed by a bad year to reset your sales goals to an attainable level.
> To many bonuses are tied to group effort which penalizes a top performer in a poorly producing financial center.

summary: Citi life has it's ups and downs.
advice: Evaluate all levels of management and use employee surveys to address the way the business is being managed. Sometimes it's worth it to put employees before the bottom line.
pros: The benefits and salary were well above industry standards. Having this company on your resume will open doors for you. It is nice to work with some of the smartest people in the industry. The work environment is nice. There is a lot os potential for growth.
cons: A lot of colleagues and managers had superiority complexes. A lot of management was not a approachable and managed through fear. It sometimes felt like high school with all of the cliques. They did not really try to make new hires feel welcome. Long hours, but worth the benefits.

summary: One of the worst companies one could ever encounter
advice:
Look to your right-Fire that guy. Look to the left-Fire that guy. Hire two people for 10% of that money who will make the company a better place to work.  
Cut the red tape that is associated with a bank at all costs.
pros: The best reason to work here would be the money if you were paid right.  If you have connections and can get into the in crowd, you can make a lot of money.
cons: If you are not in the right "crowd", you will run into a wall very quickly.  Management is cut throat and very protective of the lofty roles that they don't deserve but are holding on to at all costs.  They were willing to see the company go down in flames rather than cut fat at the highest level.

advice: Stop frustrating the good employees into leaving by encouraging them to stay and pointing them into a positive direction within the company.
pros: There are absolutely none for this department.
cons:
Pay and Incentives are not competitive with other institutions.

Statistics are a top priority.

There is an overabundance of red tape and compliance issues.

There are a lot of Legacy computer systems and programs agents use are not updated. The Call Center that is not properly maintained as well as outdated equipment.

Career growth is unclear though possible.

When things go wrong with products or a store associate charges incorrect amount to clients accounts the process for a correction to be made is a long and  arduous one.

You get 2 breaks that are 15 minutes and  30 minute lunch.

Overall if anyone with Call Center experience may want to explore other avenues for other companies or other departments.

advice: See the cons section and remember your employees are not transactional robots.
pros: Strong company. Good benefits. Colleagues are great to work with.
cons: Technology is very outdated. Hundreds of workarounds via several layers of systems to complete your job. Broken promises of individual career development with the excuse of a "hiring freeze". Approximately 50% understaffed in the mortgage department. Capacity is a major issue that doesn't seem to light a bulb for leaders. New leadership every 6 months and of course they come with their new set of ideas that just make things worse. In the works of "defining roles", leaders decided that every responsibility that wasn't attached to a role should be the Processor's responsibility.

advice: Invest more in recruiting, then try to promote the good people before they leave for your competitors at other banks.  Don't be afraid to exit unprofitable countries and businesses, it makes sense to be in only of the few RIGHT places.
pros:
Lots of different countries... which is a good thing if you want to have a very international career.  Otherwise, it just makes things hard to manage from the top.

Biggest upside is the low expectations of people around you, it's easy to astound them.
cons: Truly uncreative environment.  Competitive and political, but in a vicious unproductive way unlike other FIs where competition spurs excellence and a desire to thrive.

advice: Hire more people so that 10 people don't have to do the work of 20.  Most times it is nearly impossible to attain objectives and complete assignments.  Stop being too stuffy.  There still seems to be a boys club mentality.  Managers need to make the work environment more fun.
pros: Nice amount of paid-time off, holidays, etc.  Can definitely learn a lot about marketing, banking and finance.  Most people are nice.  Let you work at home 1-2 days/week.
cons: Workload is too heavy.  A lot of favoritism.  Hard to maintain work/life balance.  A lot of managers looking to move themselves ahead without consideration of their subordinates.

advice: can be difficult, it is really all about who you know and some kiss up
pros: it is a great company to work for. benefits or ok. you would be lucky to work from home. you are able to focus and get work done
cons: as long as you keep work at work and personal very quiet then you should be ok. it can get very unprofessional if you allow your personal at work. this is based on all the issues that I have seen through co workers. I kept my personal to myself and was one of the only to maintain a job until the major layoff. communication can be off. GET EVERYTHING IN WRITING!

advice: Choose from your talented tellers a supervisor, make sure they are friendly and made for that position. Good employees never leave good companies, they leave bad mamagers or supervisors. Pay attention to your branches turn over rate and look to their immediate manager or sup.
pros:
Great family and work balance.
Great bonuses
Wonderful recognition peogram for too performers(citi stars) not seen anywhere else
Easy systems to work with
No stress for me atleast
cons: I got nothing negative to say other than keep the branches here. People really love this bank and its culture. Stop closing branches and losing valuable customers. You will love woeking here, especially if you have a great manager. Its like a family!

pros: Citigroup incentive plan is great in ways that there are many ways to make money. Through lending, client deposit build, and overall customer service experience to name a few are many ways to increase your salary. Citibank's culture is awesome when you want to work in a team work environment where everyone is coaching each other and lifting everyone to their full potential
cons: With constant change  in Citibank policy and procedures, and regulations, its hard to see and make changes on day to day operations. Rules may be to vague , or rules may not be clear when processing truncations at the bank. this can lead to concerns with higher ups, and management.

summary: Always have a back up plan
advice: too much stock in youth that are just using this as a stepping stone with no obligations ,or dedication
pros: I have experienced different areas of knowledge in mortgage ,  chosen to be assigned to reporting by office management, had the opportunity to do trainings of new hires, was assigned as compliance over seer. Liaison between investors a wealth of experience in the 7 years I have been here.
cons: the company lays off a lot so I am always wondering if my name will be on the next list because the layoffs are not seniority based or performance or attendance related.

advice: Give the employees more freedom to try out new things and make sure you have competent people at the managerial level who encourage employees and push them to come up with innovative stuff instead of micro-managing them to do the same repetitive work for months together.
pros: As part of the Analytics Information Management (AIM), you get an opportunity to work with some diverse data across markets from the Asia-Pacific, EMEA and the North America region.
cons: The whole system is too conservative in nature. There is minimal scope to try out new things.  The senior management does not want to alter any of the existing processes even if there is a chance to enhance them.

advice: Some times to many things are throw at tellers at once since it the bottom of the totem pole, makes it increasing more difficult to remain accurate while having to do 8 more additional tasks.
pros: Decent start up compensation, foot in door for advancement to other lines of business within Citi.
cons: Typically branches at least in Texas have very few bankers so tellers are required to do quite a bit of referrals compared to other tellers I've spoken in this area at other banks. Also typically required preform cold sales calls and such to help bankers get more client without receiving any additional compensation. Very slow in terms of advancement.

summary: Good if you just need a job
pros: Great culture. Casual dress environment. Many opportunities to earn overtime. good cheap benefits available. Opportunities for fun on the citi campus. Nice cafeteria. Workout room available.
cons: I had a work schedule from 1-10 pm so I didn't enjoy that. Management was always down your throat to push people to pay. Newsflash no one is going to pay a delinquent home depot bill. This just absolutely wasn't the job for me, but some people do just fine with it and are actually good at it. So I wouldn't discourage anyone from applying. Heavy sales and persuasion skills will be vital for success in this position.

summary: Good job and benefits, just not for me
advice: If someone is successful in current position, allow for change in department, might help retention.
pros: Easy to get time off, had good manager and was able to make up time off on another day, vacation time/holiday pay/sick time and benefits from day one, unlimited overtime, not too difficult to make bonus, insurance was inexpensive, hefty cell phone discount, relaxed atmosphere, casual dress code, tons of volunteer opportunities, free food at least once a month.
cons: Worked collections, just not the place for me, probably would have been better suited for customer service, have to stay in current position for one year before transferring to different department.

advice: Keep up the good work!
pros:
I've been working for Citi for more than a year now, and could not be happier.

My peers are all exceptional and want to contribute above and beyond their required roles. My manager is outstanding, both technically and on the personal level and the work is refreshing and challenging.

Citi has one of THE best benefits packages around and supports a strong balance between work and family.

I've been working in corporate America for over 19 years now and Citi is head and shoulders above everyone else I ever worked for.
cons: Bonus was a bit lackluster, but that's about all I got to complain about.

summary: End of learning and development at Citi
advice: Get rid of "forced" ranking of performance. Develop managers to care as much for people as profits (and the profits will come).
pros: Recognition that leaders and managers need to be supported in their development. Knowledge of how to do it. Sometimes willing and able leadership, who want themselves and their staffs to benefit from learning/training and other development approaches
cons: Lack of funding. Focus on metrics not on people. Constant re-organizing makes it difficult to create a network.  Constant financial challenges diminishes probability that funding for learning will endure. The performance management system stack ranks people and doesn't do it well. This leads to continuous unhappiness.

summary: An environment that forced to conform or decide to control your own future and leave for greener pastures.
advice: It's time to clean house in the management ranks and create a management team that understands how to communicate with people and understand what it means to be a manger
pros: Fantastic coworkers; Freedom to grow at your own pace;
cons: Blatant favoritism from management creates an environment where you don't even want to try, because you know that the favorite employee is going to be promoted; Upper management have been in their positions for far too long and are no longer able to innovate or change due to advancements in technology or working styles; limited flexibility with staff

summary: Poor technology infrastructure makes it hard to serve customer properly
advice: Invest in technology and improve processes
pros:
Compensation is reasonable. The people are generally nice. The work load in my department is also reasonable
New CEO (Jane Fraser) seems more people oriented and communicates more.
cons:
I work in the marketing department and the head of the group does not care at all about the people. Also lacks vision.
Overall, the infrastructure and technology of Citimortgage is really poor and behind competitors. Makes it hard to provide good customer service.
As of beginning of Sep 2013, they are getting ready for massive layoffs. Because of the increase in interest rates, refi volume has plummeted. So, expect cuts of ~40%

summary: Challenging experience but of a bad kind
advice: Scrap hollow good-only-in-name "initiatives" where people **are volunteered**.  Initiatives where nearly all "volunteers" don't believe in what they are doing will only exacerbate the problems
pros:
Some great people
A lot of exposure, get to experience things out of my comfort zone
Allocations of Increments, promotions and bonuses within the department are fair (although the pool from which they are allocated is rather meager)
cons:
Extremely process and paperwork intensive
A lot of unnecessary pains and waste of time due to insufficient underlying tools or poorly trained support personnel
decade old technologies
Not a conducive environment to cultivate software engineering talent
Constant fire-fighting and support duties which distract me away from working on permanent/long-term solutions

summary: You won't find good managers, you are free to be of your own
advice: Need a new management.
pros:
Many technology veterans are around because firm allows them to work from home (under flex program), so they are happy to stay home and do other side-businesses or taking care of other good things in life.

People managers has no professionalism and has lot of behavioral problems. HR and management agree with this management?! style as it achieves the company goal of becoming the most mediocre and sending out good people to good places they deserve.
cons: To work as an employee. Benefits are poor and unstructured. HR is virtual, you won't know where to go when you need help.

advice: Improve the culture.  Value skip level feedback.  Take action by eliminating MD level personnel that don't deliver.
pros: The company has good benefits.  Remote work location contributes to a reasonable work life balance.
cons: The culture is very cut throat at the MD level.  The executive management team really knows how to push issues down hill and protect its turf.  There is a lack of communication and desire to cultivate careers.  Everyone is "encouraged" to seek their own training.  Promotions are few and far between, most often reserved for the chosen. Annual employee feedback generally leads to no where.  The results are consistently poor year over year.

advice: Take care of your senior staff, they do alot then you know. Bosses are covering up to make themselves look good as if they are doing their work and get their promotions. Unfortunate for some that have to be let go because of useless bosses.
pros: Good employees benefits, nice colleagues.
cons: Sales and number driven. Tonic environment, Insurance is top priority. Nothing else matters (investment, employees feedbacks) prepare to be micromanaged and scrutinised by your boss. Redundant boss that gives no support, only chase you for appointments and sales figures. 2hrs meetings every morning. If you're in a bad team prepare to be let go easily. Always putting the team down.

summary: Citi is good but Photon(contractor agency) is terrible and exploiting others
pros: Employees here are nice and senior position are really experienced and skilled. Work-life balance. No meeting on Friday.

advice:
Citi is not NPO, but an entity who make profits, yet did not honor basic employee rights , disallowed the staff to claim OT reimbursement....

i achieved my full KPI every single working day, and delivered good case review quality as analyst....
The reason we are required to clear cases allocated to us during weekend/PH was due to deficiency of staff members in Citi..

regards,
An unhappy staff
pros: overwhelming workloads , work on PH/weekend?!
cons: No OT payout for PH or weekeend OT

summary: If you can survive here, you can survive anywhere
pros:
Challenging environment which will push you to learn quick and think even quicker
Lots of opportunities to put yourself out there and get noticed
Good place to start your career in
cons:
Work life balance? Never heard of it.
So much time spent on learning to read between the lines when announcements are made
Re-org changes are made far too often for anything to work well
They overwork you so much you either get pushed to quit or have to take days off just to breathe
Overtime pay was barely given even when we went it on a holiday, instead we could take a day off in exchange (had to be scheduled first)

pros: Amazing company to work for with the ability to move laterally and if you work hard enough vertical as well. They seem to practice what they preach and put a genuine effort to put employees first. I’ve been with the company for a year now and have enjoyed my time here so far with a good work/life balance as a major contributor to this sentiment. There’s also great diversity networks that can get you plugged in with the right groups if you feel isolated. It will probably take a lot for me to leave
cons: Can’t really think of any but I wish there was a stipend for wfh.

summary: World leading market franchise with chaotic executive management
advice: Citigroup needs to focus on its key business franchise and strengthen its risk management systems.
pros: Prestige, market position and quality of the work colleagues was a key benefit of working at Citi.  The firm's market dominance in the corporate fixed income, equities and M&A markets allowed me to work on high-profile transactions with the world's premier clients.
cons: Chaotic management environment.  I was with Citigroup and its predecessor firm, Salomon Brothers, for over five years.  While the management of the Investment Bank was dominated by executives of the former Salomon franchise, there were numerous executive changes, which coincided with a severe market downturn.

summary: Collections: The most underappreciated job at Citi!
advice: Get on the phones and interact with our customer.  Understand what it is like to do our job day in and day out especially in this awful economy.  We do our best and it is still not enough.
pros: The flexability of working close to my home and working part time and getting fulltime benefits.
cons: I feel that people who have dedicated their years at Citi do not get compensated as they should.  The pay is horrible.  Insurence benefits have sky rocketed so that the tiny pay raise you get is completely eaten up by the premiums.

summary: okay, but only as a last resort.
advice: bonus in cash- be honest with employees
pros: average salary, decent benefits that start day one, used to have good reputation, a firm with cache, has long term future for who remains with firm.
cons: gov't bailout, loss of reputation, having to sell one piece of citigroup that makes money (smith barney), mgt. not honest with rank and file, they chose to only tell you what they want you to know. HR is a joke. The systems in this place are crazy, it is a hodgepodge of different systems for bonds, stocks and mutual funds. I mean they still have paper after hours tickets, I mean who still has that.

advice: Structure of raises once you start working in the company, its very difficult to get a raise that correspond to the promotion as well as increased responsibility. Couple of cases in immediate surrounding of promotion without raises. Since 2007. Top performers can only wait so long for a proper reward.
pros: Benefits, experience, great team spirit. Bonus not too bad if you perform though basic pay is below average.
cons: Need to stand out and prove value to team and process. Competitive environment. Low morale due to recent layoffs but comparatively to friends at other company, Citi employees still win hands down on dedication and resilience.

advice: Employees would be happier working for a company at which they feel secure in their positions.  During my tenure with the company, nearly every colleague I came into contact with was constantly worried about their position within the company.
pros: Citi had a great culture in how management treated the employees.  Senior and front line management in my experience were very respectful of the employees they managed.
cons: The company is going through a massive restructuring and has laid off a significant number of employees in the last couple of years.  This has made it a very unstable place to work with very little job security for most positions.

advice: Don't hire contractors.  Hire Employees
pros: Management went out of their way to accommodate the employees during the pandemic. Encouraged taking time off. Gave an extra "free" day off. Proud to work for a company that demands equal rights and equal opportunities within the firm for all regardless of race, color, religious beliefs, sex, sexual orientation and such. I know that management doesn't tolerate discrimination in any form
cons: If you are a contractor, you don't receive the same pay for the same work. Of course they pay as much or more for the contractors, but the company holding the contractors contract gets more money than the contractor

advice:
Weekly catch up with manager

pros:

Big brand name for CV

the inhuman manager that expects you to deliver results when you are sick couple of times. Phone call from manager that if i don't deliver , my career path in Hong Kong will be threatened

A bank a truly never sleep- modern day slavery

advice: Break the silos. Try a bottom to top approach. Fixing things at ground level will show positive results. Invest more in engineering teams who could come up well researched solutions that are concrete and would work.
pros:

summary: How not to make your employees feel like a "little fish in a large pond"
advice: Give more authority and decision making ability to the managers within the business channels.  Too many decisions are made at high levels.
pros: There are a lot of opportunities to work in different areas of the company and learn new skills due to the large size and scale of Citigroup.
cons: Due to the large size and complexity of the organization, it is hard to feel like you matter to senior management.  Often times, it is difficult to get changes and improvements made due to the substantial layers of management and the amount of bureacracy involved within the company.

advice: Listen to your analysts because we do most of the nitty gritty work.
pros: Prestige - that's about it...for now. Citi is weathering this financial storm in a mediocre manner. If it does not improve soon it will be another Lehman Brothers. Senior Management and higher ups feel the only way to "improve" is to cut analysts and higher VERY few people. Next year's analyst class is going to have a rough time because the Ops work is BORING AS ANYTHING. I want to get the hell out of here.
cons: The culture is very disconnected, it is hard to make relations and senior management is unapproachable. ALso, exit opps are not great as well.

summary: Good place to start as a FA but there is an image problem currently
advice: They really need to understand how the advisor build his business and that the reputation of the company is so very important. Having to defend Citi's reputation has been extremely difficult and leaves a bad taste in the mouths of employees and clients alike.
pros: Freedom and flexibility to do the right thing for your client. There is no pressure to recommend products that are not in the best interest of your client. You are free to build your business the way you want.
cons: It takes a lot of work to build your practice to the point of it being self-sustaining.

summary: If you can , avoid Citi at any cost
advice: Please focus more on people, I know Citi is going thru tuff time right now , but without us there will be no CITI
pros: Citi offers its employees a very good benefits, the 401 k matches you contribution 1 $ to 1 $ .
cons: Citi will work you to death, Citi never sleeps and you will too. Burocracy is literaly whats killing them, you may spend most of your day making sure that you follow the procedures, it leave no time for actual work. Budget cuts everywhere, no coffee, no caps nothing left but more work. NO bonuses, no rises this year, most likely next year too.

advice: Even though you work hard, it might not be recognized by the upper managers because it is such a huge organization.  Higher managers should try to listen what their staffs are thinking otherwise they'll loose smart young people instead of losing bad mid-level managers.
pros: Although I worked for outside of United States, many HR recruiters took a look my resume because Citigroup is a really big name. This company will open the door for the another great opportunity.
cons: HR really doesn't have any power, so this causes unfairness between departments in the company.  Now, I moved on to different industry and realized that the Citigroup culture was too aggressive.

advice: Give more recognition to hard work
pros: Good atmosphere in general, you can get into a good group and have a great social life. When you joing the company there is a feeling that youv'e signed up to something great.
cons: Work life is not great, long hours and pay package is pathetic. Very very political. Hard work doesn't pay at all. It seems like the only way to be successful in the company is saying the right thing at the right time. Getting a promotion is next to impossible unless you are always on the right side of management. You get away with doing nothing and staying long hours and getting rewarded for it.

summary: One of the worst professional experiences of my life
advice: Become better at evaluating talent and investing in human capital for the long-term. Replace/layer low-performing middle managers with employees that know how to lead and can inspire others.
pros: Still maintains brand recognition, good facilities and infrastructure (albeit not as good as JP Morgan Chase), very friendly co-workers, great opportunities to work remotely if one were so inclined.
cons: Dishonest middle managers, poor understanding of the advantages of using technology, implied threats of termination used to "motivate" employees into working 80 hours a week (salaried/no OT), very poor consideration towards employees that are high achievers/performers vis-a-vis rewarding performance with more work without the additional acknowledgement of added responsibility/title/salary, mostly ambiguous goals/unclear strategy, overall very poor morale, very poor work/life balance, and generally just not a good environment to start or advance your career in.

summary: The company has no value for employee.
advice: Please take time to understand employee concerns. While deciding on Compensation do consider   vintage and do give weightage to the amount of work being done by an employee when the team is short staffed. Hikes come once a year. Please consider the number of opportunities an employee has had on adjusting their compensation with the vintage compared to the market.
pros: Brand name is the only reason why anybody should work with this company.
cons: Not employee friendly. HR has no role in helping address employee concerns. Management cares about is only to make people. No work life balance until the level of middle management.

summary: OK, but the AML dept hires too many underqualified people
advice: The AML dept is a mess, don't continue to hire underqualified people without a banking background or office experience. The mess and disorganization of AML comes from those who are not familiar with working in a professional office environment.
pros:
Great work/life balance, ability to work from home multiple days
Skip level meetings are encouraged
Voice can be heard
cons:
Red Tape
Highly bureaucratic
Important depts such as IT is too decentralized (to fix PC issues, expect a week wait time for results)
Process Improvement takes way too long
Pay increases are minimal to non-existent

advice:
- Instill less of a facetime culture where possible
- More work / life balance especially in times of downturn
pros:
- Global firm
- Lots of resources
- Great opportunity
- Work with high calibre recruits
- Fantastic analyst & associate training programs in NYC
- Strong pay in the investment banking sector
cons:
- When markets are not performing well pay / bonus suffers
- Global mobility not easy at all despite global nature - especially in times of downturn. Even if not you have to be a top performer to be considered
- Can be a political game in the investment bank - face time and setting the right impression almost as important as high quality work

summary: It has what it takes... but can be better
advice:
Identify that some tools do not promote performance, such as the current performance evaluation policy - it empowers politics and ability to influence supervisors but it creates friction in a well efficient team that could potentially be at the same level of performance.
In addition, most issues with projects lie in the fact that most people fail in execution, even though they have a good sense of the overall strategy. There are too many people thinking strategy versus people actually executing.
pros: Great benefits, amazing campus, international assignments
cons: Huge office politics, really unfair performance evaluation policy

summary: Citi can be a great place to work
pros: Citi offers a very diverse environment and is very open to movement within and between functional groups. Functional groups can differ wildly in culture and process, so chances are you can find what you're looking for with a little shopping around.
cons: Citi is big. Citi can appear to be very disorganized, at the macro level. However, at the micro-level things run pretty well. Compensation and benefits are average, but over time I think you're treated fairly. Don't expect to show up, work for a year or two, and see huge raises. It generally doesn't happen.

pros:
Analysts get benefits like $25 meal credit everyday, Uber rides past 10pm and on weekends.
The senior bankers have made significant improvements in recognizing junior's efforts. MDs often send us email about how the meetings went and include thank you notes to the junior team.
Most people are very nice and chill. A large population of Mormons in the office, so not a big drinking culture. 
MDs offer their cabin in Tahoe, country club in east bay, and mansion in the city to employees for retreats and holiday parties.

Provide roles based on strength of resources but not on recommendations or lobbying. Make every group regional and accountable and if they fail to deliver and improve stock price, then break Citi into regional consumer banks and list them separately.

My review is specific to Global Consumer Bank Organization in Citi and specific to Senior and middle level Management. 
 
Difficult to grow up the food chain, due to lot of politics and internal issues. Lots of different political groups based on regional/racial basis.

pros: Citi puts you amidst probably the best people in the industry, across the globe.  You will learn a lot not only from the well-entrenched corporate culture but from the dedicated and driven professionals you get to work with.  The organization is merit-driven so you can go as far as you push yourself.  To a certain degree you are also empowered to make decisions regarding your work.
cons: Citi demands a lot of your time.  Change is also a constant in the company so you need to have the tenacity to keep on keeping on and the flexibility to go with the flow.

advice: Get out of the limousine, away from the sycophantic handlers, and mingle with frontline and operational employees to see the challenges they're facing, and then actually commit to making things better instead of just returning to "business as usual". Also, stop awarding bonuses to managers for abusing their staff.
pros: A resonably competent, intelligent person will have an easy time at Citi. But you will have to deal with a lot of stupid people, especially in the "management" bureaucracy. And you would do well to remember not to care, no matter how much they try to force you to care, because otherwise you'll be very unhappy caring about stuff that doesn't matter.
cons:
Management constantly tries to overtake your life, applying ridiculous pressure to achieve goals that were assigned by people who have no clue, on timelines that bear no relation to reality. Always push back because there's no punishment; they just want to intimidate you into getting more work out of you for less money. If you accrue overtime, they'll often make you roll it over into another week where you'll work fewer hours, so they don't have to pay overtime rates. Citi is already involved in a class-action lawsuit over that practice, but they keep doing it.
Citi laughably reveres the uninvolved upper management as "the seniors". Title inflation is rampant. A simple team lead/supervisor is labeled Vice President, President or Director.
Employees have good benefits but no work-life balance. Having 5 weeks of paid vacation is useless because you can never take it when you want, only when management says you can. Usually they just tell you to take a week off, with no warning, so you can't plan for anything. Then they still expect you to work on your vacation.
Citi harps on "compliance" and following all sorts of rules, but they often follow only the letter of the rule-- there is a well-established workaround for every rule.
Citi relies heavily on Indian and Pakistani contractors, so women at Citi often suffer from a hostile work environment. If you're Indian/Pakistani, black, lesbian, transgender, or ideally a combination of all of those, you're in a "protected class" at Citi. Everyone else, not so much.
Remember, banking is one of the worst industries to be in (like farming, only with less death and dismemberment). Pay is low, morale is low, opportunity for advancement is low. So in that regard, Citi is typical. There are MUCH better places to work. I work here because it's convenient and I don't have to work hard for the money. But I would not recommend Citi to anyone as a career, or as anything more than a stepping stone to your next job at a different company. "Soul-sucking stupidity" is a good summary of the work environment at Citi.

pros:
* If you can get in here at the beginning of your career, then you will learn a lot as they have some of the best product, marketing, and operational processes along with financial discipline that I have experienced in my career to date.
* As things happen at light-speed at Citi, sideward promotions are done quickly so you can move around the different teams within a business unit quite quickly. Upward promotions are another story (see cons).
cons:
* Unlike other organisations, Citi is extremely tight with expenses. Everything is analysed to death before a decision (normally a "no") is made. I noticed a big pull back around the GFC, and it didn't let up many years thereafter. I believe this stifles innovation and risk taking, and unfortunately I see that Citi has gone from an innovator to a follower.
* Middle management is too focused on protecting their own nests and fighting for the top promotions when they come up from time-to-time.
* The overall culture in the bank is dog-eat-dog -- people are generally so overworked and competitive that they aren't willing nor have the time to help you...and why would they help a competitor for a future promotion that they're going after?!
* The pay is really average compared to the big 2/4 - like I said, really great place to learn but terrible if you want to get financially recognised for your experience.
* Overall, there seems to be a lack of cohesiveness with the strategy of the consumer bank -- do we just focus on the Credit Cards business which is a cash cow, or should we actually become a proper bank and accept deposits and write mortgages? The branch network is orientated towards Asian investors, and sends a mixed message.
