cons: It may be harder to get ahead but with hardwork ,it is not impossible. It sometimes causes pressure (both bad at the same time good) being in a company that has a lot of exemplary employees. It can be competitive but you can learn from them as well.

advice: my boss was the best boss i ever had, so no.
pros: good hours, interesting work, great boss, good salary, frequent promotions, mobility between divisions. 17 PTO days + 2 floating, turns into 22 days + 2 floating once you hit VP level. also ~5% bonus as an AVP level. i made $25k recruiting 5 people ($5k a pop). citi treated me well!
cons: in the sanctions and AML space, once you get higher up the ladder, it’s hard to get promotions. but to be honest, i think it’s like that everywhere. 6 sick days, but that’s not terrible.

pros:
* Internal mobility is very good so hopping around to try something new out and find a good fit is a possibility.
* There are many smart people working at Citi and I had some great mentors. 
* The compensation is also decent and there’s genuinely cool stuff to work on.
cons:
* The hours on my particular team were astounding, whatever semblance of work life balance was completely obliterated by the time I left. 
* Management didn’t seem to allocate resources effectively at all, leading to high turnover in my area.
* Some of the technology is old and you have to fight to design things in a modern way occasionally.

advice: At the moment, none.
pros: Good benefits.  For the most part, the people are good.  They'll help pay for an undergrad degree (in an appropriate field.)  You get two weeks vacation, plus two personal days and a floating holiday.
cons: Amount of work is often overwhelming.  Branch-level management is for the most part clueless about how to improve morale.  Depending on where you work, the financial advisors can be odd - but I'm assuming that's going to happen at any job.  No definite yearly bonus.  They'll pay for an undergrad degree at the branch level, but they won't help with a graduate level degree.

jobTitle: Treasury and Trade Solutions Summer Analyst
advice:
- Be more open to suggestions
- Treat your analysts with more importance, don't look down on them, most of us are way more intelligent than the jobs that have been given to us
pros:
- People are very nice, willing to help you as an analyst, definitely looking for you to succeed
- Collegial environment
- Great starting pay
- Friendly and comfortable work environment
- Hours are better than general banking (for most divisions)
- Very global and accepting workplace
cons:
- Product managers are very protective of their products & P&Ls, sometimes even to the point where it might not be beneficial to the company or the different divisions
- Work is boring and uninteresting

summary: Citi helps you think more globally
advice: I realize that your labor force in the Northeast is shrinking, but please take the time to create meaningful career paths for your high performers.
pros:
As the world's only truly global bank, it helps you think on a more global scale.
Working at Citi is a way to learn many best practices and the skills you need to advance your career.
cons:
The Bank is focusing more on cost cutting than revenue growth so jobs are moving to lower cost locations or being eliminated. 
Sadly, I don't think the best talent stays at Citi as there aren't enough opportunities for advancement (at least not in the Northeast).

advice: Some managers are just plain blind and clueless about the people who work for them and their contributions, while too busy playing personal politics. A nice purge would not be uncalled for.
pros: It is one of the few truly global enterprises in the U.S., so the breadth of what you may see or the resources you may draw upon is truly remarkable. Most egos are checked at the door, thank goodness, which makes for a very comfortable and collaborative environment.
cons: Depending on your business, the possibilities for on-wards and upwards may be limited, but at least an effort would be made.

advice: Employee benefits and engagement could be improved.
pros: The culture within Citibank is actually remarkable for a bank. I thoroughly enjoyed myself and the monthly happy hours my department hosted we always a plus. There are lots of opportunities to move around within the company.
cons: The work itself wasn't terrible but there was very little training. I would have liked to see more employee engagement as well. Citibank's systems are OLD. They know the issue and are working on fixing it but it will take several years. It's seriously a hinderance on the capabilities of the company in my opinion; hopefully the transition will be finished within the next few years.

summary: A great place to work in finance
advice: Management provided semi-yearly and yearly employee reviews that were vital to salary and or bonus increases. This provided you with great insight.
pros: Citigroup offered very competitive pay, if not higher pay than most of the bulge bracket banks located in New York City. Not only was their compensation very good, but also there were many bonuses such as discounts and rewards programs associated with being an employee.
cons: I was not completely satisfied with the role I was in. It didn't offer me the upward mobility or daily challenges I wanted.

advice: Pay more attention to making sure hardworking underlings are promoted and given reasonable annual increases, even small ones, so employees are incentivized to continue to work hard.
pros: -Great colleagues, excellent benefits, fantastic exposure to challenging assignments, good work/life balance (in my particular role-this is not true for all positions), and pleasant work environment.
cons:
-Very slow/limited growth path for those who do not come in as top managers or through management training program. 
-Every year compensation pools are decreased further so pay is stagnant (in many years, pay is flat and bonus pools are cut, so pay actually doesn't go up in line with inflation for many employees).

summary: Customer Service- Home Depot in Gray, TN
advice:
Increase the pay!  We're dealing with a lot of sensitive information.

Get a little more "hands on"
pros:
Insurance
All the PAID TIME you get
Voluntary Time Off (if needed)
The cafeteria isn't bad
Overall, it's an easy job
cons:
Company is very "hands off"  meaning they give you a lot of responsibilities that should really fall on managers.  

Where banking and credit cards are so regulated,  if you fart out of compliance, someone is down your throat.

Depending on the department you're in- the pay.

Seems like when it comes to certain things, they'll give you enough rope to hang yourself with.

advice: Senior management (SVP+ level) is mature and focused on delivering business. What we missed was true people managers with proper attitude towards personal  needs. Take into consideration what is driving people's work motivation, especially if there's no easy way to promote anyone above AVP level.
pros:
Internal mobility is a huge plus, dozen of roles available worldwide
Technically interesting projects from software development perspective 
Local management is mature and thoughtful
cons:
UK/NA managers are very restrained and not looking forward to good ideas and new technologies
In some teams there is no person who can explain more business details about what developers should do
It's hard to negotiate any rise due to strict policies

advice: hike up the prices a bit, to make money you need to spend money, not little money.
pros: great place to learn about the business, the industry, the training on sales and other related fields, Citi knows how to make sure you are ready for the market
cons: in wealth management business your income depends on commissions, which is fine. however, by being part of the business in a small market, it became obvious that as advisors we have to push clients based on commssion size and not not on need-based requirement, even though the bank stresses against mis-selling theres ano way around it when you are paid little to have a life

summary: Bureaucratic Culture - No Understanding of Winning!!!
advice: Fire more upper and middle managers,  stop hiring from third tier.  Change your culture, change your model.  Start listening, the way you did it for ten years did not make you N1 so why should it next year?  Fire most of the upper and middle managers, their sole role is to do nothing and worse, see their main function as presenting failure as success in meetings.
pros:
Good Benefits 
Large organization for those looking to hide
cons: The definition of a bureaucratic organization.  Managers who are not market forces nor have then been winners in the past.   Head count reduction model vs revenue growth model.  Lacks strategic vision, the best leave.  Use measurements for the sake of measuring but usually measure the wrong things.  Compensation as suffered with lack of profits.

advice: I would recommend that senior management involve staff more in what is going on so that bombs aren't dropped on a regular basis.
pros: State of the art, global organization with boatloads of career opportunities throughout the corporate world and the operating units. Hard work is rewarded but given the size of the organization things can get very complicated. Top management is very clique-like and decisions get made without everyone getting an opportunity to contribute to the possibilities.
cons: Firedrills on a regular basis, especially when things aren't going well. Bonuses somewhat arbitrary and at the discretion of your manager. Long hours are expected if you want to do well and although they talk work life balance it is mostly talk. Health benefits are costly and getting more costly every year.

summary: Not all that it is made to be
advice: Guys, you really need to stop being a bunch of pricks. Money is not everything in this life and the way they go about in sniping each other is ridiculous
pros:
Being in the Summer Analyst program was considered prestigious.

Working for Merrill, Goldman, Citigroup or Lazard is a great accomplishment.
cons: The whole summer analyst program is simply over hyped. Interns don't really make that much and are forced into cold-calling, answering phones and essentially doing b--tch work. You learn very little in terms of finance and struggle to even grasp concepts of what the financial world is really about. Financial Advisers are selling bs advice from above and invest your money without much of a guarantee or foresight. It has given me a very negative opinion on finance

advice: Please pick a strategy and stick with it.  Before you quit, please outline your strategy for the department and hand to HR.  It would be fantastic if HR would hire someone who agrees with at least a small portion of the outgoing manager's vision.
pros:
My salary was excellent, especially considering the economic environment.
There are a number of opportunities to advance, if you keep your eyes open for them.
Management is surprisingly accommodating when it comes to taking time off.
cons:
Extremely high turnover - people can't stand the place, and quit often.
Erratic management - mistakes that should elicit a panicked response don't, and minor mistakes bring about a world-class freakout.  This is a cultural thing, apparently.
Management changes strategy often.  Be prepared to throw away months of work based on someone's whim.

summary: Much depends on your manager. Compensation not commensurate with job duties.
advice: Recognize your employees for who they are...the Company. Promote based on skills and dedication and ability, rather than manager favorites. Encourage and support, rather than demean and threaten. Get rid of managers who do not model the code of conduct.
pros: Benefits include medical, dental, vision, 401K and more. Generous time off: sick days, Holidays and Vacation days that start at day one.
cons: Communication is almost non-existent. More often than not promotions and raises are dependent on the "social" climate, or your relationships within the company. A manager can make or break you, literally. Compensation is not even close to appropriate for all the work you are expected to take on, and barely meets basic needs without working overtime or a second job.

summary: Great place to learn. Lack of direction and multiple redundant positions.
advice:
- Remove 2-3 layers of management and flatten organization.
- Less global teams. Try to keep teams co-located if possible while maintaining a global function. Too much time spent organizing meetings and working around time zones.
- Hire external talent. We rely on external vendors too much to plan and deliver solutions.
pros:
- Every possible job under the sun.
- Can easily horizontally move across different departments.
- Remote work available
cons:
- Management is constantly changing direction.
- Too many layers/senior managers and not enough individual contributors.  More time is spent planning and creating power  point decks rather than actual execution.
- Every department has redundant roles and are typically going after the same goal. Creates confusion for the team on the ground level and wasted effort.

summary: Good culture, challenging work but cost cutting creating pain across
advice: Merit should be given due respect in appraisals. If a function earns you more than another, it should earn more as well that year. Invest in systems for the long term.
pros: Ability to move across departments and geographies (after spending some time), good bosses (at least for me), intelligent people around you in general, good opportunities for learning and development
cons: Cost cutting to become lean and mean is creating too much pressure now, so much that you do not get time for learning and development and work life balance is getting spoiled. Merit is not given due respect and functions earn money as per budget allotted to them. Operations are bureaucratic and systems are not up to the mark for a global organisation.

summary: Too much new "middle-management" trying to prove itself resulting in MAJOR Micro-management.
advice: ;You hire quality people, not children, so treat them that way. Give them thier goals/assignments and then let them produce. If they don't, then they don't deserve to work at Citi. Pressure is not going to change thier abilities, it is only going to force good people out.
pros: Citi hires quality people at branch level. Has a good training program. Doesn't have long/Sunday hours. New, innovative products.
cons: MICRO-MANAGEMENT from Division managers on down resulting in higher than ever turnover. Very Low morale in the branches.  Too many changes. Tell us to "build relationships" then want numbers-numbers-numbers. Constant PRESSURE to produce. Never enough.

summary: Great company with strong leadership but cost savings measures hurting talent.
advice: Every organization that goes through significant cost savings measures eventually realizes they cut "too deep".  Sometimes when it's too late.  Recommend that as much time and effort is put into understanding organizational change impact as much as what financially makes sense to cut now.
pros:
Senior leadership is upfront and invested in organization and people.
Dedicated talented staff members with flexible work arrangements.
Opportunity to take charge and contribute.
cons:
Cost savings measures are driving great talent and intellectual knowledge out of the company.  
Focus on saving each team, division and department taking priority.. 
While a globally diverse workforce,  promotions are driven by location over talent.

advice: You need to give your employees incentive in order to make them work harder. Check the ethical selling of your employees. You preach it, but certain sales people are given everything and being coddled, while the other sales people are not being coached and being left out to dry. Stop hiring people from other banks who think they can change the company for the better when they do not even understand it! Invest in technology!!!!
pros: Bank has well known name and brand
cons: Benefits are not the best, every year the varibale compensation capacity is cut, corporate culture promotes unethical behavior even though they say it does not, managers do whatever they want-do not lead by example, upper management is always the rejects from other large banks, they do not value talent, rather hire from outside instead of promote from within, most of the time.

summary: Good people generally except many senior mgmt dont care about people
advice: Make changes faster. Layoffs every three months makes for a scared,  unmotivated workforce. Fix the benefits contributions and review system.
pros: Work/life balance, smart people, pay can be good. Some realy nice people below?senior?levels.
cons:
Benefits contributions are crazy high if your title is even moderately senior ($1000+ / month),  you never feel much job security... seniors think nothing of slow rolling layoffs or transformations for years while everyone fears for their jobs. Reviews are bizarre because managers have to submit ratings long before any conversation with directs... so no possibility of convincing boss to improve rating.
Bonuses seem barely related to performance. So you can do a great job and not be recognized much more than someone who barely contributes.

advice: Focus less on cost cutting and more on increasing market share to make the company more profitable. Tie performance of senior management to compensation.
pros: Employees are professional, Smart and team oriented. Training is encouraged and a wide range of courses are available.
cons: The morale is poor. people go about doing their jobs best they can but the prospect of layoffs is constantly hanging over their heads. Too much focus on cost cutting. There is constant focus on moving people and jobs to low cost locations, reducing operating budgets, outsourcing to vendors.  They have recently resorted to sharing workstation space to reduce office space and confiscated Blackberrys.

advice: Remember, you were once in your analyst's shoes. Don't treat them like you were treated.
pros: You'll have great opportunities after you leave and some opportunities to advance if you stay. Work can be intense but interesting. You are able to have a decent amount of exposure to senior people, although a lot of that might end up happening when you are being scolded.
cons: Every director thinks their work is the most important and Citi would crumble and fall without them, so managing egos is a skill everyone will gain. Hours can be long but that is expected, and everyone is very siloed into their role.

summary: Stay away unless you like abuse.
advice: I don't know what to tell you. You won't listen anyway. Do what you think is best.
pros: Pay was pretty good that's about it. If you like redundant work (like i  do) this can be a interesting opportunity.
cons:
Toxic. Toxic. Toxic. Citibank has a culture of narcissistic rage. People yell and scream for very little reason in meetings just to flex their authority. Directors will work to devalue you and attempt to force you out if you don't enable the narcissism. Just like any bad behavior without consequences this culture will never stop. It's horribly stressful because most people are overworked. In the end it takes a toll on your health. I feel 5x better after leaving. 

I should have known i was in for a wild ride when one of the leaders of my department told us during our 1st week orientation that Citibank wasn't a big happy family and people will withhold information from you.

advice: There is no need to micro-manage employees with unreliable software to increase productivity.
pros: Nice work location, plenty of parking. I tendered my resignation as soon as I found a better job.
cons: Poor Salary and unwilling to negotiate on better pay. Software (ESP) used to micro-manage every single minute of work including bathroom breaks. Managers were telling employees they could not have more than 2 3-minute bathroom breaks on an 8-hour shift. Mind you the bathrooms were at the ends of the building and it was a large massive room with hundreds of cubicles. Many employees with management titles but zero management skills. Management is unreliable and plays favoritism.

advice: Get to know your staff/employees and offer help/advice when needed as asked for.  Don't just close your office door for the day and hibernate.
pros: Good benefits package.  Other than that, not a thing.  Unless you happen to luck out and get a half way decent manager that is willing to back you and support you ( of course only if deserve it) you will not and I repeat will not make any type of progress in your career.  And unless you step in a pile of you know what, you are stuck at the spot in which you first applied to.
cons: Management has no idea what they are doing if they actually do do anything at all. Nothing but politics and who a popularity contest.

summary: Great people, excellent work environment, tremendous learning opportunities
advice: Less newsletters, less conf calls, less meetings.
pros: I have been working for Citi for more than three years. I really like the people, my job and the working conditions. The benefits, cafeteria and learning opportunities are excellent. Work life balance is good. The managers really listen to me and provide feedback. If you are proactive then you are at the right place. Be open minded and listen to suggestions and look for the opportunities.
cons: Tons of emails, newsletters, updates. It is a huge, global company and so many things happening here. Once in a while I found it very difficult to follow all those changes.

advice: Clear house at the lower level and get rid of people with "can't do" attitude.
pros: You can gain global experience. The company is on a path of restoring its good reputation producing solid results and repositioning to a better operating model. You have the opportunity to communicate people on the global scheme and build a network.
cons: High turnover due to cost cutting, subpar compensation and uninspiring work environment. While senior leaders are great, some of the lower level directors and SVPs are incompetent and do not foster a great mentorship culture. Talent and hard work is recognized in certain groups, however it is not rewarded financially. Uneven distribution of work within groups.

pros: Underwriting is very liberal and underwriting managers are very easy to talk to.  Will go through scenarios and help when needed.  A lot of other banks have "hours" for when you can contact underwriters and these ops people are happy to help!
cons: Very conservative as an employer.  Requires lots of work on improving KDS scores but then doesn't do things to help employees do their jobs better.  For example, tellers have to ask clients about their mortgages, finances AND help them with their banking needs.  In order to keep the wait time down for the line, a teller cannot possibly try to sell these products to clients.

summary: no work life balance, actually, no life at all
advice: hire more people.  we are working to death.
pros: office location, decent people (peers), good brand, honesty and integrity of operations
cons: with its global challenges the profitable office/entity needs to "support" those in need, meaning no matter how profitable we are, it doesn't reflect on the increase of capacity and resource, nor on our personal compensation.  1 personnel has to do the jobs of multiples, therefore it's a 9 to 11 - 9AM to 11PM job most of the time.  the team is great, peers are from great schools, decent and honest, but executive team is absolutely disconnected from reality.  they live in bubbles.

advice: Gd luck
pros: People generally fine, low expectations of work. People don't yell at one another. Good mobility opportunities as turnover can be high.
cons: Many good staff have already left. Many who stayed are those that don't cut it elsewhere. Many returned to Citi after not being able to take more demanding work environments in other banks. Many who have been here forever are good at taking cover from responsibilities and not responding to emails or phone calls. Strategy to cut headcount at country level teams and beef up regional level teams who push down initiatives blindly will backfire eventually. You need eyes on the ground, not orders from people  stationed in ivory towers.

advice: Provide better onboarding training to new employees. The current paradigm leads to high turnover among those coming to Citi with any experience as systems knowledge is limited and the opportunity to come up to speed is nonexistent.
pros: The pay is good, the benefits are ok (insurance, like everywhere else, is prohibitively expensive) and other benefits are competitive.
cons: Silos exist from department to department and, along with the lack of any accountability, leads to an inability to successfully navigate the bureaucracy to actually accomplish anything. If you're coming to Citi from the outside, stay away.. The culture is such that you won't be accepted and you won't be given the resources to succeed.

jobTitle: Applications Development Tech Lead Analyst - Vice President
pros:
- Global Reach
- Good learning experience working on financial projects
- Good exposure to many tech and skilled people
- A good name for you to get another job in the financial industry
cons:
- Short-sighted. Everyone just cares about the end of year bonus and getting promoted so they can get another job in the financial industry
- They have an army of incompetent managers. 
- Consistent management turnover. New directions every quarter.
- Bureaucratic, politically charged environment, highly-regulated institution. It can be challenging to get things approved.
- Bad coffee
- HR practically unavailable and inoperative, overloaded with paperwork, policies, and regulations,
- Working in a global environment, you have to wake up late for meetings.

summary: I would not suggest anybody to be here in at least AML.
advice: Make a place where people can enjoy working. You have policy to report for things but ultimately HR or Management doesn't care about it and Person is only been evaluated by his/her manager. So what's the point if Manager is not letting people to grow.
pros: Big Name in MNC but fact that AML department is not so good and filled with politics.
cons:
So much deep and pathetic Politics,
Talk about Multi Culture but the fact is that they do not let you grow. 
Not a good money compare to other players in market,
Illogical Policies that keeps you stressed.
Majority Manger's are so much filled with ego and proud.

pros: It is a call center job, collections specialist. It’s a bit tough to get used to being on the phones 8 hours a day, however the company is great. The starting pay is almost twice the minimum wage in my area, benefits start from day one AND are better than any company I’ve ever worked for. From bonuses that are easily obtained, medical, dental, paid vacation & sick time, FMLA, short term disability, paid maternity AND paternity time....it’s wonderful. Constant promotion opportunities.
cons: Being on the phones, and lately changing managers every 2 months...whom all have different requirements that can make you fail Qualities.

advice: You are employing people who deserve a proper work life balance. Promoting stupid people to get them out of teams doesn't solve anything but cause more problems. Stop with all the forced overtime and weekend work, people quit once they burn out.
pros:
Money

Health care & pension

Free Cycling changing rooms with showers.

Lots of other offices making internal rotations easy.

WFH options.
cons:
No work life balance. Extremely long hours and far too much overtime.

Working with far too many stupid people. Really bad hiring processes. Contractors hired because they are easy to fire while waiting to find the right person. 

Extremely poor senior management that have no idea.

Being treated like a number not a person.

No exit survey because it will all be negative. No way to provide feedback which just causes the same problems to keep happening with no change.

advice: REDUCE SALES GOALS. Put more care towards your employees and LESS about hitting numbers!
pros:
-Slightly above average pay
-Great benefits package
-Matched 401k up to 6% of your annual salary
-Coworkers are very supportive
cons:
-Fake as hell HR who don't give a single damn about you or your needs
-Sales goals are RIDICULOUSLY high 
-Little to NO downtime in-between tasks, you're constantly expected to be active and doing something
-30 minute breaks (for a full time job??)
-Have to work for minimum 1 year before you can be promoted
-Commission/Bonuses SLASHED throughout the last year, reduced to more than 50% of what they used to be. 
-Hours can be RIDICULOUSLY long (8:30-6 or even 7PM)

summary: Great People, Not So Good Company
advice: Great Senior folks.
pros: Definitely the people. I enjoy working with them and being around them in general. It's a culture where everyone gets along with each other and the senior folks definitely try to take care of the new folks. During my internship, everyone was very supportive and understanding. I was invited to go back but decided to look at other options due to the state of our economy.
cons: It is a company that is very unstable at the point. The lack of job security has led to an outflow of talent. The company has struggled recently due to the economic crisis and I hope for the best for everyone there.

summary: My experience in Citi has been wasteful
advice: Please take a look at the people who really work and not the people who only talk.
pros: The Organisation provide a huge experience in multi geographical projects. If the person is committed to loose family life for a hard work 24*7, the organisation is a good place.
cons: No Opportunities, too much of red-tapism. Opportunity is only provided who probably love to play office politics. The HR itself is not strong and is an unknown department. No work life balance and expectation is to work even weekends all the time. Weakest of the Project Management staff. In short horrific place to be. Compensation is one of the least in the market.

summary: Best part of working at Citi  - the people.
pros: Throughout my time at Citi, I've worked with very talented and genuinely nice people. There are plenty of opportunities for employees to develop their careers. The salaries are competitive and the benefits are great.
cons: There are days where you will have to put in long hours. In HR, there isn't really a training program, you pretty much learn on the fly and have to trust that the person walking you through the process knows what s/he is talking about. Because it's such a large organization, sometimes it's difficult to navigate through it and there can be a lot of bureaucracy involved.

advice: You could probably eliminate 1/3 of the staff people in Dallas without any impact on the business.
pros: There are a lot of bright people in the company and people who want to do a good job.  Excellent benefits.
cons: There is also a massive amount of dysfunctional behavior.  Relentless cost cutting yet tons of highly paid staff, who add virtually no value and in some cases detract value, because of the burden they place on others.  Large fiefdoms are tolerated.  Work ethic, at least in Dallas is weak.  An incredible number of rude people in terms of interpersonal skills, being late for meetings, contempt for people of lesser titles.

advice: Entice junior research associates to somehow be more entrepreneurial and out of the sometimes groundhog-day like routine of modeling / data entry. You will produce a better product in the end and challenge the incumbent senior analysts.
pros: Great opportunity to learn the ropes of equity analysis under a relatively stable enterprise / platform. Good opportunity to interact with other teams: sales, trading, etc to learn how the bank ecosystem functions and relates to the buy side. In summary, a good entry point.
cons: Resources are dwindling and pay isn't what it used to be. A lot of senior research analysts solely manage up as a result without regards for developing their juniors.

advice: It is unfortunate that management was not able to find a way to make things work in Canada, most of the employees had been with the company for nearly 10 years and helped to create a family atmosphere.
pros:
Great location
Great Atmosphere
Good People
Most managers are flexible with start times allowing employees to run errands in the morning
Onsite Cafe that is subsidized by the company allowing for affordable meals
cons: Citi has chosen to leave the Canadian marketplace (Investor Services) no longer making it an option for people who want to work in the Investor Services industry and stay outside the downtown core.

advice: Develop supporting by the back office.
pros:
It's a good platform to learn and develop the banker career, required selling wide of banking product, including mortgage, loan, investment, insurance. 

It's a stepping-stone if you want to be a relationship manger/consultant, personal banker in Citi has good reputation in banking industry in Hong Kong.
cons:
Not enough support by back office, it's like an 'one man bank', if you are looking for professional support, you have to figure it out by yourself.

Insurance would be the main revenue of the incentive, so everyone would be mostly selling insurance very hard, sometime it's like working in an insurance company.

Long working hour: about 9am - 8:30pm

advice: Listen more to what people want, if you cannot offer cash, give employees  more freefom instead...in the form of better work life balance, possibility of regular remote working in general, not as an exception.
pros: Employment stability, health insurance provided to all employees, pension from a certain level, recently getting better at work life balance, mobility options, blue chip company, multinational company experience
cons: Not really employee oriented - a few bonuses, the offices are outdated, big pressure on decreasing operating expenses and thus keeping salaries low. Entry Salaries avaregare for the industry, no bonuses in non revenue generating roles, difficult to get promotion due to cost of empoloyees restrictions

advice: Stop the fiefdoms, and political BS and lets work together to fix the serious issues. Kill the big bonuses for the fat cats.
pros: Exposure to wide varieties of technologies. Nice people. Opportunities to hone your political skills. Lots of diversity, lots of different kinds of people to meet. You get to interact with a vast array of people.
cons: Too much politics. Real workers who want to just do their job are not allowed to work sincerly. ITs a political jungle in there. Extremely vertical groups, each group only does their thing, and nothing else. ITs like wearing blinders to work. There is no sharing of data/information between groups, and there is a lot of back stabbing and back biting.

advice: Just check the cons, there is many place for improvement
pros:
workload is balanced
salary is a bit over the average
the cafeteria has been increased a bit at end of 2017
cons:
the team / company socialising events (Christmas party, etc.)  are paid by the employee (not kidding)
very old equipments, old systems, three different tools for conferences, everything is like in 1990
no laptops, only desk computers (hard to take notes on meetings)
no flexible working hours
lack of home office (one per week is below the average)
no or minimum yearly bonus
missing cafeteria elements (no tax free housing benefit)

summary: Good benefits not very good professional experience

summary: It has been a long stressful experience with Citibank.
advice: Compensation needs to take into consideration work-life balance. They should allow employees to take vacation without the worry or fear that they won't meet their sales goals for the month and have it held against them.

pros: Good benefits, variety of jobs and positions, opportunity to be a part of creative problem solving, fair working policies, and HR practices.
cons: If you don't like change or high standards, this is not the company to work for.  The change/standards were generally practical and made good business sense.

summary: Citi is the company without a soul!

pros: Good work/life balance, I was able to work two days a week at home, which helped to reduce my stress. Good benefits, 401k, health insurance, vacations, etc.
cons: Citi is a very, very large organization, to many chiefs and not enough Indians! cons: Citi hires a lot of uneducated people that move up the ranks by brown-nosing and playing internal politics. The dress code resembles a night club at times and a lot of the employees seem to spend more energy trying to get out of work than to just get in a do what they're paid to do.

advice: Listen to the workers who are actually trained and performing the functions daily to better the processes.

cons: Unorganized in some departments, not much room to advance to management levels, not receptive to change, outdated and divided systems make it difficult to manage work, various levels of employment don't always fit with a person's experience/educational background.

summary: Citi is built on bitter employees with the "minimum range pay gets minimum productivity" mentality.
advice: You've long forgotten who is rowing the boat you so smugly point in any direction you think there's treasure.  Stop coming up with new projects to save money because you and most project managers don't comprehend that your great money saving idea is on paper only.  Once the change is made an you spend money to make a mistake that in the end costs the company 3x as much to undo, you haven't saved anything, and to absorb the lost revenue there will be layoffs. In short, your great ideas to justify your jobs will cost jobs.  One day you'll see that 1 firefighter on a fire truck and 1 paramedic on an ambulance is a great way to save money, until you actually need them.  Saying "moving forward" is not how you apologize, and not how to fix anything.  I've yet to hear a criminal at their trial say "moving forward" and expect to be set free, why do you?
pros: Insurance is ok, it gets worse every year.  Most mortgage related positions get monthly bonuses, while IT gets the mushroom cap.  IT hasn't seen a bonus since 2007, raises in IT are 2% (enough to go out to an ok dinner once a month).  Most managers operate on the hospital model, meaning the doctors (managers) get paid well, while the nurses (administrative assistants/leads) do all the work of their managers.
cons: Citi is generally a "Joy Free" zone.  Every URL you go to in the Google Chrome browser is logged, your calls are recorded, your IM conversations are logged and reviewed by legal, this is often a good excuse for "house cleaning" of employees.  If your spouse works for Citi, be suspicious!  Chances are they're out in someones' car in the lot or at Busch Wildlife hooking up, this is a fact, and everyone knows, male or female.  Female employees (usually in the Loss Mit area) have been known to hook up with male co-workers, managers, and even the landscaping crew.  The few long time employees are just hanging on to retirement, lots of those positions (coincidently) are JD'ed (Job Discontinuance) just before retirement...but the good news is those people are let go saving the company money, making the stock price go up (that's all that counts right?), and the work is absorbed by other employees..Job discontinuance means that "job" (work) is no longer required...then why is that work that is no longer required passed on to other employees?  Someday the company will be sued because of this.  The local hospitals comment as soon as you say you work at Citi that the majority of their cardiac patients come from Citi.  All the good IT talent leaves Citi, they always ask why and do nothing to change it.  The answer is low pay.  Employees have complained about outsourcing, Citi responds by bringing people from India (and their families) and puts them up in an extended stay hotel, paying for a rental car, meals, etc (and their families) and calls it "INsourcing"....cute.  When it's time for reviews, you have to stop what you're doing to fill out timely self evaluations (twice a year) where you have to justify your own job, only to be kept on, and receive a terrible excuse for a merit raise once a year.  A $500 raise per year (after taxes) is enough to treat yourself to a single person meal at Outback Steak House once a month...as long as you use a coupon though.  Most mortgage workers will leave under good terms to go to a competitor, only to come back to Citi within 6 months to a year at a higher rate of pay, and repeat this to pad their salary.  Upper management doesn't know who you are or give a tinkers damn, and has the audacity to thank you for your hard work during town hall meetings, and claims they have an open door policy if you have a problem.  I really could go on, sadly there's really little to say in the "pros box".  Outsourcing to India has slowed only because people in Budapest are cheaper.  Outsourcing the the already outsourced, when will it end?  Outsourced workers in India are rude, demanding, and when you can understand their broken and incorrect English, are terrible at what they do.  Even the programmers put out embarrassing bug-ridden code...but good news, the company saved money, and thats what allows the well oiled machine to keep running.

pros: One of the too-big-to-fail banks (for now), and there's a lot of ambition? (but not much thought and resources to match up to it)

pros:

cons:

summary: Relatively new employee wishes Citigroup knew anything about technology.
advice: Give me a real operating system. Give me a better computer. Don't make me pay for an intern to sit in a cubicle for 3 weeks twiddling his thumbs because you can't figure out how to assign a login and password. Move your password assistance branch out of Mexico. Do not take risks with supposedly risk-free investments. Cut back the beaurocracy and try and actually get things done in a logical and timely manner, as opposed to your current convulted and incredibly slow method of doing business.
pros: Citigroup is a powerful financial institution with a lot of resources unique to the institution. As a financial advisor, I have access to a lot of in-house resources and tools for my clients that are, as far as I can tell, unique to the industry. They pay fairly well and the overall environment here is not bad, and there is a good deal of comraderie between advisors within the office. Once everything was set up, we've had a good deal of autonomy as to how we run our business within the firm, so in that respect I'm quite satisfied.
cons: Citigroup has more beaurocracy than any company I have ever seen. Anything in my branch can be done relatively quickly, but setting up accounts for interns, making any changes to my workstation, or attempting to do anything that requires outside approval takes forever. My HR director has been working for the firm for almost 20 years and still is confused by the system, not because she is less than competent but because the system makes very little sense. In addition, the firewall and operating system all computers are required to have almost, but not quite, completely cripples my ability to do any work with technology of any kind. There is a fairly good software suite preinstalled on the computer, but any applications that I want to use that haven't gone through the endless Citigroup approval process can't be installed. Upgrading or replacing technology of any kind is also very difficult. In addition, in the recent market Citigroup made some financial mistakes that were extremely costly to my busniess and my clients, so I'm entirely less than happy about that, but some of the other deals I have managed to get for them mostly makes up for some of the recent fiascos.

cons: Long hours, frequent reorg to structure, low bonus/increment, bell curve grading so some that are deserving of a higher rating are bumped to a lower rating, lack of diversity in some teams as hiring manager tends to favour certain ethnicity, some promotions seem to be given to inner circle of friends instead of being based on merit

advice: Get rid of sales!
pros: Friendly co-workers, great training and OJT. Good pay, and benefits. Different schedules available and multiple departments to work in. Every supervisor that I worked with really cared about their teams stats, if a team member wasn't performing they would receive additional one on one training and encouragement. Employees were given multiple chances to correct stats. (Maybe too many chances.)
cons: Corporate! It's a bank and pretty much the root of all evil. Cross sell on a customer service call comes of as forced most of the time and the sell bonuses were practically reduced to nothing towards the end of my time there.

summary: Employees in the Irving office were looked down on by people in the O'Fallon office.
advice: You threw our the baby with the bathwater when you merged best business practices between Irving and O'Fallon .  Irving had proven policies and proceedures which had passed agency and internal audits versus O'fallon's policies and procedures which were in shambles, but O'fallon took control and history proved they didn't know there butt's from their elbows.  Senior Management needed to listen to line Management rather than turning the process over to O'Fallon to make the decisons.
pros: Wage scales and benefits for senior employees were good.
cons: No job security or career path for Irving employees.

summary: Great experience working at the Citigroup Private Bank
advice: Overweight in front end sales staff and need to start hiring product specialists to support them or the model is going to break (lack of client & product support). A growing business with a strong sales force needs the back end to support it.
pros: Wonderful clientele, educated colleagues and a strong and growing business.
cons: Constant change in management and direction, too much hiring on the front end (bankers who do not fit in with the Citi culture), too many communications about the same topic, need to beef up support staff - people are becoming stressed, overworked and their company morale is diminishing.

summary: Good overall first job that led to other great opportunities with a recognizable name. Fabulous benefits- no comparison.
advice: More communication over new procedure changes and how that affects your job.
pros: Benefits - company matched up to 4%. Good health benefits and a gym in the facility that I used everyday. Training was decent and coaching was valuable. Remote capability and worked from home 3 days a week.
cons: Slow at progress (disadvantage of being a large company) and might be overlooked if you don't volunteer yourself for special projects often and work from home (invisible).

summary: Its embarrassing who they hire as managers
advice: Branch Managers need more training in common sense and respecting there employees. Its never ok for a manager to call a teller stupid,slow or ignorant because they didnt get  5 referalls that day. The company culture seems like its ok to treat people under them like garbage.

summary: Good start but not a place for a career...
advice: Look at the bigger picture.  Pay your people what they are worth, listen to their concerns, take a day and spend it doing their job....retain and reward your employees for their hard work.
pros: Excellent vacation time, some amazing employees with passion and drive.

Very poor morale.  HR favoritism and having to learn how to keep your mouth shut when you see something wrong/unethical.

advice: Lighten the structure and improve the efficiency, this way Citi will be able to adapt to global market the fastest.
pros: Citi is a great company. Its working style is flexible, you can always find the work/life balance at Citi. Sometimes you can also request working from home. There is no office politics, everyone at Citi is very nice. You will have a lot of oppertunities working with people all over the world, and you will have chance to travel to many countries.
cons: Citi is a global organization, its structure is too complex, for any good product idea, it is always not easy to implement and publish to market.

advice: Improving work life balance would be the first step. Senior managers should better exemplify the culture and values they espouse. Overall Citi is not a bad place to work but could be better if more attention was paid to details.
pros: I found that most of the low to mid-level management to be quite good. They cared about the professional development of their staff. There was a lot of promotion from within the company.
cons: Work-life balance was not very good. People routinely worked over 50 hours per week. The management tried to make lip-service to their commitment to work-life balance but the commitment didn't last.

advice: Distribute power more evenly over the various management levels.  Management of the technical groups should report to management of the client side at a lower point in the org chart.
pros: Citi corp provides a great environment to work.  I was able to push new concepts in the UI of one of their trading systems.  Our group acted like a small company within Citi.
cons: Our group was working in close relation with our clients (traders) however, I feel business units could be driven more by the clients.  Management of the technical groups should report to management of the client side (sooner in the org chart).

advice: Train your employees better.  CSR were terrible to customers a lot of them not giving the correct answer to customer.
pros: You get a lot of days off because of the holidays.  Could take time off if it was slow, however, no pay.
cons: I worked the phones and had to sale.  All they cared about was sales.  If you did good they liked you if not look out.  Quick turn over.  Manager had favorites.  Always had to make sure my commission was correct. Bad training, customers always complaining CSR people had different answers.  Nobody helped the customer correctly.

advice: The majority of their offices and buildings need a massive face lift. Please, please, please invest into the Financial Centers!!! Your customers are noticing the problems!!!
pros: Most things are laid back at Citibank, and you have the potential to make a lot of money in the company. Definitely would recommend for people wanting to be in the banking field. They have the power of a big bank with the customer service orientation of a small bank.
cons: Most computers, software, and things in the bank are incredibly out dated. In many occasions it's also massively disorganized. This just makes works for employees harder.

advice: Be honest with the workers. Be honest with yourselves. Admit mistakes and take all necessary corrective actions.
pros: I'm familiar with the company. I know several people who currently work there. The company utilizes technology and processes that I understand and am completely competent with. The position I interviewed for was one I am fully capable of performing well. The position is located near to my home.
cons: The company is currently downsizing. Many positions are in transition or being eliminated completely. Many people are nervous about their continued career prospects. Many positions are being moved out of the state, thus forcing people to either relocate or be downsized.

advice: Hire and retain managers that have people-skills.  Break down the silos by making management "walk the talk".  This is Citi's biggest challenge in managing its massive, global organization.
pros: Your co workers are great.  You will meet many really smart people who will share what they can with you.
cons: The silos still exist.  Its so frustrating to try and get a project done when you aren't able to talk to the people that really have the knowledge you need.  Despite senior management's push to break down the silos there are still lots of sandboxes that you aren't allowed to play in.

summary: Really great place to work with excellent growth opportunities.

summary: Pretty great place to work at
pros: Mobility - You can move pretty  much anywhere and have a job with Citi.  You might want to make it big in NYC...Or maybe enjoy the sunshine beaches down in Tampa...Or maybe even go overseas!  The mobility is the greatest part at working for a big company.
cons: Well...its a big company.  That means they have to reduce headcount and do whats best for the business.  You are merely just a number to get lost in a shuffle - and some departments its all political so really good people either quit to work for other banks or get fired!

advice: Please think of more than just the bottom line when making decisions. when promoting, take less stock in employee network participation and connections, take more stock in actual work performed.
pros: Good pay, great benefits, direct managers (OM and below) are mostly great. Strong recognition programs. Numerius Site Employee appreciation events and quarterly town halls make employees feel appreciated. Great culture.
cons: Decisions made by upper management are too often made to cut costs at all costs, with no thought given to customer experience or employee morale. Promotion decisions are often politically based rather than merit based. Yearly Wage increases do not keep up with yearly insurance premium increases.

advice: I wouldn't suggest any changes to the current direction set forth by management.  People who thrive on individual success do very, very well.  Management has emphasized ethics and doing the right this as of late, which is having positive results on work environment.
pros: Global footprint second to none in the Banking world. Uniquely positioned to offer customers access to global markets.  On the whole, very smart people comprise the workforce.  Very competitive atmosphere drives company forward.
cons: While a gross generalization, the competitive atmosphere rewards individual actions/success vs that of a team or general department.  Not a 'team' oriented culture, which I prefer.

advice: Being one of the best banks in the world, it would be great if Citi would have a more competitive salary so it would be less likely for people to  consider working for other banks/companies.

cons: Working at Citi means sacrificing your personal time. The work load is really demanding and it requires 100% of your attention. The salary is quite low considering the amount of work a single person does.

advice: At the very least, give employees (especially the ones you praise for their hard work) salary increases to keep up with inflation.  If not that, at least provide utensils.

pros: Actually a really good company to work for. Good management. Easy to apply for leave. Salary is pretty good (depends, it's good enough for me). They let you change department (idk how it works but it's possible). Good colleagues; they will support you.
cons: I feel like you will only be able to execute very well if you put 100% in it. For myself, I feel like I've tried but it's not good enough as compared to my colleagues. It can be a little overwhelming because you have to maintain daily productivity. Expect to work beyond 9-6 (not always). Definitely apply for this job if you're a fast learner.

advice: Stay strong, continue what you are doing. It was an absolute pleasure and honor to work for you guys for 5 years
pros: Citibank was a great company to work for. There was a very competitive salary package, first class benefits (I had the highest possible health insurance package 100 deductable for my entire family and was only paying 300 pretax money including vision and dental - the company paid 2600 on my behalf - just for the medical!!) all my benefits alone equaled half my base salary, and they also provided extensive training and licensing for their employees. Within the five years that i worked there I was promoted twice. The management always showed respect to their employees and was very much a sense of family and team spirit in the office. There is really nothing negative to say about this place and I can only hope they make it through this economy as it is still the "home" of hundreds of thousands of employees and I hope I will be able to return to this place one day.
cons: The ONLY thing I can say is the idea of job security in this economy we are in. Other than that I have no complaints. I know a countless number of people who have left the bank thinking they found a sweeter deal elsewhere (mainly meaning higher salary) but they have ALL returned or at least tried to, dependind on how bad they burned their bridges on the way out. The balance of income, benefits, work/life, respect, training and licensing  and support from management is second to none. Also as far as the aspect of salary, citibank was by no means giving their money away, but you were WELL compensated for meeting goals and hurdles as well as commision. I knew of several  personal bankers who were making over 100,000 in income.

summary: It all depends on the division.
advice: Great company.  However, a lot of times the smaller guys are not given attention ... resulting in inefficiencies when left to run themselves.
pros:
Pay comparable to other banks (more beneficial at the junior level... ie raise and bonus increases)
Benefits, people, culture - all AMAZING
Global industry/consumer risk is well coordinated and well-compensated
RIsk policy/architecture teams are great as well
DEFINITELY a great place to work, but you have to go to the right dvision
cons:
-The risk organization is great, however, there are large disparities between the divisions and the way that they are treated.  If you are working on the risk team supporting the main business side (banking and trading), you are much better off than supporting a smaller division.  (Also note that working in risk policy/architecture is great too) Even within the business side, it is split between two main industries: global industry/consumer (probably the best place to work within risk) and all other financial institutions.  The financial side is run completely differently (sometimes appropriately given the nature of the business), and is often inefficient when it comes to policies and procedures.  As a junior in this division, there is a lot of back and forth.  They aren't used to having juniors ---> resulting in a lack of serious responsibilities and a lot of grunt work.  Because the seniors in the FI group tend not to be as open to other perspectives, there is a lot of back and forth on minor documents resulting in inefficiency.  It's a little better for more senior level people (it's great if you are running a group or division), but the back and forth inefficiencies are still in play. If you're going to do risk, go to the global industries/consumer side on all levels unless you are running a division or subdivision.

- Transferring between businesses is difficult (know EXACTLY what you want to do when you come in).... but in the same business different industry, it is MUCH easier

summary: Good but bureaucratic.  Beware cons of teams reporting to overseas management
advice: Consider hiring more on shore if possible.  It can be very hard to work when staff and management are on 10+ hours difference.
pros: Seemed good overall. Smart and knowledgeable people people. Great opportunity. Good perks and salary. Interesting and challenging work.

Lot of early morning and late nights when reporting to overseas management, and still have 20+ hours of meetings per week during normal hours.

summary: LOTS Of Benefits in attempt to cover up the fact they dont care about you.
advice: Stop treating your employees like garbage just because you want your bonuses and multi annual trips to Disney. Your staff cant afford to hardly live.

You might have 5 different managers who dont pay any mind to you in a single year, they find any reason to not pay you the bonus you deserve and you can forget the annual raise. Working here for only 14 months put such a strain on my mental health that its taking YEARS of therapy to cope.

Good Name.  The company definitely looks good on the resume and bolsters peoples expectations of you in future opportunities.

summary: Great life balance environment, but unsure about the future.
advice: Needs to set stratigic direction both for the corporation and individual departments.  Many employees come to work each day not knowing if today is their last.
pros: Great work life balance.  Citi encourages people to work from home as necessary and many people do work from home one or two days a week.  Some actually work from home and come into the offices only when necessary.
cons: Department undergoing changes in senior management.  Unsure if department will be retained or outsourced.  No information is conveyed down to the staff about the future direction of the department.

summary: Investment Consultant role has a long way to go
advice: Be honest in the job interviews!

cons:
If you're working for a bank, you better believe you'll be selling checking accounts...even if your job description doesn't specifically point this out.
The base salary is all you'll be collecting until many years into this program.

This program is kicking it into"desperate mode" meaning they are asking their salespeople to do things that were never a part of their job description in order to salvage the program.  A double whammy if you work there because you will either be doing something you don't like or the program is going to completely fail.

advice: Better performance reviews.

Generally the people I work with are friendly and I enjoy working with them.

cons: The structure of management needs to change. There needs to be more competent managers who are passionate about working at the bank and can lead business initiatives and be a positive influence for the company. Also as an employee your work is not valued and you are treated like you are disposable which is why there is a very high turn over rate.

advice: Be more transparent with employees. The link between employees and managers in driven by relationships. Employees will do more because of the relationship, than because its a part of their job description.

cons: Though, salaries are competitive, raises after you are an employee are not that good. 2% average or nothing. Signals are not always clear as to how you're doing. You have to prob to get real information about your status.

Company has work strategies available but managers typically don't like it. Bureaucracy, compliance related concerns and approval process make lives difficult.

summary: Not really interested in more than band-aids for issues.
advice: Try something out before it gets implemented. If it doesn't work....forget about it. I worked for years for a bank that got perfect scores from customers because reps & mgmt actually cared. Our clients were loyal to a fault.  TRY ACTUALLY CARING ABOUT PEOPLE ....THEY'RE A LOT MORE THAN JUST ANOTHER ACCOUNT # OR AN EMPLOYEE ID#.
pros: The campus was beautiful! The trainers were very nice and knowledgeable. Our site leaders were fairly decent people too.
cons: Everything is all about numbers. How many calls you take. How quickly you can dump the client off the phone. How much extra you can sell the client is far more valued than what you can actually assist the customer with.      Was told to stop ending the call with "is there anything else I can help you with?" because people could tell I meant it and actually wanted me to deal with another issue. Motto was basically ONE AND DONE.... You had to do a sales offer even though the client ONLY wanted customer service, then you helped with a single problem and then got them off the phone in 189 seconds!!  You fixed one problem or issue only and got rid of them. Night shift pays the best but you deal with a lot of computers issues that can take way longer than 189 seconds to clear up. Highly stressful. unless you are one of those people who really don't care about truly helping others anyway.     The other real objection is nothing ever stays the same 2 weeks in a row. Someone gets a brainy idea about a service or new way to handle an issue and they inplement and then cancel half the time without any advance warning. Really frustrating to both reps and clients.Our team had only 5 monthly meetings in 12 months ! How does that help the reps do their jobs properly? Frustration level very high.In the 2 years I was there only 4 people were left from our original 32 member class.

summary: Private Banking Used to be a Good Business ...

summary: Pockets and Layers of Seriously Poor Management
advice: Investigate the operational practices and procedures of your departmental/regional management/directors, including the layers above and below them.  Many of these managers are simply incompetent because they have not kept up with modern tech or business practices and refuse to be open to new ideas that can literally save millions of dollars for the company.  Their leadership styles suited the company as it was 10-20 years ago, NOT the company it needs to be today and to become in the future.  The organization is so large and intertwined, smaller units are handcuffed by outdated policy, procedure, technology and leadership.  They have completely lost their operational readiness and business agility.  There is no longer promotion of new fresh ideas, rather, constant fire drills are necessary to keep up with mistakes from the past that were never addressed properly, sucking all time and creativity up like a black hole.  It is a serious daily beat-down that is killing the company from the bottom up, and inside out.
pros: Overall enormous company that means well and has global reach to do so.  Extremely diverse in job types. Committed to Green technologies and practices.  Full of brilliantly talented people that only want to help make the company better.
cons: The company is absolutely not too large to fail.  The sheer size of the company allows for pockets and layers of extremely poor management to thrive using outdated, archaic management practices and defeat all attempts to improve the company with new ideas and technology.  Entire departments and divisions led by poor management can self destruct before management layers high enough up to do anything about it even notice.  Employees who come in from other more successful companies with far superior best practices and ideas are easily shut down and soon ushered out the door because these poor layers of management "know better".  It is easy for these poor managers to hide what is really going on (if they are even competent enough to be aware of their mistakes) due to the size and complexity of the company.  The scary details in the weeds are hidden by flashy (actually poorly done) PowerPoint slides with graphs and pictures.

advice: Invest in technology;  it will take some time for the investment to pay off, but you will need so many less people going forward.  This should reduce operating costs in the long run
pros: Exposure to many different types of transactions, asset classes and capital structures.   Global reach allows the firm to a serious contender in several products and services.
cons: a very big place to work, takes a very long time to get up and running at the firm and too figure out the systems, what's important and where things are.  Technology is not good and slows you down significantly.

pros: great work/life balance (if that is important to you); benefits; empowerment (depending on your manager) - 3 of my 5 managers have been great!  2 were backstabbing, power-mongers.  but then again, those people are in every company!  you own your career
cons: pay/salary; departments are known to hold back employees advancement due to "business needs"; not very good HR support system.  it is a daunting task when you have to find a HR person to ask a question about benefit;  i've seen too many promotions not because of abilities, but due to who the person knows.

advice: Is this a joke?
pros: Not many left. There used to be some respect and team atmosphere. Some of the buildings are ok. All I can really think of as a solid positive is probably having Citi on your resume might open doors for you else where.
cons:
Intensely political, meaning that who you know matters far more than anything else. Game playing management tactics abound. If you are not playing golf and loosing to the boss in the right way they'll manage you out. 
Not many people are fired, management will have a lot of fun managing you out. There is so much deadwood due to political promotions, the buddy system and sheer machinations that there are very few competent enough to do the work. If you are demonstrating you know your job and are willing to go the extra mile then woe to you. Essentially what happens is all the work that should have been done by favorites will be loaded onto you. They set you up to fail. They will joke about you in management meetings. "that fool, that looser"
How do you survive? Fit in. Find out immediately what your department managers are like. If you are a xerox copy of them, maybe you'll be invited into the club. You'll get 1's and 2's no matter what. Ramble on in endless sentences in the interminable meetings. Ape the speech patterns of the bosses. 
Basically the culture is hard core Brooklyn NYC: antagonistic, cut throat, devious and full of power games. It's street hustling, machiavellian types that get ahead. If you are professional, forget it. This is a filthy knife fight in the streets. Departments are rival gangs. It all comes down to fists.
The little people by and large are nice. They don't get promoted. They don't fit in. Don't be nice. Don't play by the rules. It's better to drive the work than do the work. That's what's valued. The work is nothing. Talk loud and interrupt others. Be unpredictable. Make the work harder and criticize everyone and everything below you. Make your coworkers look like fools. Humiliate, denigrate, subvert, undermine. Suck up to those above you.

advice:
First of all, management should understand that they are working in a global company and stop being afraid of foreigners. Citi CSC in Poland is managed as a Polish local company without any vision of diversity or equality. Management should be fair and equal to everyone without considering their ethnicity. 

Management should not be afraid of skill and on the contrary, should use skilled people to deliver better results compared to now. 

There is a reason that Citi is losing all their best high performers now. As you preferred to promote people not because of their skills/results/achievements but only because they are in a development program or just because they have good relations with you; now you are losing your best people. 

Be open, be global, be fair and respect talent and you will have the all success in the world.

Give people a reason to miss Citi after they leave.
pros:
Great corporate culture (globally). 
Great visibility in job market. 
Very good start point to start your career to learn corporation 101.
Good benefits but below the market salaries. 
Talented young people, friendly atmosphere. 
Global career opportunites
cons:
In Citi you will never get promoted because of your skill set or your achievements. If you want a successful career with career growth, you need to learn who to be friends with and learn to never say "no" (even in impossible situations). 

I have witnessed, many times, the struggle of the foreigners, as the general mentality in Citi is that, you have to know Polish to be successful. Otherwise, you are just a person who is closed to communication. With no chance to be in the management team. 

You will be asked to do overtime (paid) almost every day (including saturdays). In the mean time, you will witness tons of people not doing the target but getting the same credit as you do. 

Management mentality usually based on "saving the day", instead of fixing the problem. There is this saying in Citi management: "There are no problems until someone says so". And "someone" here is the upper management.

If you would like to be successful in Citi, the easiest way is to be in a "development program". Just to make the programs look "better", all program members are always get promoted to positions that they don't even have an idea. And the people who actually have a great experience, will be doing their job without any chance of promotion and half of the salary. At the end of they these people will receive official certifications while experts/high performers receive nothing.

Senior management prefers their management team to be obedient people without any skill requirement. This creates a huge issue in times of challenges as they are usually incapable of handling the pressure or finding solutions to even small matters.

If you win a prize (instant recognition), there is a big chance that you won't receive it but instead get a" day off" replacement. In Citi, there is always a budget cut.

Management is usually too lazy to speak English (with some exceptions)

There are no free coffee, tea or milk. You need to bring it yourself.

pros: Citibank offers very good benefits and 401k contribution matches.  They are also very fair towards medical leaves.  I was diagnosed with depression and twice Citi gave me a month off paid.  This position in particular is very easy and customers thank you all day, you are also very empowered to take care of most client situations unless its a high dollar amount (9/10 of every billing dispute is low dollar amounts).

summary: It wasn't bad for employees, but wasn't great either

Disorganization abounds, and reorganization of the company happens at least once a year.  Terrible performance rating system, terrible pay, and managers with no leadership or managerial skills.  Quality of life within the company is insufferable.  High turn-over with mediocre new hires.

summary: Great benefits, not a grey culture

summary: Not very steady for such a big company

pros: Management is more than willing to let you do your job without interfering. You can also move around in the company as long as you are at your present job for one year.

pros: You will gain a world of experience on how NOT to conduct efficient operations and master redundant processes with the minimum amount of staff possible.

There are employees in this division that have not received a pay raise in 5 years. 
Senior management seem more than content with dishing orders from behind closed doors with minimal employee interaction and/or feedback. 
Outside talent always prioritized over internal qualified candidates.
Every decision revolves around saving money rather than being efficient.

advice: Actually listen to your employees.

pros: Great to have that big bank experience on the resume & you get to meet a lot of people
cons: Almost too big to function,  so many people doing so many things. Weird focus on pushing people to make lateral moves instead of promoting within.

pros:
Large platform where we get to work with diverse and talented workgroup.

cons:

jobTitle: Business Unit Manager - Assistant Vice President
summary: Outstanding company to make a career from
advice: Keep up the outstanding work .. Thank you for 8 great years.

cons: The only CON would be that annually merit increases did not outpace the increase in healthcare costs each year. I would like to see Citi be the industry leader when it comes to merit increases and healthcare costs for their amazing staff.

summary: Know your rights, and your worth. Duct tape
advice:
Happy Employees want to work hard, and deliver good results. We really just want to be appreciated and respected. Without them, your department would not function.  YOUR JOB IS TO SUPPORT THEM! THEY ARE DOING THE WORK! 

Generally, people beat themselves up enough if they make a mistake.. don't beat a dead horse, just bury it and memorialize it so we don't forget something died there.
pros:
Co-workers - For me, my hiring manager hired a lot of amazing people. This was an entry-level job, not in a call center, so everyone was around my age. We are all millennials and pretty chill and hard-working. We understood the assignment. 

Good internal growth opportunity - very large company, a lot of moving around room within the company.

Depending on the position - can look very impressive on a resume.

Voice of the employee - This allows employees to come together and give honest feedback to internal team members and managers. THIS CAN DRIVE REAL CHANGE IF ANSWERED HONESTLY AND WITH GROUP CONSENSUS.

1-year rotation - You can change positions after 1 year if unhappy.

Everyone is generally nice.

Great benefits! including in-house child care.
cons:
Management - Typical story. Management doesn't know what you do but tries to direct your work. VOE can help with this. Know your rights! If something is wrong, and you know it... i.e. having an hourly job, but the manager says not to clock OT if you work late. This is illegal and wrong! Take them to HR!

Uneven Pay raise - Typical... you have worked there for a year, and find out the new guy is getting paid more than you are.......(I really can't add enough, etc. dots)

They preach a lot of values, but those only apply when things are going easy...when things get hard and stressful, things start to bend.

General compensation is fair. Base-level salary positions are the worst.

You can see a lack of funding and investment for certain business activities. a lot of things seem to be held together with duct tape.

summary: It was an excellent learning experience and overall a decent company to work for, however, management could be improved.
advice: talk to your employees honestly about what could be done to improve the workplace environment.

cons: Too many managers do not push these types of requests through so it can be very frustrating. I hadn't had a company party in the whole 5 years I worked there, or a bonus due to a failing u.s. economy although executives and management continued to receive enormous annual bonuses.

advice: My former manager was great at receiving both positive and negative feedback from employees, even providing advice as to better ways to communicate our complaints.  Most other managers were not open in this way.

advice: They appear to be doing what they can to fix the mess. They really need to look into employee morale in the wake of what's happening around.

cons:
