Bankers with higher salaries end up paying a ton for health insurance premiums.

summary: Shielding bank from s#@$%t hitting the fan
advice: Things are changing, times are changing, if Citi wouldn't change - in fact,not in wordings - it will go belly up sooner, than anybody can expect and with much surprise to its managers and shareholders
pros: Big international bureaucracy  - an insight view at what the banking is really about, how it works and how it's being sold to sheeple
cons: No respect to people at all."Too big to fall" mindset with respect to all others. McDonalds in finance - especially at lower grades in retail banking

summary: A global company with a local feel.
advice: Unfortunately, I really am not ready to complete this field. I would need more time to work on this.  They do some things very well, and there are areas to improve.  It would be nice if we hadn't gotten into the risky CMO's. It would be much better if we were not in the news regarding whether or not we were less than diligent in the products we offered investors or invested in ourselves.  But hind sight is 20/20.  I am not qualified to make these judgements, and certainly don't have all the information.
pros:
It is a global company, with opportunities all over the world.  It is very multicultural, co-workers from around the world. The people are interesting and talented. The people I work with are talented.  The manager has done a great job of hiring people with different strenghts.  The team approach to completing our tasks works very well.  It is very easy to come together to work on projects, resolve problems.  Among our competitors we are among the leaders in technology to get our jobs done.  I am able to have some control over were I work, avoid long commutes, and flexibility in working from home or several different offices.

The upper management will travel, hold town hall meetings where any of us may attend.  No one is excluded, and we are given an opportunity to be heard.
cons: These are pretty tough times for the financial services industry.  The industry has been going through downsizing, and we have not been spared in this process.  Sometimes it is difficult to get some things done due to the size of the company.  Change can be difficult or slow due to the maturity of the firm,and the size.  Upper management is many levels up and other than the town hall meetings noted above, can sometimes feel impossible to communicate with.

advice: Do what's right for the customers and profits will go up because they'll be happy and not leave. Yet the reality is management has no control over what happens at this job site. They're just the little puppets delivering the bad news over and over. Pay is also lower than comparable places. Schedules suck because they're open 24/7/365, forget about being with your family on Christmas or many holidays. Even if you have a set schedule, they'll change it in no time and leave you with no other choice than to quit because you have kids and need to work during daycare hours. Lastly, they speak a lot about diversity, but they're just trying to fill certain mandatory quotas. My Black friend who interviewed & was highly qualified literally heard them say in the next room that he was great, but they've already hired enough of "them" (!).
pros: Decent benefits package. Decent daycare on site.
cons: It's the epitome of corporate America, so they will do whatever helps profits at all costs. This means customers will get a very bad, downgraded experience, thanks to decisions made by executives thousands of miles away in New York. As employees who actually speak to the customers end up being told off and the customers complain and blame us. They care nothing about the client experience, it all comes down to lining the executives' & shareholders' pockets. We've seen the worst, illogical decisions being made & implemented time and time again. Most staff and managers who work there are miserable, and miserable people usually spread negativity and drama. Lots of managers are on a power trip and constantly threatening you with being fired. It's also in a terrible location in the middle of nowhere, basically in Castroville. You can't even leave for lunch, cause you won't make it back in 30 minutes. They don't provide anything to help your back, get studies prove desk jobs cause lumbar deterioration. By the time you get a doctor's note, it's too late on your back is already permanently disabled.

summary: Challenging but opportunities abound for the right candidate
advice: It's difficult to change the culture of a bank especially when it's unnecessary and half of your competitors are gone, but fostering one of respect and excellence (such as D. E. Shaw) will be worth your while.
pros: Global opportunities abound and this is a great place to make things happen. If you get them to trust you then you can get far.
cons: Bureaucratic and slow moving. lack of personal communication with HR and with upper management. loyalty lacking among team members. culture of abuse among the ranks in investment banking

summary: Be ready to make your own way
advice: Make more concerted efforts to ensure that managers of people are groomed to manage people
pros:
Opportunities for professional growth for those who want it; that is to say one needs to be proactive in making their strengths, abilities and desire to advance known.
Work/life balance, at least for me; I know of other colleagues who complain of long hours and/or managers who are not supportive of flexible work schedules and/or working remotely
cons:
Lack of effective communication and oftetimes, clear direction from management
Persistent "us vs. them" politics between corporate functions and businesses

advice: Continue to engage employees and focus on both the Voice of the Employee (VOE) and Voice of the Client (VOC) surveys.
pros: Citibank is a solid company with great people working there. They offer competitive pay and good benefits with consideration of work/life balance. There is a strong talent pool that works extremely well together.
cons: Citibank has global reach and requires global communication between internal organizations, if these lines of communication were strengthened, it would certainly optimize overall performance.

advice: Not too big to fail, but too big to manage. Need a map to find the right person to speak to about anything
pros: The credit crunch hit hard but my line managers always treated me fairly. The crisis made the firm look at itself hard and adapted some tough changes.
cons: There was sometimes an assumption that being bigger is better. Also, it seemed they found it tough to hold on to people, there was always some changes every month. I think Senior Management is better now than it was when I was there.

summary: Tough environment now, but should get better... eventually
advice: You need to see how hard it is to get things done with convoluted middle management structure and make changes accordingly
pros:
-Good benefits (although have been getting worse over the years)
-Exposure to big challenges: if you can do it here, you can do it anywhere
cons:
-In the consumer area, very little opportunity for promotions/big raises. You need to come in at a good title/salary or you are doomed
-Work environment very depressing- so big and full of silos that getting things done takes a small miracle every time. Overall strategy keeps changing

summary: Just Enough But Not Too Much...
advice: Re-Evaluate the need for all of the layers of management and try some pilot programs that have a different structure from an operational standpoint and see how they work.  Its so tedious trying to do business at Citi becuase of the number of people that need to be involved in even the most simple client related activities.
pros: If you are happy with your job and work hard you can work at Citi for your entire professional career, as many people do.  They are masterful at providing you with just enough of a salary bump and/or other incentives to keep you content and suck you back in year after year.  Its never anything over-the-top to get you super excited about but its also nice enough to make you feel appreciated and valued.  That feeling coupled with its infrastructure, resources, solid benefits, good 401k options and other random perks of working for a global bank is enough to keep many people there for 20, 30 and even 40+ years.
cons: Anyone who has worked there will confirm that the layers and layers of middle management is absurd.  These middle managers are non-client facing  people who somehow feel that they know more about sales than the bankers, more about compliance than compliance analysts, more about the banks clients than the relationship managers, and so on.  Because they really don't serve any real purpose they feel the need to involve themselves in anything they possibly can and more times than not make it more difficult to conduct and close business on a daily basis. There are so many instances where if people were removed from the reporting chain or had their abilities to approve certain things taken away the process of doing business would be drastically improved.  Its all about validating themselves to ensure it appears that they are needed, when ultimately they just need to go away and Citi needs to recognize it....but never will.  This is one of MANY issues that Citi has in every part of the bank.... the list of cons could go on for a long time.  Career Advancement, salary increases, career mobility, recognition for going above and beyond all take a very long time and a lot of self lobbying and often times you really need someone with influence on your side to get anywhere or get recognized for extraordinary work both internal and client facing clients.  There are a lot of instances where poor performers, weak producers and general underachievers who play the game of politics and kiss up to the right people are given promotions and raises and awards while many exceptional people who don't play the game and don't make it their job to be a kiss-ass or put on an act dont get recognized or given the promotion or raise and its disgusting and disheartening to watch.  So much of your ability to a success at Citi rests on how willing you are to "play the corporate game" and not actually on how good you are at your job. LOTS of PROBLEMS.

advice: If you like to work in a fast passed environment, competitive and with a huge opportunity to lear new things and grow as a leader go for it!
pros:
- Great People 
- A lot of learning 
- Fast passed environment 
- Recognition
- Team work 
- Internacional experience 
- Recognized around the world
- Great work / learning environment
cons:
- Hard work 
- Affected by the financial crisis 2007
- Sometimes you have to develop patience in order to achieve some goals 
- Regulations can be hard to deal for the business sometimes

summary: They say they promote based on merit, but it is not really true
advice: Management should listen to employees, and really take their opinions into consideration.  If you say "people are our most important attribute", then your people should be treated in a way that they know you mean it.
pros: Good benefits, decent pay, decent vacation policy, work life balance is respected, some really good people running the company at the top
cons: Promotions are given based on favoritism, communication among departments is horrendous, communication from your own manager about what is happening currently in the organization is almost non-existent

advice: Wake up!  2008 can happen again.  Get rid of the unnecessary layers of management and invest in resources that actually get the work accomplished.  Example:  I don't need 5 managers asking me for seperate presentations for the same project.  That's a problem!
pros: Not many pros.  Pay and benefits are okay, but other companies provide more.  The people are nice enough.
cons: Citi is a bloated bureaucracy with non-value add processes and too many levels of management.  The federal government is more efficient.  Lack of training, poor communication, and a 'sink or swim' culture result in managed chaos.  If I was an investor I wouldn't touch Citi stock with a ten foot pole.

advice: To go back to basics and focus on what Citi was good at and not charge down the path of glory for the sake of it. We have competitive advantage that is unique in the playing field, so use it to our advantage.
pros: Opportunities are vast at the right units. However, you will need to have the right political connections to get to them as and when they arise.
cons: Extreme levels of showmanship is frustrating at times. Many times we are expected to be available for discussions and meetings that yield no fruit.

advice: Try hiring within before bringing in people from outside that don't even know how to lead. Listen to the people that do the work everyday when they tell you that something needs attention. Also show some appreciation!!! No one wants to work for people that don't value their employees. You lose good people that way and the people that remain will see no point in going above and beyond when they know management doesn't even care about them. Take care of your employees and they'll take care of you.
pros: PTO, health benefits are ok but not as well as what other companies offer, they gave free ice cream one day. Hard to think of many pros.
cons: Turnover is terrible, management knows absolutely nothing so you're better off asking another coworker if you need help with something. Some managers pace the floors like prison guards, some are never anywhere to be found, and the rest just stand around talking, won't even come help if you call for them. Sometimes they treat their employees like prisoners yet wonder why people keep quitting. I was there nearly a year and never once did I hear a manager thank or show appreciation to ANYONE for the work they did. Even people that worked double shifts when asked of them got nothing that made them feel they were appreciated. Upper management would continually make changes to things that had nothing to do with work yet the things that needed attention went ignored, sometimes for months. This was one of the most unhappy work environments I've ever worked in. No one wanted to be there and they weren't shy about letting it be known. No one cared because management didn't care. Also don't think you'll move up because you'll be there for 10 years before they even consider you for a higher position. It's not worth the minimal pay. There are gas stations that pay more.

advice: I think high level senior management should be more in touch with middle managers who have the pulse of the company which with better communication will make for better synergy.
pros: The managers have a great deal of knowledge of work flow and are aware of week to week challenges of work load. They are very understanding with work-life balance for each individual.
cons: There could be a more robust employee review  system. This would better serve employees in providing growth internally for future opportunities.

summary: Not great, but definitely not bad.
advice: Although the call center is a small part of Citigroup's global business, it has a large impact in the small city that it is.
pros: Pay is decent. Job is stable. Benefits are fair. Ample paid time off. Company is very structured, and provides great training.
cons: No room for advancement. Management was condescending towards employees. Promotions were not based on merit. Many of the unit managers were promoted based on seniority alone,  it was obvious that they didn't possess the leadership skills. Call centers easily burn their employees out, hence the very low retention rate.

summary: Flawed annual review practices, but overall great to work for
advice: The employee annual review/assessment practices should be re-evaluated. It's difficult to feel fully appreciated when I must own the recognition of myself and my work.
pros: Flexible with scheduling and work location. Great people and good company culture. Decent opportunities for advancement. Nice diversity in employee base.
cons: The employee review process for decisions on annual  pay increases and bonuses is not the best. You must ensure ion keep track of everything you do because you are responsible for recognizing and calling out your work.

advice:
1. Address items highlighted in the employee survey.
2. Re-allocate resources when projects are completed instead of initiating a RIF
3. Minimize the yearly reorganization
pros: For the IT organization, Salary and benefits are decent.  Good peer working condition.
cons: Reorganization and RIF on a yearly basis.   Working hours are long in order to meet with offshore resources.  No clear definition of role responsibilities, opportunities, or advancement.   Employee surveys are ignored.  Departments work in silos, and cooperation between departments is poor.  Project are too often delayed due to poor commitments by sponsoring departments.

summary: Citi offers consistent employment and has opportunities for those willing to achieve.
advice: Continue identifying and developing internal employees.  Many bright individuals are within the ranks that need challenges to keep motivation levels high.  Identify ways to work smarter with improved efficiencies.  Productivity can improve with a few meaningful changes.
pros: Citi has a very diverse culture allowing an opportunity for just about anyone.  Drive, ambition, and patience work well in career development.
cons: Citi also is doing what's necessary to control costs which often comes in the form of tightened salaries and minimal merit increases.

advice: Streamline the organizational model, and decentralize non-strategic decisions. Allow the centers of revenue to make their own investment/expense decisions. These actions will certainly help in making the Bank more agile and more competitive within the markets, while reducing expenses.
pros: Global presence, career opportunities, good compensation and benefits, leadership team focusing in making the company a leader in the Banking industry through innovation.
cons: Complex matrix organization with long decision making process. It is not an easy task to identify ownership and accountability within the organization, which fosters the creation of too many bureaucratic processes.

advice: Appreciate your employees more and stop focusing only on trying to be innovative too often. Its the people that you need to invest in, not technologies. The innovation/technologies will take care of itself if you invest in your employees.
pros: Great people and environment. Loved my whole team and I've met some really great talent there.
cons: The pay is definitely lower than other big banks out there and upper management does not have appreciation for all of their employees. Work life balance wasn't really there and they could do a better job with encouraging professional development.

jobTitle: Technical Information Security Officer, Vice President
summary: Happy People, Challenging Work, Competitive pay and benefits.
pros: Best team environment I have experienced in civilian life. Pay is competitive, Benefits are good, Paid vacation is excellent. One of the happiest/most satisfied group of employees I have worked with.
cons:
Moves at enterprise speed (the aircraft carrier, not the spaceship), so change and innovation takes time and effort.
You must work smart, hard, or both to keep up.
 VDI thin clients are standard equipment.

BYOD is not mature (Good for Work)

pros: Despite taking a reputational hit during the crisis, Citi had turned the ship around and is making good decisions to secure the franchise. cons: The politics of big companies is still at play and it is still about who you know in order to get promoted and get salary increases, its not unheard of for people to be flat for years!

summary: It was amazing being a Citi Banker
pros: Citibank is has a very wonderful  working environment. Like any normal working place, it has its pressure but the professionalism of your co-worker lessens the tension in the office. When it comes to compensation package, they are way much better.
cons: It has been a tradition and a daily living that you work and live 9 hours a day, 5 days a week coping with loads of work, pressure and tension plus added that some co workers are totally pain in the neck. CitiBank is not exempted to this.

summary: You can not get anything done. Everyone's blaming the next person.
advice:
Pay attention to your employees more. 
Dressing nice - but not getting anything done is the principal at Citi
pros: Free coffee. That's about it. Nothing else really. No acknowledgement of good work. Requirement of doing something that is not your field
cons: Bad Teamworks. No leadership. No understanding the value of teamwork. Overall bad experience. I got hired for a job then ended up doing something totally different. I forgot almost everything I've learned before professionally because I and my team mates were given junior tasks.

summary: A good company to work for especially if you are driven.
advice: Be fair when it comes to compensation.  Everyone should be entitled to a basic cost of living increase, and nothing less.  To compensate one person over another when working in the same team does not boost morale nor does it make anyone want to work any harder than they already are.
pros: Good, hardworking people and management.  Was given growth opportunities early in my career there.
cons: If you are not in the right "pool" salary increases are minimal. Also not very accommodating to new families.

summary: Lots of work and overall management trending up
advice: There are very poor senior managers who have not fulfilled their responsibility to the company in their areas which causes major performance issues for their own staff.  Instead of staffing appropriately they literally delegate their goals to their staff, dangling the possibility of a bonus.
pros: Salaries are generally higher than most companies. Plenty to do and opportunities to learn. Flexible working arrangements.
cons: Many are overworked and have to put in extra hours. Compliance driven culture which means you are always in trouble for things that is out of your control.

summary: Last year was 2010 this won't go thst far back*
advice: If things haven't much changed, straighten up. Be professional, but have some empathy. Do not fraternize with subordinates outside or inside the work place. Leave work at work, do not take it home. Ask about volunteering in the community if this is still on hold. See what can be done to do these things again. It leaves a good mark in the commumity, boosts employee moral and sense of self worth, and make sure every employee does time sheet correctly, and make sure you ALL get paid!
pros: At the time, this was the highest paying call center in Tucson. With increases in state minimum wage, hopefully Citi made the appropriate increases due to min wage increase and cost of living. So, it's probably still a top employer in Tucson. Also, benefits were truly outstanding. No more pension offered, I did get the tail end of their pension plan, but they offer 401k of course, short and long term disability, which they give you quite alot of that time up front, and you accumulate more time over the time you work there, and it's actually more than a decent amount of time. They offered the top Health, Dental and Vision insurances in the state of AZ. I miss those benefits. Benefits and pay, if you got paid, were only pros. Well, and two of my immediate supervisors who are no longer there. They were awesome.
cons: Everything else is bad. Politics, work environment, monotony, no room for growth or advancement if you aren't someone's favorite. HR act like you're an inconvenience to them. In the beginning there used to be volunteer opportinities, Humane Society, Habitat for Humanity. By the time I left, they hadn't done anything in the community not sure why. Hope this changed since then.

advice: Provide managers with additional trainings on how to be a be an inspiring leader.
pros: The Day to Day work remains the same and 9-5 work days.  Also you work in both  a team and individually environment.
cons: I can not speak for every manager but my manager was unfair, she showed little to no appreciation on any work completed.  Many felt treated differently than others.  Also would be judged if you took your mandatory hour lunch break.  Very hard to move up in this company seemed extremely political.

Citi is overall a Reputed Brand Name

Free Transportation facilities across Mumbai

summary: Large firm plagued with process/people inefficiencies
advice: I know Citi is hiring and firing left and right, but there needs to be quality control around the managers themselves, which are responsible for so much of the process problems. There are also too many people in the SVP, Director, and Managing Director levels without proper management training, let alone the ability and knowledge to actually implement solutions (but that's why they hire armies of consultants, right?).
pros: Pros: Good benefits including ample PTO and holidays, separate balance for medical and unplanned leave, long maternity/paternity leave, 401k matching, and fancy office (388 Greenwich)
cons:
Cons: In my experience, it always comes down to poor management. The team I work in is intended to improve problematic processes, which can be found all around the firm (and hence the Consent Order from the OCC). Unfortunately, the manager in charge of the team is one of the most ineffective I have come across. He is unable to clearly offer direction, end goals, resources, or even simply track daily tasks. There is no project management system in place, so that in weekly meetings (that have no scheduled agenda) team members have to remind him over and over again about what is happening. What's worse, he is constantly checking his phone during these meetings and not paying attention. Most of the projects we end up doing are initiated by sudden requests/whims from his superiors, which are not necessarily suited for our team, not properly formulated, and lead to dead ends. Overall, a frustrating experience.

FYI: My exit process was like this. After sending a sincere and detailed email to my supervisor explaining my decision to resign, his response was, "Okay, thanks for letting me know. Have a great weekend." When I asked him what steps I should take to inform HR, there was no follow up. After finding information to process my resignation in Workday, a few days later I received an automated link to an anonymous exit survey that was broken. That's it. Nice.

summary: Deadening corporate culture of the most depressing kind
advice: The company becomes less dynamic with each passing year
pros: It's not a sweatshop.  Reasonably accomodating to working from home.  Little sense of job paranoia given the financial crisis.  Some very capable, intelligent and friendly people.
cons: Restrictive network policies - IE 6.0 only 'legal' browser, many restricted sites, 'no downloading'  policy, all 3rd party software subject to IT dept 'wrapping'.  Intra-company communications stuffed with corporate blather.  Very little communication/co-operation/sharing between businesses.  Employee productivity takes second place to data entitlement restrictions in software development environment.

summary: Tech spending is way out of line with required resources which are available and yet not easily accessible for their use
advice: Look at your software spending relative to what the audit controls in place look at for compliance to licensing and usage by the users
pros: Free checking account and some banking services that the company provides to all employees.  Banking Holidays are additional days off - paid
cons: Many people work at their jobs for over 50 to 60 hours each week.  Lots of folks end up doing more than one job at the same time.

summary: Improving, but still catching up to do

pros: Global scope of the business, strong performace in several major areas especially debt capital markets. Firm has had some very good company analysts. Firm is generally good at offering people opportunities to work in different areas/countries.
cons: A higher than normal level of uncertainty regarding the future of Citi Global Markets business. Due to government pressure, the capital markets business may need be sold/spun off.

advice: more concentration over the career for the staff to know what you could offer..
pros: can deal with different customers in an international bank, at the meanwhile, we could get a lot of opportunities to see how culutre and civilzation influence on people, and deal with different other contents such as credit card loaning, credit card promoting, complaint  etc. which national banks would not offer.
cons: highly pressured and not used to the overwhelming complaint laid by the pollicies, and lack of a wholesome policy for the staff to know the way they could head for.

summary: Pretty good company...especially if you get hired in the MBA program.
advice: Look to promote more from within. Just because someone has an MBA does not make them more valuable than a current employee with 10 ears experience.
pros: Co-workers were fantastic...we worked well together and enjoyed spending time together outside of work. Everyone was positive and I felt a good sense of team.
cons: With such a large company, it is easy to feel that you do not matter. If you come in on the ground level, you may stay on the ground level.

summary: it was very exotic and i like to work for big banners.
advice: I was in sales so there are so many opportunities to get high permotion ease and rapidly but if your management will with you otherwise it hurts.
pros: It is a big umbrella which covered of all their employees i means secure future.
cons: one of my best buddy , he is still working Citi Group ( Citi Gold ) in Pakistan , he has team members to work with. But unfortunately i was in 3rd party contract so i get fed up due to management.

summary: Great leadership / large span of control / Big Bureaucracy tough to make any real changes

empower leadership & create accountability

inability to manage poor performers out of organization

senior leadership either unable or affraid to make decision

cons: Even the most minute job postings have to be approved by very senior management (Executive MD and higher) which means that most managers cannot be bothered to run this gauntlet; resulting in too many long term contractors who should really be FTE's despte policies that go against this.

summary: Citi, Decent Compensation, Too much management, Bureaucracy
advice: Foster more communication and departmental interaction.

Flexible Hours - manager works with you and your schedule
Working from home - In the departmental division certain jobs allow you to log around 1/2 hours from home at least at our location
Decent Compensation - Decent benefits / perks / discounts
cons:
Bureaucracy - takes forever to get things done and red tape over everything

summary: Positive.  It is what YOU make it!
advice: Listen to employees and continue to push them to do better and be better.

cons: Some of the metrics were hard to meet, but not unmeetable.  Not a TON of room for advancement, but it is a very big call center.

advice: Invest in your human capital. Be interested in our needs and well being. Give staff more opportunities for career mobility and streamline your processes.
pros: Decent work environment, structured processes, decent enough compensation.
cons:
no chance to move between units. Someone can spend his entire career in a unit, even though he/she has attained qualifications relevant to other units.

Also, bonuses aren't great, and there are some processes that can be made easier.

pros: I've worked for Citi for over a decade and have moved up the ranks at a fairly decent pace for my location. Competition isn't as fierce as a main HUB but still there. I can say the company has taken a stance to relay on it's other locations much more in recent years moving thousands of jobs to these locations which has been a plus.
cons: The hesitation to move some of the higher paying jobs to non-hubs is a bit frustrating

summary: Great place to work, opportunities for technology
advice: Be comfortable moving faster. Try to reduce roles that bring little value, and increase roles that are the actual delivery teams.
pros: Great benefits, work life balance, nice coworkers, I know what's expected of me. Good pay. Very diverse, committed to equality and promoting staff personally and professionally. I feel very welcomed here.
cons: Some of the techology is frustrating and needs to be upgraded. They're working on that though. Processes can be annoying too because there's a lot of administrative work needed to do basic things.

pros: In the CRM role you have more freedom than other retail branch roles, and are not tied to the branch 100% of the time, allowing for client meetings etc. Citi also provides a variety of events that you can participate in with your clients. I felt there was a decent team mentality within the branch, and not the cut throat nature typically associated with banking.
cons: Our sales goals were increased dramatically, and the system that determines bonus payouts made it very hard to bonus compared to previous years.

advice: Need more focus on making day to day process more streamlined.
pros:
- Very supportive senior management and immediate managers
- Good work life balance
- Ctc to in-hand salary ratio is very close to 1
- Very playful and interactive team members, joyful culture throughout hierarchy 
- Transparency in career development and appraisal discussions, very frequent discussions, analysts at the center of this discussion.
cons:
- Base pay and total compensation slightly below major competitors JP Morgan and BoFA. 
- Processes not standardized, use of excel files for workflow management

advice: Care for the health of your employees. I see people in the team accepting the working conditions (extending for hours on end) because they're getting paid and they don't see any other way around it. My manager once told me, "Citi pays well but they will extract every single cent from you."
pros:
Brilliant team
Good pay
Lots to learn from
cons: In my team, it was required to extend hours, work on weekends and even holiday. Unpaid. You are compensated for weekend and holiday work but it's little to none almost. I suggest doing a background check on the team you are joining while on the interview before saying yes to them. I doubt they'll be honest about the working conditions but it's worth asking about.

advice: There are opportunities opening up in different avenues at times and they allow you to explore if you get bored in one area or need time away.
pros: There’s always someone available to help and keep you company if need be or even play a game or 2 when you have the time and win not only recognition but …. there’s so much more too! They got you covered for sure!
cons: I do feel like I have to share a lot of my personal information at times.

advice: implement some of the lip service about how valuable staff is
pros: if not affected by cutbacks, it's a job. systems, programs and rules are set up to make it a place to grow and achieve but rank and file management are too dis-attached, watching the price of their stock to worry about day to deliverable or quality of the work or product provided (should go in downsides, I guess)
cons: too clannish, not as professional as other global financial services firms. my world, mainly 20 years in plus, you are more at mercy of direct managers and his (my world was not at all female-friendly) peers than at many other similar firms. little interest in outside best practices or knowledge

summary: Great environment for the right fit.
advice: New computers, operating system, softwares in the office. they are old enough to damage the work efficiency.
pros:
- excellent management
- fast paced work style yet relaxed environment
cons:
- office politics, people who work there often formed different groups and edge out people didnt belong to their group.
- old computers, old system, old software.
- outsourcing employee. most of the office entry level employee were outsourced. most of them were on contract with outsourcing agent such as "Manpower" and hence did not have benefits like those full-timer.

summary: If you need a job not a career
advice: Your employees need to be heard and a process setup to help them grow. There are a lot of employees who work here for the wrong reasons like commute, salary and not for the job satisfaction
pros: Citi has a friendly work environment, cutting edge technology, cooperative peer groups.
cons: No growth or career advancement, management abuses power and if you are not a manager you have no say. Management has no communication with its employees. The performance review has no link to personal growth

summary: It can be a good place if you are in the right position but its easy to get lost in such a large company.
advice: Nothing - its such a large company everything ends up trickling down. As long as you know this going in you should be prepared for that.
pros: Good bonuses and can learn quite a bit about corporate politics. Ultimiately this can be very frustrating because its very hard to get anything accomplished.
cons: Long hours and being in IT you are the first thing to get cut (at year end bonus/raises)

summary: So far, so good but a massive machine
advice: I do not have any specific feedback or advice to give to the leadership at Citigroup at this particular time
pros: Good global brand and nice friendly people within a global environment. Hygene factors all good as well as the atmosphere
cons: Cog in a big, big wheel with lots of employees so very bureaucratic and can therefore be quite hard to be recognised as you are only responsible for part of the process rather than the whole thing so not always able to see outcomes

summary: Good place to start but difficult to make a rewarding career
advice: career mobility is something not very easy. Good people should be identified by and trained to make future leaders by means of rotation.
pros: Citigroup is good place to start and learn technologies. They give you good opportunity yo try new technologies and are open to adopting open sources
cons: Your big challenge to build your career and move up the organization. Often you are stuck at one place and need to really pull your strings from all directions to move up

summary: The average person is exactly that
advice: Pay your employees better.  you will attract and retain valuable employees and will have better performance for it.  Otherwise, you'll always be bottom tier.
pros: Citigroup has a good name recognition and a rich heritage.  Although a lot of that has been watered down with mergers.
cons: The average employee at Citigroup is exactly that, "average".   Because of its size, the top employees are some of the brightest i've seen.  But, Citigroup also has more than its fair share of duds.

summary: A fat bloated pig with lipstick
advice: Quit and let more competent leaders take their place... Vikram can stay, but his ultimate goal is to turn Citi into an even more massive, fat, bloated, too big to fail bank.  Once again, job security is key here.  Just don't act too smart or else you will get black balled.
pros:
Job security
You can sit around and not work
Hard to get fired
Annuity
Competition is thin
cons:
Promote mediocricy
Lack of direction
Senior management lacks leadership / knowledge
Legal counsel incompetent

advice: Have some more structured training, maybe a class as a group or something, because it seemed to be "learn as you go", nobody in the department seemed to have a clear understanding of rules and procedures.
pros: Good food court, gym inside the building. Management was flexible. Citi is large so there a lot of positions and opportunities to find a position you might like.
cons:
Almost no training, department was unorganized, every worker was completely overloaded with work piling up, too much work and not enough employees. 
Low salary

summary: Only companies that gives you opportunities, but politics rules the roost
advice: Make merit the marker again, and follow HR policies, don't just make them and implement on paper.
pros: They allow cross functional moves every couple of years... Very good learning experience in each role. Gives you plenty of responsibility from day 1.
cons:
Responsibility from day 1 means total learning on the job, no real training/handovers.
Very political environment, stick to the right seniors and you're a superstar, else everyone praises your work but year-end appraisals suck. No longer a market leader in compensation.

summary: Awesome place to work and build your long-term career
advice: Increase more avenues for cross-functional learning/development and provide more opportunities for IJPs within the company. Set-up framework for cross-functional or cross-unit collaborative programs to determine industry best-practices.
pros: Competitive salaries and pay, good work-life balance with ample Holidays and good Leave Policy, Great place for fostering new and innovative processes and execute new ideas, friendly and supportive upper management with no airs about them, amazing work culture.
cons: No cons. Best place for professionals and industry experts who want steady, sustainable growth in their careers.

summary: Citigroup is not a good place to work
advice: I think they should use better judgment in how each part of Citigroup works with the others.
pros: there are not any good reasons to work there
cons: The entire infrastructure in the entire Citigroup company is very poor.  I worked in a program that was just starting out marketed to middle to high middle class investors.  The products we offered were extremely second rate.  The entire program never seemed to be thought out before hand.  My manager new little about the program himself.

summary: It is no wonder that people don't last more than a few years.
advice: Treat the clients like human beings not just account numbers.  Although gross commissions and profitability are the end goal, the management should consider how they actually treat the clients.  Perhaps we could work on keeping the average client happy rather than constantly trying to get new clients.
pros: The compensation package is competitive with other national wire houses.
cons: Training for new brokers only focuses on selling, there is no consideration for teaching new employees the science of managing money.

advice: have an aswer for what is going on within the company and dont stay behind your desk and hide.  active communication and proactive resources.
pros: the benefits (medical, dental, life insurance) were a great part of working there.  I came to find that out after I left.
cons: the breakdowns between business groups provided no incentives for another group to service your client.  i.e. sending my referral to the mortgage group for a client refinancing, it would take extra effort to get them to help out in a timely fashion.

summary: Things are moving in the wrong direction
advice: Value your employees based on the quality of their work, not your perception.  Also, involving people in decision making will help the organization move in the right direction.
pros: I like my peers that I work with and the location of my current job.  They allow you to work remote and are flexible when it comes to work/ personal life balance.
cons: Things seem to be moving in the wrong direction.  There's a lot of bureaucracy in the organization and perceptions are more important than reality.

advice:
- Clear up compensation disparities 
- Treat people based on their work not on their networking skills
pros:
- Lots of opportunities for personal and professional growth
- Lots of resources and training opportunities
- Management listens to ideas from employees to drive business forward
- Top Notch employees
- Lots of opportunities for career mobility
cons:
- Compensation is very disparate: two people doing exactly same job completely different compensation
- Review guidelines very vague
-Top performers are not rewarded 
- Promotions are based on frequently on popularity or nepotism and not on merit

advice: Management should take a collections phone call at least once a week to remind them of what their floor agents are doing. They need to be a bit more realistic when they demand things from their subordinates
pros:
*Nice incentive pay if you can pass the QA phone calls and meet a certain % of time spent on the phone per day. 

*Pretty relaxed dress code.
cons:
*Management is out of touch with what it takes to be a collections agent. 

*Constantly talk to angry or upset people all day. 

*Quotas

summary: it has very nice working environment and the opportunity to work globally.
pros: Very good coworkers and the opportunity to work with global teams.
cons: Sometimes, it's hard to balance work and life. Besides the technology used is a little out of dated. For technical guy, you may loss your skill after being here for a long time. A lot of their IT systems are very old..., and it does not have good documents. You would have to figure it out how it works by looking at the code line by line....

advice: spend money on quality people, and retain the ones that provide added benefit.  promote form within
pros: great location, flexible work schedule, great facility including gym.  Work regularly challenges me and makes me think critically.  Work with partners globally.
cons: pay is down, specifically in my region (south east).  my organization has a difficult time promoting from within.  often enforces 'unwritten' standards before employees can be considered for advancement.  many managers do not have time to dedicate to developing their employees

advice: Update training methods to reflect current business practices.
pros: The training schedule is well thought out. I also enjoyed working with people from different branches and positions. It allowed for me to get tips on how to do my job well, as well as what other people will be going through.
cons: Because of training being mixed, some items on training menu may not apply to your position and seem like a waste of time. A lot of the training materials need to be updated as well.

advice: Please show more sympathy for your employees.
pros: Benefits are alright, though health insurance is a bit lacking these days.  There is 401k match, but is it now matched at 4% instead of 6%.  The pay level is alright, but could be higher.
cons: I feel like a little mouse in this gigantic company.  Senior management is hard to get along with, and there's a thick wall between us.  Technology is poor and communication is lacking.  Please downsize this company and improve teamwork.

advice: You do a Voice of the Employee survey every year and you pretend like you are doing something about it, but you are not.  Additionally, you allow for no innovation and discourage creativity.
pros: Large corporation, can sample different types of lending analytics, good technology, work from home available, encourage community giving, great benefits, good place for women generally
cons: Work you to death, Layoff people all the time, disorganized, no collaboration, refuse to recognize subject matter experts, not many opportunities for officers at other sites, analytically unsophisticated.

advice: Really figure out, and not just talk about, learning about your customers and making them loyal. Citi does not leverage all the information about their customers to have a deeper engagement.
pros:
Great work/life balance is really reflected at the company
Very strong efforts to give back to the community
Generous vacation and  personal day policy
cons:
Very hypocritical in documenting processes and procedures yet no one follows them. It is like the wild west.
Lack of transparency on the compensation model, particularly bonuses
Averse to learning best practices from other industries

summary: Prepare quarterly reports for CFO.  Analyze investment summaries and make valuation adjustments.
advice: The management team at Citi is very bright.  They are aware of all the details in every aspect of a deal and strive to make the best out of any corporate action.
pros: Global presence with solid brand name.  Ability to learn from a variety of talented individiuals with a wide range of backgrounds.
cons: It's a very large institution.  Climbing the corporate ladder can be tough.  Sometimes the hierarchy makes it difficult to advance.

advice: Bring more jobs to the United States. The pay is excellent when compared to similar positions at different banks...loved working for the company even though I was recently laid off.
pros: I have worked in two different areas of Citi and both times, I have found them to be very flexible as far as employee/work balance. Good benefits too.
cons: There aren't very many opportunities for advancement within the company outside of the state of New York. Would love to see more domestic jobs instead of international jobs.

advice: Help retain employess by providing proper training and growth opportunities.  There are huge inconsistencies in the way referral credit is given between branches.
pros:
Employees receive great benefits as soon as you begin working.  Salary for teller, banker is better than other banks. Most people are fun to work with.
- stable bank
- decent training
cons: Managers will choose to hire from outside over training someone that wants to advance from within.  Expect employess to use scripted "signature" lines with customers that are totally un-natural and robotic.

advice: Leave politics to those in Washington; focus on rebuilding the firm into a single integrated company rather than many fiefdoms. Make profits, pay people more.
pros: Large firm, impressive history, good benefits and lots of challenges (read: opportunities for those that want to tackle major challenges).
cons: Large firm, bleak future and lots of internal challenges that management does not want to address directly.  It's a cult of personality - within each division - so hard to feel like you are working for one company.

summary: Miserable, cant get much worse but senior mgmt strives to make each day worse than the prior one.
advice: I see an undercover boss episode here, mangement has no clue the stress employees are under
pros: Rewards can be good if you are in the top 5%
cons: Not enough time to do what is asked of you, goals are unrealistic, and mgmt tells you every day if you cant do the job, let them know so they can find somebody else to do it. New mgmt philosophy is to manage by fear, produce or else. Rolled out a campaign to focus on improving service scores, then fire all the service managers a few months later- Stay far far away from this company

advice: Promote the employees within your firm who have been there for a long time, instead of handing out titles of to new hire employees.
pros: Management is very flexible, somewhat laid back environment, people are very friendly and willing to help out.
cons: Too BIG, no clear lack of structure...Still have not recover from the financial crisis, still lay-offs, management hardly cares about your year end reviews, Have to be within the "IN" crowd if you want your career to prosper here. Raises & bonuses are an insult to the employees.

advice: Show more support to your sale force that is driving your pay...  Change is hard in this company but without your support it becomes impossible.
pros: Experienced a time in the business where nobody really knew up from down.  Overall career was tough but rewarding.  Not much help from management.....
cons: Company could not adjust to the changing enviroment within the industry.  not really sure how things are now, but eventually my whole division was disolved as we could not remain in the wholesale side of the business.

advice: Ops needs more, better managers and staff.  Seniors need *MUCH* better insight into the quality of their managers.  So many managers are gifted in appearing to do good work while doing as little as possible
pros: You can shoot up the ladder quick--it's a real meritocracy in my area
cons: You have to work very hard and be legitimately meritorious to advance, but you must also be aggressive with lateral movement and networking to find an area that is progressing.  Much stagnation in some departments

advice: Provide better training and support for the sales teams. Need a stronger emphasis on building and deepening relationships, providing great service and true value rather than focusing on new business through promotions and gimmicks.
pros: Great resources, analysis and research available. Great pipelines and unlimited clients to contact. Easy to obtain new business. Lack of organization, process, procedures which hinder sales. Overly complicated.
cons: Too big. Their stated vision is one thing and their actions are a whole different story. The current compensation plan and layout causes too much internal conflict.

summary: A Great Place For A Long Term Position
pros: You have all the opportunity in the world when it comes to working at Citi. The pay is great, the benefits are great, and they have many noncustomer facing positions. The company is very accommodating when there is something you could do to better your working environment to suit your needs.
cons: Most of the positions you will notice are call center based, therefore it seems like you are tied to your desk for your shift. You will do a lot of sitting.

advice: Get over yourself let younger people move up. There are to many people without degrees at the C12 and C13 level. They should retire those folks or let people with degrees jump up to C14
pros: Large Company many opportunities and places you could go.
cons: Very racist undertones at the mid management level. Its very hard to break through past that mid level of C13 if you are a POC. Not the companies fault Citi tries to be inclusive the issue is the management at that level will hold you back.

advice: Build a positive work environment that puts employees well-being first.  A happy and engaged staff is much more likely to help you the managers reach your goals with the company and upper management.  Toxic workplaces kill productivity.
pros:
- Large and reputable financial institution
- Opportunities for advancement
cons:
- Poor Management
- Culture was toxic and it reflected on the team
- Management focused more on appeasing Area Managers than well-being of team
- Policy and processes were too rigid, you felt like a spoke in a wheel

advice: Keep the senior management team stable for a while.  We are losing good talent to our competition.
pros: Mobility, presence in 100 countries, potential for rapid career advancement, commitment of employees to company objectives.  There is a very good Leadership Development program for business grads (undergraduate and MBA)...this will promote quick advancement if you are qualified and provide the opportunity for global travel for each of your rotations, three at 1- year each.
cons: Too many reorganizations, frequent recruiting for key senior positions externally.

summary: Great place to start your career
advice: many mid level managers are either into empire building or it is simply easier to hire their own support. issue in accountability.
pros: It provides  opportunities for global experience, nice if you work in a good team. good brand name, establash contact all over the world/country as employees tend to move on after a few years. Senior management are great speakers,many are good leaders.
cons: can be political; too big. At some point of my career ( after Mexico event), it was run by compliance.

advice: Some managers are extremely incompetent in a leadership role. Nasty attitudes abound. Get ready to be treated like a second class citizen
pros: Good vacation days compared to other entry-level jobs. I got 17 vacation days and 6 sick days.
cons: I worked here for 2 years straight out of college (Ivy League) and was enrolled in one of their analyst programs. This program was misrepresented on college recruitment presentations and made much more glamorous than it actually is. Most of us were placed in positions within the firm that required the intelligence/ability equal to that of the highschool level. You don't need a college degree to do 99% of the mundane work...at least not an ivy league education!

summary: Seems like a nice place to work with oportunities aplenty
advice: Make the end of year assessment more fair. Allow team members the chance of getting a number one rating. ok.
pros: Seems like a nice place to work with opportunities aplenty. I would recommend them to anybody. Although I haven't been there long yet.
cons: Some people say the end of year assessments are unfair as no one gets rating one and ratings two are only available to one member of team despite more than one member potentially deserving a two rating.

advice: Citi should focus on being the best financial services provider in the industry instead of trying to be the largest in the industry. Focus on being the best in class in its core businesses vs trying to be everything to everyone.
pros: Citi makes makes it easier achive worklife balance by allowing non-exempt employees to to work remotely at least parttime, without haveing to complete a flexible work arrangement schedule.
cons: Merit Increases and bonuses at Citi are all but non-existent. Citi does not invest it's employees by best-in class training.

advice: Ethics are still important. unethical, dishonest working environment will not bring up your sales reports and will not improve anything. Upper management most of the time hires on managerial positions rejects from other companies, which brings horrible experience. Stop doing that. Try to promote within.
pros: It used to be a great place to get really solid banking experience. Benefits used to be also very good (not any more).
cons: Unprofessional micromanagement (to the extreme). Company does not care about your work experience, gets rid of all older employees because they can hire someone younger for much less pay. Upper management  (area directors , area managers) only concern about keeping their jobs by reporting overblown sales numbers. No life/work balance.

advice: Don't call people on the phone with a one minute phone call to tell them they are a victim of "Redundancy"...  Very unprofessional...
pros: Ability to work from home is a great plus (if your career allows it). I worked for Citi for 12 years.  Worked for many different IT teams.  Learned a great deal of technical skills.
cons: The pay "stops" at a certain level.  You are lucky if they do not take away a portion of your pay at your annual review.

summary: if you like high speed business, been part of the change  and doing what you like, citi is the place!
advice: continue developing great workers
pros: global company, great opportunities, lot of changes, opportunities to learn form different business and countries, great people, facilities to learn, decision making, opportunities to growth
cons: high speed business! no time to loose, change is the business as usual, and if you dont like been in a world of change this might be a con (i dont have cons because i liked a lot my job!)

advice: Work harder to get your employees to see each other as people, not as something they have to get past to get their work done.
pros: Usually the people are great.  It depends on the department.  The benefits, even for non-employees, are great.  It's a crap shoot.  Sometimes it's great, other times it sucks.
cons: Some of the people are really mean.  They don't care that you're another human being doing your job, they just want what they want and they want it now.

advice: Would be nice to tell potential candidates exactly what they are getting into when getting a job with you.  I was told that it was a customer support job and was later told that customer support is the last thing you should think of and focus on making upsells.  Not everyone is a sales person.
pros: Good money if you like doing sales.
cons: Told that it was customer support.  Then when put on phones, told that it was all sales.

pros: Everyone was very friendly and easy to speak with during the interview process. I will use the experience gathered in future interviews. I would have considered accepting if I had received an offer to Citi for the Technology Leadership Program.
cons: I am not quite sure why I did not receive an offer. I am guessing it was due to the fact that I tried to make my comments concise during the group case interview and that they were probably instead looking for the more dominate speaker position.

summary: Complicated political environment with good pay and a comfortable place to work, with nice amenities.
advice: Think about how you treat people.  If someone works directly for you for 3+ years and you still don't know their wife's name or how many children they have, something is wrong.
pros: Good opportunity for advancement up to middle management level, above manager level, politics and being a member of the right political party becomes more important than skill or experience.
cons: Very political environment.  Some of the Senior Management team have primitive people skills

summary: Difficult place to work for involved parents who care about actually raising their children.
advice: Some working parents are as interested in their children as they are in their careers: please don't make us choose. Try to live up to the awards somehow won for "best place to work", "top 100 best places for working mothers". Seriously? It's not true.
pros: Prestigious, stable (at least in my early yrs 1994-early 2000's).
cons: Matrix environment, reporting to many "bosses", difficult, hard-driving work environment. You can never leave it there, you always have work to do/it never ends.

summary: Great firm to work if you are a MD. Director Ok...VP forget to work there.
pros:
If you find the right group to work with you will be happy. I had the opportunity to work with very talented people but my boss was terrible manager brought from London that did not have a clue how to manage a group.

Health, fitness programs are excellent
cons: Poor management with lack of direction. Pay is one of the worst on the street. Too many directors and Managing Directors only giving orders and doing nothing.

summary: Generally nice people, job pressure not too severe, pay a little below bulge brackets, quite bureaucratic
advice: delegate authority downwards more to front line people; make the firm lean and mean
pros: People are generally nice and helpful; bosses sometimes understanding; personal time allowed; pressure not too hard; extremely international and diverse work environment; chances to work with colleagues overseas; very large and active in most market areas so many opportunities to learn
cons: bureaucratic and slow to get things done, need to escalate a lot to senior management; pay a little below bulge brackets

summary: Don't come work here unless you are part of an IB or CIB team.
advice: Change your management team. The culture is awful.
pros: Good name to have on your resume. Analyst class is fun and filled with intelligent people. The Tribeca office location is great!
cons: They value all of the wrong things: FaceTime, analysts who suck up, and "seniority" regardless if they are actually intelligent or not. I quit in 13 and sadly most of my class who were filled with very intelligent people did as well because of the toxic culture and lack of quality work.

advice: Stop letting people that brown nose and don't work as hard move up over people that take pride in their work and performance.
pros: Benefits are great and the job is fairly easy as long as you have a basic customer service skills. There's also an abundance of departments to choose to work in.
cons: Unless you're willing to stroke egos all day you will see people that do less work than you get promoted before you. You will also notice that people who are "buddies" with management are not hel as accountable as everyone else .

advice: Management is doing a great job
pros: Amazing company to work for, they truly value their employees and provide benefits and perks. If you are a hard worker, have great work ethic, follow company guidelines, you will be successful here.  Has some of the best insurance and paid time off I have ever seen with a company. The managers are incentivised to help you succeed, so career development and mobility is a major theme here.
cons: Having to deal with incompetent employees that make it harder for good employees do their job.

advice: Listen to your employees. We are the people that make the business. If we are unhappy itll show customers will sense it and scores will continue to fall
pros: Insurance Benefits and onsite gym
cons: They keep hiring new Senior Managers that dont listen to their employees. They have no positive direction. We are told just take the call dont educate the reps that are transferring no time for that so basically we are a dumping ground. If a rep doesnt feel like handling a caller they'll just transfer n keep transferring calls which makes for a bad customer experience and a bad experience for the agents who have to take the dumped call and you cant bring that up in meeting in fear of being reprimanded.

advice: Was a broker and got fired by a manager who wasn’t qualified (didn’t obtain series 9&10 after 4-5 years) after she was removed from the position.
pros: Great benefits, they match a percentage for your retirement plan as well. Great way to get you feet wet as they pay for licensing.
cons: Management usually isn’t qualified for the position and instead of getting terminated for not meeting requirements they are moved to manage a different department. Not many opportunities for advancement, many coworkers were in same position 10+ years.

advice: Think of how you are investing on your people, people in general work really hard even with limited resources.  Time for the company to give back.
pros:
Global Brand and Presence
Good Diversity
There is flexibility in the workplace, good for working mothers. You can be secure after coming back from maternity leave. 
There is great opportunity to move to other countries.
cons:
Too much red tape. Everything needs to go through regional approvals. Global mandates don’t necessarily fit the local or in country environment. 
Too much cost cutting, the budget just gets smaller each year.

summary: Diverse in opportunities, poor in consistency
pros:
- Plenty of opportunities to interact with higher management and know more about the business. If you are truly interested in Finance, they will help you make a change from tech to finance roles
- Pay is pretty decent for a new grad
cons:
- People are unhappy that new graduates get paid higher than a lot of employees. Adds to a lot of workplace issues
- Rating standards are very team dependent. In some teams, you hardly have any work while in the others, you need to slog.

summary: good company , but gives feel of service based company instead of product base
advice: be more approachable personally ,
pros: takes care of employee, work from home, female friendly, free ac transport, leaves, club mahindra
cons: poorest coding standards, extremly complicated processess for software downloads, your mailbox is always full with useless mails,indians have to work in usa timings mostly, canteens are placed secludedly and crowded , they hire lot of female employees , but cant digest if she is technically good and logical. sometimes females are typecasted as DIVERSITY ,funny

advice: Root and branch review of management practices, experience and professionalism required in Citi Dublin.
pros: Working with a wide range of people from different cultures.
cons: Staff at lower levels are not treated well. Management accepts a high level of turnover so does not properly invest in staff. This reduces the chances of getting promoted, getting decent pay rises or even bonuses. The hiring process in Citi is also notoriously poor. No interest by management to improve it.. very political as well. Much worse than other companies I worked for. Not good...

summary: Overall great place to work at.
advice: Streamline systems, keep on automating manual tasks as they take away precious time spent on meaningful work.
pros: Big name, great culture, good management, ok salary. You are encouraged to explore opportunities within the company. Flexible working arrangements (not just due to covid).
cons: Overtime is regular. Benefits are below average. Lots of pre-automation manual tasks that take up too much time that could be spent on more meaningful work such as analysis and insight generation. So many systems within the company that don't communicate well with one another.

summary: People are great to work with but firm has trouble keeping its best
advice: empower employees more
pros:
friendly atmosphere - most people are great to work and chat with 
great office locations
decent facilities (gym, health center, good view)
internal mobility made easy 
good benefits - free dinner if you stay late, free admission to museums, discounts, training
cons:
good employees are often incentivized to leave because of strict rules that limit compensation
many different systems interacting with one another but owned by teams that do not work together, hard to figure out what's technically going on

summary: I'm well diverse in the Mortgage Industry of CitiMortgage
advice: Continue to maintain the company core value for the employees and the community.
pros: CitiMortgage is a company whose concern about their consumers and have maintain a good name in the community. I'm former employee currently trying to return my to CitiMortgage. After working for the competitor, I prefer going back to CitiMortgage, they have proven to me to be more professional toward their customers and employees. Which is highly important to me.
cons: I've worked for CitiMortgage for 14 years, there are no downfalls that I'm aware of.

summary: Would have loved to continue further but not granted the opportunity.
advice: Hiring managers need to communicate with employees on better training strategies and not blindsiding employees with temp agency calling to terminate employees.
pros: Great atmosphere. Great coworkers. Great cultural diversity. Great employee benefits.
cons: Should effectively communicate with temp workers on needs and expectations instead of having the hiring temp agency terminate temp workers for unspecified reasons. Temp agency let me go and did not give a really specific reason for termination. While there I noticed a lot of people working for temp agency Ranstad being let go for no real specific reason. I should have known then. Citigroup AML positions are in abundance there but do not expect to kept there for entirety of contract.

advice: Clarification of roles and reduce the cross matrixing
pros: Citi is a global diverse bank.  One could make a career here learning about the many facets of finances, wholesale and retail.    It can be problematic to make a change across the major business lines but within a business line, one could change area of expertise.
cons: Multiple managers create confusing and conflicting priorities.  No clear decision making responsibilities.  The size of the bank and the regulatory oversight required makes any changes to product or customer service very difficult.

advice: Promote a culture of collaboration rather than a culture of competition. Competition makes hard to build good teams and destroy the few good teams.
pros: Worldwide presence in the corporate business. Moderately easy to switch jobs. Good culture. Depending on the position work and manager easy to ask for remote work.
cons: A lot of groupthink and bureaucracy (the devil's advocate is the bad guy). Bad current senior management (they dismantled an awesome team of senior leaders). A lot of teams with few people. Difficult to move up the ladder.

advice: Get rid of the dead weight and not the great employees. HR needs to get on the ball with open postings for those that have applied that were laid off. To wait 2 months and never hear anything is so disappointing.
pros: Great co-workers and benefits.
cons: Corporate America BS: Several lay offs where great employees were let go while the dead weight still has a job. To satisfy the US Government, must keep a diverse culture so great employees with strong work ethic and quality work get let go.

summary: Good salary, poor employee retention policy at Universal Banker Level
advice: Management needs to work on employee retention of people joining at CB, CC grade
pros: - High Salary & Incentives
cons:
- Dull working environment - no celebration during any festival
- Poor employee retention policies at Universal Banker level. Higher & fire situation at U.B. level. Every 6 months the entire U.B team changes. A very few people are able to survive at U.B role.
- Very limited job roles if you are able to reach the Q grade which is above Universal Banker role.

summary: I have been working in IT at Citi for over 5 years.
advice: Compensation needs to change. Employees who are not productive are not reprimanded and this is terrible for the people who actually care.
pros: The work-life balance has been great, the teams are generally a lot of fun.
cons: The compensation is terrible. In 5 years there have been minimum to no increases as a top rated employee I have only received an increase of 4 percent with a bonus of 4 percent. Being an dedicated employee who is underpaid this is very fustrating.

advice: Lack of consistency in senior leaders and management styles. Lack of dedication to employee retention. Main objectives are to outsource whatever can be outsourced and reduce costs. No thought given to long term impact of cost cutting exercises.
pros: Dynamic ever changing company,  recognized name.  Good place to gain banking experience.  Flex time,. 401k, gym. Large complex organization that challenges.
cons: Constant changing direction and changing management teams.  plans are put in place and repeatedly  changed before objectives can be meet.

summary: Good benefits, Bad career growth, ugly politics
advice: Please focus on investing in talent at all levels. Eliminate MD / D levels that promote local heroics over talent management.
pros: Good for junior staff starting out a career looking for experience in a global bank.  Citi is a recognized brand with a fantastic network globally. If you are flexible and willing to relocate to different parts of the world on projects, citi offers the opportunity to explore, learn and decide your career interests
cons: Watch out for the internal politics. It can really slow down your growth , limit your potential and hurt delivery if you are not on an "visible" project. Decisions are purely driven by cost, managed by an absolutely ridiculous budget process

advice: With the fast pace of technology growth, Citi needs to keep up with the technology trends. Citi's entry into Apple iOS is a very positive move.
pros: Citi has a fantastic work culture. Citi is fortunate to have great team players. Citi offers wonderful training opportunities for soft and hard skill growth.
cons: With Citi's global reach, it works 24x7. Not a bad scenario as people think as Citi has great talented workforce.

advice: continue to support your teams of people, as they are the backbone to your department and continue to encourage them to better themselves everyday
pros: An excellent work environment, man ways to lean and grow and freely move around the corporation, encouragement from managers to reach for the stars and live up to your potential
cons: the banking industry has its flexible moments and there have been many layoffs especially in the default department, however there is the options to move to other departments to continue a working relationship

advice: No real advice here.  It's always dependent on your manager and the person at the level above that.  As we all know, sometimes it's hard to meet all the expectation of our managers, and sometimes it's nearly impossible.
pros: Large company and it's easy to move from one department to another, and lots of opportunities for advancement. Very formal evaluation.
cons: It's a large company and it's easy to move from one department to another.  Sometimes I think that's how incompetent employess manage to hide there.

summary: Generally good but have execution issues
pros: Focus on the right areas for innovation and process improvement.  Global company with global mind.  It is a good company in general to build career with global network.
cons: Meritocracy not well followed and improvement in transparency in performance evaluations.  Inner politics and self promoting interest overrides sometimes.  Policy execution not well followed - esp for the regions outside the US.  Accountability is often not clear to management and often not viewed as one company due to finger pointing between functions/departments.

advice: Dont push your top performers until they collapse. Ask questions and learn what your team does well and cultivate that talent. Dont be afraid to lose top talent or stifle their opportunities to move elsewhere
pros: They are organized and there are often additional opportunities to transition out of your current role.
cons: Management roles are tough to get into and they do not increase salary that much which you transfer from within the company to another role even when you add additional and substantively higher education levels.

summary: Great place to start, hard to stay
advice: continue to develop the newer employees but hire a smaller number so that your investment in their development can stay within the company for the small number of promotion positions
pros: collaborative culture, holds employees to high standards but is willing to offer the help that younger employees need in order to learn, competitive compensation
cons: somewhat low job security, not a ton of room for promotions - many entry level employees are hired to work for the relatively small amount of senior employees

advice: Add slack to expectations of employees as so much of the job is out of the control of the representative.
pros: I liked the opportunity to get started in finance as a career opportunity and to test the waters there. Benefits are good to great and the office is fairly comfortable for a call center.
cons: Unrealistic metrics and expectations, confusing and constantly changing legal regulations and Citibank rules. Difficult and depressing work, dealing with death, misfortune, illness, and the like all day every day. Typical call center grayness.

advice: Support analysts and associates more, bring them into the process. Encourage junior personnel to pursue international opportunities. Continue to work on efficiency on process.
pros: Hardworking, talented group. Senior executives really took care to help junior employees. Hours were not obscene for banking. Plenty of support when it came time to look for opportunities after two-year banking program.
cons: Typical banking complaints - long hours, inefficient process. Very large company, can get lost in the bureaucracy at times.  Could do more to help employees move between global offices.

advice: You do you, boo. Never change.
pros: If you're clever and politically savvy, you can get a sweet cushy gig that can last a lifetime!
