cons: I worked here for many years and was told by various managers, in different departments, don't rock the boat.  This place is so resistant to change that they make a big announcement every year about how this is going to be the year they change.  They are constantly downsizing.  Every promotion is an opportunity to get RIF'ed.

advice: When trying to migrate and automate away people's jobs, help them retrain and find a strategy to keep the best and the brightest there.
pros: Citi will invest loads in you. There's frequent training sessions, and you are likely to get more responsibility fast, be put in front of senior management, clients and others as a junior person if you have the right attitude. Endorses and participates charities.
cons: Work life balance. Extremely busy. Can get chaotic with several departmental initiatives all at once. Risk of being replaced by a robot.

summary: One of the best places to work
advice: Keep up the good work.
pros: This is one of the best places to learn about banking and financial industry.  The company has inculcated a great culture of sharing information amongst its rank and file.  People are always ready to help.   Plus, being global organization helps if you would want to relocate and take on new challenges.
cons: I found too much of outsourcing of technology and processing to third party companies, perhaps raising risks for the company.

pros:
Offers great health, dental, 401k, and maternity benefits
good way to get back in to the work force
plenty of time off including discretionary time (sick time) and vacation time
full time permanent work
cons:
Worked on the phone the entire shift
consistently pressured for high sales, and low call time despite customer needs
logging of all time off of the phone, such as bathroom breaks, etc
management seemed unable to find creative ways to meet the needs of their employees
transferring between departments was extremely difficult unless a good rapport with upper management is established

summary: bureaucracy, bullying, poor communication, outsourcing around the corner across the board.
advice: none - they aint listening, theyre living in the same culture even at higher levels, so take action based on fear, so dont blame them for just playing the game.
pros: good name on cv,,,,if the person has no experience of company.
cons:
Incessant buzzwords in all internal communications, pay freeze for last 3 years, benefit cuts announced three days after annual employee survey, (classy!), 
oh, and you'll learn more about what the company are doing through the press than within teh actual company.

summary: Good place to be with lots of young people but a rather poor pay
advice: Try to identify what are the real talents of your employees and put them to good purpuse. It seems like a waste for a guy with perfect arabic to be working for a team that does not have any contact with that language, or for a girl with a good law degree and experience to be an AML analyst.
pros: great office culture and international environment as well as useful perks
cons: chaotic management and poor pay

summary: The job itself was not too horrible, but the company shows almost no signs of care for tenured employees.
advice: Pay senior members of staff more than new hires. Turnover rates are very high and taking care of existing employees would solve that problem and boost stats.
pros: Retirement and benefits package are very competitive. On site cafeteria is a nice perk as well.
cons: Pay and retention policies leave much to be desired. I found out that a new hire with no experience was making significantly more than a multi year tenured rep.

summary: Great environment, good benefits, the people are great
advice: In corporate positions the life work balance is great. Citi offers great benefits.
pros: love the people who worked in my dept in back office, management is friendly and understanding, you still have a life at home, dress code is chill.
cons: Hard to move up with company, system they use sucks, no one really knows actual procedures so we set ourselves up for failure. No one is fully trained on a poaition. Management recently changed and def made some great changes for better so far.

advice: Take advantage of the large network and make sure you look out for your group and employees. The best bosses are the ones who make sure their employees get promoted and get plenty of exposure in the large web of Citi.
pros: Exposure to some of the largest transactions around the world with all the household company names you are used to hearing. Large company with plenty of professional options.
cons: Large environment that creates an unnecessary amount of bureaucracy. Not the best paid employees and sometimes not the best talent in the industry.

advice: Training felt rushed, was told that it would be 4 weeks of training and it turned out to be only 2 weeks!! So lots of your daily duties won't be explained until you're on the production floor which can be overwhelming
pros: Lots of ot availability, shift differentials of 10%, weekend differential of 20%, so good money if you work weekends and after 5pm
cons: This is a call center so lots of customer interactions over the phone, some customers can be very rude and so that does start to wear you down

advice: Take more consideration into the people you hire and the ones you dismiss. The person giving the interview should not talk more than the prospective employee.
pros: the interviewee was nice and the building seemed nice also
cons: During the interview asked long winded questions and seemed to  only be looking for specific answers and act as though they had not even looked over my resume before asking me questions. I was qualified but got a no the job has 9 weeks of training so whatever i didnt know I would have learned.

advice: Work on retaining younger talent, focus efforts on improving tech infrastructure and adopting new technology. Many director level employees; reduce that number to help promote younger staff and create opportunities
pros:
Great great people, flexible taking time off, better culture than most banks
Good career track, good feedback from management and good mentorship, Pay is higher than peers
cons: Tech systems can be very cumbersome and inefficient. lot of beaurocracy and having to play political games to manage career. too many cooks in the kitchen and staff should be reduced.

advice: Interview all management level and get their honest feedback without intimidation or fear,  The will provide you with their honest feedback and you will an all round perspective on how to become best in class.  It's not one person statement that changes a company. Try it and you will see.
pros: The company international exposure and helping and developing communities
cons: The quality of line management / leadership needs to be addressed quickly.  Delivering exceptional customer service and becoming best in class, they need to go back to basics They have to many hidden Gems and talent and line management do BAD JOB of managing that Senior Leaders do not know how these individuals can help them transform their company.

summary: It's a great Institution to work for, but the several Management make employees workplace hard and stressful.
advice: Treat all employees with respect and equally.  Make the goals more realistic and they most find source of referrals for the whole Team not to an particular group only.
pros: Good benefits, decent salaries and commission.  Comfortable offices/cubes; Diversity: people from many countries.
cons: Unfair Management. Opportunities of business and growth are for their selected people.  Constantly changing Management and so are  the goals, which are not only high but difficult to accomplish.

summary: Challenging Work in a Global Company
pros: Benefits are generous and the work can be challenging. Flexible work schedules allow me to work from home frequently where I am more productive. The culture can be positive but I have learned that the work culture is very dependent on the site where you work and your immediate team. Each location has a different culture and work-life balance.
cons: Working across the globe means a lot of phone meetings at odd hours. There are very few in-person meetings, which can make building relationships difficult.

advice: Take off the blinders and see the talent around before they migrate to other company
pros: Good benefits laid back management equipment is fairly new good location good vacation and sick time available availability to flex time off on site gym and on site cafeteria also on site banking services company sponsor vendors with especial prizing and offers divers culture and good networking options as well as volunteering
cons: Management lack vision and doesn't recognize internal talent production floor it's hectic upper management lack touch with production cut throat business

summary: Good place to start your career
advice: Try to compensate your best employees similar to your competitors if you would not like to loose them.
pros:
I am working in a great team, with exceptional and easily accessible managers.
You can learn a lot during your job.
Tasks are allocated based on ability and skills.
You can participate in many different projects from early on.
cons:
The compensation package is less generous compared to the competition.
No support for external education, few on site training.
Long hours compared to back office (especially at month end).
High fluctuation of employees.

advice: Bring back the bonus structure or the annual pay increase based on merit.
pros: 3 recruiters called me from Citi, 2 for AML position and 3rd was for trade settlement. - I ended up with Latin America trade settlement. Benefits are great. The tuition reimbursement is great and there are the financial courses that the company offers for free. You can move around to other locations where the company is found.
cons: Pay is a bit low for the industry. It can be hard to move up the ladder.

pros: The work life balance can be good in some groups, but not all. Overall, great place to start a career build a good reputation and then move around. Started as a BA and promoted to svp through several strategic career moves within the firm. Benefits are good, and with the right team, you can have a very supportive and engaging team to work with
cons: Very bureaucratic and s[low moving. programs take a long time to move through, with lots of layers to move through

advice: Performance review process needs to be more transparent.  It should not be possible get excellent employee ratings with minimal to no reward for it.  Process should more closely reflect performance/reward and be clearly outlined to all employees.  Current process allows for greater reward at lower ratings, which can be very disheartening to workers.
pros: Solid benefits (401k match on 6%, cheap healthcare plans available, flexible work schedules)
cons: Low pay, highly political environment.  Very hard for outsiders to thrive despite skill and expertise in the field.

summary: Decent place to work with good work life balance.
advice: Have a better hiring and training process.
pros: Time off and benefits are good.  Pay is ok. Performance incentives are rewarding.  There is also a good focus on recognition and culture.  The company has also been successful in recent times.
cons: The company has not shown itself to be very progressive in relation to other comparable businesses.  Training and promotion of qualified individuals is very sub par.  Talent is not easily recognized by upper management and not well developed.

advice: Be fair to your employees, be honest.  Making an employee pay out of pocket for parking and travel expenses as a low paid teller is ridiculous.  Stop the constant transferring.   A lot of company and labor violations that the hr department does nothing about.
pros: Corporate jobs are fairly nice, benefits are excellent
cons: Treated like a dog in the retail branch. No room for growth, poor pay and watch out for travel expenses that company makes you pay out of pocket. Unfair policies and practices.

advice: lack of vision and understanding of where Citi is heading relative to the mortgage business and where this fits in for the company as a whole.  no operations support
pros: flexibility in work schedule when needed, however nobody does your work when you're gone.  decent money but that changes like everything else there pretty often.
cons: lack of vision and understanding of where Citi is heading relative to the mortgage business and where this fits in for the company as a whole.  no operations support

advice: Keep focusing on the customer.  Make courageous choices for long term success. Leaders should check their egos at the door and focus on the greater good.
pros:
Great People who want to do the right thing
Opportunity for advancement
Global with a strong brand and legacy
Always evolving and changing
A new leader and team with a strong focus on the customer
cons:
Too Big to steer
People often work in silos
Under invested in technology
Talk about a customer focus at a Senior level but business actions are strictly sales and revenue oriented

summary: Citigroup treating its employees like the US economy---grinding their bones to make its bread.
advice: Not inclined to offer any because I didn't seem to make a difference before.  The word is out though Expect an exodus when the economy changes if things there don't.
pros: health, dental, 401k, educational reimbursment, on site child care, shifts, decent severance packages---icing on the cake of getting laid off which was actually a good thing
cons: Really, really bad corporate culture.  Good people get hired but don't stay long.  Unfriendly, not open to change, poor communication, punitive.  Very far behind the curve in systems and business practices.  Just not a nice place to work as evidenced by the look on the employees' faces.

summary: My team is unique in it's support of each other, however overall it's a dog eat dog world.
advice: Consider what is best for your team as opposed to just being a "Yes Man".  You'll create a large pool of supporters as opposed to burning the candle at both ends. Sr Management will never be satisfied.
pros: They gave me an opportunity based on faith and have provided me with full benefits and a more than fair salary.
cons: Senior management is out of touch and incompetent.

advice: Communicate clear mission and goals.
pros: Current technology and product introduction, many opportunities to develop if you are self motivated and highly driven. Committed to diversity and provides a rich environment. Very involved in communities.
cons: Workload is excessive and relentless, uncoordinated, fast moving changes do not consistently provide a place for people to do their best, take risk and to feel successful.  Forced ranking environment breeds competitveness, not for the weak of heart. Depends on what location and what department you work in

advice: Have an more clear and transparent work culture .Citi produces one of the best managers which unfortunately learn all the wrong this and move this to the new bank where they join. More clatiy of job profile, expectations and a more transparent work culture on promotions and appraisal will help your company retains its best talent of pool..
pros:
Good brand to be associated with
Salay as per market standard
cons:
Too much of policitics
Lack of oganised /clarity on roles & responsibility .
You are expected to be a jack of all trades

advice: There are few real leaders, the rest are people that have been doing that job just because!  Time! Or relationship!
pros: Good for working virtual but careful the location and the level you post to, you will find surprises in leadership.
cons: Not very good, the principles and value that the company states are not solid nor remind to employees, so it creates a jungle fight inside. There is too much diversity in the organization professionally speaking, too many people with so different backgrounds and expectations.

advice: Give clearer direction about the future of the company/business lines. Make changes faster instread of dragging them out for months.
pros: Global, used to have lots of opportunities to travel/live/work abroad (not so much anymore due to expense concerns), diverse and interesting culture
cons: Middle management (business line heads) are weak and don't inspire confidence in the future of the company. Too much focus on expense cutting without any real strategy around how to acheive the desired margins. Too much uncertainty and no clear direction for the future.

advice: In the absence of major changes in procedures, I think upper management has it about right - they cannot improve the job much, so great benefits are what can be offered.
pros: Great benefits - health insurance, plenty of vacation and sick leave from day one. Flexible schedules depending on the position. Used to have great tuition reimbursement, not sure now.
cons: Great benefits are to offset the "corporate hamster wheel" day to day experience. Managers treated employees like children - small "rewards", contests etc... A monotonous clock-watching job.

summary: Citibank is similar to a roller coaster ride
advice: I know the saying "the customer is always right" but sometimes they are not, sometimes managers must think about protecting their employees instead of just satisfying the customer
pros: I have met some great people while working for Citibank and have built some great friendships.
cons: We have our good days but we have tons of bad days. These bad days are filled with dealing with clients who are very disrespectful and in many cases we have to sit there and take it.

summary: Good place to start your career
pros: Great training, supportive community, good opportunities to move around within the firm, international exposure. Citi's a great place to start your career and learn the basics for how to do business as an international financial services firm.
cons: Professional development opportunities can be limited, it can be easy to get lost in such a large firm. Promotions can be very political so it's easy to get stuck in a particular role without having too much ability to propel your career forward. Compensation is okay.

advice: They don't care.
pros: Good cafeteria, good benefits, mostly friendly coworkers, lots of employee appreciation events,
cons: Typical corporate good old boy network. If you are a parent and don't have anyone to take your child when they are sick, forgeot about raises or promotions unless you are willing to sleep with someone. Changes are made regularly for the sake of change. People are promoted based on looks and flirting and kissing butt. Bonus structure is impossible. Employees monitored by five different teams. Nothing you do is good enough.

advice: The entire firm needs a management shakeup
pros: Paycheck to pay your bills... really nothing more
cons:
Too many to list, it is the worst firm I've ever worked for. Working there were the worst days of my life!
To list some problems and I mean some, because listing all cons will requires a book:
1. Toxic culture with no values or respect
2. A joke unqualified HR
3. Managers were selected and promoted based on the degree of social psychopathy 
4. Too many managers, more managers than employees (mostly in New York)
5. Disconnected from the business and management in New York
6. Office was calling centre crowded with no space to move
7. Hiring and promotion decisions based on the origins/race not qualifications

pros:
Great training programs for young talent

Mobility is encouraged and made easier by the global platform; also a philosophy that once they recruit someone, they would like to keep you

Impressive progression out of the financial crisis
cons:
Political and fragmented due to the mere size of the organization. Therefore individual experiences can vary a great deal, depending on who your most direct manager(s) are.

Management has ambitious goals, which is great. However, execution is lacking.

Laid back environment  encourages lack of professionalism at times

advice: People are not credit cards there are differences.
pros: You are not unemployed.  Your paycheck will not bounce.  The company will be there tomorrow giving you plenty of time while employed to evaluate several job offers before you thank them for the opportunity and quit.
cons: You are employed by Citibank  Citibank is a credit card company not a bank they are cold and plastic just like a credit card.  Quotas are unreachable.  Sell Sell Sell or your Fired Fired Fried

summary: Ok to obtain experience but tough to stay for the long haul.
advice: You are overworked because you do not hire enough resources. Change that culture and make it a place that people WANT to stay in for the long haul. This way you won't lose all of your talent through a revolving door every twelve months.
pros: Big Bank and you gain a lot of varied experience. Great resume builder.
cons: Always sings the blues around raise and bonus time. Employees that are overloaded and working 15 hours days are very common.

advice: Keep a focus on ethics and responsible finance. Be more Googlish with the overall culture - cooler working environment, healthier meals available in the canteen.
pros: Good opportunity to progress. Multiple business types means you can branch out into many directions. Good career mobility both domestically and internationally.
cons: Very big - can be difficult to get things done. A lot of focus on networking and getting your name out there in order to progress which can be a disadvantage for the more introverted person.

summary: Senior Vice President Operations Technology Risk Management
advice: Don't try to reinvent an employee's skill set to "fit" a particular project the employee was not originally hired to do.
pros: Worked from home 4 days per week.  Interesting work in Operations and Technology group which handles and resolves issues from examinations by various regulatory agencies such as the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) and other governmental agencies.
cons: Management was lacking with respect to fairly evaluating employee's responsibilities and skill set.

advice: It seems that the best thing at the moment is to get more organized to avoid bureaucracy caused from the volume of the organization and get renovated.
pros: Globally, there are  many opportunities to grow with high mobility within the same department or in different ones. As Citi is a huge company you get the chance to get to know a little bit of everything.
cons: Sometimes the bureaucracy can make things complicated but in the end everything seems to find its way. Insisting and escalating is the key.

advice: Listen to your employees-I presented solid numbers showing the increasing amount of work that had very tight deadlines with less workers to get it done.
pros: Great benefits! Very accommodating to work from home as well
cons: Poor management. We were overworked and continued to have work shoved at us even though we didn't have the bandwidth to cover at all. After our numbers doubled yet we still had no new highers i presented this to senior management only to be shut down. The hours were long!

advice: NIL
pros:
Fair compensation
Managers are friendly and approachable
Big companies that allow you to work with colleagues overseas
Culture varies from teams, some teams are really nice, and some are not. I believe this is similar in other companies
cons:
Hard to learn about the business as significant portion of learnings come from on-the-job training and seniors are usually too busy with issue resolution to teach

Outdated documentations make it hard to learn for new joiners

Some teams work very long hours. Again this depends on your luck on which team you join.

advice: Listen to your employees and expect more not only from your Staff but start from yourself. Stop the toxic blaming culture.
pros: Good salary and financial benefits. Competent team members, supporting and cooperative.
cons: Complete chaos, lack of flexibility and consideration for employees' needs. They do not listen to employees, just impose rules and if they do not work in practice, then blame Staff. Weak regional leadership, focused on their own career progression and scared to share any concerns or suggestions with the senior leadership in the US. Terrible work-life balance.

summary: A good place to work in tough times
advice: Link executive compensation to the long term success (or failure) of the company.
pros: The firm is number 1 or 2 in most of the businesses in which it operates, giving its employees access to the most sophisticated clients,significant deal flow and unmatched internal resources.
cons: The downsides are well publicized: a behemoth of 250,000 people sometimes uncoordinated, sometime competing against each other, and (so far) lacking the internal risk control necessary to keep our heads above water when things get tough.

summary: $20 billion bailout & you still laid off 50,000 people?
advice: Don't forget about the people who work for you.
pros: Global reach. Best resources and the best people. Smart, motivated, and driven. People from all over the world you can tap into and gain knowledge from. The learning was quite good. I was in marketing and I learned more there than any other place I worked before. They know how to market well.
cons: They put no value on people. Get the work done and increase shareholder value. I tried to find a place in the company where they valued people and was told by HR that Citigroup is not the place to work if this is what I am looking for.

summary: A great entry level job with a decent wage
pros: Citi treats its employees really well. The structure is great with teams, management, and the escalation team. When help is needed, it's literally a quick phone call away. Good PTO, GREAT benefits, 401k matching, onsite gym and cafeteria, discounts, etc.
cons:
It's a call center. That work can just be very draining. But I recommend the SPG portfolio; the customer base seems a bit kinder. 

Schedule changes can be hard to come by, so make sure you're ok with what you're hired for.

advice: Before hiring someone and telling them they have the ability to move up let them know that the move up is only for Tellers to become bankers or for bankers to become managers it isnt for bankers to move to other tiers.
pros: Pay is higher compared to other banks in the area. Many locations to choose from in DC Metro Area and flexible management
cons: No upward mobility available other than to management positions. No ability for freedom of thought. Everything is very regulated and the bottom line isnt considered.

advice: This company needs to avoid always being involved or at the center of every financial crisis or class action lawsuit. Need to minimize the number of restructurings that increase job insecurity among your workforce.
pros: Excellent health and dental benefits and a decent 401K plan that includes a company match up to 3% of your salary. Dynamic work environment is constantly changing.
cons: This company is always under scrutiny by the regulators and always seems to be at the center of any financial crisis or class action lawsuit.

advice: Please try to implement atleast a portion of what is said in big town halls ..
pros: Management respects the employees ... Good multicultural environment  ...decent progress opportunities (depending on which team / division you are working in  ) ....
cons: Hardwork may be appreciated in words , however not necessarily through monetry benefits ...Prospects for financial progression are quite bleak ...Employee retention is not at all a top priority for the firm .... Work processes are not best at all and can be fustrating at times .....

advice: Management did as best a job they could considering the vastness of the company. I always felt like there was someone I could turn to for help without being ridiculed.
pros: Plenty of upward potential. Large company with many departments that promotes mobility in the workplace and encourages community involvement and interaction with coworkers.
cons: Citibank is spread out throughout the country. Often times you will be working with someone on a day to day basis and never meet them in person.

summary: I was fortunate to have senior management who did take an active interest in my current role and professional growth.
advice: Continue to set an example to its employees and the world that Citigroup is and shall continue to be a better than average place to work.
pros: Overall compensation package potential, career growth and flexible work schedule.  It helped that I worked with senior managers who supported me in my endeavors and were unafraid in providing constructive criticism.
cons: Lacking good coaching from and interaction with my direct supervisor.

advice: Managers should know in and out about the business. Manager's lack of knowledge on products and procedures were so frustrating.
pros: If you got skills in making friends in high places, this company will let you move up fast. If you are a good sales person, you can get great support from the management.
cons: It is all about sales, granted that I signed up for a Personal banker (Sales) position. The business is all about selling the products, not selling the "right" products for the customers.

advice: Managers were getting fired left and right. Terrible public reputation made it hard for customers to trust employees
pros: Wonderful benefits as far as health insurance benefits, 401k and time off.  Most generous company with flexibility of schedule at least when you had flex time.  Before they closed the site location there were lots of events always going on each week and a good atmosphere for the most part.  When it was all moved to work at home everyone changed and it got really tense
cons: No opportunities for advancement and high turnover rate.  Customers of course were extremely rude and difficult to deal with.  Pay was very average around $12-$13 an hour and opportunity to bonus each month.

summary: Citibank good company to work for, but can be better.
advice:
-Take into consideration that the retail bank is bringing in all your revenue, that means tellers should be paid more since we have more responsibilities on the job
-Bring the benefits back, that means more sick days and cheaper cost for health insurance
pros:
-Friendly working environment
-Flexible hours 
-Management treats subordinates with respect
cons:
-Not enough vacation days
-Not enough sick days
-Salary not too attractive
-Goals to receive a bonus are too high
-Limited advancement opportunities
-Benefits are cut to the minimum from previous years

summary: If you're looking for a real family friendly career, look elsewhere.
advice: If someone comes to you with issues regarding family or time off be more helpful and offer more options than "push time around". That's not an option for everyone and emergency time runs out too quickly on smaller teams.
pros: Paid time off, reasonable work environment, entry level positions with room for growth, decent starting pay.
cons: Never guaranteed that you will have a job or have a friendly environment, more so than other businesses. Lots of favoritism.

summary: Peers are great, performance review process bad
advice: Trust who you have hired to do the right thing.  Guide them as they learn rather than punish and micro manage projects.
pros: Some of the best reasons to work at Citigroup are the benefits, the peers you work with on a daily basis and the flexible work environment.
cons: Citigroup uses the Forced Ranking process to conduct year end performance reviews.  If you work with a high performing group of professionals, this can be very demoralizing and counterintuitive to getting good performance.

advice: Treat your employees fairly. Senior management bring back recognition and company events. Raises need to be reevaluated to compete with area call centers to retain talent.
pros: Health insurance is great even though it keeps  getting more expensive year after year. 401 K Match is great as well.
cons: Call Center Associate.....poor senior management. If your not in with the cool group then your a nobody. Not competitive salary wise with the other call centers in the area but expected to do twice the work with minimal training. Cant approach management because they gossip like high schoolers. Poor recognition and lack of empathy from the top/down. Senior Management needs adequate training in the areas they are responsible for.

advice: Upgrade computers as they are starting to show their age.
pros: I was reached out to by a Citi recruiter who sent my resume to the Branch Manager where i currently work. From that email to my hiring was about a month. Thorough background check. Very fair compensation in line with that I made in the best even with no banking experience.
cons: If i had to nitpick it would be that their NYC training center distance is far for some. But its only a 1 day orientation for tellers.

pros: None to report at this time
cons: We need a better system in place when helping our customers. I had a call today with a customer who has been with us for over 7 years. Her account was blocked do to our error and I had to advise her we could not remove the block even though the reason her account was in the negative was our error.  I advised her to call back once her direct deposit hits and we can remove the block. I felt bad because this block should not been put on in the first place.  If I was management I would start a class on better customer service and how to meet customers needs.

pros: Citi has more of a heart than most of the big banks. Knowing other analysts in investment banking at other banks, I genuinely felt that my managers at all levels took a greater interest in me than managers do in their subordinates at most other banks.
cons: Citi is a big, slow, and bureaucratic organization. Even nearly a decade after the fact, it has PTSD at an institutional level from the financial crisis and has an aversion to taking risk in many places. This should not come as a surprise.

summary: Best Premiere Banking Program where I have worked
advice: Continue to improve technology and systems. Love the new contact mgmt. software that was rolled out in 2018. More branches in Washington DC area.
pros: Best Big Bank Premier banking program I have worked in. There is structure, but lots of autonomy. My boss encourages me to think like it's my business..he calls it "my shop".  We really cater to a very affluent and wealthy clientele.
cons: RMs must complete all work during branch work hours-- We can't work from home ever. Systems

summary: Use as a launching board to go elsewhere...
advice: Look at your C16 and higher levels.   They need to worry about their employees versus their own careers and own self worth.
pros: - Good benefits and 401K Match
cons:
- Long Hours and workload 
- Executive and Senior Leadership is out of touch with reality.   No support and lack of transparency.
- Employees are constant in fear of layoffs
- Until you leave you think it is normal how you are treated.    There is a wonderful life outside of Citi so use your time there to gain as much knowledge and experience you can and use it to find a great company.    Wish I had left earlier.

advice: Too many regimes to comment
pros: Multinational corporation; selling its International pieces
cons:
It can't decide what it wants to be...it has changed it business model 5 times in as many years. Lacks identity
Internal propaganda is inconsistent with the reality (specifically as it relates to customer service)
Want to eliminate people interaction and be the google of banks (people want people handling there money) 
Too many internal competing agendas
The mantra is you get experience laterally not through upward mobility
No pay increases if you take a lateral role (unless you know the system)

advice: Communicate better with Bankers, not only on sales needed and to make calls but on recognizing performance. Citimax needs to be reworked and made more clear to avoid last monute suprises.
pros: Good management, office hours are 9-5 M-F and some locations S 10-2. Pay is ok and there is potential to make great commission when not capped.
cons: Little compensation for Mortgages, commission is capped, underwriting process could be vastly improved. POLITICS. Too many changes happening at once, with digitalization, to KDS, to Account opening procedures, systems being updated.

summary: Being a Team Favorite Is A Must to Be Happy
advice: Train OS in team building. People who are on the phones more and socializing less get ignored for special projects. Managers could care less about your other talents,  just want uou glued to the phones and getting high quality scores. The same people get chosen for special projects over and over, even ones who barely show up for work or have low adherence
pros: Close to home, great benefits
cons: Too much favoritism for slackers who run in social circles

advice: The leadership and management needs an overhaul.
pros:
Generous leave policies
Good work life balance with ample work from homes
cons:
Need to use personal computers while working from home
Job description usually changes significantly between the interview and joining phase. The change in role is not communicated before joining.
Office is located in the outskirts of the city. Travel times can be huge, no good place to have lunch around unless you bring from home
There is not enough desks to accommodate all people.
Senior management is biased towards good-looking female employees.

summary: Nice culture and exposure to different business units
pros: The quantitative analyst program is a two-year rotation program which would enable you to work in different business units either in trading, quant, research, structuring or even sales. It's a good platform for people who are still not quite clear about long term career path yet and want to have exposure to different roles
cons: The company culture is a bit laid-back compared with other bulge brackets. The longer you stay here, the more you can feel about what I am saying.

advice: None. Due to the industry management procedures are standard all across the board so there is not much wiggle room.
pros: The pay and hours are steady. If you are looking part time job with strict, predictable hours than this is the place for you.
cons: You are almost trapped behind the teller line unable to move for large portions of time. You also have multiple cameras pointed at you at all times. If you like walking around or stretching your legs this is not the job for you.

summary: Tampa site is a second class site in a state of decline. No long term opportunities
advice: Stop getting in the way of productivity.
pros: Used to be a great place to work. Morale and productivity have sharply declined.
cons: Poor leadership, especially at the Tampa site. Cafeteria closed indefinitely due to rodent infestations. Lack of transparency from site leadership. Outdated technology.  Open work spaces very poorly executed. Loud and exceptionally dirty without regular cleaning. Tampa is a  "second class" site in a state of decline, and unlikely to offer long-term opportunities.

pros:
Decent pay
Insurance cover most everyday
cons: Not alot of opportunities to move up, in collections, stats are based on luck, one call collect $5000, next 9 hours you talk to people who don't even believe they have a credit card, haven't made incentive except twice in 3 years of service. And when I try to apply for management, which is my previous experience, its denied, but someone else who just starts gets into management with no education like bachelor degree, and gets the promotion in 6 months.

advice: Be more flexible in how you manage the Analysts.
pros: 2-Year Rotational Program gives Analysts 2 Rotations 1 year long, emphasizes networking and challenging projects.
cons: Will not be helpful unless you actually take the initiative to create you network within the company to go far, as most companies. I've interned other places, and the HR here seems like they are working against you at times but if you play your cards right you will get what you need.

summary: Very good company to work for starting out. Pay at the teller level is better than most other retail banks.
advice: Spend more time working rather than discussing office drama.
pros: Global company with lots of room to advance. Pay and benefits are about as good as you'll find at any retail bank. At my location most of the workers were very laid back.
cons: Management tends to play favorites. Managers were also switched around numerous times in my location, and I was there for only 6 months, leading me to question job security.

summary: The pay is okay but the work is not challenging.
advice: When someone consistently says they need more work, find a way to give it to them. Cultivate top performers, don't ignore them.
pros: Pay is good, benefits are great.
cons: it's a HUGE organization and you get lost. I spent 6 years trying to find a challenge and never found one. I got multiple promotions in my time there and each time I thought I would finally be challenged. I ended up leaving to find something that stimulated my brain.

summary: Good if you work at a busy location
pros: the bank that pays the most is this one.
cons: The branches are not busy and since its  a bank that is not known its very hard to get customer to open accounts. You better have a center of influence otherwise you will crash and burn. They just laid off 100 people in small cities including Miami. I left before they reduced me as well but so many people were left in the dark and shocked. Beware of the lay offs continuing to happen.

advice: Promote those who are deserving not those who are friends of senior leadership. Also, establish a leadership program to help develop those who show any inkling of potential.
pros: The position has diverse responsibilities and gives you an opportunity to interface with multiple vendor types. Overall, it's a position of visibility and a opportunity to display leadership skills.
cons: Unfortunately the training is non-existent, promotions are rare, the compensation is below market value, the company practices are outdated and it's kind of a "blind leading the blind" type of hierarchy.

advice: Slow down.  Everyone's trying to rule the world.
pros: Have worked for the bank in various capacities for 25 years.  It's has been fairly stable. Flexible work schedule is a plus and the benefits are good.  Close to my home so commuting is stress free.  Work environment is pleasant and uncrowded.
cons:
Unreasonable expectations that require long hours.
Inexperienced managers give too much responsibility in a short period of time.  Times of uncertainty if your job would be eliminated.

summary: Associate & Analyst position in Investment Banking
advice: Culture if the most important aspect for long term success of a franchise. Also, there has to be a very clearly defined career progression for junior bankers. Culture of mentorship needs to be inculcated.
pros: Very challenging and exponential learning in initial years. Great brand name and respected across the industry. Great training ground for honing hard skills such as time management, technicals, etc.
cons: Lack of mentorship & empathy towards junior employees, lack of an on-job training perspective & limited constructive feedback from seniors.

advice: Continue to love your employees and provide the utmost care.
pros: CITI Bank is one of the leading global financial institute. Our company offers employees first-class training and a variety of career opportunities. We have a challenging and competitive work environment for employees with a desire to succeed and make a difference.
cons: In lieu of the high level demand of BAU, one must learn to manage work/life balance. You will be surprised how time flies so fast while you work and have fun in the office.

summary: If you like to get permission from your manager before you talk to people, this is the company for you!
advice:
CUT the FAT
You don't need 9 levels of management to run a business
pros:
Vacation time off
Health plan
Prescription Plan
Vision Plan
Dental Plan
401K
cons:
It is a Two Hundred Year Old Company and it behaves like it
Honestly, I had to ask my manager's permission to talk to another manager in that place
It is so siloed, that it now makes sense to me why they have a year and a half product release time line

advice: Be nice to each other.
pros: Largest financial institution in the world.  Opportunities to find a niche.  Fairly good benefits package.  Always bounces back from a crisis and remains standing.  Working from home two days a week is not at all unheard of.  Parents are accommodated well.
cons: Administrative assistants are not part of the bonus structure ever.  Salaries stagnate.  Current management is extremely cut throat.  This is changing.  Wait it out before you apply to work here.

advice: Invest more in your top talent.  Don't let top talent go in an effort to reduce expenses.  Your top talent will find a way to win, but the Bank cannot cut itself to success.
pros:
People are  high caliber and generally very supportive
Company Executive Leadership has a strong vision for the future, and solid plan for execution
cons:
Constant churn of Managing Directors results in a disjointed execution at the local level
Continuous expense pressures make job stability/security very tenuous

advice: Company is great, but management can improve in handling business requirements.
pros: Company takes care of employees well with good benefits and compensation. People having long term plan can stick with company. Lots of projects keeps you busy with career and interesting working environment and flexible colleagues at much needed times.
cons: Managers don't have technical knowledge. Be prepared to spend hrs to explain them about the issues, resolutions and precautions. Management sometimes does not have good workflow. Also, be prepared to work round the clock.

summary: Good Starting Job for Office Environment
advice: Make bonus incentives more attainable.  Most people laugh at the current plan, knowing that very few will hit the mark required to receive anything quarterly (formerly monthly)
pros:
Good base pay
Good benefits (medical, dental, optical, 401k company matching)
flexible work schedule
great people
relaxed environment
cons:
limited career mobility
unattainable bonus incentive plans
over-time availability dependent upon market trends
too many channels that "evaluate" and review performance, listen to calls, etc. - always being marked down for something
almost feeling like we're being set up to fail at our jobs

advice: More granular communication to employees about strategy.  Encourage middle management to do more team-building / community.  Restructure IT and internal compliance/audit to be less of a bottleneck.
pros: There is not a lot of pressure and benefits are quite reasonable.  The atmosphere is very quiet which could be appealing to some.  Good intra-company mobility.  Resources of a large multinational.
cons: Employees are undermotivated to drive company results.  Lack of sense of community.  Very siloed, and surprisingly difficult to navigate intra-company organization.

summary: IT is not the focus of this company and it never will be.
advice:
Embrace Open Source technology.
Avoid paying for licensing.
Hire engineers to architect and migrate you over to a new infrastructure.
pros:
If you plan on branching out into a focus that encompasses the financial world then this job may help.
Learn how a large global financial institution operates.
cons: The company mainly hires Contractors to do most of their IT work so it's difficult to obtain an FTE position unless you've been working there for a minimum of 1 year.

summary: Old school way of thinking, this is the same with the archaic technology in use.
advice:
embrace new technology as it's necessary 
attempt to take some risks instead of only making calculated risks or else the company will stay behind the curve.
pros:
Good Benefits
401k matching
San Antonio main location had a decent cafe and is very family friendly
cons:
Old technology from infrastructure to customer facing.
shorten training with OTJ experiences
The company seems to have a vast amount of people who are comfortable with their current positions and don't aspire to advanced positions.

advice: If an employee is part time, let them be able to go to school (University). Make sure that employees feel recognized and appreciated once in a while
pros: good hours, paid time off, holiday's paid, bonuses (sometimes), and being able to work at a bank.
cons: stressful with KDS (customers surveys), horrible employee recognition, Not flexible with schedule, Does not help employees that are going to school and upper management stresses out the branch and assistant branch managers which stress out the personal bankers and tellers

summary: Lack of opportunity to step forward
advice: Please provide equal opportunities to the contractors because ther are many discriminative roles at the CITI whiches inhibits the personal development in the work related areas.
pros: The CITI SSC is a safe workplace on the Information Security area much safer than other Business positions. You can plan with your job for a long term.
cons: Uncleared processes. Really really difficult to brake out from C5 grade despite of you ar working ther since a long time. Does not matter if you have avards and merits.

advice: Always have an open door policy
pros: Good benefits, great people to work for and around, I came to work every day so I never had any issues with time off requests.  Citi is a diverse company.  They are fair in decision making.  Compensation was very beneficial.
cons: Some Managers play favoritism but that is any business I have found

advice: At the cost of 1 management associate you can take two normal employees. Double productivity and happy employees
pros: Salary, Movement Opportunities within division provided you can play real smart
cons: very monotonous, no learning opportunity, i was shocked about the quality of work, for the first few months was just confirming whether a document has been scanned or not. For management students from good B-Schools an advise- please take a job of half the salary but a good profile. You will not regret the decision

summary: Great place to work if ignore hierarchy
pros: Loved the place for atmosphere, innovation, opportunities (I had 3 jobs in 4 years, my own choice and initiative), great people and a lot of fun - yes, you have to create your world but if you manage to do that - it's a lot of good times.
cons: Lousy rewards and compensation at my level, under market standard, old school, overgrown hierarchy and senior management playing only with their buddies and in their own playground.

pros: Citi is an excellent place to work. In Dublin, the workforce is very diverse and there is wide spectrum of roles and grades. I enjoy the ability to work fully remotely when I need to
cons: We're a multinational, which means that changes that impact the global operation can take a long time to come into effect. This can be annoying if you see something that should be a simple quick fix but would take months / years to implement.

advice: The bell curve is outdated, this form of performance review need an overhaul.  If you take care of your employees, they will take care of you.
pros: Flexible Work-life balance. Starting to make changes in competing with competitors benefits by now offering 2 weeks paid parental leave for fathers
cons: They do not stand behind their "Pay for Performance" philosophy, in regards to paying to retain talent, looking at external competitors salaries, and they do not review/ adjust current employee pay levels to keep up with the current market.

advice: Work out a new system for quality assurance.
pros: The best thing about working at Citibank is the structured environment. Some may not prefer it, others may, but I thought it was a great thing. Next would be the pay and the health benefits.
cons: It can be very mundane and repetitive. Quality Assurance monitors calls regularly, and that can add a lot of pressure, unless you're a seasoned pro. The highly structured environment can also fall into the "con" category for some.

advice: do NOT hire Branch Managers from outside. No matter how much experience they might have. Promote from within.
pros: 1-Nice benefits (if you use them that is) 2-Supportive supervisors and co-workers
cons: Branch Managers hired in from outside who know less than you would as a teller! 2-Sloppy training that misses a lot of important things such as mortgage accounts, cash advances, linking and non-linking accounts 3-Training is too cliche leaving plenty of room for on the job mistakes 4-Irrelevant training modules that don't pertain to the job at hand

advice: keep up the good work but plan a little longer term,  this may prove difficult in times of declining budgets, but workers need to understand the big picture and plan for themselves.
pros: diversified company that allows individuals to move within its various divisions.  the process is not straight-forward, but can work when people persist
cons: a large employer with a very large organizational bureaucracy that at times is unable to deal effectively with individuals.  However, with a little personal touch, issues get resolved.

advice: review compensation benchmarks around different areas, review Bonus calculation, just as the Financial ratios to the regulators, employees would love to understand the base of calculation for their BONUS.
pros: The learning experience is unbelievable, you can actually do whatever kind of job you are inetersted on.  time balance is ok, and at certain levels of seniority you manage your own time
cons: BONUS are 100% @discretion, so you may never now how your variable pay can come.  very political and low pay against market.

advice: Fix the issues that are causing employees to leave.  They're repeated each year in the employee survey, yet nothing is done.
pros: Great people and talent.  More relaxed culture than some banks, good work life balance.  Management is very approachable.  Benefits are still good even though they used to be better.
cons: Pay is significantly lower than competitors despite HR repeatedly telling us they pay "competitively" keeping turnover high, constant technology projects because they refuse to use vendor software and build their own

advice: Choose a direction and stay the path. Citi doesn't turn on a dime and culture can't be changed overnight.
pros: Great people, there is a lot of work to be done, benefits are quite good. You won't make a significant impact, but you will have the opportunity to learn a lot
cons: Pay remains stagnant of long periods of time. In place promotions are exceptionally rare and the company is so large that changes in direction happen before the benefit from a previous change can be fully realized.

advice: Don't let business unit managers be technology architects. Stop with the politics and the pettiness. Take a pay cut and give raises to your teams so people stop leaving. Don't promote incompetent managers who are not technical. Abolish SN tickets.
pros: Job security, lots of resources, huge company with global impact.
cons: Huge company means it is slow to get anything done. There is a lack of direction/clarity on projects and requirements. Too many stakeholders with their own interests and not much bandwidth to build long term technology infrastructure. Instead, front office teams focus on one off requests and as a result are constantly re-inventing the wheel. Furthermore, the deluge of paperwork/ticketing makes it nearly impossible to accomplish anything.

advice: How about hiring a manager who know what hes supposed to do when you assign them to a new hire class of reps? That wouldve been great
pros: They have a cafeteria, good pay, awesome people,great trainers, get overtime pay after 5, bonuses for referring new employees
cons: Boring call center work, sitting all day, they hired a new manager that didnt know what he was doing for a new hire class of reps, repetative work, wants me to pay back my last paycheck which is never happening

summary: Great company and work life balance but...
advice:
Increase pay
Allow teams to have input on manager performance reviews and ensure their goals are met as well
More seating
pros:
Work from home option
PTO
Benefits
OT
Cafeteria is amazing
cons:
No bonuses
Upper Management doesn’t care or respect those in the frontlines
Direct management can be rude disrespectful unethical and bias 
More likely to get a promotion or hired if you are hispanic
Little to no direct hire is done almost everyone starts as a temp through an agency and is screened for a year before offered to become an employee

summary: A great place to start out.. regardless of education level
advice: keep up the good work!
pros: Medicial insurance is excellent!! Pay is competitive if you work nights and weekends ..especially if you are bilingual. Management is very good at recieiving feedback and changing procedures if it is needed.. you can definetely learn discipline, time managementm multi- tasking and communication skills. It is also a very nurturing environment for the most part.
cons: you get sick time that you can't use without serious consequences... sometimes the company can feel "too big"

advice: Develop your talent. Columbus is a low-cost facility, so try and take advantage of the area and find pivotal individuals who stick with the company.
pros: Decent pay in comparison to other Operation facilities in the area.  They will teach you the basics surrounding the stock market operations. Great work life balance.
cons: Much less pay in comparison to other banks in the area. A low ceiling and difficult to breakthrough. Will only pay the normal 5,250 toward external classes and will not pay or encourage designations.

advice: I think management should do a better job recognizing strong work beyond great review.  If you get consistently great reviews, why would you be passed over for promotion?
pros: The company does a good job supporting diversity, opportunity to work in many areas, good benefits, nice office space, opportunities for career training and development with senior staff.
cons: In my experience, the company is not a meritocracy.  It is all about who you know and who likes you when it comes to advancement and opportunity.

pros: The benefits are very competitive and affordable. Beginning hiring wage is several dollars more an hour than most other entry level positions. Great people to work with too.
cons: I've been there 3 years, my son just got hired there too, and his wage is only .50 less than mine. Citi would do well to "reward" employees that are committed with appropriate cost of living wage increases. It's discouraging to give 3 years to this company and a new hire gets almost as much as you.

summary: Citi - Great job titles, lousy commitment to employees
pros: Citi has jobs with impressive titles such as Technology Infrastructure Site Manager that is at an Assistant Vice Presidential level.  They also have above average pay scales.
cons: Citi has zero loyalty towards its workers.  Because Citi brings people into the organization in management capacity, they can and do hire and lay-off at will.  There is zero incentive to advance within the company, even after their famous tuition reimbursement has garnered you Bachelors Degrees and even Graduate degrees.

advice: Would be glad if employees could claim their OT and feel appreciated
pros:
Provide on job training and guidance to new hires
Seniors are helpful
Managers very attentive n caring
Friendly colleagues 
Able to wfh due to pandemic
Career growth depends on high quality perfomances
Good starting salary for fresh graduates
cons:
Sometimes have to work more than regular office hours to achieve productivity but cannot claim OT

Encourage work life balance but do not consider that there are circumstances that need longer time in reviewing which affect the productivity of the day

summary: Depends on your department and manager
advice: Treat people well and they will work hard and be loyal.
pros: Overall, there was a fun and interesting employee base. I still stay in touch with many of my former peers. Also, It was fairly easy to move within the organization if you wanted to explore other areas.
cons: At times, there was poor oversight of department managers. This may have been due to a good amount of manager turnover. Like many big firms, they were constantly looking to outsource jobs to cut costs.

advice: Allow employees to experience real cross-training by moving them to other teams for six months or so to do different technical work. It would make for happier more motivated employees.
pros: I am very happy with my salary and benefits. It is a very collaborative and collegiate atmosphere with dedicated and motivated co-workers.
cons: I am very siloed so it has produced substantial gaps in my knowledge as a Windows system administrator but anyone who has worked in, at least, large banks, will know what I mean.

advice: Need to start finding ways to either provide raises to the employees that have been loyal and receive good reviews
pros: There has been more focus on allowing employees to have flexible work schedules or to work remotely. Certain departments do a good job with employee appreciation events.
cons: So much of the work has been transferred to offshore sites that the onshore jobs are disappearing and it is virtually impossible to move up within the company anymore, have seen  very few raises in last 5 years

advice: provide your employees the tools they need to be successful instead of only caring about your bottom line
pros: good benefits, new CEO seems to care about the company and its image
cons: It's super clear the company doesn't give a crap about their employees. My manager is fine, and my coworkers are ok, but they don't provide their employees any kind of WFH support. Not a laptop, a stipend, nothing. If Citi doesn't care that I can't do my job properly from home I certainly don't either!

summary: Call center employees are treated as human chattel.
pros: Good pay, especially with shift differential. Decent benefits.
cons: Draconian scheduling policies. Difficulty scheduling any vacation time if hired during the latter half of the year. Came down with life threatening pneumonia and missed 8 consecutive days of work, which was not long enough for short term disability. Not only was not allowed to bring a physician's excuse (per PTO policiy) but was instead placed on a performance warning for excessive absence when I returned.

advice:
Be more transparent around how bonuses are calculated.

Continue working on improving the firm and with the bewell program.
pros:
Great pregnancy benefits! 4 months at 100% pay if you've worked 90 days prior.

Good time off.
cons:
Depending what job you take, you may work long hours with no work life balance or have a healthy amount.

If you do exceptionally well, their aren't discretionary bonuses throughout the year only at year end.

Bonuses if eligible are like a black box, their isn't much transparency around how they are calculated.

summary: IT Program Manager within Capital Markets
advice: Define and communicate the corporate culture, and start paying some attention to compensation.
pros: Large organization that supports career mobility. Increasing focus on consolidation and eliminating redundant technology, which means there are many new projects using the latest technologies.
cons: Communication of strategy is ineffective, so teams within the same functional groups don't even know what each other are doing. No common culture. Compensation is not competitive with peer group, especially for those who have been with the firm since the start of the depression.

pros: Work life balance at it's best. Rarely worked overtime, learned a lot, peers were cordial with the exception of a few toxic collections reps on the same floor.
cons: Regarding the monthly review score, an above average was super difficult to obtain, and average reps who were favorites would often receive a higher rating and receive promotions to team lead or often available for other roles such as AML where they then failed, due to lack of work ethic and experience.

summary: Citi is constantly changing and you need to keep your skills current and desired by those you work for to advance.
advice: Management is too political and afraid to speak up for the good of the company.  Executive management only wants to hear how to make money and cut costs, but are not as concerned about the risks that may occur.
pros: Many resources and people to work with whom you can learn from
cons: Management is very budget conscious and reluctant to spend money for quality work.

advice: Be honest. Don't use people for their skills and after you stop using the technology, get rid of them. Retrain them!
pros: a lot of work and challenging. Team colleagues were great had fun!
cons: Management was not honest. Did all work, promised me they would transfer me. to an internal role, that did not happen. Gave me bad reviews even after I did all my work. found out later it was to get rid of me because they were going to close my role.

summary: Company appears to be trying, but actions don't seem to support the words.
advice: Pay for talent, and try to retain good employees.  It seems most of the money is paid to the investment bankers and sales teams.  You need to support the operations employees as well.
pros: The company is very flexible, and the benefits are pretty good overall.  Although this is not consistent across managers.
cons: Mortgage Industry is volatile and declining.  Forecasting is extremely difficult and nothing expected to get better until at least 2015.

advice: Stop being pretentious to care for your employees.
pros: Higher salary than other companies because it is BPO.
cons: They have the pretense of listening to your concerns, but NO. If you raise your concern on a townhall, moderators will not approve your question. With regards to Return to Site questions, instead of supporting employees they are threatening with HR action. Basically, employee care is 0 here. Comments raised on Voice of the employees are being filtered as well. Living in a delusion that the employees are not encountering issues.

advice: Better Bonuses and rewards based on contributions to the company
pros: Opportunity and diversity, never boring, company reinvents itself every 3 to 5 years = Global opportunity for advancement, Can be a challange so long as you find the right job, free to express new ideas
cons: Market crash has impacted growth, major consolidation in technology sectors, major outsourcing of entry level positions - excessive technology outsourcing has caused mangement of those resoruces difficult due to language and training both technological and corporate policy related.

summary: Be Careful if you are looking for a long term career
advice: Learn to appreciate your people. Wondering why your stock is not moving has prompted you to make terrible decisions regarding people. You've lost a lot of experience and talented people. Best course correction: focus on delivering products customers want and policies that are people focused, not profit focused. If you make a true change, profits and trust will come.
pros: The Medical benefits are good.
cons: The raises are terrible; 1% to 1.5% if you are top rated. Downsizing/outsourcing trends are increasing.

advice: Standardize hiring processes. HR should not take months to hire people.   Also, there is a disconnect between what your manager can do for you and what they promise you.
pros: Good raises and decent pay helps. Just make sure you get what you want when you come in and before you commit.
cons: Office culture is brutal. The culture is filled with politics, competitions and fighting. Things take forever to get done. Also ,the culture is work harder to compensate. The hiring practices are not standardized across LOBs.

advice: Quit hiring consultants: they don't care about the company, they will never be loyal and fully committed .
pros: Flexible work hours, lots of cutting edge technologies, transparency with the trading desk.
cons: Typical corp culture, everything requires approval delaying the necessary changes. Favoritism within the ranks, line managers are pushovers, middle management ignorant towards their employees, all business is deviated towards London while NY takes the backseat. Ppl turnover is crazy, tons people get laid off all the time, very frustrating and demotivating. Consultant culture dominates over perm employees.

summary: The Citi Compliance department is so large it's easy to get lost.
pros: The 401k match is excellent.  In theory, the company is large and diverse enough that moving around the company should be easy.
cons:
The Compliance management team has too many levels. It allows for poor managers to go unnoticed until it is too late. The quality of management is also very poor. 
Regarding the above "Pro", Citi puts way more resources on bringing in new hires than retaining current employees. It is very difficult to move around the company.

summary: When I was at the Citi I enjoyed it very much and learned A lot in Back in Collection
advice: No advice for Management at this time
pros: Best reason for working for Citi is the benefits the people the Experience you gain &  if you have a Degree this Company will be something that you wanna consider as a long-term stay cause the pay is very nice
cons: I would say that the cons would be the hours starting out you have to bid for shifts depending on the Department you're in.

advice: Be more professional with employees. Pay employees equally.
pros: Health Benefits are unbelievable. Time off your given is exceptional! Managers are Farley east to work with as long as your actually working.
cons:
Management does play favorites/who you know game. Which is very unprofessional. The pay is okay considering but in my specific department I had higher goals but was paid the least. 

Also application/hire process is unnecessarly long. Don't count on the job if you need one now. It was about a month before my training class started.

summary: Good place to work for self starters.
advice: Managers need to be trained how to develop their people.  You are letting go of a lot of senior people with industry knowledge and experience.
pros: I had a great career at Citi for 22 years.  I learned the mortgage industry inside and out.
cons: You have to be self motivated.  There is no career path.  If you want to move up, you have to look for and take advantage of any and all opportunities.  Nobody else will do it for you.

summary: Perfect to build a long and stable career
pros: Great atmosphere, magnificent people, easygoing management, many directions possible after entry level positions, perfect for motivated people willing to have stable growth, multinational environment, company is growing currently, overhours usually paid, overhours not obligatory, transparent rules
cons: Have to be patient to be promoted, need to perform more responsible duties for current salary, dealing with quite tough however stable corporate system, work space may be found physically inconvenient, some offices located in hard-to-access areas, salary competitive however not so good comparing to living costs

advice: I understand that you are being measured in 90 day window frame, but at some time a true leader has got to rise above this petty short term mentality, as if it were a family business.
pros: Great clients, products and services to offer.  Due to 2008 debacle, the major focus reverted to compliance rather than what clients saught
cons: Lots of great products and services overlaid by lots of ambiguity due to environmental constraints.  However in relative terms these were no less than at a competitor

advice: Give equal creative flexibility and hire local technical talent and you may be quite surprised on the amount of money that can be saved while trusting that a best in class customer experience will be delivered without spending exorbitant amounts of cash.
pros: Flexible Schedule, Benefits, matching 401k starting at 6%, Lots of bank holidays and planned and unplanned time off.
cons: Turnover is imminent for top level executives every 2-4 years. Constant restructuring of departments is inevitable leaving employees without a planned process to continue ongoing work loads.

summary: This job will be made by your team
advice: Help your employees more.
pros: There is room for growth in the company and they strongly prefer to promote from within. you are only able to work within banking hours and you cannot take your work home with you.
cons: it is extremely corporate. there is no flexibility for anything, systems and technology are terrible, and you are often asked to pick up other peoples slack or do things outside of your job description and do not get recognized or paid for it.

pros: Do not leave this company. Citibank has exceptional opportunities worldwide. Work on developing knowledge and talent before you go any apply. moreover, there are lots of tools to develop talent be it with degreed, udemy, internal learning tools, etc. you will find lot of intelligent people across broad so try to make friendship and stay connected with them to grow.
cons: You should be smart enough to deal with politics across company. if you are not happy with your manager then go explore other opportunity within organization.

summary: TOO MUCH DIVERSITY, POOR REGIONAL LEADERSHIP
advice: Have employee engagement survey annually and don't adopt practices from other big firms you can't successfully implement
pros:
Entry pay is good
WFH arrangement
cons:
Diversity is okay, at least all race are represented, right? But you have to admit that putting more Indian leaders isn't working for Citibank. All work and no play, no empathy to employees at all (unless maybe you're a VP?) Mobility is a joke (this is why I joined Citi in the first place, but looks like your managers aren't all well trained on people development)

Poor HR service whether you're an active employee or resigned employee. It takes them weeeeeeeks to respond.

Not following local labor laws on the timeline of releasing final pay

advice: Senior Management needs to focus more closely on creating an acceptable training curriculum for new team members.
pros: Citigroup has come a long way in the last few years.  Work Life Balance is amazing.
cons: Compensation.  Perfect ratings year over year over year along with an MBA are not enough to get a decent merit increase.  I'd be better off leaving and then coming back in 1-2 years.  My salary would come close to doubling by being an external applicant.

summary: Great place to work if you don't mind lack of job security.
advice: I know the environment is tough and you're doing what you can, but take the time to make sure that your best employees don't get laid off when lower performers are kept.  Attention to employee-level detail instead of department-level detail would help in this matter.
pros: Good compensation package and opportunities for advancement.
cons: Long hours and not a lot of job security even if performance is excellent

summary: Reconsider working in Account Maintenace Department.
advice: Do not make your company so compartmentalized. The process to get simple jobs functions completed required several steps. I understand that this is how most corporations operate but I believe if you combine certain departs it will allow you to save money and it will also boost employee morale by giving them more responsibilities which in turn gives individuals professional growth.
pros: My depart manager was very easy to approach.
cons: Job was very repetitive and required very little true skill and technical aptitude.

advice: Promote larger and more frequent gatherings of departments or the entire office. Provide the employees with opportunities to connect and relate to the larger organization.
pros: The office environment is generally friendly and down to earth. Depending on the department, employees can be fairly social and helpful. Small offfice parties are common.
cons: The office is large and can be very bureaucratic. Technical support is slow and difficult to obtain. Logins, passwords, access codes, and both paper and electronic forms all complicate basic processes.

advice: Learn how to make use of your time. With a little work on organizational skills, deparments can function better. Promotion should be based on quality of work not how many years spent at position
pros: Secure job, pretty good benefits with good vacation and holiday time sick and personal payed time off. Intelligent staff to work with.
cons: Little opportunity for advancement, stupid management. People in charge do not know how to run the departments efficiently. Disorganized management not knowing how to make use of staff

advice: Instead of giving lip service to your employees, actually listen to them.  If you practice what you preach, Citi could be a great place to work.
pros: Decent vacation amount when you can take it.  Diversity.  Support of Community through Charities.  Available learning materials are nice.
cons: Extremely political - tons of red tape.  HR doesn't effectively resolve management situations.  Poor management.  Management does not take into consideration Voice of Employee surveys.  Hostile work environment.  Excessive # of hours worked by salaried employees.  Low pay when you consider the number of hours you have to put in.  Management specifically discouraged continued education because it would reduce availability.

summary: Good place to work in the past; now can't decide on a direction
advice: Choose a direction and stay the course over six months.
pros: On average with salaries, a lot of opportunities to grow.  My division promoted getting training.  Many good people who will help you if you ask.
cons: Reorganizations every six months or so.  Management doesn't really care about staff and most are not honest about upcoming cuts, etc..  Outside management has been brought in and existing staff not thought of as being competent.

advice: Make things happen for employees on all part, so they can be flexible in all the business.
pros: The bright side of this that the company has been growing in the field of Compliance, lots of people getting hired due to growth in Credit card, commercial business, etc.
cons: The only bad part is that Citi is not that much in the business of Mortgage, and it appears that they might be cutting their mortgage business, and so they will shift or cut people on the mortgage side.

advice: Managers and above are better in their outcome when they have been in someone else shoe before.  Having that experience enables them to forecast and set real goals instead of someone else's ego and hidden agendas.
pros: Corporate banking set up, all types of online training to keep with technology, health care benefits, 401K, 3 weeks vacation + bank holidays
cons: Multiple layers of bureaucracy.  Upper level management runs without knowing how the real world in the industry works.  Highly political.  Expensive benefits.

advice: I can't - they're useless
pros:
Vacation time is generous 
401K match to 6%
