Some flexibility to work from home on days that you need it
cons:
Technology is backwards 
Slow decision making 
HR function is deplorable
Career development is non existent 
Promoting people is based on whether or not you're in the 'club' with the right folks and has nothing to do with actual competence

advice: Support people and try to get some good work
pros:
1. No pressure
2. Department like tts, cet are good with compensation and with good project
cons:
1. No challenging use cases or projects in ETS
2. Bad management, US managers think is a support group and mostly give supporting work
3. In ETS, never think that you will get good hike or bonus because it is a bad devision. Business is not interested in ETS, since it is not revenue generating devision.[avg hike-20k, avg bonus-5%]

advice: Great people will for with you, but will not stay for the long term once they feel they're just exploited and promises never come.
pros: Can be a good place to start working.
cons: Management promises while knowing well it won't happen. It's always the promise that next time it will be different, we promise. It would be a fairly good place, but reality is that there's too much dishonesty from management. In the end probably everyone knows this is kind of a standard in much of the financial industry.

advice: Value and positively embrace your teams as individuals, stop being lazy, being tyrannical does not equate with better performance at all.
pros: Simple, to the point tasks. Pto. Benefits. Friendly atmosphere.
cons: Rude, entitled customers. Monthly metrics can be difficult to stabilize, sometimes unable to acheive due to circumstances out of your control. Non effective management, pay can be better, doing everyone's job under one role. Schedules can be much better. Promised shift bids and after two years still have not gotten the chance to bid for new shifts.

advice: Improve your canteen service, reduce the meal price or increase your food quality
pros: relax company, not much over time.  and college are friendly , lot of events and social groups. lot of chance to meet all nations people which is quite interesting. remote working from home and lot flexibility  if you work at IT firm
cons: bad canteen, always dirty and not clean, staff in canteen not provide good service even we paid lot on low quality meal. need to improve a lot on that.

advice: This depends on what department you were in, but for upper management, better communication to employees especially when it’s regarding whether or not the job of continuing and consistency regarding layoffs and severance.
pros: Benefits, quarterly events, food days, room for growth if you play well with others
cons: No job security at the moment, lack of recognition for achievements by upper management, communication is lacking

summary: Awful work life balance for okay exit opps
pros: Standard investment banking pros. Good modeling training, great analyst colleagues, good exit opportunities depending on which group you're in.
cons: Truly awful work life balance. Associates are almost all post-MBA with minimal internal promotion. The A2A kids are the ones who couldn't find a job anywhere else. Citi has mindless policies that result in a lot of asking other teams for help that delays getting pitches / deals done. Deal flow has gone down as boutiques poach the best managing directors.

summary: Senselessness is an understatement. Worst decision ever. Glad I got out. Bought a bridge and a bottle of snake oil.
advice: You will never retain top talent with your current archaic model. Awful managers that lie and connive to keep their positions. Lack of tangible incentives for hardworking retail associates. Empty titles with no compensatory benefit. No growth.
pros: Holidays off. Cool clients. That’s it.
cons: Recruiters should be charged with grand theft and false advertisement. Call center vibe. Outdated systems. Gross mismanagement by inept managers. Egotistical area directors. Lazy, petty branch pretenders I mean managers that crush the spirits of staff. Littered with cronyism and favoritism. Cutthroat culture. One team ideology is a stone cold myth. DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME!

advice: Communicate with the employees, hold managers accountable for completing reviews, care more about employee's career development
pros: Great resources,  can get additional responsibilities if you ask, request for vacation is usually honored, okay compensation, you will find some supportive managers
cons: Lack of communication from upper management, terrible review process (if any at all), very political, promotion based more on how well you are liked than on merit, no one really cares about your career development as the main focus is to bring in business.

advice: To deliver clear information about changes within the business.  Changes occur frequently and employees must have a clear point of view from leaders of company to better prepare for changes.
pros: Flexible schedule despite being FT, Many on site resources for health/fitness, post office, daycare and family oriented activities, positions are available to allow you to work from home.
cons: Despite long work tenures i've witnessed that its possible to be laid off, internal communication between different departments is poor, especially between customer service and collections.

summary: Its not the shining Citi on the hill anymore
advice: Burn it down and start over. New board, new leadership, new culture. Clearly, Sandy sold the world a bill of goods.
pros: People in line of business were great. Plenty of opportunity to grow and learn. Relatively easy to shine among some of the duller blades in the drawer.
cons: Corporate culture was one of fiefdoms. Managers cared more about territory than doing the right thing for the business or the customer. Wholesale destruction of wealth resulted.

summary: Very political organization where opportunities and pay are dependent on your ability to play the game.
advice: Provide information specifically relevant to the divisions in which people work and developments within that division.  The corporate level information provided is good but provides little guidance on the direction of one's specific division.
pros: Citi applies a great deal of resources to technology development.
cons: This is a bank so if you are in one of their non-banking divisions they make you appear to be unprofitable to justify minimal raises and bonuses.

summary: Citi is an amazing organization to work for!
advice: Keep closely connected to your teams.  Sometimes management can get pulled so far away from things going on that they miss items of importance.
pros: The culture at Citi is fabulous and it makes work much more enjoyable!  There are locations across the globe which provides additional opportunities.
cons: Citi is so large that getting things done can sometimes be difficult.  There are multiple systems, platforms, and processes that it can be difficult to be on the same page with peers.

advice: Listen to your workers and pay attention to the surveys. Promote based on merit. Some of them have been there too long and don't know anything about boosting morale or treating  employees with respect and dignity.
pros: Well known bank, Full-time work with benefits, retirement, vacation.
cons: Poor management, no real definition of expectations from year to year. This was a very hard company to advance your career unless you happened to be a recent colllege grad. HR was of no help in this area, either. They do discriminate based on age. Also, their technology was always slow and systems were inefficient which made working in Operations very challenging. The bank lacked organization and principles.

advice: The culture is constantly improving, but more improvement is needed with respect to the way people are treated.
pros:
Lots of interesting challenges.
Plenty of smart intelligent people.  
Concensus oriented.
Massive global footprint.
Seemingly infinite resources to get anything done that it wants to accomplish as a goal.
cons:
Massive - so many functions are redundant.
Too many people doing nothing, so it's ineffecient at times.
Too slow to move and action, so opportunities that require quick decision making and action are lost to the more nimble.

advice: Double check your managers' performance in small countries. Usually there the good employees remain at the bottom and a bunch of friends remain at the power.
pros: Fantastic training, good systems, international exposure. I would suggest it especially to entry levels. Possibilities to change business areas quite quickly and learn different skills.
cons: It is very difficult to step up and move your career forward. Too big and bureaucratic.It is very difficult to see the big picture and understand what you are contributing to.

summary: My experience at Citi Bank was lacking.
advice: During future interviews, elect a few of your staff employees to ask one or two questions to the candidate in order to gain a feel of the person's personality. Upon conclusion, have management obtain feedback for the candidate on how the employee would rate the candidtate's persona to mesh with others.
pros: Pros working with Citi Bank was having an opportunity to connect and learn about numerous businesses through daily engagement.
cons: The cons were the disengagement amongst employees at the branch.

advice: Hire branch managers that are fair and reasonable and that are willing to work.
pros: Once you leave work you are done for the day.  You also build relationships with customers which makes the day go by.  Good intro position.
cons: A lot of sales pressure as a teller and you are not paid on the sales you bring into the branch.  The Branch manager has all the discretion over any potential bonus. There was also a bigger focus on sales then compliance and accuracy.

summary: An organization that is still finding its way in the post financial crises world. Decent structure, still some overlap.
pros: Job mobility is the number one attribute, with brand recognition a close second. Truly a global bank, Citi is actively working to reposition itself.
cons: Micro management in the retail bank is simply off the charts and is driving away the talent in droves. Could be the most elite consumer bank in the world if it would find a way not to micro manage the talent.

summary: I had a great experience working with Citi for 14 years. Opportunities for mentoring and advancement are available.
pros: Advancement opportunities, time off benefits, health benefits, 401k/company matching program
cons: Too many gaps in communication due to the size of the departments/groups. Technology is out of date and there are no real plans to get state of the art technology because of costs. Also the company lacks a great deal in the training department for new hires. This is also because of costs and no good technology.

advice: Management should pay better and they would keep the quality people they have, currently everyone is leaving for more money.
pros: Benefits are great, vacation/sick days you get several. Good life/work company business model. company goes the extra mile to the community and to make having a family easy
cons: Pay is very low for expected work, personal cell phone used for all company communication when not at work, company does not seem to care how many people are losing jobs

summary: I absolutely loved working for Citibank.  The management supports their employees, as long as you are giving 120%.
advice: Always remember where you started in the company.
pros: Management will support you as long, as you prove you can do the job.  Growth within the company is very obtainable.  In my opinion, it is all up to you how far you can drive your business.
cons: Can be somewhat of a high pressure job when you are not cross selling.

advice: For management to all be on the same page. some managers play favoritism.
pros: Very flexible and fun people to work with. I enjoy collecting debt from clients. overall a great place to work. benefits start same day as hired. Citi has the best vision insurance.
cons: there are always changes in policies and the goals to make bonus change every month. everyone works their accts different and makes it hard to hit bonus sometimes, because some co workers don't work as a team.

pros: Higher base pay than most other banks, opportunity for monthly and quarterly bonuses, decent benefits...
cons: Stress on tellers for sales is high as well as customer service survey scores. They have made a lot of cut-backs in the last couple years so branches are functioning at minimum capacity, so when someone is sick or on vacation, you will work 6 days. The expectation for sales scores and customer survey scores are so high that it is impossible to get a 5 star annual review rating.

summary: Former employee with several positionsin different locations
advice: Find ways to reward employees for hard work even if not monetary.
pros: Global corporation with lots of opportunity for movement and various career experience.  Internal mobility is encouraged.  Always very good people to work with.
cons: Work Life balance in some positions is difficult.  Compensation/Bonus structure has worsened over the years but expectations for going above and beyond have only gotten higher.  Being rewarded for the work you do is a challenge in the appraisal/performance structure.

advice: The only advice I would give to management is to work to improve the work-life balance within the company. Although work is important, morale is also very important
pros: Very good benefits! Lots of places to move within the company but VERY hard to transfer to different positions. But overall its ok
cons:
Unprofessional enviornment, employees do not dress professionally
Difficult managers
Extremely high turnover. Do not go to work for this company thinking you will enter in at a lower level and move up. It is almost impossible

advice: As a manager you should always be able to view all situations and are able to provide a fair and safe review for all. You should also know the importance of creating a enjoyable work space.
pros: Citi is a very diverse place to work, they are very involved in the community and make sure their employees are active as well.
cons: When working for Citi or any other bank you are at risk of a layoff. This would be the major con working for Citi

advice: better hours, you guys should give better hours because I get really tired and I really need my sleep so the poor hours affected how easily I could get sleep and be well rested.
pros: fun, good pay, I really had a good time working for citi because they make everyone there feel like they belong to be there
cons: bad hours, the food nearby sucked, every morning I would go out and hope that I could find a damn parking spot. The city, am I right?

summary: Great growth and learning, poor pay
advice:
- evaluate your pay practices, especially as it relates to underrepresented minorities
- elevate women, black, and brown talent
pros:
- longstanding bank with clear structures and procedures 
- great learning opportunities 
- frequent advancement opportunities
cons:
- although growth/promotion/career advancement opportunities are plentiful, salaries are extremely low compared to competitors. 
- mediocre performing employees are kept for far too long, thus few high-performers doing most of the work 
- very hierarchical and political 
- lack of diversity at the senior executive level with US

advice: Form a team dedicated to employee engagement so that employees do not have to extend hours for activities that they are not paid for.
pros:
1. Little to none office politics.
2. Competitive salary.
3. There is equal opportunity (Citi doesn't look at gender, race, school you graduated from).
4. Meritocratic culture (when you do your best, you get promoted)
cons:
1. Employee engagement (there is no dedicated team that works on this, employees have to organize themselves).
2. Work hours are so long (I think this depends on the department).

summary: Everything is good about the company except work

Train your managers to respect juniors
Train managers on Agile
pros:
Good Pay
30 PL
12 sick leave
WFH policy
Bank holidays
insurance, paternity leave and other facilities are very good
A really good company for working women or mother.
cons: Just work life can be hectic and managers will only promise to do something but nothing is done. If you can handle work pressure rest everything is good about the company

advice: Increase the salary of your employee.
pros: If your working in ROHQ, there's a lot of workload but not required to take OT (depends on your time) Has a flexible schedules. WFH privileges up to thrice a week (if the role is not critical)No weekend work (again, it depends on the criticality) And lastly, they promote importance of mental health and diversity.
cons: Low salary, Not much bonus. No 14th-16th month pay, A good training ground for fresh grads but no promotion at all. Too hierarchical

summary: Pathetic , horrible, terrible, harassment, worst company
advice: I learnt how to survive in fearful environment because of you guys.
pros:
May be initial package. Later you will realize what big mistake you have done by accepting to join just for few extra bucks.

There could be other good things but you wont be able to leverage them because of the culture created by mgmt.
Leaves - So many but you wont be able to take it.

Club mahindra - Forget it. You will anyways be able to take limited leaves so you can not plan anything. That has so many constraints as well and 30% of the amount has to be paid my employee.

Annual health check up 8k - This is very important as your health will degrade by working here hence you atleast have a tool to measure it.

Cab facility - wont matter because mgmt will schedule scrum calls when you have cabs. So you will always be worried for every single day that should I cancel cab today or not. Taking cab early is not an option because of workload. Later you wont be having any cab so you will eventually start coming by your own vehicle. 

WFH - A nightmare actually. Citi is misusing this policy. You will be asked to connect anytime, anyday because Citi has given wfh. Things to note here is you need to have your own laptop and proper internet. Internet bill will not be reimbursed (In COVID they started reimbursing for below AVP level).
If you dont have proper system them mgmt will say Citi is paying you so much. Buy multiple screens. There are the words from my SVP.

Diwali gift of around 2k valuation.

As you can see most of these benefits are to lure new joiners to join the organization. These points have made jobs are HR very easy so that they can mention so many benefits working in Citi. These are just for branding the organization. In reality nothing exists on the ground which you will get to know when you are onboarded.
cons:
- There is no clarity on what exactly you need to do. If you ask your manager (terrible SVP's), they will not respond. You try to reach them by call/email/texts; they would still not respond. Then suddenly one day they will come up and ask where are we with this. Then you start telling them that requirement is not clear, we tried reaching out to you daily but no gains. Now the harassment starts. They will pressurize you to deliver in very short time, every day late night calls, daily requirements changing. You somehow deliver it but later you will get to know that was not at all used/required. There is no use of that feature. Then what was the need of so much unnecessary pressure ?

- SVP's are so so horrible. They will scold you in front of whole team/floor. They would insult because you were not available on Sunday 2PM to attend SVP's call.
You will be required to be available 24/7. You are offending management if your are not looking at whatsapp message and not acting accordingly (like responding, logging in to system etc.). Its a real expectation. If you don't do it get ready to be insulted very next day.

- There is a constant fear daily. What's going to happen next now. Who is going to come up with unrealistic deadline. What exactly suddenly going to come to you in one line, for ex - build a private website, pull data from API's. Now go and understand what to pull, what to show, where to store data, which all API's. No one is going to respond you for any details. You would definitely need to coordinate with other teams but they also wont respond. Your SVP thinks that you are some god who would understand requirements on his own. Then mgmt. will keep on asking about the feature. When you say that no one is responding then that's also your fault. Its like - You don't know how to approach to different teams.

- If a person is spending some time in cafeteria it means that the person is not LOADED with enough work. His manager will be called in by SVP to check why is he not LOADED enough.

- There is no uses of any process or tools like Agile/jira. There is no BA,QA, Architect. You are just given things in a line. GO ahead and do it.

- Leaves - They have so many leaves but man you can not take it. That's like a gold scuffle. This is just for HR to brand the company that we have so many leaves. Management wont let you take. If you take, SVP's will shout on floor or in meetings that you took one week leave 2 months ago, why do you need again. They will insult you till that level where after some time you would start neglecting all these people. You will go in very bad state mentally.

- No work life balance. Forget about this, you will always be scared of what's going to happen now.

- There is NO KT at all. Nothing on business side, nothing on tech side. You are expected to understand each and everything when the one liner requirements email comes.

- SVP's are so fake. SO much interested in fake branding of their org to befool people. When you go inside, you are like what. Seriously its that good an organization ??

Hiring - You are forced to hire female candidate at any cost. Statement from mgmt. - If you are hiring a guy, then he needs to be Rockstar. supper talented. Then only we will approve offer. If a girl, then we are fine with average or below average. Offer approval for a guy will go through lot of troubles.

- Managers are expected to be intelligent enough to know who is going to leave in near time. When a person from my team resigned, Words from mgmt. - you are not intelligent enough to understand that this person could resign. They always need a scapegoat for any bad thing that happens.

- There are some apps installed in the machines which calculates your login time, productivity time and most importantly your coding score. So if you were working on some tool or some POC or some new designing/architecture where less coding required, your score will go down. Your manager will be asked why the coding score getting down. You and your manager will be having very hard time explaining things. Think for normal use case where we have less work - you will be worried this time as well because your coding score is going down. Appraisal/promotion decisions are directly taken on these scores. Team effectiveness is judged on the average time team is logged in. Managers will be pressurized that why their team's login-logout time is so less. No one will tell about these tools in HR induction.

- You will definitely loose your self esteem by working in this organization. I wasted 2 fruitful years of my life working in this organization. They don't have any probation period as well. From day1 your NP is 3 months.

- I have been asked to purchase an iphone on my own because Citi's email can be opened through that phone only. I was told that you should buy an iphone so that you can look and respond to the emails by checking quickly when you are off work (weekends, holidays and vacations). So basically in order to work during my off time I have to purchase an iphone on my own. So many things we can extract from this statement to understand the culture.

- Not a SINGLE project/bu party. no outdoor activities at all. 

New joiners - I would say stay away at any cost please. Believe me. 

This is my experience in a specific BU and specific team. I am not sure about other BU's and teams. I am just sharing my experience.

Benefits were competitive
Pay was competitive

pros:
medical/ dental and vision insurance
decent paid time off policy
maternity/ paternity leave
not a lot of pros to list

advice: Pay attention to the front line staff, they know what is going on and have great ideas for improving things.
pros: It was a very good place to work for many years.  Employees are treated well overall and benefits are good.  A good place for a woman to have a strong management career.

advice: Work to improve employee recogintion and to provide postions that allow employees to grow.

advice: Value Sales employees more
pros: A good place to have exposure to sales, generally good leads. Colleagues are generally helpful and blessed with a good manager.
cons: Micromanaging is killing productivity, management doesn't seem to realize it. It is like a sweatshop for sales. An employee's scorecard or KPI is killing productivity. Contradicting sources of acquisition with different weightage in acquisition cases. (e.g acquiring a case from referrals does not equals to acquiring a case from other sources). summary: A company that can't find its way.

advice: Employees are people with lives. Get back to maximizing shareholder wealth and stop chasing every woke shiny thing that appears in todays culture.

summary: Citi not as great as I thought it would be
advice: to focus more on their employees development and provide ongoing feedback. No just say "i need you to do this" especially without giving any direction to what needs to be done. Communication needs a lot of improvement as well.

advice: Management should concentrate on more stability of personnel.

summary: Citibank is a nice place to work
advice: Invest more in Technology
pros: Citi is a very diversified company with presence in many countries world wide. Citi is a very nice place to work with many opportunities to learn and grow. It offers one of the best work life balance programs with very flexible working hours and telecommuting options.
cons: Compensation has not grown in the past few years and Citi is falling behind its competitors in attracting new talent. The decision making process is very slow.

summary: Great firm with focus on junior development and significant responsibility for analysts
advice: Hire more junior people
pros:
- Analysts expected to play up, travel for work, significant client interaction
- Great pay, perks and benefits (401K full match)
- Great paltform, there's experts on everything you might need to do, globally and very easy to learn much more than just the job function
cons:
- Bureaucracy can be annoying
- Too lean, need to hire more junior people

summary: Great environment, good benefits, the people are great
pros: I love the people who worked in my dept in back office, management is friendly and understanding, you still have a life at home, dress code is chill.
cons: Hard to move up with company, system they use sucks, no one really knows actual procedures so we set ourselves up for failure. No one is fully trained on a poaition. Management recently changed and def made some great changes for better so far.

summary: Horrid the company the managers are awful they won't answer questions or help in any way.

advice: Stop yelling to motivate employees.  Maybe you are trying to show enthusiasm or get people's attention but employees are actually tuning you out and just hear noise.  Stop just cutting staff to cut costs but balance with client, employee and corporate needs.
pros: Global Brand Name.  Good reputation globally.  Short branch hours.  Good possible incentives although difficult to attain, Public Relations
cons: Computer systems old and cumbersome for employees and clients, Employee development lacking, Training is superficial, employee morale very low

summary: worked as system analyst in Brazil

should invest in building trust throughout Citi. The return will be a more vibrant enterprise, more innovative products and more satisfying relationships;

work from home three/four days per week, depending on your project and team;
status: people think that Citi is a great place to work and all employers are smart.

advice: Not all "millenials" are lazy, arrogant, and have no motivation. Companies shouldn't have to cater to their employees but they should certainly be aware of the changing workforce and know what younger employees are looking for in a career.
pros: Great healthcare and good company values. Lots of added perks for employees
cons: So large that employees are only numbers. Career advancement opportunities are all hidden in a huge pile of ambiguous titles that mean nothing when there are hundreds of "Senior Vice Presidents".

advice: Pay more and show your appreciation to valued employees.
pros: Good health, retirement benefits and ample PTO.
cons: Company is trying to cut costs and increase revenue so will not hire additional personnel to cover increasing volume of business which results in employees being stressed and overworked, making it hard to find healthy work-life balance.. Expectation of middle management is that persons work excessive hours to manage workload without additional compensation and often times with little appreciation for the hard work employees put in.

summary: Pays very well, you work very hard.
advice: Continue to reward those that work hard, but also reduce micromanaging those that are performing well.
pros: Good compensation plan. 1 month PTO. Great middle management. Competent training. Great tools for getting the job done. HR does great job of screening potential job candidates to reduce the bad hires.
cons: Work life balance can be a challenge if you want to be successful. Aggressive goals. Systems are outdated and constantly being "upgraded" which results in glitches and work arounds.

advice: Evaluate existing departments and processes before implementing a better mousetrap.  Sometimes you just need to change the bait!
pros: Nice people to work with
cons: There is always something new to learn, and not because you want to, but because there's a new boss in town in a department you interact with.  Internal battles are nonstop. Supplier management processes are so poorly managed, there is no path to success.  Partners are not pleased with internal delays and it affects overall job satisfaction.

advice: go work in a normal company, or ask friends how normal relations look like. you are probably from small city focused on career - first learn high expectations to yourself, respect, organization, later think abouot management position
pros: stable work, without high expectations
cons: boring, uneficient, unmotivating system, they encourage you to do more work, but they give a bonus only for few best workers. end of the month they ask to stay over hours - sorry but you pay me to be  a half- slave what you pay is what you get, if you are a manager - you are paid as manager and your responsibility is to organize the work to avoid situations like this.

advice: Need to know that employees deserve to be paid for the work that that did and in the amount they were promised....
pros: Some of the benefits were ok, but I expected better than that. Nice cafe and nice child care on site.
cons: When a company tells you that they are going to be giving you a  $1k bonus if you do a certain amount of work and you do. Then you DESERVE TO GET THAT BONUS CHK.  I went up the chain of command ALL THE way to HR just to get the run around.  I still NEVER GOT MY BONUS CHK.. THEY CAN'T BE TRUSTED!!!!!

advice: Be more consistent with focus and priorities. Constant shifting takes its toll on morale.
pros: Citi offers really great benefits and has some of the smartest and most diverse people working for them.  The diversity is really incredible,  and they are very supportive in many ways.
cons: The internal politics can be a bit much, and change is the only constant in terms of management in some areas. It's a "always on" culture, meaning, there are no bankers hours at Citi.

advice: You will be able to shine if you establish yourself as an expert, be willing to lead several tough projects and force your way into rooms to discuss performance with directors
pros: Great culture, knowledgeable and cooperative peers. Some room to advance. The company really understands that you have a life outside the company that needs your attention.
cons: Pay is slightly off based on market. Mortgage is dissolving and the management staff doesn't really know anyone from the other lines of business.

advice: Good luck.
pros: Good commission potential, overtime is a plus alot of extra hours, can sell personal loans to consumers which sells itself. People need money so its not hard to sell product, global presence so product is trustworthy.
cons: Goals of bank is difficult they expect you to bring in ridiculous amounts in balances every month. sometimes the department that works in calculating your points for commission takes forever to update your numbers.  65% of your scorecard is measured by the balances you bring in.

advice: focus on what is important, reduce the watchers and increase the doers, compliance and regulation is imperative for sustainability but don't allow the organization to get buried in it losing focus on growth opportunities, just use common sense
pros: well rounded employees, variety of business, operational and functional jobs, global organization, multiple physical locations, work within teams can be exceptional
cons: buried in process and red tape, many walls are in the way to restrict productivity, some of the mindset that we've always done in this way

advice: Great job of keeping employee satisfaction at the forefront. After all, it's happy, engaged, and committed employees that keep customers happy.
pros: This company takes great care of its employees, in terms of pay, benefits, perks, and plenty of opportunity for advancement.
cons: It seems like there's a lot of movement within certain businesses, and some jobs are not as stable as others. Always have yourself positioned for other roles within Citi, should you find yourself in a job elimination round.

advice: Focus on acquiring and promoting talented individuals,  ask your employees for insight and suggestions about how to improve processes and put your foot down when necessary.
pros: It's one of the best companies in the world! The pay is good, the people are gifted and well-rounded and the opportunities and in supply.
cons: It can at times be impersonal due to the size. There are also areas where can be disorganized and in need of stricter management.

advice: Continue paring down non-core parts of the business!
pros: Rotated through a couple of desks in Citi's quant analyst program. There was good training provided at the start, and people were generally helpful, compared to other Wall St banks. Fast-paced, with a good exposure to different asset classes.
cons: It's such a large place that it's easy to get lost, literally and figuratively. Direction of the company is not always clear due to many layers of management and asset sales.

advice: Focus on furthering the team instead of keeping them to keep them
pros: Very flexible, casual attire, get your work done attitude which is great, managers are all over the country so they aren’t sitting directly with you which is challenging at first but teaches Internet relationship building
cons: Lack of upward mobility which is very tough when you’re first starting your career. If you’re looking for good experience in recruiting and lots of stretch assignments Citi is the place to be.

advice: Appreciate your employees more and if they have the skills and experience to grow let them take on new opportunities instead of hindering them.
pros: They have great benefits and tuition reimbursement. They also have flexible schedules and work with your school schedule. The pay is competitive in situations where you don't have a degree. Promotional opportunities.
cons: The politics within the company can be bad and cause some great employees to be under appreciated which leads to a high turnover rate.

advice: Shake up your middle management. Stop trying to portray a sense of family by promoting tedious, vapid gestures like "take your daughter to work day" and "PRIDE day". Where were you when the competition were handing out bonuses?
pros: Large diverse group of employees
cons:
No real training opportunities
Pay is better elsewhere
Middle Managers are like scorpions...they take credit for success and dump failure on the people under them.
Middle managers are cliquish. They have a private club which they guard entry into.

summary: Worked at Citi for over 25 years and for the last 20 years the bank has been struggling
advice: Take care of your employees. Happy employees will give you happy customers which will enhance stock performance. Stop sending work overseas and laying off local staff just for the bottom line. There is no relationship between performance and decisions. My entire department was displaced to send the work to India  where the employees lacked the required knowledge.
pros: Lack of commitment to long term employees . Everyone is on edge and expects layoffs
cons: There is no dedication to the employees . They only care about the stock price and the top senior management and their bonus

advice: Upgrade the systems and stick to the priorities.
pros: For a call center the atmosphere as for the most part be pretty laid back. Many events to try and get moral up and going.
cons:
The company is getting out of the business of supporting mortgages post-sale.  The partner company Cenlar is taking over this role.  As a result, this an other offices have been having ongoing layoffs for the past year an a half. 

Databases and programs are also very outdated.

advice: No advice, you should be capable of figuring it out on your own.
pros: Compared to other employers benefits are great. The salary was better than other banks when it came to entry level positions such as teller jobs.
cons: Worked every other weekend. Management was mediocre with high school education level backgrounds. Sales driven environment that can force employees into unethical sales however, if you enjoy sales this would not be an issue. No work life balance. Asking for vacation was always an issue.

advice: Hire more managers at a 15/20 max team size, so we can coach and develop, and be able to take time off with out feeling overwhelmed  when we come back.
pros: Citi benefits are great. Company really does seem to care about their employees
cons: Work way too many hours. Unable to use vacation time or will get backlogged on work. Teams continually exceed the promised 20 agents (25-30) due to always being understaffed. Always asking more of us and needing it done yesterday.

summary: Inclusive environment with lots of opportunities
pros: Inclusive environment, affinity groups, good base salaries, international opportunities, the chance to work on global projects even at a junior level. It's also hard to lose your job, as underperformers are getting a development plan, rather than firing them in the first place.
cons: Benefits and YE bonus can be a downside (at least in Budapest). Requires a lot of patience as many employees can't talk English proficiently. All the bureaucracy of a TNC.

summary: Great place for fresh graduates to gain experience in a well established MNC
pros: Your productivity is recorded in the system automatically. So your performance will always be measured by merit. You can get promoted in a short period if you are really really good in your job. Your career opportunity is limitless as it is a huge company that located across the globe.
cons: High expectation from top management for stellar result and productivity on daily basis even if you are still new.

advice: The strategy of removing or relocating the company's IT resources has resulted in loss of valuable human talent and with that comes little to no in house innovations.
pros:
Remote work option (depending on team culture)
Diverse culture
Good work experience
cons:
Citi has been slashing away at staff for years, and the IT organization has been taking its share of layoffs. This won't change any time soon.
Overworked IT employees due to this.
Little/no raises or bonuses. You're lucky to have your job for another year.

advice: Management needs to find a way to adhere to their own timelines and give more training and development to it's employees.  There is no reward and recognition structure for employees that do a good job. Too much red tape to get recognized for a job well done.
pros:
Good employee benefits exist. Employee savings and health benefits. 
Nice place to learn a few processes to get you ready for next job.
Nice mix of employees young and old.
cons:
No room for development and promotion. 
Roles are constantly switching and sometimes causing employees to take on the work of someone who would have been paid more. The little underpaid guys doing majority of the work.

summary: Good job to work for in Tucson
advice: Be more open with advice on moving up the corporate ladder, proactively reach out to employees for areas of growth (not just to write someone up), and have a TRUE open door policy without the conversation jeopardizing employees' job
pros: Good benefits that start from day one, nice amount of vacation time, and possibility of advancement
cons: Internal job transfers can be paid a lot less than external employees,  even with the same experience

advice: Reward to retain top talent.
pros: Great people, role model leadership. Flexibility to take on other jobs and get 360 exposure to the business. Opportunity to learn both the private level cards business, and that of the retail partner. Citi has a presence in more than 100 countries, so opportunity to move around the globe.
cons: salary... need to go somewhere else, then come back. Otherwise, difficult to even get a good raise when earning a promotion.

advice: Take a look at your midlevel managers. If there is excessive turnover under a specific manager, there is a reason for it.
pros: Citi is a large bank complex organization with many opportunities to learn about products that span various businesses throughout the globe.
cons: Not a very friendly environment. People are expected to do their work and not ask questions. Culture is very tense and people are "stressed". Managers do a good job at managing up, but  are terrible are leading teams.

summary: Overall Citi was a good company to work for
advice: Don't be afraid to tell upper management that it's not acceptable for employees to do more with less.  You can only cut so many employees and still expect the work to get done.
pros: Great work life balance (flex time / remote work).  Many tools available to enhance your career options (online training)
cons: Saving money is the bottom line.  Management just looks out for themselves.  No job security in technology.

advice: Encourage sr. managers to take risk (at least in IT) and achieve value to the company rather than focus on CYA. Value people who can deliver rather than smooth talkers. You are fooling yourselves.
pros: Will get to solve challenges you never get to solve anywhere else. Fantastic environment to take up real challenges.
cons: Has lost its mojo in the recent years due to too much regulation. People are more interested in CYA than doing the right thing, take risk and deliver value.

advice: Get it together.  Stop the nepotism. Put very competent people in management and stop the revolving door.  It makes the company look like it is schizophrenic.
pros: The banking holidays and liberal time off is great.  Great benefits also.
cons: Change that makes no sense.  Endless cycle of layoffs.  Never seem to know what they are doing.  The most competent people are not in management. Even in IT, they must be so frustrated with the lack of communication between business lines.  Takes FOREVER to get a new process going, again because the most competent people are not at the helm in most departments.

advice: During my time I always thought that there was a contradiction between the overall mission of the company and what was actually carried out by middle management.
pros: A very secure job with nice benefits and a comfortable workplace to work in. Reachable sales targets in most cases and an uncapped commission structure.
cons: Mediocre entry level base salary and in most cases not possible to make more than 75k a year with commission.

pros: I have worked with Citi for 13 years and it has some really great benefits; I have been in several departments, and have only been able to obtain positions in these departments through word of mouth; when there is opportunity, you have to make the move, pay is similar to most companies.
cons: the only positions obtained were through word of mouth, I have yet to see anything productive come out of the HR department.

advice: Keep pushing out and reinforcing the mission statement. It does eventually filter through and jmbed itself throughout the firm.
pros: Great income and Benefits. Friendly colleagues. World class client list. I was very sorry to leave Citi but I am looking forward to a busy retirement travelling the States and the world.
cons: There's not a lot wrong here - it has the usual irritants that are to be found in all very large scale global organizations - but nothing of great significance.

advice: Pay more attention to employee growth and development and not just of the one employee you like but of all employees who demonstrate the capability to get the job done.
pros: Good work life balance. Most managers and peers are respectful towards each other. Good resume builder and place to start but not necessarily build a career
cons: promotion and opportunities for growth often based on favoritism and not performance. Mediocre salary and bonuses. Can get stuck in one position easily.

advice: Invest in technology and systems. Have a better project management team who can plan the time lines of projects in a reasonable and sensible way with proper design.
pros: Reasonable work hours, Primarily a Unix shop  with opportunity to learn how a bank works. The people who work here are usually reasonable and nice cafeteria, On site medical room
cons: Very bureaucratic place and some times things happen slowly. Time structure is rigid and people are expected to show up before 9.

advice: Think about all possible ramifications of the decisions you make.  For example, if near term cost cutting impedes your ability to grow revenues in the medium term, take a minute to decide whether the cost cutting action is REALLY necessary (i.e. firing senior analysts, cancelling conferences, etc).  Don't talk up the bonus pool in Sept and then pay people down yr/yr in Jan...happens every year.
pros: Great people across the divisions.
cons: Poor leadership within the investment bank/global markets division.

advice: Flexibility can be hard to work into an organization as big as Citigroup, but it is what you need to remain on top.
pros: Engaging work, very good boss, I felt my work was valued and important.  The pay was also reasonable.  There were a lot of other very smart people working there and a lot of opportunities to form fruitful relationships.
cons: Bureaucracy can be constricting, hard to get some things done because of the sheer size of the organization.

summary: It is neutral. Not good not bad
advice: As in any other company managers should listen to own employees and try to understand their problems and not just worry about own carrier. It is though relevant to any other company.
pros: Big bank company, good salary, interesting work, new technologies, interesting people. The company is highly recognizable. They pay bonuses. And Citi never sleeps.
cons: long commute for me, people not very friendly. Managers worry about own carrier only. There is no good relations between coworkers.

summary: Many excellent co-workers and great opportunities among the silos
advice: Please continue to get back to Citi's core traditions and the Reed model.  The Weill "supermarket" model would work well if somebody could connect the silos that provide the pieces.
pros:
Global presence in diverse lines of business
The brand is still strong despite recent troubles
The bank is coming back into favor
cons:
The "silo culture" lives on
Internal politics can be intense
The bank tends to try to re-make itself in the image of its latest acquisition

advice: Well, company is TOO big for any body to go any thing.  Consolidation of activities to STE groups creates too much dependency and too coordination to get things done.
pros: Too Big to fail company, so relative job safety for full time employees. Once one gets accustomed learning curve is climbed, experience is relatively easy.
cons: Poor work life balance and over work . Too much coordination needed and too much dependency for even a small activities

advice: Stop diluting title rewards, focus more on management directors to be hands on rather than hands off.
pros:
Citi is an equaliser. Consistency, perseverance, and hard work is rewarded. The company achieves a good balance between pushing performance vs pushing over employees to insanity levels.

Management is top notch.
cons: Fluff is still around. Citi like aig always put bodies and focused less on efficiencies. Mgmt has woken up and concrete efforts being made to make it a lean, mean org.

summary: Know how to talk and you don't need to work much!
advice: Have a better reward/punishment system.  A lot of employees are not putting in their weigh into company performance but are sticking around as a headcount.
pros: Good company culture.  Has annual employee survey.  Managers attempt to empower staff.  Company cares about work/life balance.  Job security as HR keeps management in perspective.
cons: Salary not very competitive.  Very low bonus if any.  Little salary increase.

pros: For those who are chosen to participate in the Management Associate Program, this firm opens the doors to the senior management team and opportunities throughout the bank. Coupled with an excellent cross-border and cross-cultural training program, it's no wonder the slots in the program are so coveted.
cons: Most likely due to the rapid acquisition and expansion of the bank in prior decades but there were corporate silos and internal divides that were still in the process of being integrated.

advice: Please make sure you're W/L balance and MERITOCRACY programs reaches to all your staffs in all corners of the globe where Citi is located...Please also make sure that your HR is hiring the correct personnel's some paper tiger's who only look's good in the're resume then that' it!
pros: Better Salary than normal or local companies. nuff said...
cons: TOO MUCH OFFICE POLITICS! IN THE DEPT THAT I AM LOCATED THOUGH! TOO MANY PEOPLE WHO LIKE AND LOVE TO KISS A.....

pros:
Good company to work for
My manager truly cared about us
Insurance and benefits were really good for the area and started when you're hired
Multiple shifts to choose from
Good, thorough training
cons:
Very stressful job if you are a phone representative
Needed seniority to get better shift hours
Not allowed to take a few seconds to breathe between calls
Call center never shuts down even if roads are dangerous in winter, so you have to use vacation time if you cannot make it to work

advice: End of the year reviews are great tool to evaluate employees but in some circumstances other factors should be taking into consideration.
pros: Great place to work, some of the team leads are amazing
cons:
Be careful with the End of the year review, it can really impact you career at Citi.
Second chances are not part of the culture

advice: Give country more rights and freedom
pros: Good culture, excellent colleagues, good environment
cons: Country has little freedom, all things need to seek for regional headquarter's advice, who may not be familiar with the  local rules and situation, everything is tooooo slow, the process is complex and very looooong, which does not encourage innovation; the system is so out of date, Eclipse system is so hard to use and often doesn't work, which impact the business and customers

advice: Overall I would have to say that it was a great experience and I would highly recommend working for them.
pros: Great Company to work for.  Pay is good and they are easy to work with as far as work schedules go.
cons: The Supervisor gave me the impression he was inexperienced.  There were a few occasions that my phone calls were not returned in a timely manner.

advice: Become more customer friendly and care for your employees also. Move into smaller markets. Share more wealth with employees and do more career development.
pros: The biggest brand in the retail banking world and a great place to learn and prove yourself. Wonderful if you are a tp level performer.
cons: the company does nothing for career development and employees are stuck at a certain level. There is no opportunity for lateral movement.

advice: Be consistent. Grant the same opportunities to all members of the team. Be more transparent.
pros: Good team environment in my work area. Large organization with people throughout the world.
cons: Very open environment that can be noisy and hard to hear when on a call. Difficult when managers and the business are in one location and you in another. Manager can be hit or miss. Some teams allowed to work remote while others are not.

advice: support your loan officers, and actually pay attention to the needs of your LOan officers. Help your loan officers with marketing and other support to gain trust and maintain that trust with consumers and Realtors.
pros: Training was decent, and coworkeRs at bank branches were really great.
cons: Where to start. Processing system is still part of the stone ages although Cities started to develop their own brand new processing system, which still sucks. Management pushes unrealistic goals on loan officers. Pay structure sucks.

pros: WFH Options. Flexible hours, Full healthcare
cons:
Now for the cons, where do I start...

1. Working hours: Citi has the fixed 37.5 hours as most companies do however your workload will almost guarantee a minimum of 45-50 hours per week

2. Overtime: As mentioned above there will always be considerable overtime and zero overtime pay. The salary at case manager level does not even remotely make up for the amount of overtime required.

3. Politics: The politics in this company is an absolute farce, senior directors from LATAM visiting the Dublin office and giving orders/direction of how another hub should be run, ideals were given by one particular director and he was overruled by a majority vote of the directors, what he suggested was ludicrous, that a case manager should have at least 120 KYC records in their name, he would have caused individuals to collapse form stress and possible hypertension issues if this occurred.

3. Culture: Citi has by far the most toxic culture I have ever witnessed in my career, the process of cc;ing someone’s manager as if to say "Im telling on you" when you have a professional disagreement with someone, most notably relationship managers. When issues do occur in Citi, especially if a deliverable is late, there is always someone to play the scapegoat and take the blame and this is 99% not the individual who is solely to blame.

4. IT Infrastructure: Everyone's favorite topic in Citi, the company and their so called internal KYC system is well and truly a disaster, instead of fixing issues with the system they invent interim controls to essentially go around the problem instead of identifying the root cause and fixing the problem at the source, do you as a company actually realize how ridiculous this is, you first get someone who is skilled at writing procedures to write a new procedure for an issue, you then have to perform a training session with case managers on a global scale to understand this new procedure and if QA did not pay attention to some aspect of the training the case manager will get an instant rejection point, the auditors must dread having to audit the ICG BSU. What are your IT team doing?? when I say IT I am referring to the individuals who write the logic/source code for the KYC system. 

5. Administration; I understand that every job will have elements of administrative work but Citi is ridiculous, their internal tracking tool on each record keeps on getting more long winded, and due to this it takes more and more time to complete, as mentioned below 100 records in my name amounted to a total of 2 hours and 35 minutes to complete to perfection, the senior case managers take it upon themselves to check this rigorously as if we are babies and need to be checked on constantly. Do you think I had nothing better to do than spend almost 3 hours updating a tracker??? in that time I could have done research on 5 or 6 KYC records, wasteful.

6. Career Opportunities: There are none, it really depends on who you know, to be promoted from a C9 to a C10 position is only an increase in 4k, and your job is essentially the same, and that is also the same level as a senior case manager (supervisor), most companies pay 48-50 for a supervisor. A colleague of mine interviewed in another department for another role, it is common practice to state to your supervisor if you are looking for alternative opportunities to see if your role can be changed or given more responsibility but also to prepare for a departure and hire a new employee. In this instance my colleague was called into an office and was told sternly by his supervisor that "I can stop this process" are you actually kidding me that he tried to stand in the way of advancing his career, this is considerably unprofessional behaviour and this is in fact actionable from a legal standpoint.

Finally, I was considered to be a strong case manager within the department, I was extremely knowledgeable of the policies and procedures, I built professional relationships with staff and management and my quality was exceptionally high and because of this Citi seriously took advantage by putting almost 100 records in my name and then my targets started to suffer naturally because of getting pulled in 100 different directions every day, what really agitated me is that with the tracking tool I could see how many records was in everyone else's name on my team and not one had more than, 40, this was absolutely unacceptable from a team of 26 and one person is given 100 instead of these being shared out.

summary: Toxic Culture, Selfish/Incompetent Managers, Promotion based on politics, social class and if you're a good looking girl
advice: The Board of Directors need to fire all of senior management en masse and allow the employers that have put many years in the company and know what the hell their doing to actually run it.
pros: Excellent Cafeteria/Clinic/Gym at 388 and so so benefits.
cons:
Almost Everything Else.   This place has one of the most toxic corporate cultures I've ever seen with around 80-90% of employees dissatisfied with their jobs. 

-Incompetent Senior Management; Senior management plays an annual game of musical chairs where they reshuffle/eliminate huge parts of the company instead of actually dealing with the real problems (kind of like demoing a building constantly instead of actually going in and making the necessary repairs)  and  in the process cause major disruptions to the functions of the company with any regard on how it actually impacts the operations of the company or the people employed.  In many cases, they will come in with an exact opposite philosophy to that of their predecessor instead of establishing any sort of continuity.  Not one project I've seen in my 10 years here has been driven to completion due to this constant half assing by Senior Management. This is not to mention that many of them happen to also be severe alcoholics that get wasted every day after work.  Just visit one of the bars around Tribeca and you'll see them in droves downing cocktails and shots (while sloppily trying to hit on their female coworkers). The company is also highly bureaucratic with many layers of redundant management; what some of them do is an absolute mystery. 

-Sociopathic/Selfish Managers:  I've only ever had one good manager in my time here that actually continued to drive my learning progress and allowed me to learn more than my actual function required.  The majority of managers behave like pimps and are very controlling and territorial and will attempt to limit your growth as much as possible so that you don't become a potential threat to them or eventually leave them.  They will also use you to benefit themselves and screw you over when they don't need you.  Performance Reviews are based on how much you get along with them and how much you are will to play along with their selfishly motivated agendas.  Teams/Divisions operate more like rival street gangs/fiefdoms that constantly compete with each other and will do what benefits them first and foremost before putting the company's interest first.  It's no wonder the company needed a bailout and failed 2 stress tests. 

-Internal Mobility:  This is pretty much an absolute joke.  99.9 %of internal positions are filled way before the job requisition hits the site.  The hiring managers usually know who they want (based on politics & favoritism) and post the position up as a formality.  HR is pretty much a useless and powerless function here that spews a bunch of politically correct jargon to make it appear like everything is fine and dandy.    

-Promotion based on Meritocracy:  Another major sham.  Any attempt at even defending this is an absolute insult to the many hard working individuals that get screwed over year after year on promotions.  The company has a created a culture where it's become almost mandatory for you to leave for another company every 3-4 years in order to get a decent raise.  If you do end up getting lucky with an internal move, your move is deemed "lateral" usually and you won't get any raise in pay or title.  There is also a HUGE pay/compensation gap between Front Office and Back Office employees with Back Office getting screwed most of the time.  

The only REAL way to get promoted is if you come from a well off family that brings business to the company (like JP Morgan's Sons & Daughter's program) , have a father/uncle/boyfriend that works for a strong division and has a lot of pull with the hiring manager, or if you are a good looking girl that's willing to play eye candy (and possibly more) to fat middle aged sexually frustrated executives twice to three times your age.  The latter is by far the quickest way to get promoted here.   As a matter of fact, the higher up you go  floor-wise at 388, the better looking the girls get (senior executives sit on the higher floors).  I know a good looking girl that went from Analyst to VP in just one year and another that got hired as a VP with nothing but a degree in poetry and 0 experience in the financial industry.
